0.content:
Abyss Order (also: Order of the Abyss, the Abyss Order): The Abyss Order is a secretive legion of intelligent monsters of the Abyss, such as Abyss Mages, Heralds and Lectors, who hate the Seven and Celestia and work to overthrow the world the gods rule. Most of its members were once people of Khaenri'ah, the godless nation destroyed 500 years ago, who were cursed into monstrous forms. It was founded by Chlothar Alberich after the cataclysm and is now led by the Traveler's lost twin, whom the Order reveres as its Prince or Princess. Dainsleif hunts it constantly.

Ordinary people in Teyvat know almost nothing about it. Diluc, who has access to Mondstadt's underground networks, calls it an enemy of the human race about which even those networks rarely hear anything. Its members usually live in the Abyss and emerge for specific operations, often using hilichurls as manpower.

Leadership: The Traveler's twin sibling (Lumine if the player chose Aether, Aether if the player chose Lumine) leads the Order. Their goal is to restore Khaenri'ah and confront the Heavenly Principles, and they refuse to reunite with the Traveler until their war against the gods is over.

The sibling was once named heir of Khaenri'ah and hailed as its "Savior". After waking from Asmoday's seal they travelled Teyvat with Dainsleif, met Chlothar in Sumeru, and in time decided that Chlothar had been right about the world. They joined the Order and became its leader, while Dainsleif chose to fight it. The sibling still loves the Traveler and asks them to keep travelling and see the truth for themselves.

Goals: The Order wants revenge on the gods for destroying Khaenri'ah, an end to the curse on its people, and the rebirth of Khaenri'ah.

Dainsleif says the Order seeks to destroy the nations watched over by the Seven because the gods destroyed Khaenri'ah. Under the sibling the aims are more specific. The Order wants to cleanse the hilichurls' curse, so that they either return to the cycle of life and death or become the foundation of a rebuilt Khaenri'ah. It wants to complete the **Loom of Fate**, weave the ley lines of a new Khaenri'ah, and set that world down somewhere so that the sibling, backed by an entire world, can speak to the Heavenly Principles as an equal.

Methods: The Order corrupts and manipulates powerful beings: it poisoned Dvalin's mind into attacking Mondstadt as Stormterror and planned to rebuild the sea god Osial as a mechanical god. It scavenges Khaenri'ahn technology, especially the Ruin Guards that Khaenri'ah called "Field Tillers". It works through hilichurls, whom Abyss Mages can talk to in a long-forgotten language. It also tampers with ley lines, which carry memories as well as energy.

History: **Origins (about 500 years ago and after).** When Khaenri'ah fell in the cataclysm, the gods cursed its people. Pure-blooded Khaenri'ahns became immortal, and the rest became hilichurls. Chlothar Alberich's half-Mondstadter son Caribert became a hilichurl. In Avidya Forest, Chlothar and the travelling sibling found Vedrfolnir, a Sinner of Khaenri'ah, as a chained crystal worshipped by hilichurls. Vedrfolnir's Abyssal power restored Caribert's mind. Chlothar decided that the Abyss could do what the Seven would not, began to worship the Sinner, and founded the Abyss Order. He named his son the "Loom of Fate", free to weave his destiny anew.

**Present day.** The Order poisoned Dvalin against Mondstadt (Prologue, 1.0), plotted to make Osial a mechanical god from the Defiled Statue beneath Mt. Aocang (Chapter I Act IV), tried to cure the hilichurls in the Chasm (2.6), and secured the Loom of Fate (4.7). In 5.7 it attacked every Natlanese tribe at once as a feint while the sibling wove the ley lines of a new Khaenri'ah.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Order is active. It holds the Atlas of New Khaenri'ah and needs only a place to set it down. Its leader was last seen in Snezhnaya with Asmoday.

Its large Natlan force was badly depleted in 5.7. Dainsleif meant to make the campaign painful enough that the Order could never again mount one so large. Haden is immortal and cannot truly die. No Order operation was found in the main 6.x Nod-Krai story, which centred on Rerir and the Wild Hunt.

1.content: "Loom of Fate" began as Chlothar's name for his Abyss-touched son Caribert, who he believed could weave his destiny anew. It then became an Abyss Order operation. Before Fontaine it meant building a mechanical god from the Defiled Statue, Osial and the eye of the first Field Tiller. After the Hydro throne fell, it meant a device that, fully activated, can weave new ley lines into the world. While unfinished it could weave memories, and Caribert used that to calm the hilichurls around Vimara Village and give himself false memories of village life. The sibling secured the eye in 4.7 and, in 5.7, used the Loom in Natlan's Night Kingdom to weave the ley lines of a new Khaenri'ah, stored in an "Atlas" until a suitable place is found.

2.comment: Abyss Order: Chlothar Alberich and the founding
2.content: Chlothar was a Khaenri'ahn noble of the Alberich Clan who resented his predestined life and had a son, Caribert, by a Mondstadt woman. At the cataclysm he was cursed with immortality, and the half-blooded Caribert became a hilichurl. Living in Avidya Forest under the name "Eide", he met the Traveler's sibling. Together they found the Sinner Vedrfolnir's crystal, and its Abyssal power, together with a forbidden medicine, briefly restored Caribert's mind. When Caribert unmasked and Abyssal power poured out, Chlothar was won over completely. He declared that only a sinner could save a sinner, hailed the sibling as Prince/Princess, and founded the Abyss Order. The Traveler relived this through ley-line disturbances in Caribert (3.5).

3.content: Abyss Mages are the Order's common casters. They are shielded, elemental, and able to speak with hilichurls in a long-forgotten language that is said to give them power. Abyss Heralds are blade-wielding melee elites, and Abyss Lectors are their ranged spellcasting counterparts. Both can draw on intense Abyssal energy. Iniquitous Baptists are rarer and more powerful, and Haden, the Natlan commander, takes this form. Not every being of these kinds belongs to the Order.

4.comment: Abyss Order: The Defiled Statue operation
4.content: In Liyue the Order hid an inverted, Abyss-holding Statue of the Seven, the Defiled Statue, in ruins beneath Mt. Aocang. A talisman carried by an Abyss Mage described the first phase of the "Loom of Fate". The plan was to attach the sea god Osial's limbs to the statue and place the eye of the very first Field Tiller (Ruin Guard) in its hands, creating a god able to challenge Celestia. Abyss Mages searched dormant Ruin Guards for the eye in vain. The Traveler and Dainsleif found it at Stormterror's Lair, and Dainsleif kept it.

5.comment: Abyss Order: The Chasm curse experiment
5.content: Deep in the Chasm, hilichurls were drawn to a pool whose water suppressed the curse and went there to die. The sibling approved a device meant to amplify the water a hundredfold and turn the hilichurls back into Khaenri'ahns, knowing that failure would cause them terrible pain. Their Hydro Abyss Herald, the "Presager of the Abyss", defended it. Dainsleif, insisting the curse cannot be undone, fought it with the Traveler, and the Black Serpent Knight Halfdan destroyed the device. The Herald died there.

6.content: Enjou is a Pyro Abyss Lector and the Order's self-styled "lowly clerk", who chases ancient lore and knows of, but is not part of, the inner circle. He posed as the Traveler's helper in Enkanomiya (2.4) while seeking Before Sun and Moon. He then revealed himself, fought, and left on friendly terms, warning that Paimon might one day betray them. In Natlan he reappeared under new aliases, traded favours with Kinich, and finally walked into the Mare Jivari. He is a long-lived sage of unknown origin who has forgotten his homeland, and he avoids fights where he can.

7.content:
Adventurers' Guild (also: Adventurer's Guild, Adventurers Guild): The Adventurers' Guild is Teyvat's adventurer-for-hire service. It gathers word-of-mouth information and requests from ordinary people and organisations and redistributes them as commissions for registered adventurers. Its motto is "Ad astra abyssosque" (to the stars and the abyss), though in practice the work runs from finding lost kittens to exploring domains. Every region has a branch or post with a receptionist named Katheryne; most known branches are led by a Branch Master. Its headquarters is in Snezhnograd, Snezhnaya.

Each adventurer carries an Adventurer Handbook that logs completed commissions and is used to pay out rewards. The Guild is not a government and does not give orders to nations; it sells a service and keeps submitters' identities confidential where it can. Its Snezhnayan roots are tied to the Fatui through Pantalone and Sandrone, which most adventurers never see.

Structure: One branch (or reception post) per region; most known branches are run by a Branch Master (none is named for Inazuma or Fontaine). Katheryne receives adventurers at each. Known branch masters: Cyrus (Mondstadt), Lan (Liyue), Kamal (Sumeru), Mansa (Natlan), Sarin (Nod-Krai).

Branch Masters write the entrance exams for new adventurers, advise newcomers on where to go and where not to go, and keep local information useful. The Guild has two known departments. The Intelligence Department does not take commissions: investigators collect information in the field, and organizers sort it and give it to adventurers. The Recruitment Department finds new members. Organizers rank commissions by difficulty from S downward to help newcomers adjust. Companions of a registered adventurer are recognised as members too: Paimon is listed in the Traveler's Handbook as their guide.

Leadership: Pantalone is the Guild's president (Pulcinella's artifact text calls him its "nominal president"), and Katheryne in Snezhnograd addresses him as branch master and reports the Guild's expenses to him. Dottore taunts the Traveler that adventurers claim "minuscule rewards" from Pantalone. Sandrone, a Harbinger, built Katheryne and holds a share of the profits, which Fatui artifact text says Pantalone ceded to her sincerely after Pulcinella's failed attempt to use her to claim a share. Branch masters answer upward to headquarters in Snezhnograd.

Members: Branch masters: Cyrus (Mondstadt), Lan (Liyue), Kamal (Sumeru), Mansa (Natlan), Sarin (Nod-Krai). Other named members include Alfry and Fischl of the Intelligence Department, Bennett, Nadia, Linnea (advisor), Talalikhin (clerk in Snezhnaya) and the retired Lohen and Valerina. The Traveler is a registered adventurer.

Goals: Publicly, to match people who need work done with adventurers willing to do it, and to keep adventurers safer by sharing knowledge about ruins and dangers. It is run as a business: rewards are paid in Mora and posting a commission carries a processing fee.

Methods: A client files a request and pays a fee; a commission may be designated so that only named adventurers are offered it. The submitter's identity is kept confidential unless the adventurer must know it to finish the job; if an adventurer deduces it from unrelated information, that is not the Guild's concern. Stalled commissions pile up at each branch and are reviewed periodically. If no capable adventurer can complete one, Katheryne talks to the client about cancelling it. Adventure Rank is a gameplay progression system, with rewards claimed from Katheryne.

History: The Guild's origins are unknown. It is present in Mondstadt and Liyue from the start of the story, and Lan's dialogue indicates its headquarters is in Snezhnaya. In Natlan, after the Night Warden Wars ended, some Natlanese adventurers were among the first to travel beyond their borders.

Relations: - **Fatui**: tied to Pantalone and Sandrone, yet the Handbook lists Fatui as enemies and some commissions target them. The wiki reads this as a sign of outward independence.
- **Mondstadt**: the Mondstadt branch advertises for recruits on the message board in the Angel's Share.
- **Akademiya**: Kamal hopes the Akademiya will not interfere with adventurers' activities.

Reputation: Seen as a reliable, if unglamorous, service for odd jobs. The Mondstadt branch struggles for recruits, with recruitment ads filling the Angel's Share message board, and Cyrus uses stories of danger and bravery to entice young people. The would-be adventurer Doolan says he refuses to join the Guild because of its boring clothes.

Status as of 7.1: Active everywhere. As of 7.1 it still operates posts in all eight regions, with Katheryne at each.

No canon event up to 7.1 shows the Guild changing hands, disbanding or openly taking sides in a conflict.

8.content: The Guild's receptionist, found in every region. She is a bionic Snezhnayan puppet created by Sandrone. Multiple identical Katherynes exist. She assigns commissions, shares local intel, and pays out daily commission and Adventure Rank rewards. Her idle lines are system-style messages ("Error", "Rebooting"), and she greets Sandrone as "My Lady".

9.content: Each adventurer is issued an Adventurer Handbook that records completed commissions and is used to pay out rewards. It also records commission history, income statement, evaluations, statistics and average positive ratings, since clients can rate an adventurer. When a Handbook is full a new one is issued; each has a serial number recorded in the adventurer's file. The Handbook lists Fatui as enemies.

10.content: Cyrus leads Mondstadt, which is short on members. Lan, Liyue's Branch Master, is a former mercenary who joined the Guild for its information network while searching for her missing brother's sword. Kamal, a former mariner, leads in Sumeru City. Mansa is a shaman of the Masters of the Night-Wind and leads Natlan. Sarin leads Nasha Town's Nod-Krai branch.

11.content: During the limited-time 7.0 event Great Expeditionist Challenge, the Traveler and Paimon visit the Adventurers' Guild Headquarters in Snezhnaya and take part in a tournament among adventurers. Details revealed there: Branch Masters can issue a part-time adventurer's certificate, so the Eremite mercenary Lemta can be paid for commissions; Urville is registered as Nadia's strategist; Ophelia manages Guild supplies in Fontaine; and the Pilgrimage veteran Liliuo joined the Guild after the Night Warden Wars.

12.content:
Alberich Clan (also: Alberich, House Alberich, Alberich family): The Alberich Clan is an old, pure-blooded noble family of Khaenri'ah, the sunken kingdom destroyed in the cataclysm 500 years ago. It was known for producing leaders of the kingdom's knights. It is not royal, but members stepped in as regents when King Irmin failed. Its present-day line includes Kaeya, the Cavalry Captain of the Knights of Favonius, who was raised in Mondstadt as Kaeya Alberich.

The clan existed at least as far back as the Eclipse Dynasty. It also produced Chlothar, who founded the Abyss Order, so the same family name connects the kingdom's last defenders to the Abyss Order, which Kaeya counts as an enemy. The clan survived the kingdom's fall in secret and still keeps no written records.

Structure: The Alberichs were nobles of Khaenri'ah's pure-blooded aristocracy, held to strict standards of conduct and given access to institutions such as the Royal Library. They had no royal blood. Canon names no head of the clan and gives no internal ranks. In the present day the clan keeps no written records of its affairs, a rule Kaeya's childhood scrap of clan history was saved in defiance of.

Members: Anfortas, the Knight Marshal and regent; Chlothar, founder of the Abyss Order; Kaeya, the present-day Cavalry Captain of the Knights of Favonius.

- **Alberich** (name only): in the book Perinheri, commander of half of Khaenri'ah's knights, counted among its four strongest. Whether this is the clan's founder or a later member is not stated.
- **Anfortas**: Knight Marshal and leader of the Schwanenritter, who declared himself Marshal Regent when Irmin could not rule. Canon never says outright that he was an Alberich; the inference is strongly supported.
- **Chlothar**: a young noble who resented his predestined life. He fathered Caribert with a woman from Mondstadt, was cursed with immortality in the cataclysm, and later founded the Abyss Order.
- **Kaeya**: a descendant of Chlothar by Dainsleif's account, left in Mondstadt as a child by his unnamed father.

Goals: The present-day clan's aims are not explained. The clan history Kaeya was taught says the Alberichs could not restore Khaenri'ah to life and should live as those who blaze like fire rather than wallow in embers. Kaeya's father sent him to Mondstadt as an agent of Khaenri'ah, and Kaeya long feared he would have to choose a side if Khaenri'ah and Mondstadt fought. He now says he will not carry out that duty and treats the Abyss Order as an enemy.

History: **Before the cataclysm.** The clan stood at the heart of Khaenri'ah's military. Perinheri names an Alberich as commander of half the knights, which shows the name was established by the time of the Eclipse Dynasty. The legend itself cannot be verified.

**The cataclysm.** When King Irmin was 'indisposed' and dark beasts attacked, Anfortas took over as regent. He and the Schwanenritter chose to lead survivors out of the kingdom to the surface, using old Ruin Golems against the beasts. The clan's own history says the Alberichs, who had no royal blood, ruled as regents when Irmin's strength failed.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Alberich Clan exists only in the shadows. Its only publicly known member is Kaeya, who lives in Mondstadt and does not serve the clan's agenda.

No new information about the clan was found in the 6.x Nod-Krai or 7.0-7.1 Snezhnaya story content that was checked. Its history is known from the Caribert quest (3.5), the Hidden Strife event (2.8), Kaeya's character stories and the in-world book Perinheri.

13.comment: Alberich Clan: Anfortas and the Schwanenritter
13.content: Anfortas was Khaenri'ah's Knight Marshal and leader of the Schwanenritter. When Irmin became unable to rule and dark beasts attacked, he declared himself Marshal Regent and led the Final Kingdom Council. The Schwanenritter decided to evacuate able survivors to the surface, into Sumeru, and used Ruin Golems to hold the beasts off. He is presumed to have died in the Dharma Forest as the last of his order. Whether he was an Alberich is inferred, not stated.

14.content: Chlothar Alberich, who first introduces himself to the Traveler's sibling as Eide, was a pure-blooded noble who loved a woman from Mondstadt. They had a son, Caribert. When the cataclysm came, Chlothar was cursed with immortality, and Caribert, not pure-blooded, became a hilichurl. Chlothar's search for a cure led to the Abyss and eventually to founding the Abyss Order. Caribert, whom Chlothar later called the 'Loom of Fate', disappeared. Chlothar went mad about a century after founding the Abyss Order and seemingly disappeared; a later burial that the Traveler took to be his suggests he escaped his curse before dying.

key: School of the Theory of Living Things
15.content:
Amurta (also: Amurta Darshan, School of Biology, School of the Theory of Living Things, Darshan of Biology): Amurta is the Sumeru Akademiya's school of biology, which also covers ecology, botany and medicine. It is recognised as the oldest and largest of the Six Darshans, and its colour is green. Its sage is Naphis, a famously short-tempered man of integrity who is now also the Akademiya's Grand Sage. Tighnari, the Forest Watcher, graduated from Amurta under Naphis.

The Darshan grew from the researchers who helped Greater Lord Rukkhadevata cultivate the rainforest, and its symbol carries a bird that resembles a Huma. Because the rainforest, its creatures and the public hospital all fall under its subject, Amurta is the Darshan most visibly tied to Sumeru's living land.

Structure: Amurta is one of the Six Darshans, each led by a Great Sage who sits on the Akademiya's advisory councils. Its members run from students and Driyosh (travelling scholars) up through formal researchers. Two institutions belong to it in practice. The Bimarstan, Sumeru's free public hospital, is staffed by Amurta researchers and students. Pardis Dhyai, a botany research site in the Dharma Forest, is run by Amurta, and Tighnari keeps close ties with its researchers. Disciplines taught include biology, ecology, botany and medicine.

Leadership: Naphis is Amurta's Sage. Tighnari calls him a man of integrity who sticks to his beliefs. Researchers fear his legendary temper, and even the former Grand Sage Azar gave him leeway.

Naphis was Tighnari's master and academic adviser. He wanted Tighnari to join the Amurta faculty after graduation but did not push when Tighnari chose a freer life as a Forest Watcher. During the Akademiya-Fatui plot, Naphis and Baladhuri of Vahumana opposed the plan and were locked up by the other four sages. Someone else posed as Naphis during that period. The other sages used his name on letters to recruit Tighnari. After the plot fell apart he was freed, weakened but otherwise well. By 6.6 he had been appointed Grand Sage, as stated in the 6.6 Archon Quest, while remaining head of Amurta.

Members: Tighnari is Amurta's best-known alumnus: he was admitted early, studied botany under Naphis and graduated, then left the Akademiya's centre to serve in the Avidya Forest. Collei, his trainee ranger, is expected to enrol in the Akademiya once her studies finish. Kaveh once suggested Amurta for her, since it is Tighnari's Darshan. Khedive Pursina is an Amurta ecologist who studies the Chasm's changing life forms. Khayyam retired from Amurta because of a patient's condition, according to a Bimarstan record. Zakariya, a Bimarstan doctor, is probably Amurta, but this is not stated.

Goals: Amurta studies life: plants, animals, ecosystems, and the health of people. Khedive says Amurta takes a dim view of those who rely purely on theory. The Darshan was founded by people who helped cultivate the rainforest.

History: Amurta is described as the first Darshan, created by the researchers who helped the old Dendro Archon cultivate the rainforest. It has been the largest Darshan ever since. The Akademiya has changed around it, but Amurta's mission is still natural science and medicine.

Relations: - **Sumeru Akademiya**: Amurta is one of its Six Darshans. The Akademiya's other schools are Rtawahist, Spantamad, Haravatat, Vahumana and Kshahrewar.
- **Forest Rangers**: Tighnari, an Amurta graduate, serves as a Forest Watcher, which ties the Darshan's botanical work to the ranger corps.
- **Vahumana**: its sage Baladhuri was Naphis' fellow prisoner and remains a sage with him.
- **Matra**: they enforce Akademiya rules on researchers, including Amurta, as Tighnari's remark about Karkata shows.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Amurta is led by Naphis, who is also Grand Sage. No Amurta-specific story was found for 6.7 to 7.1.

Naphis and the other sages took part in the 6.6 Irminsul crisis response from Caravan Ribat, where Tighnari and Cyno also appear. The 7.0 and 7.1 Archon Quests take place in Snezhnaya and did not touch the Darshans.

16.comment: Amurta: Naphis and the sages' plot
16.content: Naphis, a short-tempered, principled scholar, is the Amurta Sage and Tighnari's former master. When Dottore and four sages plotted to build a new god out of Scaramouche, Naphis and Baladhuri refused to go along and were locked up. The conspirators kept up the pretence that Naphis was working on the project, writing to Tighnari in his name. Tighnari's suspicion about the missing details in those letters led him to ask Cyno to investigate. The Traveler learned the details when the plot was exposed. Naphis was freed and later became Grand Sage.

17.content: Two Amurta institutions are worth naming. The Bimarstan is a hospital where Amurta researchers and students treat residents for free. Pardis Dhyai is a botanical research site in the Dharma Forest where Tighnari holds seminars. A Bimarstan record about the retired Amurta scholar Giyath Khayyam mentions the Amurta sage Siman Farrokhzad overseeing his treatment.

18.content:
Arataki Gang (also: Arataki-ha, Arataki's Gang, the Arataki Gang, Itto's gang): The Arataki Gang is a small band of friends in Hanamizaka, a district of Inazuma City, led by the oni Arataki Itto, who calls himself its "first and greatest head". Everyone in it means well, but its flyers, events, late-night music and accidents keep landing members in front of the Tenryou Commission. The Commission refuses to treat it as an official organisation. Deputy Kuki Shinobu gets the others out of trouble and handles the paperwork.

Itto insists that the gang is for outliers and those shunned by society. Granny Oni, who raised him, thinks it is only Itto and his friends spending time together. Both views fit what canon shows. The gang's odd jobs include logistics and transportation, home repair and performance, and Shinobu has added tax, legal consultation and event management.

Leadership: Arataki Itto leads. He is brash and loud but honest and fiercely loyal, and he treats members with the respect of family.

Per the wiki, apart from Shinobu the members are not very intelligent, so she is the gang's practical brain. Itto admits that nobody questions his leadership except Shinobu, who challenges everything he says, returns loot he brings back to share, and gets him out of jail. He lets it slide, and says an angry Shinobu would make his life a nightmare. Their relationship is the core of how the gang runs day to day.

Members: Besides Itto and Shinobu, the named members are Akira, Genta, Mamoru and Ushi, a young Akaushi bull.

- **Kuki Shinobu**: Deputy Officer. A masked, ninja-trained former Grand Narukami Shrine maiden who studied law in Liyue and holds many certifications. She joined and brought the others to heel within days.
- **Akira, Genta, Mamoru**: the gang's rank and file. Itto says Akira snores loudly and Mamoru is colourblind. Akira's account of the gang's founding is in the uncertainties.
- **Ushi**: a young bull the gang counts as an auxiliary member. He cannot communicate with the others but has his own principles, refusing anything unreasonable or law-breaking, and he sometimes helps Shinobu. When she advised him to find his own path, he insisted on staying with Itto. He assists Itto in combat through Itto's Elemental Skill.
- **Grandmaster Hanakado**: a boy obsessed with Onikabuto beetle battles, who joined after losing to Paimon and the Traveler in the 3.4 beetle event.
- **Traveler**: named a member by Itto, who says the gang will always answer their call.

History: **Origins.** After Itto's parents died of illness, the young Itto was driven from a village where his oni family had been suspected of theft. An elderly human woman saved him from a beating and fed him, and he eventually settled in Hanamizaka. The gang grew out of his friendships there, but members give conflicting accounts of when it began (see uncertainties). Shinobu joined after leaving the Grand Narukami Shrine, and her arrival gave the gang its first deputy, legal advice and discipline.

Relations: - **Tenryou Commission**: acts as the gang's opponent. It arrests members regularly and refuses to recognise the gang. Its officials once logged Itto as "unemployed", although he does odd jobs. Shinobu's friend Kujou Sara, a Tenryou commander, once took Itto's Vision under the Vision Hunt Decree, and Itto still wants a sumo rematch.
- **Yashiro and Kanjou Commissions**: the Yashiro Commission is the gang's route to festival venues, and in Itto's account it complained about the photo on the message board, while the Kanjou Commission demanded advertising tax over it.
- **Watatsumi Army**: Itto has a contact (Masato) at its Yashiori Island camp.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the gang is active in Inazuma. It is led by Itto and Shinobu, still unrecognised by the Tenryou Commission, and still getting into minor trouble.

Takuya was expected to be released from prison as of the 2026-06-01 birthday mail. The Traveler remains an honorary member. No Arataki Gang story developments were found for versions 6.x to 7.1.

19.comment: Arataki Gang: Kuki Shinobu in the gang
19.content: Shinobu introduces herself as the gang's deputy who handles its affairs, and tells people to contact her about Itto's inappropriate behaviour. She fled the shrine's duties and received a Vision, and later wore her mask after a child recognised her as the shrine maiden who never smiled. In the gang she mediates, litigates, cooks, repairs lacquerware and keeps the others in line. Her outfit is called Arataki's Demonic Deputy. In the hangout "The Gang's Daily Deeds", the Traveler acts as a "Chief Advisor" while helping her with bylaws and trouble the gang causes.

20.content: Ushi is a young brown Akaushi bull with golden horns, a crystal-shard-shaped tail tip and a small roof on his back decorated with oni faces. Itto found him before the Traveler arrived and he joined as an auxiliary member. He has a principled streak but cannot communicate with the gang. The wiki says his design is inspired by the akabeko, a traditional toy.

21.content:
Ayn Al-Ahmar (also: Ayn Al Ahmar, Ayn Al-Ahmar brigade): Ayn Al-Ahmar is a small Eremite mercenary brigade based in Port Ormos, whose members are fervent believers in King Deshret and hate Greater Lord Rukkhadevata. It is a subgroup of Deshret's Relics. Its leader Mizri bought a Divine Knowledge Capsule in a secret auction, convinced it held Deshret's power. Using it drove him mad, and the Matra took him away.

The name borrows "Al-Ahmar", which the Eremites treat as King Deshret's alleged true name. In the Archon Quest the Traveler meets two of its members, Tariq and Tumart. The group is poor, zealous and willing to scheme to raise the Mora for the capsule.

Structure: Ayn Al-Ahmar is one brigade among the many under the banner of Deshret's Relics, whose headquarters issues orders to its subgroups. In practice the Port Ormos group acts on its own, with a boss, two named lieutenants who talk and negotiate for him, and a handful of rank-and-file mercenaries. Its fighters, such as crossbow users, sword-dancers and halberdiers, use ordinary Eremite combat styles.

Leadership: Mizri leads the brigade. His followers call him "boss" and credit him with fervent devotion to King Deshret.

The Port Ormos business is run through Tariq, a talker who sells information, and Tumart, who speaks for the group on rivals. Both defer to Mizri, who appears in person only at the end of the Archon Quest. By then he is already deranged.

Members: Named members are Mizri (leader), Tariq and Tumart.

**Tariq** is a smooth, hostile spokesman who takes 500,000 Mora from the Traveler and Paimon in exchange for a merchant's address. He is the brigade's loudest preacher and spews contempt for the Akademiya. **Tumart** appears alongside him, assesses rival brigades and shares Tariq's views. The wiki has no further profile for him.

Goals: To bring King Deshret back. The brigade believes his power can be recovered, and that he will then punish Rukkhadevata's followers and the desert dwellers who forgot him.

Tariq tells the Traveler that Deshret founded the great desert nation of his people's ancestors, that he was the rightful God of Wisdom, and that Rukkhadevata betrayed him, took the title and destroyed his civilisation. He claims the voice of the Oracle has been heard in the desert, prophesying Deshret's resurrection. Members treat the Divine Knowledge Capsule as the vehicle for that return. They also refuse to let the Akademiya study it, because, in Alhaitham's words, that would tarnish their deity's soul.

Methods: The brigade is short of funds but determined to get the capsule "by any means necessary". Alhaitham says they have used methods "more foul than fair" to raise the Mora. They bid in a secret auction held among the Port Ormos brigades. When challenged, Tariq settles matters with a duel at an agreed time and place rather than negotiating.

History: In the Archon Quest chapter "Through Mists of Smoke and Forests Dark" (3.0), the Traveler and Paimon go to Port Ormos looking for an item the Akademiya lost, which is said to be linked to the gods. Several Eremite brigades were competing for it. Alhaitham explains that it is a Divine Knowledge Capsule that the brigades were bidding for in a secret auction. Dori's information shows that Mizri bought it. In the arranged duel, Tumart's and Tariq's men are beaten. Mizri arrives after using the capsule, mad, and attacks his own people. Alhaitham breaks his Akasha Terminal and the Matra arrest him. Alhaitham quietly keeps the capsule, and neither the Traveler nor the Matra notice.

Relations: - **Deshret's Relics**: parent organisation. Dehya describes a group whose brigades are willing to cross all kinds of lines for Mora.
- **The Caracal Battalion**: rival Port Ormos brigade after the same capsule. Tariq and Tumart dismiss it as "money-grubbing opportunists".
- **Alhaitham**: hostile adversary who undermines their business and who ends up with the capsule.
- **The Akademiya**: hated by the group. Tariq believes it helped Rukkhadevata cover up her crime.
- **The Matra**: arrest Mizri. The capsule's buyers were to keep their win quiet to evade the Matra.
- **Corps of Thirty**: a Port Ormos local says the Citadel of Regzar is getting fed up with the group's shouting about Deshret.

Reputation: Port Ormos locals hear them as noisy fanatics who keep shouting about Deshret's "resurrection". Alhaitham calls them poor but dogged. Dehya places them among the Relics, whose brigades she distrusts.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 nothing is known about the brigade's present state. Its leader was arrested in 3.0, and its parent group is described as dismantled.

22.content: Mizri is the leader of Ayn Al-Ahmar and a devout believer in King Deshret. He bought the Divine Knowledge Capsule in Port Ormos. After using it, he went mad, attacked his own men and was subdued by Alhaitham, who destroyed his Akasha Terminal. The Matra took him away, and he muttered "World... forget me." Beyond a flashback in a later quest, he has no other canon appearance.

23.content: Tariq and Tumart are the brigade's talkers at Djafar Tavern. Tariq takes 500,000 Mora from the Traveler for an address, adds a sermon about King Deshret and challenges Alhaitham to a duel. Tumart fills in the brigade's view of the Caracal Battalion and the rival bidders. Both are beaten in the duel.

24.comment: Ayn Al-Ahmar: The Divine Knowledge Capsule affair
24.content: A glowing red Divine Knowledge Capsule that the Akademiya lost in the desert was contested by several Eremite brigades in Port Ormos. Alhaitham negotiated for the right to study it. Ayn Al-Ahmar refused, bid and won. After Mizri used it he went mad, which Alhaitham likened to the researchers who lose their minds after taking knowledge from Irminsul. The Matra took Mizri, but Alhaitham took the capsule. The quest does not say what it contained.

25.content: "Al-Ahmar" is treated by the Eremites as King Deshret's alleged true name. Both Ayn Al-Ahmar in Port Ormos and Dakan Al-Ahmar, which was led by Dehya's father Kusayla, took it for their names. They are separate brigades with separate aims.

26.content:
Beret Society (also: the Beret Society, Dougier's Beret Society): The Beret Society was a prisoners' club in the Fortress of Meropide in Fontaine. Its founder, Dougier, presented it as a way to help inmates turn over a new leaf, and its members wore berets as a badge of pride. In truth it was a scheme that ruled members through fear. Wriothesley and the Traveler exposed it during the Cerberus Chapter, and it was disbanded.

Publicly it was a model-prisoner organisation, and Wriothesley, the Duke of Meropide, helped it get started by approving Dougier's application. Privately Dougier meant to use it, and a stolen force of Gardemeks, to seize control of the prison from Wriothesley.

Structure: Dougier was the sole leader. Members were organised into groups of five, and a whole group was punished for one member's offence. The society met near the Coupon Cafeteria in the Fortress, where it offered drinks, snacks, books, seminars and relaxation. It ran on donated goods and Credit Coupons from its members. Behind this front was a hidden headquarters beneath the Production Zone, which the quest calls Dougier's "Kingdom".

Goals: The stated goal was to help prisoners look out for one another, improve their state of mind, make friends and start a new life. The real goal, revealed late in the Cerberus Chapter, was to topple Wriothesley. Dougier believed Wriothesley lived in comfort on the prisoners' labour and wanted that wealth and workforce for himself.

Methods: The berets were an identity badge. Dougier said he wanted a visible mark of belonging and pride, and the hats also helped recruit members. Hidden in them were thorns, which could inject a dark liquid called Aqua Doloris, a concentrated form of fear, into a member's head. The society's real rules forbade speaking to one another without permission, leaving without permission, and breaking Dougier's orders. They also required groups of five to share punishment and rewarded informers with food and water. A breach brought "censure": the liquid was injected while the member was conscious.

History: In the opening of the Cerberus Chapter, Reborn in the Land of Grievances, the Traveler and Paimon meet Faissolle, who has lost his hat and is hiding in a box. Wriothesley then introduces the Beret Society as model prisoners and takes the Traveler to see its daily life. Wriothesley had investigated the society, which Dougier knew about and judged he could hide from. In the third part, "It's What He Deserves", members escape into the Production Zone, and Wriothesley and the Traveler find the hidden headquarters, rescue victims and destroy the Gardemek force. Dougier drew a revolver on Wriothesley and then on the Traveler and Paimon before Wriothesley disarmed him. Wriothesley sent him back to confinement, and the society ended with his arrest.

Relations: - **Wriothesley**: approved the society and later destroyed it. He ran the prison as the Duke of Meropide.
- **Traveler and Paimon**: found Faissolle, visited the society with Wriothesley and helped uncover the scheme.
- **Gardemeks**: machines that served the Fortress and became Dougier's muscle.

Reputation: Within Meropide it looked like a harmless, popular social club with well-attended events. Its true nature was known only to Dougier's inner circle and its victims.

Secrets: The berets concealed the thorns of Aqua Doloris, and the society's real rules and the hidden headquarters were never meant to reach Wriothesley. Dougier believed his cover would hold.

Status as of 7.1: Disbanded. Dougier was arrested and held in confinement after the Cerberus Chapter (4.1).

No later canon, up to 7.1, was found that revives the society. The Fortress of Meropide itself carries on under Wriothesley.

27.content: Dougier is the quest-only prisoner who founded the Beret Society. He seems a friendly do-gooder, but is manipulative and abusive toward his own members. He turned the society against Wriothesley and fell short when confronted. Wriothesley calls him a coward without the hat, the members and the Gardemeks. He was imprisoned again after the Cerberus Chapter.

28.content: Aqua Doloris, Latin for "Water of Pain", is a dark liquid that is a highly concentrated form of fear. In the Beret Society, thorns hidden under the berets injected it into the head, and the fear made members compliant. It was kept in a black gem that Dougier obtained from unnamed contacts.

29.content:
Black Serpent Knights (also: Black Serpent Knight, Windcutter, Rockbreaker Ax): Black Serpent Knights are one of the two forms of the cursed Royal Guard of Khaenri'ah, alongside the Shadowy Husks. They fight with greatswords (Windcutter) or dual axes (Rockbreaker Ax). Canon describes them as once-honoured knights of the realm whose reason and memory were stripped away by the curse. For the wider group, see the Black Serpents.

Halfdan, Irizar, Zephaniah and Ynghildr are the named Knights with stories.

Structure: The Adventurer Handbook says members are called Husks or Knights depending on how much wear they have undergone, so the Knights are not a separate organisation. The two Knight types are Windcutter (greatsword) and Rockbreaker Ax (dual axes). In the Chasm, Halfdan led a band of them. Individuals carry epithets, such as Buliwyf, Guardian of the Desolation, a Windcutter in the Stony Halls.

Members: Halfdan, an elite Royal Guard, appears as a Windcutter. Irizar appears as a Rockbreaker Ax and Zephaniah as a Windcutter. Ynghildr, a Schwanenritter titled "Sword of a Lost Homeland", is fought as a Windcutter inside the Ruin Golem in Vimana Agama: Jazari's Chapter.

Goals: Halfdan's band kept Dainsleif's order to protect Khaenri'ah's people, now hilichurls. Irizar and Zephaniah guarded the Children of Echoes by holding back the Abyss. Others guard places, like the Ruin Golem's control module.

History: In the Chasm (2.6, Requiem of the Echoing Depths), Halfdan's band (fought in the quest as Shadowy Husks, though the quest steps call them Black Serpent Knights) first attacks Dainsleif and the Traveler, then stands down at his order. He later gives his life shielding others from the light of an Abyss Order amplification device while the Traveler shuts it down. In Natlan (5.0), Irizar and Zephaniah's long battle ends when the Traveler breaks the hold of the Shadow Pins.

Relations: Dainsleif is their former captain. The Children of Echoes, the hilichurls and the Schwanenritter all cross paths with them. The Abyss Order's amplification device, meant to lift the curse, only tormented them.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Knights survive only as enemies. No new story involvement was found in 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

30.comment: Black Serpent Knights: Rockbreaker Ax and Windcutter
30.content: The Windcutter (added 2.6) wields a greatsword and, when a shield fully absorbs its hit, gains attack and can blink away from the next blow. The Rockbreaker Ax (added 3.5) uses dual axes, enters a Geo-infused rampage and can shield nearby Husks; outside quests it appears only in the Spiral Abyss, Imaginarium Theater and some events. These are gameplay behaviours of the enemy types. Their Archive entries call both "a guard of some standing in the court" using the sword art "Truthseeker", and the Windcutter's adds that the Twilight Sword was once one of their number.

31.content:
Blazing Beasts (also: the Blazing Beasts, Dehya's brigade, Dehya's mercenary brigade): The Blazing Beasts are a small mercenary brigade of Eremites from Sumeru's desert. Their members are tightly bonded and loyal, and their best-known member is Dehya, the Flame-Mane. They take paid work as bodyguards and fighters. Dehya says outright that they are not a large group.

Most Eremites work in loose bands rather than one organisation, and the Blazing Beasts are one such band. Dehya counts them as her chosen family.

Structure: There is no formal hierarchy in canon. Like most Eremite brigades, the Blazing Beasts take commissions on their own account and do not answer to a larger body. Dehya is the most renowned member. The wider Eremite tradition is that anyone can join, and Dehya says "Eremites" is only a title that any Sumeru mercenary can use.

Leadership: Dehya is the face of the brigade. Her profile calls her a legend among the Eremites for her strength, passion and conscientiousness.

The sources never give her a formal rank. Later event dialogue treats her as the one who manages the brigade's affairs (see the sub-entries on the events).

Members: Dehya is the only named member in the game's main content. Raised among mercenaries, she joined the brigade at a young age, after her last argument with her adoptive father Kusayla. She regards its members as the family she chose for herself, trusted comrades who can say a great deal with a glance.

Goals: Dehya describes the brigade as small, but loyal and brave. Her profile says she works for good pay on reasonable commissions. She wants to bring hope back to the desert, which she considers her home. Members place mutual support above everything.

Methods: Mercenary work such as bodyguard commissions, escorts and combat for hire. Dehya's profile says she is a conscientious professional who charges a high premium and has a long line of clients. Her character story says the bonds between companions grow through fighting side by side. The brigade sings a simple campfire song praising Dehya, ending with a warning that she is to be feared when angry.

History: Dehya was found as an infant in the desert, according to the wiki, and raised by Kusayla, leader of Dakan Al-Ahmar, an Eremite group under Deshret's Relics. The Relics bound their members by recording their shameful deeds. Kusayla did not want Dehya recorded, and he referred her to the Blazing Beasts, who took her in. After an argument between the two, he burned the records room with himself inside, an event told in Dehya's story quest Lionsblood (3.5). Kusayla had once saved the family of Shahzaman from bandits, and in the quest Shahzaman and Dunyarzad recall that it was the Blazing Beasts who sent Dehya to work as Dunyarzad's bodyguard.

Relations: Within the Eremites the Blazing Beasts keep clear of Deshret's Relics, a faction that crossed all kinds of lines for Mora, as Dehya says herself. Dehya is also tied to the Corps of Thirty through her past, and to Candace, the guardian of Aaru Village, who is her close friend.

Reputation: Among Eremites, Dehya is celebrated and her brigade shares in her good name. Outsiders often judge all Eremites as unscrupulous, but this brigade is portrayed as honest.

Status as of 7.1: Active as of 7.1. No base is stated for the brigade, and it was last shown staying in Aaru Village (6.1 event).

Dehya remains in Sumeru during the 6.6 events as a mercenary. No Blazing Beasts developments were found in 6.7 to 7.1 content.

32.content: During the Whirling Waltz flagship event (5.6, May 2025) in the Court of Fontaine, Dehya agrees to take part and Paimon jokes that she and the Traveler are now official partners of the Blazing Beasts. Uncle Scimitar, a mercenary actor, also appears and calls the Traveler his boss. He admits he once fought the Traveler before he knew they were Dehya's friend. This is event material, not main story.

33.content: An event-only Eremite NPC listed in the wiki as a "mercenary actor" of the Blazing Beasts. He appears in Whirling Waltz (5.6) and Dance Dance Dynamic Disco (6.1). He calls himself one of Dehya's lads and treats the Traveler as an honorary sibling because they are Dehya's friend.

34.comment: Blazing Beasts: Fieldwise Center security work
34.content: In the Ruins Exploration: Fieldwise Center event (6.1), the Akademiya's new Fieldwise Center has a Security Division that ensures field teams include trained fighters. Candace says some of this work has been given to the Blazing Beasts and other mercenaries, though team members can also qualify by passing the combat test. She says the brigade will be staying in Aaru Village for the foreseeable future.

35.content: In the co-op event Dance Dance Dynamic Disco (6.1), Mualani says that the People of the Springs have become friends and allies with the Eremites' Blazing Beasts through the dance exchange. She hopes for regular get-togethers and a Natlan-Sumeru fusion dance style.

36.content:
Bubu Pharmacy (also: Bùbǔ-lú, Not-Divining Hut): Bubu Pharmacy is the pharmacy and clinic that Liyue calls the finest in the land, set below Yujing Terrace in Liyue Harbor. Dr. Baizhu owns it and treats patients there. His apprentice Qiqi, an undead girl, gathers herbs, and the pharmacist Herbalist Gui makes up the medicines and minds the shop. It is especially busy during and after the Lantern Rite.

Its Chinese name, Bùbǔ-lú, means "Not-Divining Hut". A nursery rhyme spread through Feiyun Slope sings that Dr. Baizhu's skill cures every illness but his medicines are terribly bitter, and parents use it to scare children into staying healthy.

Structure: Baizhu owns and leads the pharmacy. Qiqi works as an apprentice and herb gatherer, and Herbalist Gui is the pharmacist behind the counter.

Gui is still in training, so he will not hand out the stronger ingredients without a prescription. Because Baizhu is frail, Gui is also the one who puts the medicines together. When Baizhu and Qiqi are out gathering herbs, Gui keeps the shop. The roof has a viewpoint over Yujing Terrace, and the door on the eastern side leads to a back room with living quarters.

Leadership: Dr. Baizhu runs the pharmacy. He is courteous, says he treats every patient alike regardless of wealth or status, and is rarely seen without his white snake Changsheng.

Liyue's citizens trust him. Keqing considers him the right person to see when symptoms cannot be identified, and Xinyan is grateful for his voice-preserving medicine. A sickly young girl, Hongdou, dislikes his medicine but visits because his kindness makes her feel better. Gui credits Baizhu with the pharmacy's endless stream of customers.

Members: - Baizhu: owner and physician.
- Qiqi: apprentice and herb gatherer, a zombie raised by the adepti.
- Herbalist Gui: pharmacist and shopkeeper, still completing his training.

Qiqi's memory is poor and she keeps a notebook. In her profile she wandered into the hills to gather herbs out of an old habit, met Baizhu, and was taken in even though she could not sort the herbs. Baizhu would go and find her whenever she forgot to come back at night. Changsheng, Baizhu's snake, is a regular presence.

Methods: The pharmacy runs as a clinic and a herb shop. Baizhu sees patients, diagnoses and prescribes. Gui prepares and sells. Qiqi collects materials. Stronger ingredients need a prescription, while ordinary herbs can be bought freely. According to a boy named Ayu, Baizhu also runs a clinic in Qingce Village during the Lantern Rite.

Relations: - **Wangsheng Funeral Parlor**: its director Hu Tao distrusts Baizhu's quest to defy death.
- **The adepti**: their arts preserved a thread of Qiqi's consciousness, which Baizhu says helped him devise a way to save someone near death.
- **Millelith**: in the search for Ayu's father they could not spare many people, so the pharmacy's staff helped look.

Reputation: Liyue regards Bubu Pharmacy as the finest in the region, and Baizhu's skill is known across Teyvat. His reputation for terribly bitter medicine is a running joke.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the pharmacy is still operating under Baizhu in Liyue Harbor. No wiki page checked shows any change to it in 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

Baizhu's goal of immortality is not resolved in anything checked.

37.content: Gui is a pharmacist at Bubu Pharmacy and a trainee: he says he has yet to finish his training. He prepares medicine because Baizhu is frail, sells herbs, and refuses restricted ingredients without a prescription. He has known Baizhu to be ill since they first met but does not know the cause. When Shenhe visited Liyue Harbor and asked for herbs, she ate them immediately in front of him, which astonished him.

38.content:
Champion Duelist (also: Champion Duelists, Fontaine's Champion Duelists, official Champion Duelist): The Champion Duelists are Fontaine's official trial fighters. A person on trial who wants to defend their honour can request a duel against one of them. The duelists are drawn from the country's best fighters, and the strongest at present is Clorinde. If the defendant wins, they are acquitted; if they lose, they simply stand trial.

Duels are a legal right, not a spectacle, though they are staged within Fontaine's theatrical court culture. Few defendants can beat an official duelist, so most who request one end up conceding.

Structure: Canon describes the Champion Duelists as a group of selected fighters, not a ranked order. No leader, rank system or parent body is named. A Gardes member says the duelists keep an office in Quartier Lyonnais of the Court of Fontaine, across from the Adventurers' Guild headquarters.

Members: Clorinde is the best known and, per the wiki, the strongest of them: undefeated in formal duels. Savinien, an open-world NPC in Quartier Lyonnais, is a duelist who jokes about an extra fee. Guillaume Marais is named as a current member in the lines of Sir Arthur, the Steambird newspaper-seller. Ismenor, now retired, spends his evenings in the Vasari Passage and talks about the profession wryly.

Methods: A defendant who does not accept that they should be tried can request a duel to defend their reputation. Ismenor says only a concession or expiry of the duel can end it, and few people can defeat an official duelist. The worst case is the defendant being killed, which per the wiki only happens when they refuse to yield.

History: The origins of the office are unknown, but it existed over 500 years ago. The earliest known member, Marfisa, lived in that era.

Relations: The duelists work within the justice system alongside the Gardes and the court. Clorinde once served as Furina's bodyguard and stood ready to duel at the trial that exposed Furina. The Spina di Rosula's president Callas died in a duel with Clorinde, which shaped her later bond with his daughter Navia.

Reputation: Citizens treat the duelists as a sobering last resort. Opponents tend to surrender rather than face Clorinde, and journalists follow her. Vitruvia says she would have liked to join them, and Savinien jokes about extra fees.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Champion Duelists remain active in Fontaine. Clorinde is still the strongest and is no longer on a bodyguard post; she now works as a senior Game Master with the Tabletop Troupe and is travelling with Navia in Snezhnaya.

No change to the office's legal role has been shown after the events of Fontaine's Archon Quest.

39.content: Marfisa was a Champion Duelist over 500 years ago, originally from Fleuve Cendre and a spear fighter. She was beaten by the Marechaussee Hunter Emanuel Guillotin, took up his idea of justice and became a duelist. She was later dissolved by the leader of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, who took her spear technique.

40.comment: Champion Duelist: Callas and Clorinde's duel
40.content: Callas, founder and president of the Spina di Rosula and Navia's father, was accused of murder and chose to defend his honour in a duel with Clorinde. He died in it. Clorinde saw that he had let her win, but his reasons only became public years later.

41.content:
Chasm Exploration Team (also: The Chasm Exploration Team, Chasm exploration crew, Chasm Delvers): The Chasm Exploration Team is a small crew hired by Liyue's Ministry of Civil Affairs to look into the strange happenings in the Chasm, the mining region that was sealed off after a mysterious crystal appeared. They are the heart of the Chasm Delvers world-quest series, in which the Traveler helps them break the seal, set up camp in the Underground Mines and trace the dark mud to its source. Afterwards the team became an official part of Huishan Hall.

It is a practical, mixed crew rather than a military unit: an adventurer-cartographer, a foreign ecologist, a safety technician, a bard and a reformed Treasure Hoarder, all supplied by a bureaucrat who would rather be somewhere else.

Structure: The team has no named commander. Muning, a specialist of the Ministry of Civil Affairs sent to the Chasm, handles its supplies and paperwork. The members are Zhiqiong (Adventurers' Guild, an adventurer chosen for her mapping talent), Khedive (an ecologist from the Sumeru Akademiya's Amurta), Jinwu (the Chasm's safety technician), Taliesin (a bard from Mondstadt) and Clitopho (a former Treasure Hoarder and alchemy student from Mondstadt). The team runs two camps, one near the Chasm's eastern surface entrance and, after the seal is broken, camps inside the Underground Mines.

Goals: The team's job is to learn why the Chasm turned dangerous and to map and make safe the sealed mines. Individual members want different things: Zhiqiong wants to be remembered for a discovery, and Khedive wants to understand the ecological change.

History: The team first appears in version 2.6 in The Chasm Delvers. The Traveler accepts an Adventurers' Guild commission and meets Muning, who is worried about the sealed Chasm. After the Seven-Star Seal is broken the team moves into the Underground Mines, where it meets miners, deals with Treasure Hoarders and finds the "dark mud" that spreads Abyssal corruption.

Relations: - **Ministry of Civil Affairs**: hired the team; Muning is its representative.
- **Liyue Qixing**: sealed the Chasm and, via Khedive, funds the research.
- **Huishan Hall**: the group became an official part of it.
- **Treasure Hoarders**: a recurring threat in the mines; Clitopho is a former member.

Status as of 7.1: After The Chasm Delvers the team remains at its camps as an official arm of Huishan Hall. Zhiqiong is no longer with the group. No later developments for the team were found for 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

42.content: Zhiqiong is an Adventurers' Guild member chosen for the Chasm Exploration Team for her cartography. She comes from Mingyun Village, whose mines have dried up, and she admires great adventurers such as Stanley, Alice and the Traveler. She resents authorities who do little fieldwork of their own, and her wish to leave a mark makes her reckless around dangerous Abyssal forces. At the end of The Chasm Delvers she disappears into the mines' depths. See her own entry for more.

43.content:
Children of Echoes (also: Nanatzcayan, Nanatzcayan tribe, Children of Echoes tribe): The Children of Echoes, or Nanatzcayan, are one of Natlan's six tribes. They live in the canyons of Tequemecan Valley in eastern Natlan, where the ring of hammers and the tapping of gem hunters echo off the cliffs. They are miners, excavators, smiths and gem appraisers who work alongside drill-horned Tepetlisaurs, and they are known for their love of dance and rhythmic music. Their chief is Pacal. Kachina and Xilonen are the best-known members.

Stone is one of their symbols. They are Natlan's only source of obsidian, a material used in important rites, and their Name Engravers forge the obsidian stones that carry Natlan's Ancient Names.

Structure: Like Natlan's other tribes, the Children of Echoes govern themselves. A chief, normally chosen by the previous chief, oversees the tribe's customs and may change them. Even the Pyro Archon does not overrule a chief's decision as long as the tribe agrees. The tribe works in 19 mining teams: 12 handle the tribe's own work and 7 can be hired for mining or excavation elsewhere. Large ore deals and the hire of mining teams are negotiated directly with the chief. Guards such as Avilix and Cauich watch the settlement. The tribe's Wayob, its ancestral spirits in the Night Kingdom, choose who receives the tribe's Ancient Names.

Leadership: Chief Pacal is a big, warm-hearted man who prefers looking after and supporting his people to managing the details of their lives. As a young man he hoped to be chosen by the Wayob, but he never received an Ancient Name. He took up eating to cope with stress, and once ate 71 servings of Glittering Gemstones in a contest. He made his peace with it, and he lives by the tribe's mantra: no one fights alone.

Pacal has looked out for Kachina since she received her Ancient Name. Kachina calls him "Uncle Pacal" and says he defends her whenever others in the tribe run her down. His Tepetlisaur companion is Uchu. Manqu warns that, Ancient Name or not, Pacal is not to be taken lightly.

Members: - **Kachina**: a young warrior who bears the Ancient Name Uthabiti ("toughness and tenacity"). She is a gifted dancer and a tireless digger, and her Tepetlisaur companion is Ayo. She was the Traveler's first guide in Natlan.
- **Xilonen**: a renowned smith and the tribe's Name Engraver, bearer of the Ancient Name Baraka. Her parents and most of her relatives were Name Engravers too. Most of her work is tools, weapons and machines for the tribe.
- **Pacal**: chief.

Goals: The tribe wants to keep its people, its Tepetlisaurs and its mountains safe, and to pass on its craft. Its members still dream of the glory of the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame, and they see their work as a "blessing" made by mortal hands rather than granted by gods or masters. The bulletin board's welcome promises visitors sincerity "as solid and steady as the stones and as hot as the fires of the forge".

Methods: **Mining and gems.** The tribe digs deep into the mountains for ore, solid phlogiston and gems, so deep that one guard jokes it can be hard to get enough sunlight. Members decorate their tools, weapons and accessories with gems, and some people read the gems as a sign of skill or status. Most members love tunnelling, and finding a vein of ore gives them a warmth that everyone in the tribe understands.

**Tepetlisaurs.** Tepetlisaurs can drill through rock and solid phlogiston. They have lived beside the tribe since before anyone's great-great-grandfather, and their nests are never far from human homes. The tribe treats them as equals rather than livestock or pets, and most bonds form freely: a Tepetlisaur simply starts following a person home. Legend says the ancestor of all Tepetlisaurs was a drake as large as a mountain, and that the huge drill-shaped objects in the cliffs above the settlement are the remains of its horn.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tribe lives on in Tequemecan Valley under Chief Pacal, rebuilding after the Abyss's invasion. Pacal stresses that the victory was real but temporary, and that the tribe must stay vigilant.

Kachina and Xilonen remain its best-known members. After the Night Kingdom was purified, Natlanese people could leave their country more freely. No new Children of Echoes story was found for 6.0-7.1; the 7.0-7.1 Archon Quests take place in Snezhnaya.

44.comment: Children of Echoes: "Children of Echoes" settlement
44.content: The tribe's home lies inside a gorge in Tequemecan Valley, beneath an enormous drill embedded in the cliffs. Stage Tepetl, the dance stage, stands beside the bulletin board. Muhuru's Gemporium sells gem accessories just over the bridge, and steps lead up to the chief for large ore deals. The Macuahuitl Workshop makes heavy-duty tools and weapons, and Xilonen's workshop is nearby. Duels are held on grounds in the mountain behind the stage, because, as Pacal says, the stage is no place for tunnelling. Tepetlisaurs nest close to the houses. An official map description says that, long ago, a sage of Phlogiston Engraving painted murals across the valley's cliffs, and that this is the origin of Natlan's graffiti.

45.comment: Children of Echoes: Ancient Names of the Children of Echoes
45.content: **Baraka** ("blessings") was first borne by the founder Ixquieh; later bearers include Sakkuk, Sundjatta and now Xilonen. **Uthabiti** ("toughness and tenacity") belongs to Kachina, who long doubted she deserved it. Ancient Names are given by the tribe's Wayob and forged into obsidian by Name Engravers. Xilonen, the current Name Engraver, studied under the respected engraver Teyiz, who taught that "stories and equations are, in essence, one and the same". Tlazolli, another forger, bore **Undugu**.

46.content: The Shadow Pins are great stone pillars in the Sulfurous Veins, one Greater Pin and three Lesser Pins. Children of Echoes legend says they pin down a "shadow": the Abyss that Elder Traore and his warriors sealed underground 500 years ago at the cost of their lives. The storyteller Titu looks after them. Even miners know not to touch the phlogiston around them. In 5.0 the Pins began to float and the Greater Pin fell. With the Traveler's help, Titu discovered the true story beneath them.

47.comment: Children of Echoes: Tepetlisaurs and the tribe
47.content: Tepetlisaurs are the tribe's saurian partners. Each tribe bonds best with one kind of saurian, and the Children's is this burrowing kind with its drill-horn, which helps them mine and find the best ore. Companions known by name include Kachina's Ayo, who shows affection by headbutting, and Pacal's Uchu, whom Pacal is always telling to eat less. In Och-Kan's age, the tribe protected its Tepetlisaurs from his dragon hunts, and the father of the hero Sakkuk was executed for it.

48.content:
Church of Favonius (also: Favonius Church, Mondstadt Church, the Church of Favonius, Church of the Anemo Archon): The Church of Favonius is Mondstadt's church of the Anemo Archon Barbatos, the nation's patron of freedom. Its clergy pray, run morning prayers and choir, help the sick and answer letters from believers at the Favonius Cathedral in Mondstadt City. The Knights of Favonius manage it, and the two institutions work side by side. Its Seneschal is Seamus Pegg, Cardinal of Daybreak.

The Church is a community of devoted adherents more than a ruling body. Government belongs to the Knights, and the Archon himself does not rule. The Church supplies ritual, charity and a place to bring troubles. Its best-known members are the Deaconess Barbara, the Deacon Dahlia and the unorthodox Sister Rosaria.

Structure: At the top is the Seneschal, Seamus Pegg, who also carries the title Cardinal of Daybreak. Cardinal Calvin ran the Church's affairs during Seamus' absence. Below them are deacons and a deaconess (Dahlia, Barbara), a Mother (Maria), and a body of nuns and sisters. Dahlia also leads the choir as cantor and holds the unique post of Herald of Barbatos. The clergy take turns at routine tasks, such as writing replies to letters from the congregation, and attend compulsory classes, hymn practice and morning prayers.

Leadership: Seamus Pegg is Seneschal and the senior figure. He is a former famous adventurer born in Nod-Krai who settled in Mondstadt and joined the Church. He is the father of Jean (the Knights' Acting Grand Master) and Barbara (the Deaconess), though he and Jean's mother Frederica Gunnhildr are no longer together. He joined Varka's expedition and handled its paperwork, then came home to Mondstadt and the Cathedral once the Nod-Krai conflict wound down. He greets visitors with a blessing from the Anemo Archon and says he means to shoulder more of the Church's work.

Members: Notable members are Seamus Pegg (Seneschal), Cardinal Calvin, Dahlia (Deacon and Herald of Barbatos), Barbara (Deaconess and idol), Mother Maria and Sister Rosaria (who works alone).

- **Barbara**: cheerful, hardworking and loved by the whole city. She became a healer on her father's advice and sings to lift spirits. She admires her sister Jean and is unaware, according to the wiki, that she has met Barbatos.
- **Dahlia**: a young deacon with a love of "drama" and of meddling in other people's troubles. He is not especially devout. He knows Venti is Barbatos and relays news and feedback between the Archon and the people.
- **Rosaria**: the Church's least devout sister, who skips services and dodges overtime. Her real work is investigating suspected threats to Mondstadt, and she is trusted to do it.
- **Victoria**: a nun who looks after Barbara and worries when she goes missing. She asked Dahlia to write a letter for Rosaria's birthday.

Goals: The Church worships the Anemo Archon and tries to keep Mondstadt's faith in freedom alive. It offers spiritual guidance, prayer and charity. Part of its role is practical: looking after the sick, answering the congregation's letters and giving people somewhere to bring their worries. It also cares for the sacred objects that belong to Barbatos.

Methods: Daily life centres on morning prayer, hymn practice and choir, led by Dahlia. Clergy take turns answering letters, and sisters like Barbara use healing and song. Dahlia's approach is unusual: he has been known to settle quarrels by taking the parties to a tavern for a drinking contest, which Jean thinks may not be fair or just. Seekers can bring problems to him because many believe Barbatos listens to him.

Relations: - **Knights of Favonius**: manage the Church and work with it. Jean is Seamus' daughter. Adorno was buried at the Favonius Cathedral after dying in 6.6. Albedo's 5.6 trial involved both bodies.
- **Barbatos**: the Church's god. Venti is Barbatos, and Dahlia is the Herald who knows it.
- **Hexenzirkel**: Alice, an elder of the Hexenzirkel, coached Barbara on becoming an idol, a link that has no direct connection to Church doctrine.

Reputation: Mondstadters love Barbara, so the Cathedral draws visitors who hope to see her. Many believe Dahlia has the Archon's favour. Rosaria is thought of as a lazy, chain-smoking sister, while few know of her secret work. The map description of the Cathedral muses on whether a city taught freedom by its Archon should spend so much wealth on such a grand building.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, Seamus Pegg is back in Mondstadt as Seneschal. The Church is peaceful and no Church-centred story content was found for 6.7 to 7.1.

Dahlia is active as Deacon and Herald. Barbara, Rosaria and the sisters continue their duties. Seamus has returned from the expedition and is working to share the load.

49.content: The Favonius Cathedral, also called the Mondstadt Cathedral, stands in Mondstadt City and is run by the Church of Favonius. Clergy work and pray here, and its grand architecture resembles real-world Gothic cathedrals. A basement at the back holds the Holy Lyre der Himmel under guard. The Cathedral is a place of prayer, choir practice and counsel. The Traveler can meet nuns such as Jilliana, Grace and Victoria there, and Seamus Pegg in the later story.

50.comment: Church of Favonius: Holy Lyre der Himmel
50.content: The Holy Lyre der Himmel is the lyre the Anemo Archon Barbatos once played. Its frame is rosewood, carved with a pattern of flowing wind, according to Venti. It is used in the Ludi Harpastum festival, and any other use requires signed documents from the Grand Master, the Seneschal and a community representative. The Church keeps it in the Cathedral basement. In the Prologue the Traveler and Venti obtained it, lost it to a Fatui agent, and later returned it to Barbara in damaged condition, which Venti hid with an Anemo illusion.

51.comment: Church of Favonius: Seamus Pegg, Seneschal
51.content: Seamus is the Church's Seneschal. He was an adventurer from Nod-Krai who met the wandering Varka abroad, persuaded him to return home and then settled in Mondstadt himself. He married Frederica Gunnhildr and had two daughters, Jean and Barbara. The marriage ended, and Barbara stayed with him. He dryly scolds Varka for his antics and handles most administrative work on his own. He saw Eroch's plot unfold, and he regretted the diplomatic cost to Mondstadt when Dottore took credit for killing Ursa. Seamus went on Varka's expedition, returned after the Nod-Krai conflict and now helps shoulder the Church's work.

52.comment: Church of Favonius: Dahlia, Herald of Barbatos
52.content: Dahlia is a deacon of the Church and choir cantor who holds the post of Herald of Barbatos. He knows Venti is the Anemo Archon, passes news to him and brings his feedback to the people. He was a nosy helper before joining the clergy, and he is not especially religious. Venti helped create the Herald role so that he could contribute without being tied to dull routine. Dahlia is a quick learner who memorised hymns overnight when challenged. He took part in the Knights' plan around Albedo's trial in 5.6.

53.content: Barbara is the Deaconess and a beloved idol. She joined the Church young, and her father Seamus served in it too. She has a Hydro Vision that appeared after she sang a lullaby to a feverish boy. Her father counselled her to become a healer. She safeguards religious artifacts and worships Barbatos, but the wiki states she is unaware she has met him. She sometimes hides from crowds to recover alone, and her story with Victoria shows how the nuns look after her.

54.comment: Church of Favonius: Rosaria, the Nonconforming Sister
54.content: Rosaria is a sister in name, famous for skipping classes, hymn practice and morning prayers. Raised by bandits and offered a second chance by Varka, she entered the Church and secretly works as its investigator of threats. She is unpredictable and disappears for days. Barbara keeps trying to bring her back to duties, and Dahlia once covered her letter-writing shift. She refuses overtime. The Church has never imposed serious consequences for her behaviour, and Rosaria has said she has found "other work".

55.content:
Collective of Plenty (also: Teteocan, Teteocan tribe, the Collective of Plenty): The Collective of Plenty, also called the Teteocan, is one of Natlan's six tribes. Its people farm the rich volcanic soil beside the Great Volcano of Tollan in Atocpan and live alongside Tatankasaurs, their bonded saurians. The tribe is known across Natlan for two things: the best fruit and vegetables in the nation, and a culture built around physical strength, from bodybuilding contests to wrestling. Its chief is Acatl, a cheerful masked wrestler.

Notable members include Iansan, head coach of the tribe's fitness club and bearer of the Ancient Name Uwezo ("Power"), and her star pupil Varesa, an orchard manager and Patrol Team warrior whom local children call the "Masked Hero". Of all the tribes, they live the farthest from the Stadium of the Sacred Flame.

Culture: Fitness is close to sacred here: Iansan's stories say it is second in importance only to the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame. Most adults have huge, heavily muscled frames. Young people show off their muscles to each other as a friendly greeting, and a fitness coach is only taken seriously if they are very strong. Wrestling Tatankasaurs is a long-standing tradition, and beating one is a great honour. Some warriors even seek out wild Halberd-Crest Birds to find out "whose head is harder".

Many wrestlers wear masks. When two masked fighters duel, the loser takes off their mask and the winner keeps theirs, keeping an air of mystery that invites others to challenge them. Acatl says he has never once been unmasked by human or saurian. When young tribespeople ask how they would know he is not an imposter, he tells them to face him in the ring, because "muscles... never lie".

Places: The tribe's settlement, also named "Collective of Plenty", lies on fertile plains below the Great Volcano of Tollan. Volcanic ash has made the land rich, and its golden harvests are the tribe's pride. At its centre is the Grand Wrestling Grounds, also called the Resonating Arena: a raised arena decorated with huge bull horns, where the tribe's athletic competitions are held. Varesa's family orchard stands just outside the settlement and is guarded by her Tatankasaur Vanana.

Structure: The chief leads the tribe, with the elders also taking part in major decisions such as war planning. The fitness club is one of the tribe's central institutions. Meztcala founded it, and its head coach is a figure of real authority: Acatl was both chief and head coach before Iansan took over the club. The Patrol Team defends the tribe against monsters and the Abyss; Varesa is a core member, and Iansan led its counterattacks in the three-pronged Abyss assault. Like every tribe, the Collective has a Wayob, which chooses bearers of Ancient Names. For the Collective of Plenty, the name "Power" (Uwezo) carries special weight, standing for unrivalled honour and responsibility.

Leadership: Chief Acatl is a tall, powerfully built man who always wears a horned wrestling mask. He is warm, relaxed about formalities and attentive to the tribe's young people, and he has long kept a concerned eye on Varesa.

Acatl coached the fitness club when the young Iansan, newly chosen by the Ancient Name "Power", asked to train. When she was badly hurt trying to lift a barbell, he was criticised for not stopping her. He still visited her and told her that fitness is "a question of choice", not of credentials. He also kept a watchful eye on the young Varesa, and agreed with the warriors to admit her to wrestling training. During the war he led the tribe's defence and repelled the Abyss.

Goals: The tribe's aims are simple: feed Natlan, grow strong, and protect its homeland and its neighbours. Its teaching, passed down from Meztcala, is that strength is something anyone can choose to build. Iansan has pushed this outward, offering training to people from any tribe.

Reputation: To other Natlanese, the Collective of Plenty means "universal fitness" and sweet fruit and fresh vegetables. Not everyone agrees: Suriqui, a dissenter within the tribe, calls its muscle-worshippers a "bunch of meatheads" and insists the heroes of old carried a protective layer of fat. In children's stories, the tribe's "Masked Hero" (Varesa) shows up, wreathed in lightning, wherever monsters run amok.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tribe is thriving under Chief Acatl. It survived the Abyss war, rebuilt, and fought off the Abyss Order's 5.7 attack.

Iansan's academy now stands near the Stadium and takes trainees from every tribe. Varesa is training to fight without her mask. The green mushrooms are being kept in check under Sumeru's watch. Nod-Krai and Snezhnaya content (6.0-7.1) only touches the tribe in passing, with a member found in Nasha Town.

56.comment: Collective of Plenty: Iansan and the fitness club
56.content: Iansan's family carries the "Blood of Egungun": none of them ever grow taller than a child. The tribe took the family in and always protected them, keeping them off the front lines as medics and cooks. When the Ancient Name "Power" chose Iansan, many tribespeople doubted her. She asked Acatl, then chief and head coach, to train her, injured herself badly on her first lift, and came back anyway. Her mother suggested building on what the family was good at, treating injuries and cooking. Iansan then created a training method of steady routines, controlled calories and precise nutrition, which introduced the science of nutrition to Natlan. She later beat the Tatankasaurs' chief, succeeded Acatl as head coach and set a Pilgrimage victory record. When other tribes began calling her bloodline a gift that explained her wins, she moved the club close to the Stadium as the Pilgrimage Victors Academy. Her flyers promise that toil, not birth, gives strength.

57.comment: Collective of Plenty: Varesa's orchard and the Masked Hero
57.content: Varesa's family orchard, just outside the settlement, sends fresh produce to every tribe. Varesa took it over after years of training and runs it with her Tatankasaur Vanana. Children's stories tell of a lightning-wreathed "Masked Hero" whose rescues happen to follow the orchard's trade routes. Varesa's mask is based on one worn by the tribe's heroine Fietena, and grateful villagers draw a little mask on their thank-you letters to her. She has entered the Pilgrimage five times and never got past the team stage, because she cannot bring herself to fight her fellow Natlanese seriously. Against the Abyss, though, she has never lost while defending the tribe.

58.content:
Communications Office (also: Heji Hall, Héjì-tīng, Liyue Communications Office): The Communications Office is one of the Eight Trades, the commercial sectors under the jurisdiction of the Liyue Qixing.
