It is the Hall in charge of transportation: moving goods and shipments around Liyue and arranging overseas shipping.

Its staff are officials rather than merchants. The Office also takes on related public works, so it is as much a transport authority as a trade body. Its base is Hezhe Post.

Structure: The Office is a Hall of the Eight Trades and answers to the Liyue Qixing like the other Halls. It is large because its duties cover more than shipping. No head is named in the sources checked, and no ranks are described. The Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency is listed on the wiki as a sub-faction.

Goals: By its staff's own account, the Office exists to keep goods moving. In the words of a member, good roads, bridges, waterways and docks are critical to getting goods to every part of Liyue.

Methods: The Office handles shipments and transport within Liyue and overseas shipping logistics, and oversees some construction and road management. An NPC mentions that it plans to build several small lifts, which should improve local access.

Relations: - **Eight Trades and the Liyue Qixing**: the Office is one of four Halls named in canon, and the Qixing hold jurisdiction.
- **Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency**: a listed sub-faction.

Status as of 7.1: Active as of 7.1. No new story involving the Office was found in 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 (Snezhnaya).

59.content: The wiki lists Hezhe Post as the Communications Office's base. See the location entry for the place itself.

60.content:
Conch Gang (also: the Conch Gang, Conch Gang kids): The Conch Gang is an informal band of stray children in Nasha Town, in Nod-Krai. Katya, the retired adventurer who runs the restaurant Speranza, feeds, houses and employs them while letting them live freely. The gang makes its own decisions by vote, and Speranza is its home base.

It is not an official guild or criminal outfit. Maite describes it as a mutual aid and coordination group for like-minded people of similar age. Its name comes from a local folk tale about children who ruled Nasha Town and called each other together by blowing a conch shell.

Structure: There is no named leader. A new member can join only if every existing member agrees. The Traveler remarks that the gang has many members and some pretty good benefits: food, shelter and work at Speranza. Members have great freedom to follow their own interests, from studying jellies to travelling abroad. The gang usually takes only children and sends members away at a certain age, though there is a precedent for admitting someone older.

Members: Current members named on the wiki:
- Jurva: the super chef at Speranza. She hopes everyone can live the lives they want.
- Maisie: a timid girl who works at Speranza as a host and does simple chores. Helka says her constitution is too frail for travel, and she keeps in touch with Helka through pictures and postcards.
- Mikko: a Speranza host who worries Katya is angry after he dropped and broke some things.
- Helka: a member who left Nod-Krai to catalogue monsters of other nations.
- Maite: a self-styled master thief, met at the Crab Tsar's Palace after The Mirrors, the Maze, and the Tsar.
- Auni: a small girl who holds funerals for animals, met in Friends of Moleyvalley.
- Semyon: a member who went to Maroon Basin to research Tassel Jellies.

Former members: Aino and Linnea (both playable characters) and Tapani.

Goals: The group has no stated mission. Their shared aim is to look after one another and live as they like. Jurva says Katya taught her that it is better to have impossible dreams than none, and that the younger kids living as they do now means her own dream has come halfway true.

History: Canon gives no founding date. The story of children conquering Nasha Town is folklore. In the present, Katya, a former Treasure Hoarders adventurer who retired because of injuries, took in children left to fend for themselves on the streets. She says she could not stand seeing them without shelter and warm food. The kids work for their keep.

Relations: Katya is their protector and employer, and Speranza is their base. The Traveler is a friend of the gang but not a member. Derwent taught some of them to read.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Conch Gang is active around Speranza in Nasha Town. Helka remains abroad on her monster-cataloguing journey, and Maisie stays in town. The sources checked show no appearance by the gang in Version 7.0 or 7.1 content.

61.comment: Conch Gang: Joining the Conch Gang
61.content: Joining takes a unanimous yes from every current member. Havu says it is somewhat difficult. The gang usually accepts only children and sends members away at a certain age, though there is a precedent for older newcomers. Maite told the Traveler they are too old, and Helka said age might complicate things but did not rule it out.

62.comment: Conch Gang: The Conch Shell Tale
62.content: Jurva says a story goes that children once built Nasha Town and called each other together by blowing into a conch shell, voting on every decision. She says nobody really believes it and wonders who made it up. The Traveler's voice-over line adds that the town developed into the bustling settlement it is today, and the gang no longer dominates it.

63.comment: Conch Gang: Helka and the Monster Handbook
63.content: Helka appears in the On the Trail of Behemoths event. She is a Conch Gang member who knows every monster in Nod-Krai and left to learn about monsters elsewhere. Her task is an illustrated handbook of 100 monster varieties, and she posted a commission with the Adventurers' Guild for help. She says Katya told her a good enough book might get her published. She sends copies and pictures to Maisie, who loves monster stories.

64.content: Speranza is the main restaurant in Nod-Krai, in Nasha Town on Lempo Isle, run by Katya. Staff include the chef Jurva and the hosts Maisie and Mikko. A fortune wheel stands outside, and a dog named Pavlov is nearby. The Conch Gang treats it as its home base. It sells food and ingredients, and completing the quest Rest Beyond Reach gives a permanent discount.

65.content:
Confrerie of Cabriere (also: Confrérie de Cabrière, Cabriere Confrerie): The Confrerie of Cabriere was a merchants' guild in Fontaine, founded and led by Marcel. Publicly it was one of the richest and most powerful trading guilds in the nation and a friendly sister body to the Spina di Rosula. In truth it was a front for Marcel's underground trade in Sinthe, which paid for his experiments. It was dissolved after Marcel was exposed in the 4.0 Archon Quest.

Callas and the Spina di Rosula helped it grow when it was only reselling everyday goods. Its Sinthe business was wiped out with the guild, though a successor "Imitation Sinthe" trade later appeared.

Structure: Marcel led and founded the guild. The wiki names two other people tied to it: Calcagni, a staff member (found as an open-world NPC in the Court of Fontaine, listed as formerly of the Confrerie), and Truand, an enforcer who collected debts. Its shops were built to a single design with a plain, approachable look, so that customers of every budget would feel welcome. The same buildings carried anti-theft features: walls that would warp if hammered repeatedly and a claimed 100-year rustproof finish.

Goals: In public, trade and commerce. In reality, to bankroll Marcel's experiments with Primordial Seawater. Marcel's deeper aim was personal, not commercial, and belongs to his own story.

Methods: Marcel sold Sinthe, a drug made from diluted Primordial Seawater that causes euphoria and pleasant hallucinations. It is highly addictive, can cause lasting problems with focus and emotional control, and brings withdrawal symptoms of fatigue, anxiety and paranoia. Many families were ruined by it. By the time of his arrest he had even made a fruit-flavoured version. Marcel protected the operation by removing threats. He framed Callas for murder after she banned Sinthe in Poisson and found its production base.

History: At first the Confrerie only resold daily goods, with support from Callas and the Spina di Rosula, and grew into one of the richest guilds in Fontaine. Marcel later began the Sinthe trade. When Callas, the head of the Spina di Rosula, banned Sinthe in Poisson and tracked down the production base, Marcel framed her for murder, which led to her death in a duel against Champion Duelist Clorinde. In the Chapter IV act As Light Rain Falls Without Reason, the Traveler and Navia exposed Marcel as the culprit behind the serial disappearances, and he died in the final quest of that act. Authorities then stopped Sinthe production and began confiscating what remained on the market.

Relations: - **Spina di Rosula**: the Confrerie was regarded as its sister organisation. Callas led the Spina and supported the Confrerie early on, and her daughter is Navia.
- **Marcel**: founder and leader, whose double life the guild hid.
- **Navia and the Traveler**: exposed the scheme.
- **Clorinde**: the Champion Duelist who fought Callas in the duel Marcel arranged.

Reputation: Before the exposure the Confrerie was known as one of the richest and most powerful merchant guilds in Fontaine, and as an honest sister to the Spina di Rosula. Afterwards its name is linked with the Sinthe scandal.

Secrets: Its Sinthe business and Marcel's identity were hidden until the Chapter IV investigation. Marcel was really Vacher, an adventurer from Snezhnaya who took on a new identity.

Status as of 7.1: Disbanded. The Confrerie ended when Marcel was exposed in 4.0.

As of 7.1 no revival of the Confrerie was found. Canon only mentions it in the past tense, although Imitation Sinthe smuggling (4.5) shows the drug's market outlasted it.

66.content: Sinthe is a drink made from Primordial Seawater diluted with ordinary water. It gives short-term euphoria and pleasant hallucinations, then erodes concentration and emotional control, and stopping brings fatigue, anxiety and paranoia. It is highly addictive and wrecked many families. Marcel made and sold it to fund his experiments, and the Confrerie of Cabriere was its commercial front. Production ended after his arrest. Later, "Imitation Sinthe" appeared to mimic its effects, made from ingredients that have many ordinary uses, and the Traveler helped the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol expose a smuggling ring in the 4.5 event Checks and Cats.

key: Parchamdar of the Corps of Thirty
67.content:
Corps of Thirty (also: the Corps of Thirty, Parchamdar of the Corps of Thirty): The Corps of Thirty is the mercenary brigade that guards Sumeru City. It is not an official army. It is a permanently hired brigade of Eremites, kept on retainer by the Sumeru Akademiya, and its members wear teal-green scarves instead of the crimson ones of other Eremites. Its base is the Citadel of Regzar, and its commander is the Parchamdar, Rukh Shah.

Its name remembers its origin: thirty mercenaries hired by the Akademiya's sages. It has since grown far larger, but the name stayed. The Corps defends the city, polices it, and handles the everyday problems of residents.

Structure: A Parchamdar commands the Corps (the word means roughly "standard-bearer"). A Consultant serves beside the Parchamdar as a second, administrative leader.

The wiki calls the Corps the oldest of the Eremite brigades (Rukh Shah himself says only "among the oldest"). The wiki, citing the quest "The Trail of the God of Wisdom", says it manages and coordinates the affairs of the other mercenary brigades, though what is visible in play is mostly its work in Sumeru City. The Akademiya employs a liaison, Effendi, to coordinate between the scholars and the Corps. Staff at the Citadel of Regzar include a logistics officer (Yunus, nicknamed "Bigfish"), a messenger called the "Swallow" (Sekkura) and a member nicknamed "Goat" (Udad). Rank-and-file mercenaries are posted around Treasures Street and the Puspa Cafe.

Leadership: Rukh Shah is the Parchamdar. He is the youngest person ever to hold the post. The Consultant, Asfand, is a retired veteran who still advises him.

Rukh Shah greets visitors by explaining his role and offering the Corps' help in town, then warns them to be careful of other Eremites outside the city, even in Port Ormos. According to the Swallow Sekkura, he is supposedly from the rainforest, not the desert, which is very rare among Eremites, and he gets along both with desert people and with Akademiya researchers. She also repeats a rumor that he was once a researcher himself; Effendi, the Akademiya's liaison, says the Parchamdar used to be a researcher. Asfand says he retired but was asked by Rukh Shah to advise because he has served in both the Corps and other groups, and he offers to settle unexpected conflicts.

Members: Dehya, the "Flame-Mane", was once a member and is respected by the Corps. Other named members include Sido, the Swallow Sekkura, the logistics officer Yunus, Udad, the mercenaries Hakan and Farid, and Izem, a veteran now retired to the Puspa Cafe.

Asfand calls Dehya a reliable partner and one of the best in the Corps, adds that she speaks frankly, and says she handled her recent commission well (she met the young lady of the Homayani family, Dunyarzad, and made friends). Sido says that everyone in the Corps greatly respects her. She looked out for many of its members, and many followed her into battle. The wiki lists her Corps affiliation as "formerly". Sekkura longs to visit Aaru Village again and says she has not seen Candace for ages.

Goals: The Corps' job is to keep Sumeru City safe: defend it, guard it against criminals, and deal with disorders that the Akademiya or ordinary residents report. Most tasks are assigned by the Akademiya, plus requests from civilians. The Corps does not make policy.

Methods: Corps members patrol the city, take on residents' commissions and keep watch over crowds during festivals. During the Akademiya's Parade of Providence event, Rukh Shah said he had increased patrols because the influx of tourists gave schemers cover, and during the Chromatic Ode of Candies and Roses event he asked people to report anything unusual to the nearest Corps member. Sekkura says that dusk birds now carry many messages, which lightened her errands but added the care of the birds.

Relations: The Corps works for the Akademiya, has an uneasy relationship with other Eremites, and shares Sumeru City's security with the matra.

Other Eremites are sometimes hostile toward it. In the 3.1 Archon Quest The Gaze From a Certain God, an Eremite leader named Tashfin says his brigade is nothing like "those government lapdogs who don't even get scraps", meaning the Corps. The Eremites page mentions a swindler, Kasim, who uses the Eremite name for personal gain and is known as a fraud by the Corps. Alhaitham notes the Corps' poor relationship with the Ayn Al-Ahmar, devout followers of King Deshret who loudly denounce Greater Lord Rukkhadevata. In the repeatable Reputation Request Eremite Mayhem, residents ask the Corps to deal with Eremites dumping refuse on Devantaka Mountain, troubling the road to Caravan Ribat and skulking on the outskirts of Sumeru City.

Reputation: Residents treat the Corps as the people to turn to in town. Rukh Shah tells the Traveler to feel free to seek the Corps' help there. Outside the city, some independent Eremites regard its members as the Akademiya's servants.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Corps of Thirty is still the working force of Sumeru City, based at the Citadel of Regzar under Rukh Shah.

Dehya is still regarded as a friend of the Corps, and Asfand still hopes that she will join it.

68.content: Rukh Shah is the Parchamdar of the Corps of Thirty and the youngest person to hold that post. Sekkura says he is supposedly from the rainforest rather than the desert, which is unusual among Eremites, and that he may once have been a researcher. He explains his role plainly, takes the Corps' workload seriously and warns visitors to be careful about other Eremites outside the city.

69.content: Asfand is the Consultant of the Corps of Thirty, a retired veteran who advises at the Citadel of Regzar at Rukh Shah's request. He has served in the Corps and in other groups. He calls Dehya a reliable partner and one of the best in the Corps, and hopes she will join it. He duels visitors in the Genius Invokation TCG.

70.comment: Corps of Thirty: Citadel of Regzar
70.content: The Citadel of Regzar is the Corps of Thirty's headquarters and barracks, in the middle of Sumeru City near Treasures Street. It is where Corps members coordinate and meet the Akademiya's liaison Effendi. "Regzar" is a Persian word for "desert". NPCs posted there include Rukh Shah, Asfand, Effendi, the Swallow Sekkura, Udad and the logistics officer Yunus.

71.comment: Corps of Thirty: Corps of Thirty Recruitment
71.content: Effendi, a researcher sent by the Akademiya as liaison to the Corps of Thirty, asks the Traveler to take a job as an assistant. The work is completing small commissions from Sumeru City residents so the Corps can focus on defending the city. In return the Traveler is paid per task and builds a reputation among residents.

72.content:
Courier's Longhouse (also: Couriers' Longhouse, Courier's Longhouse (Faction), Natlan couriers): The Courier's Longhouse is the courier agency of the Scions of the Canopy, the Natlan tribe of Coatepec Mountain. Its couriers carry letters and parcels. It accepts ordinary deliveries only, not anything extremely valuable, fragile or dangerous. It is run from a base in the Scions' settlement.

The bulletin board calls the couriers highly skilled professionals whose deliveries almost always arrive, though the Longhouse will not guarantee against accidents along the way.

Structure: The base is the Courier's Longhouse inside the Scions of the Canopy settlement, with a bulletin board beside it. Michica is its manager and is the person customers see to hire a courier. Commissions are taken per delivery, not for fixed periods. Couriers pay management fees, which the Longhouse says go toward standard-issue gear. Michica's gear assessment report goes to Chief Wayna, and the board invites couriers to send feedback to Miss Amauta. Couriers are ranked each month by completed deliveries.

Members: Michica is the manager. The bulletin board names Zeila, who topped one monthly ranking with 110 long-distance deliveries in twenty days, and Adama, a star courier who fell to fifth while preparing for the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame. Tundama, Sausa and Sibu are named in that order for the next places, and the top ten includes others. Sorimana is a courier who handles supply drops.

Methods: Customers sometimes demand the impossible, such as falcon-speed delivery across a distance greater than the deserts of Sumeru with no damage to the packaging, and the Longhouse says plainly it cannot promise that. It warns couriers delivering to the Flower-Feather Clan to drop off their parcels before accepting any gliding race with clan members. The clan is better at gliding, and a race could damage the contents.

Goals: The Longhouse aims to deliver ordinary items reliably, to maintain the couriers' reputation, and to improve its protective gear, whose usage rate it admits is low.

Relations: It is part of the Scions of the Canopy under Chief Wayna. Its couriers deal with the Flower-Feather Clan, whose gliding skill the board warns couriers about. The board says Kinich, a Scion, is the only one capable of the most extreme deliveries, but he is not a courier.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Longhouse is still operating at the Scions of the Canopy under its manager Michica.

After the Natlan war (the Archon Quest No One Fights Alone), Michica says the Longhouse is short-staffed. Many couriers carrying battle reports collapsed from exhaustion and others are still running between camps. Intelligence about the Abyss and reconstruction takes priority, so other parcels may be delayed. No later developments were found for 6.x or 7.0-7.1; the 7.0-7.1 Archon Quests take place in Snezhnaya.

73.content: Michica is the manager of the Courier's Longhouse and an open-world NPC at the Scions of the Canopy. Michica sounds worn down: after joking that the confiscated contraband could stock a shop, Michica insists that it was only an analogy and not a plan to change jobs. After the war in Natlan, Michica reports that couriers are exhausted and stretched thin. Pronouns and age are not stated in the sources checked, and Michica asks the Traveler for help in the daily commission "Hey, Your Letter!" because the Longhouse has too few hands to look for lost parcels.

74.content:
Court of Khaenri'ah (also: Court of Khaenriah, Khaenri'ahn Court, Khaenri'ah's court, Royal Court of Khaenri'ah): The Court of Khaenri'ah was the household of King Irmin, the last Vinster King, made up of his advisers, subordinates and others who served him in the underground kingdom. Its best-known member is the seer Vedrfolnir, called "The Visionary". It is chiefly remembered for the ceremony in which the Traveler's Sibling was named heir.

Canon says little about the court as an institution. It is a stub on the wiki, and nearly everything known comes from Dainsleif's memories and from item text about the last years of the Eclipse Dynasty.

Structure: No ranks, offices or numbers are given. The court sat around a king who ruled with a circle of trusted figures, a Knight Marshal, royal guards and the Universitas Magistrorum, but canon does not say which of these counted as the court itself.

Leadership: King Irmin was the only ruler. The glider lore calls him "the great king", and the court acted as his voice. After he was gone, Knight Marshal Anfortas declared himself Regent, according to a damaged bulletin in the ruins at Gavireh Lajavard.

Members: Vedrfolnir, the seer, is the only member the wiki lists. Rerir described him as "The Visionary", renowned throughout the court for a wisdom beyond ordinary men. He was Dainsleif's elder brother, and Surtalogi said his prophecies were never wrong.

Goals: Publicly, the court presented itself as a source of power that would bring Khaenri'ah a bright future. Dainsleif says it was loudly proclaimed that, with the new heir, all pain and suffering would be washed away. He now reads that rhetoric as covering the king's lust for power.

History: Late in the Eclipse Dynasty the king named the Traveler's Sibling heir and Prince or Princess of Khaenri'ah. The king and court announced the heir as a bringer of prosperity, and many took up the idea of a "Savior". Soon after, Irmin led the heir into the kingdom's deepest depths and used them as a vessel for limitless Abyssal power. Vedrfolnir, imprisoned for his warning, was freed when Dainsleif and four allies stormed the palace by night. The court did not outlive the fall of the kingdom.

Relations: - **Eclipse Dynasty**: the court served its last king.
- **Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah**: Vedrfolnir, Hroptatyr and Rerir were tied to the king's circle, and the group came together in a raid against the palace.
- **Dainsleif**: a young knight at the heir's announcement, later the court guard captain, who turned against the king.

Status as of 7.1: The court no longer exists. It ended with the cataclysm about 500 years ago.

As of 7.1 no court or royal household has been revived. Former associates persist as individuals: Dainsleif the Bough Keeper; Vedrfolnir, one of the Five Sinners, whose consciousness survives in an Abyssal crystal; Rerir, another Sinner, sealed beyond a gate into the moon's reflection in the 6.x Nod-Krai story; and Pierro as the Fatui's Jester. The wiki still marks the entry a stub.

75.comment: Court of Khaenri'ah: Proclamation of the heir
75.content: When King Irmin named the Traveler's Sibling heir, he and the court proclaimed that the heir would bring a bright future. Dainsleif, then an ordinary young knight keeping order in the plaza, remembers the celebration. The glider lore sets the scene: the heir gazed out at the crowd and realised only then how many people lived underground. The word "Savior" came from those who believed the rhetoric. Dainsleif calls the whole thing a cruel irony in hindsight.

76.comment: Court of Khaenri'ah: Vedrfolnir the Visionary
76.content: Vedrfolnir was the court's seer, famed for prophecies that were never wrong, and Dainsleif's elder brother. He warned King Irmin that Khaenri'ah would fall if the king continued down his path. The king had his eyes gouged out and cast him into a cell, which also took away his sight of the future. Dainsleif's raid freed him, and he later became one of the Five Sinners. See his own entry for his later life.

77.content:
Crimson Moon Dynasty (also: Red Moon Dynasty, Crimson Moon descendants, Crimson Moon bloodline): The Crimson Moon Dynasty is the earlier of the two known ruling dynasties of Khaenri'ah, the underground kingdom that fell in the cataclysm. It takes its name from the crimson moon that once shone over the realm. The dynasty is long gone, but some descendants survive and carry its Balemoon Bloodfire, most notably Arlecchino.

Almost everything known about its age comes from the legend of Perinheri, which cannot be verified. In Khaenri'ah's last years the later Eclipse Dynasty hunted its remaining descendants.

Structure: Canon names no ruler, court or lineage list for this dynasty. The legend of Perinheri shows a single 'great ruler' who answers the counsel of sages and lets them found an orphanage for children who may have come from beyond the world. In that era alchemy and the Beastmaster Knights were at the height of their influence. The legend also mentions the 'Darksprites', the first black-wolf warbeasts, created through alchemy.

Members: No member of the dynasty's ruling house is named. Known descendants are Arlecchino and, in Khaenri'ah's last years, Tholindis, Frithr and Orlog.

- **Arlecchino**: the best-known living descendant, the Knave, a Fatui Harbinger and head of the House of the Hearth. She did not know of her heritage until she met Pierro. The Balemoon Bloodfire runs in her blood, and she uses it carefully.
- **Tholindis**: from a distant sub-branch, a Moon Marrow researcher at the Universitas Magistrorum, engaged to Rerir without knowing his secret mission.
- **Frithr** and **Orlog**: other descendants hunted in the last years of Khaenri'ah. Orlog was arrested and probably killed; Frithr was spared by Rerir.

Goals: As a dynasty it has no known goals now. The Perinheri legend says the founding of its orphanage aimed to catch a child from beyond the world who could transcend the gods. Surviving descendants are mainly concerned with staying alive and, in the Khaenri'ah period, hiding their ancestry to avoid persecution.

History: **The age of the crimson moon.** In the legend, the underground kingdom was lit by a crimson moon rather than the later dark sun. Sages persuaded the ruler to establish an orphanage for children said to come from beyond the sea of stars. Perinheri, an outlander, was raised there.

**The change of dynasty.** The legend says the crimson moon set and the dark sun descended, replacing one dynasty with the other. The way this happened is not told. The Crimson Moon era ended before the events of Perinheri (II), set during the Archon War.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the dynasty is long extinct as a ruling house. Its descendants include Arlecchino.

In A Rekviem for the Underworld (7.1), Pierro starts a project with Arlecchino, using her status as a Crimson Moon descendant and the Crimson Moon's authority over death, to create new Delusions to oppose Ronova. The test at the Snezhnayan facility was only mildly successful. In return for her help, Arlecchino has the House of the Hearth stop working for the Fatui and end its training of children as spies.

78.content: Perinheri is a two-volume in-world book, also called Hleobranto Innamorato, sold in Fontaine. It claims to retell an old Khaenri'ahn legend that nobody can confirm and was written over generations. Its first volume sets the story in the Crimson Moon era and describes the orphanage for children from beyond the world. Its second volume has the knights Perinheri and Hleobrant, and Angelica, a woman who claims to be a noble princess from a defeated land. The volume names the four mightiest figures in the kingdom: Njord, Alf of the Universitas Magistrorum, Alberich, and Perinheri.

79.content:
Curatorium of Secrets (also: the Curatorium of Secrets, the Curatorium): The Curatorium of Secrets is an intelligence and commission agency in Nasha Town, Nod-Krai, owned and run by Nefer. It takes commissions from the public, such as finding lost cats, tracking down people or things, and righting wrongs. It is also the public face of the underground Northern Intelligence Network. It follows a policy of strict neutrality toward every faction in Nod-Krai, and its only official employee is Jahoda.

To townspeople it is a busy, efficient, fairly cheap commission shop with a black cat on the counter. Beneath that is a broker of secrets with contacts in nearly every nation. Neutrality is the principle it sells.

Structure: Nefer is the owner and decides everything. Jahoda is the only official employee. Ashru, Nefer's cat, sits at the reception counter.

The building stands at the heart of Nasha Town and has at least two floors. The upper floor holds a reception area and Nefer's office, and visitors can walk in.

Leadership: Nefer, who came to Nod-Krai from Sumeru, owns the Curatorium and also heads the Northern Intelligence Network. She is calm, mercenary, and several moves ahead of whoever is in front of her.

Nefer treats information and favours as currency and nothing as free. In Hidden in the Shadows she tells Jahoda never to accept favours, since they are the hardest debts to repay.

Members: - Nefer: owner, head of the Network.
- Jahoda: the only official employee, a former Seahook Gang member whose life Nefer saved.
- Ashru: Nefer's black cat, the receptionist.

Jahoda handles most field commissions, from searching for lost cats to chasing down clients who cheat. Ashru descends from cats once kept by Thoth, the Ibis King.

Goals: The Curatorium sells information and handles commissions at a profit. Through Nefer it also aims to keep Nod-Krai stable and no single faction dominant.

Methods: The Curatorium does public commissions at reasonable prices, lower when Jahoda is on duty, and brokers intelligence through the Network, where informants sell facts and clients pay for them.

History: Nefer came to Nod-Krai after leaving Sumeru. She eliminated the leaders who had divided the region, then opened the Curatorium and hired Jahoda. At some point she also came to head the Northern Intelligence Network. The doors were nearly always shut until the Curatorium announced that it would take commissions from anyone.

Relations: **Voynich Guild:** works closely with it; Nefer is a member. **Adventurers' Guild:** cooperates through an understanding with Sarin. **Knights of Favonius:** Varka is a Network client. **Frostmoon Scions:** Nefer and Lauma know each other well and spar constantly. **Fatui:** the Curatorium has refused to help either side infiltrate the other.

Reputation: Residents of Nasha Town know it as an efficient, comparatively cheap commission shop. Children remember Nefer as the kind lady with candy and slightly scary stories.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, the Curatorium is open and operating in Nasha Town. Nefer is back at its head, her sight having returned, and Jahoda still handles most of its commissions.

The agency has joined the Nod-Krai League as a representative body. Nefer has said she will stay a member only while it remains worthwhile. Since Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana (6.6) the reception board lists Nefer herself at the counter again. Versions 7.0 and 7.1 add no new Curatorium story in the sources checked; in the 7.1 Anecdote Jahoda: A Thief's End, Jahoda is in Snezhnograd and says she has another errand to run for her boss before heading back to Nod-Krai.

80.comment: Curatorium of Secrets: Northern Intelligence Network
80.content: The Northern Intelligence Network is an underground exchange of information, headquartered in Nod-Krai with contacts in every nation except Liyue. Its members are volunteers, many of whom gave up their old lives to join. It is loosely organised and has no firm rules. People trade what they know for payment. Nefer is its current head, and the Curatorium of Secrets is its main point of sale. Varka calls it the black market of intel and says the Knights of Favonius rely on it for local information.

81.content: The Curatorium of Secrets says it has always followed a policy of strict neutrality and takes no side in Nod-Krai's factions. Nefer cites it to refuse commissions that would make her an enemy of the Fatui or the Frostmoon Scions. She has refused a Harbinger's request to help infiltrate the Scions' territory and refused Lauma's request to help infiltrate the Fatui facility. She still works around it. When Lauma asked her to persuade whoever walked in next to help, she was willing, as long as she was not personally involved. She treats the rule as a business principle, not a moral one.

82.content: In Reunion Beneath the Moonlight, Nefer politely asks a startled Jahoda to help the Traveler, Paimon and Lauma infiltrate the Fatui's Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau. When Jahoda agrees, Nefer fires her on the spot, effective immediately, and says the Curatorium will take her back after the job. This keeps the Curatorium neutral on paper, since Jahoda is a private contractor, and Jahoda earns more without Nefer's cut. Lauma later praises the Curatorium's professionalism.

83.comment: Curatorium of Secrets: The Secret Base
83.content: The Secret Base is an underground meeting place used by the Knights of Favonius and other clients of the Northern Intelligence Network. It is hidden and secure. In Hidden in the Shadows, Varka leads Lauma, Flins, Aino, Ineffa, Jahoda and the Traveler there to hide from the Wild Hunt. Nefer arrives in response to a letter from a "humble knight of Favonius". She turns out to be the Network's head, and Varka asks her to help unite Nod-Krai against Rerir. The interior is only accessible during certain quests.

84.content: Ashru is Nefer's black cat and the Curatorium's receptionist. He descends from the cats Thoth once kept. While imprisoned in Aaru, Thoth took over Ashru's body to speak to Nefer, then left it before she could exploit it. Nefer has kept Ashru close in case Thoth ever speaks through him again. In daily life he is a lazy cat who eats well; Nefer keeps his bowl filled and Jahoda pets him. Ashru's dialogue hints that Lauma or Columbina might be able to understand him.

85.comment: Curatorium of Secrets: Opening to the public
85.content: According to Nefer's fifth Character Story, the Curatorium used to be a place the town feared, and the news that it would take commissions from anyone alarmed parents. The first ordinary client was a tearful little girl whose parents had not come home. Jahoda rescued the couple from bandits, and Nefer asked only for a hairpin as payment. Word spread, and the Curatorium came to resemble a river winding through town: visible at the surface, deeper currents hidden. The story adds that only one person can uncover its true secrets.

86.comment: Curatorium of Secrets: Nod-Krai Trade Expo commission
86.content: During the event Where Waves Meet the Reef (6.5, April to May 2026), Nefer asks the Traveler to help Jahoda manage VIPs at the Voynich Guild's annual expo. Among them are Beidou, captain of a large fleet, and Navia, who leads an underworld organisation, and Jahoda separates their booths. The expo's rule against violence stops visiting Liyue and Fontaine authorities from arresting an arms syndicate inside it, so Nefer lets Yelan and Chevreuse handle the arrests outside. A man called Ashvapati, who joined the Voynich Guild with a hidden agenda, lies about everything except his desert origins. Nefer later suggests that he return to the desert to build a peaceful life there.

87.content:
Daydream Club (also: Daydream Club of Petrichor, the Daydream Club): The Daydream Club is a small group of inventors and researchers from Fontaine, centred on the town of Petrichor. Its members are united by their 'daydreams', ambitious ideas that other people call unrealistic. Known members include Garcia (Numbering Machine), Xavier (Film Kamera), Felix Yogue (a perpetual-energy machine), the brothers Mecantre and Babisse (a giant cannon), Grispan (phlogiston and thermal hypnosis) and Este. Their 'President' is a cat, Lady Grobel.

The club is informal and good-humoured: a group that values curiosity and, by the account of a recording in Daydreams Beyond Space and Time, began with the idea of providing research for free. Felix Yogue says the name was chosen on purpose: since outsiders call the members' dreams unrealistic, they decided to call the club 'daydream'.

Structure: There is no formal hierarchy in the sources. The club's 'President', or 'Director', is Lady Grobel, a cat whom Grispan treats as his leader and whose meows he translates for others. Members each pursue a separate project and trade ideas and equipment; Mecantre plans to borrow Garcia's Numbering Machine to calculate a bridge, for instance. The club has a base in Petrichor stocked with unusual equipment, including divesuits that Grispan bought to study underwater hypnosis.

Members: - **Garcia**: builds the Numbering Machine, a calculating device. Absent-minded and fond of formal language, he travels with his assistant Lutong.
- **Xavier**: inventor of the Film Kamera and a filmmaker. He helped maintain the Mikage Furnace in Inazuma and later founded Musketeer Pictures in Fontaine.
- **Felix Yogue**: wants to build an energy source that runs forever using only mechanical parts. He appears in the Evermotion Mechanical Painting event (limited).
- **Mecantre and Babisse**: brothers designing a super-sized cannon meant to carry people up to touch the stars.
- **Grispan**: researches phlogiston and 'thermal hypnosis'.
- **Este**: a Petrichor resident, a descendant of the Remurian golem Este, who takes up Grispan's hypnosis notes.
- **Lady Grobel**: the cat President.

Goals: Members chase ideas for their own sake. According to a recording heard in Daydreams Beyond Space and Time, the club's original purpose is to provide research for free so that it belongs to everyone, and Garcia insists its research will not be used to make Mora. Mecantre explains why daydreaming matters: it is the reef on which a researcher's torrent of ideas breaks into inspiration, and without it research becomes a stagnant pool.

Methods: Members work by imaginative leaps and practical engineering: calculating machines, cameras, a cannon, phlogiston-powered hypnosis. When Grundeland pressured them, Mecantre and Babisse planted phonographs around Petrichor to record what he said.

History: **Garcia's Paean (2.7).** At Wangshu Inn in Liyue, Garcia and Lutong ask the Traveler to taste-test soup made from a formula, and say they are heading for Sumeru to improve the Numbering Machine.

**Evermotion Mechanical Painting (2.8).** In this event (12 to 22 August 2022), Felix Yogue introduced the club to the Traveler in Mondstadt and invited them to visit Petrichor.

Relations: The club is on good terms with Petrichor's people. When Garcia fears for his friends, Lutong suggests trusting Mr. Bossuet and hoping the Fontaine Research Institute will see them through; Officer Menthe is the authority who is to receive Grundeland. Grundeland is an antagonist who turns penitent. Outside Fontaine, members have been helped by the Traveler and Paimon in Inazuma, Liyue and Natlan.

Reputation: Felix Yogue admits outsiders call the members' plans unrealistic, and the members embrace the label. Lutong calls them brilliant people. The Traveler is warmly welcomed by them.

Status as of 7.1: Active as of 7.1 though scattered. The club's Petrichor members survived the mass dream and returned to their projects, and Grispan remains in Natlan.

The Teyvat Grand Cannon, the Numbering Machine and thermal hypnosis are described as ongoing, not finished. No source after 5.0 adds a new club appearance.

88.content: Garcia is a quest NPC from Fontaine who is building the Numbering Machine, a device for calculation. He is formal, distracted and fond of long phrases, and he is short of Mora. In Garcia's Paean (2.7) he and Lutong cooked Radish Veggie Soup at Wangshu Inn to find a recipe formula and left for Sumeru's Akademiya. In Daydreams Beyond Space and Time (4.6) he rushes home to Petrichor with Kaia and Lutong, fears his friends were exploited and leads the dive to Remuria with the Traveler. He asks the Traveler whether the machine possesses 'thought'; the question is left open.

89.content: Grispan is a florid, anxious Fontainian researcher who is working on thermal hypnosis in Natlan. Lady Grobel is the club's cat President and speaks only in meows, which he translates; she dislikes unexpected trouble. If the Traveler has finished Daydreams Beyond Space and Time, they can fill him in on events in Petrichor. He is uncomfortable around Natlan's exuberant residents and wants to return home once his research is done.

90.content: Brothers and club members in Petrichor. Felix Yogue says they are building a cannon big enough to take people to the stars and are still looking for the right fuel. During the mass dream they were under the Remurian Symphony and spoke of an aqueduct and a fast aquabus. Afterwards they use the dreaming researchers' ideas as seeds for a large bridge and a speedy boat. They hold that research needs a 'daydream' as its spark, and after the quest each says the cannonball must be 'super-sized'.

91.comment: Daydream Club: Daydreams Beyond Space and Time
91.content: A Fontaine World Quest that follows the Petrichor mass dream. Garcia and company return to Petrichor, learn of Phobos and Remuria from the Traveler, and dive to the ruins. Mecantre and Babisse find the statues of two researchers they dreamed as, and Grundeland finds the director of the Remurian Academy of Sciences. The club members conclude those researchers lacked the ability to daydream. The achievement 'In Those Ruins of Dreams...' is granted at the end.

92.comment: Daydream Club: Evermotion Mechanical Painting event
92.content: A 2.8 event (12 to 22 August 2022) in which Felix Yogue, a Fontainian in Mondstadt, asked the Traveler to rebuild a mechanical painting. He described the club's members to the Traveler and invited visitors to Petrichor. Felix says he wants an everlasting energy source made of purely mechanical parts.

93.content:
Druzhna (also: Druzhina, the Druzhna, Druzhna Guards, Winter Pact Corps): The Druzhna is Snezhnaya's personal guard of the Tsaritsa. It answers only to her, and most of its members are Vila, winged fae of the Snowland Fae. Besides protecting her, it is responsible for containing Shadow Realm breaches. Its headquarters is Druzhna HQ in the Everfrozen Earth area, and its Commander-in-chief is Vesna Strivozha.

The word is Russian: a druzhina was a warrior band that served a medieval prince. In Snezhnaya the name belongs to a force older than the Tsaritsa's own reign, founded by the Belyi Tsar. It is separate from the Fatui, which is the army and government apparatus she built, and the two are described as allies.

Leadership: Vesna Strivozha, a Vila of House Strivozha, is Commander-in-chief. Her profile calls her the Tsaritsa's "keen blade", and she and the head housemaid Danica are both called the Tsaritsa's right hands and are often at her side.

Vesna joined as a young recruit, known at first as "that little lass from House Strivozha". Her profile says that by the time she took command, "Vesna" shone so brightly that people forgot the surname. She was trained in her youth by Capitano. In her character story "Druzhna Recruit's Badge", an audience with the Tsaritsa ended with Vesna receiving a Druzhna recruit's badge and Capitano, not Pulcinella, as her mentor. Capitano told her to become a disciple he could be proud of and said he would wait for the day she stood at the pinnacle of the Druzhna. Following a story of her mother's, she left that badge high on the roof of the family estate, and dug it out again after the banquet celebrating her appointment as commander-in-chief.

The first Commander was Grand Duke Filipov Vseslavyevich, the shapeshifter and the Belyi Tsar's closest comrade, who vanished during the Cataclysm.

Structure: The Druzhna is a single armed force with a Commander-in-chief at its head and, in canon, no other formal structure shown. Ranks glimpsed include Commander-in-chief, officer of the guards and Podporuchik, a junior officer rank. Its base is Druzhna HQ, a subarea of Everfrozen Earth in Snezhnaya. It sits under Zapolyarny Palace, the Tsaritsa's seat, and takes its orders from her alone.

Members: Members are overwhelmingly Vila: winged fae with pointed, green-tipped ears and insect-like wings. Their wings let them fly briefly, which suits scouting and long-range raids. Vesna is the only playable member. Named non-playable members are Yarovaya and Akvilina at Snezhnograd. Soldiers of the Druzhna also appear in Vesna's stories.

Goals: Protect the Tsaritsa and keep peace across the lands she surveys. Yarovaya states the duty plainly: the Druzhna exists so that "all lands the Tsaritsa surveys are at peace". Its other standing task is dealing with Shadow Realms, which it treats as the opposite of that peace.

Methods: For Shadow Realms, the Royal Energy Commission detects breaches and reports them, and the Druzhna acts on each report. According to Yarovaya, it organises search groups; if the group finds the Realm's energy core, it neutralises it, and if not, it seals the Realm off. Most Shadow Realms vanish by themselves over time, so the main danger is people entering one by mistake.

History: **Origins.** The Belyi Tsar founded the Druzhna and led it as his personal guard. Its ranks were drawn from the Vila, who were among the first fae to follow him when he united the Snowland Fae. The Vila had earlier been vassals of King Miscislav of the Volkodlak, paying him tribute. After their first Grand Duchess, Vaselisa Strivozha, was beaten by the Tsar, they switched sides. Grand Duke Filipov Vseslavyevich was its first Commander.

**Under the Tsaritsa.** After the Belyi Tsar died in the Cataclysm and Anastasya became Cryo Archon, some Vila rebelled over her policy toward the fae nobility. These revolts were put down, which split the Vila. A history book says that when she moved against the fae princes early in her reign, she did not call up the Druzhna but built the Fatui instead. She later took the Druzhna as her own personal guard, as the loading-screen text says it is today.

Relations: - **The Tsaritsa**: sole master. Loading-screen text says the Druzhna answers only to her.
- **Fatui**: described as allies. The Tsaritsa created the Fatui rather than using the Druzhna to subdue the fae princes, so the two forces have different roots.
- **Vila**: the people from whom the Druzhna is mostly drawn. Vila Druzhna such as Akvilina treat rogue Vila bandits as traitors who shame their people.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Druzhna is active under Commander Vesna. It is short on hands for Shadow Realm work and is running the Special Recruitment Project to bring in volunteers.

Vesna and Danica returned to Snezhnograd with the Tsaritsa after dealing with the eastern monster. No change to the Druzhna's structure or command has been shown in 7.0 to 7.1. Nothing after 7.1 is covered.

94.content: Vesna is the Druzhna's Commander-in-chief and its only playable face. She is a Vila of House Strivozha, trained by Capitano, who holds a fragment of the Ruler of Life's authority. Her profile calls the Druzhna the blade the Tsaritsa wields and Vesna its keenest edge. For her personality, voice and personal history, see her own entry; this entry covers only her role in the force.

95.content: Druzhna HQ is the force's base in the Everfrozen Earth area of Snezhnograd. Named NPCs on the wiki map include Malinina, Musina, Rozhdestvensky, Shakhovskaya and Yarovaya, the last the "Druzhna" Podporuchik who runs the Shadow Realm cleanup. In the world quest A Special Selection (7.0) the Traveler finds applicants lining up to be tested there.

96.content: After the world quest A Special Selection, Yarovaya offers weekly training missions in which the Traveler enters set Shadow Realms and clears them. The project is a manpower measure: the force is stretched, so it takes volunteers who pass strict shooting tests. This is a gameplay system as well as a story beat, and in the story the Traveler joins as a recruit. The map description says the work might even earn the favour of the one on Zapolyarny Palace's throne.

97.content:
Eclipse Dynasty (also: Black Sun Dynasty, Dark Sun Dynasty, Blacksun Dynasty, the dark sun): The Eclipse Dynasty was the second and last known ruling dynasty of Khaenri'ah, the underground kingdom destroyed in the cataclysm 500 years ago. A dark sun stood as its emblem, replacing the earlier crimson moon. Its final ruler was the one-eyed King Irmin, and it fell with the kingdom.

Its era leaned on mechanical engineering and knowledge said to come from beyond the sky, and later turned to the Abyss. Khaenri'ah's survivors, such as the Alberich Clan, and figures such as Dainsleif, trace their roots to its court.

Structure: The Eclipse Dynasty is known mainly from fragments. A king ruled, with a military of knights, a scholarly body (the Universitas Magistrorum), and by the end a Royal Guard called the Black Serpent Knights. The Alberich Clan produced leaders of the kingdom's knights, and the Knight Marshal could advise the king directly.

Members: King Irmin, the last ruler; Dainsleif of the Royal Guard; and the Traveler's sibling, adopted into the royal house.

- **Irmin**: the one-eyed Vinster King, last of the dynasty.
- **Dainsleif**: Twilight Sword and a captain of the Black Serpent Knights, who later became the immortal wanderer of Teyvat.
- **The Traveler's sibling**: arrived 500 years ago, was adopted as royalty and was believed able to command the Abyss.
- **Rerir**: an intelligence officer and secret agent called the Rächer of Solnari, later one of the Five Sinners.
- **Anfortas and Chlothar**: Alberich nobles, with Anfortas serving as regent at the end.

Goals: Little is said of official aims. The dynasty valued mechanical engineering and secrets from beyond the skies, which drew resistance from people who held that human will mattered more than such techniques. Late in its reign Irmin redirected the Universitas Magistrorum's resources toward researching the Abyss.

History: **Rise.** The legend says the crimson moon set and the dark sun descended, replacing the Crimson Moon Dynasty, though the dates and manner are not known. The Perinheri book already shows the Universitas Magistrorum and an Alberich as established names in this time.

**Final reign.** The last king, Irmin, ruled when the cataclysm struck 500 years ago. The Traveler's sibling arrived and was adopted as royalty. Gods cursed the kingdom's people, the Abyss spread, and Khaenri'ah fell.

Status as of 7.1: The dynasty ended with Khaenri'ah's fall and no ruling house survives.

As of 7.1 nothing new about the dynasty itself was found in the 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content checked beyond Pierro's remarks and memories. Its surviving figures remain active.

98.content: Irmin was the last king of Khaenri'ah, called the Vinster King and described as one-eyed. When the cataclysm began he was 'indisposed' and unable to deal with the dark beasts, so Knight Marshal Anfortas declared himself regent. Earlier he redirected the Universitas Magistrorum toward Abyss research and ordered the purge of Crimson Moon descendants. The Traveler's sibling absorbed the Abyssal power he demanded.

99.content:
Eight Trades (also: Bāmén, Eight Gates): The Eight Trades are eight commerce sectors that run Liyue's major industries, under the jurisdiction of the Liyue Qixing. Their divisions are called Halls or Offices. Canon names four: the Communications Office (transport), Huishan Hall (mining), Shenglu Hall (glazed ceramics) and Yinyuan Hall (salt).

When Rex Lapis relinquished his post, his duties fell to the Qixing and the Eight Trades. The Chinese and Japanese names mean "Eight Gates". The English "Hall" translates the Chinese word for a government office.

Structure: The Qixing hold authority over the sectors. Each Trade is a Hall or Office with its own representatives and members. The wiki lists only four of the eight, and no shared leader or headquarters is described. The Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency is a sub-organisation of the Communications Office.

Members: Members named in canon come from four Halls: Fangju, Master Qin and others at the Communications Office; Uncle Dai at Huishan Hall; Miss Ruoyu, Wanyu and Muning at Shenglu Hall; and Wanyan at Yinyuan Hall.

Goals: The Eight Trades keep Liyue's industries and shipping running. Their activities include reopening Chasm mining, researching rare Archaic Stones, and handling transport routes and docks. Under the Qixing they also help carry on the administrative duties that once fell to Rex Lapis.

Methods: They work through official notices (such as bulletin boards at Feiyun Slope and Mingyun Village), commissions from the Ministry of Civil Affairs and trade specialists. Fangju of the Communications Office says its large staff is needed because transport depends on good roads, bridges, waterways and docks. A staff member mentions that the office plans to build small lifts.

Relations: - **Liyue Qixing**: they supervise all eight Trades.
- **Ministry of Civil Affairs**: it works with the Halls, for example by commissioning a Shenglu Hall specialist to oversee the Chasm.
- **Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency**: a guard company that works under the Communications Office.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Eight Trades remain Liyue's commercial administration under the Qixing. No new developments were found in 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

100.content: The Communications Office is the Trade that handles transport in Liyue: shipments, roads, bridges, waterways and docks, and overseas shipping logistics. Its staff is large. Fangju explains its role, and another worker mentions plans for small lifts. The Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency, whose guards escort goods, is one of its sub-organisations. Gaming's profile says the Agency has many skilled guards but only Gaming can both keep clients happy and beat bandits. The Communications Office first appears in 1.5.

101.content: Huishan Hall oversees mining and matters involving the Chasm. Its foreman is Uncle Dai. Its higher-ups are studying rare Archaic Stones from the Chasm, which Muning of the Ministry of Civil Affairs was sent to fetch. The Chasm's changes lowered the quality of the stones that remain.

102.content: Shenglu Hall governs the glazed ceramics trade. Miss Ruoyu is the industry representative. Her notice on the Feiyun Slope bulletin board says she is investigating the possibility of restarting Chasm mining. Wanyu is head of human culture and civilisation research.

103.content: Yinyuan Hall governs the salt industry and worships Havria, the long-dead God of Salt. Wanyan, an archaeologist, is the member seen in canon. Its account of Havria's death differs from other accounts, as the uncertainties note.

104.content:
Eleven Fatui Harbingers (also: Fatui Harbingers, Eleven Harbingers, Harbingers of the Fatui, the Eleven Fatui Harbingers): The Eleven Fatui Harbingers are the executive heads of Snezhnaya's Fatui. The Tsaritsa gives them god-like authority and Delusions, and each leads a division. The Director, Pierro ("The Jester"), leads them. In the early Archon Quest chapters they were sent abroad to collect the Archons' Gnoses.

Seat numbers reflect combat power, and empty seats are not filled by moving everyone up.

Structure: - **The Tsaritsa** appoints every Harbinger. She does it in person at a ceremony in Zapolyarny Palace, or through the Director.
- **The Director** (Pierro) assigns missions and calls meetings. He also chairs votes on decisions that carry national-level risk. Such a decision needs the in-person, unanimous approval of every active Harbinger. Incapacitated members are not counted.
- **Divisions**: each Harbinger commands at least one company or division, and abroad also takes charge of the ordinary Fatui in that nation.

Leadership: Pierro (Eftirvit), a former Khaenri'ahn royal mage, is the Director and was the first Harbinger.

Members: Roster as of 7.1: 1 Capitano (incapacitated, seat kept), 2 Dottore (dead), 3 Columbina (resigned), 4 Arlecchino, 5 Pulcinella, 6 Scaramouche (resigned, erased), 7 Sandrone, 8 Signora (dead), 9 Pantalone, 10 unknown, 11 Tartaglia (Childe). Seats without a note are active, as is the Director, Pierro.

Titles: Capitano is "The Captain", Dottore "The Doctor", Columbina "The Damselette", Arlecchino "The Knave", Pulcinella "The Rooster", Scaramouche "The Balladeer", Sandrone "Marionette", Signora "The Fair Lady", Pantalone "Regrator" and Tartaglia "Childe".

Goals: The Harbingers serve the Tsaritsa's plan, and Pierro explains that plan's purpose as confronting the Heavenly Principles. In practice this meant gathering the Archons' Gnoses, and later, in Snezhnaya, Project Mistilteinn, along with the energy-rationing Project Stuzha that feeds it. Individual Harbingers also pursue goals of their own. Some align with the Tsaritsa's will and some do not, as Dottore's fate shows.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 six are active: Pierro, Arlecchino, Pulcinella, Sandrone, Pantalone and Tartaglia. Capitano's body lies dormant on the Throne of the Primal Fire in Natlan.

In 7.1 the active Harbingers voted unanimously to open Hroptatyr's notebook. Pierro, the Director, used the resulting "Eye of the Fatui" Delusion to mortally wound Ronova, at heavy cost to himself. Arlecchino's deal means the House of the Hearth is to leave Fatui service, but this has not yet been shown taking effect. Project Stuzha is on hold. No new Harbinger has been appointed to any empty seat.

105.comment: Eleven Fatui Harbingers: Harbinger seats and codenames
105.content: Each Harbinger is appointed by the Tsaritsa and given a new codename and title, plus a seat number that reflects combat power. Wanderer's stories say the young Scaramouche was boosted until he matched the lower-ranked Harbingers, and that he later earned the sixth seat. Codenames can be inherited: Peruere took "The Knave" from Crucabena. Seats do not move up when a higher one empties, and they can stay empty indefinitely. As of 7.1 the 2nd and 8th belong to the dead, the 3rd and 6th to resigned members, and the 10th has never been identified. Capitano's 1st seat has been kept for him.

106.comment: Eleven Fatui Harbingers: Unanimous vote of the Harbingers
106.content:
In the Fatui, any decision carrying a national-level risk must be voted on in person by every active Harbinger and must pass unanimously. The Director chairs the vote. Pierro had Hroptatyr's notebook sealed by this rule centuries ago. In Etched in Time (7.1) he called the Harbingers to the Armory Palace archives. The votes went like this:
- Pulcinella said the old fear of making Snezhnaya a "second Khaenri'ah" no longer applied, since they were already at odds with the Ruler of Death.
- Tartaglia was in favour because the Traveler could deal with Abyssal corruption.
- Arlecchino would not leave "a valuable card" unplayed.
- Pantalone called the risk acceptable.
- Sandrone, repelled by the comparison with Dottore, agreed out of curiosity.

Pierro, who had raised the motion, did not need to vote, and it passed. Capitano was not required because he is incapacitated.

107.comment: Eleven Fatui Harbingers: Prohibition on Harbinger infighting
107.content: The Tsaritsa forbids Harbingers from fighting each other. They may insult one another, but they may not draw steel. During the Nod-Krai crisis Arlecchino said that if the ban was not lifted, she would fight Dottore as Peruere rather than as the Knave. The Tsaritsa then had Fatui Internal Affairs review Dottore's case, granted the Harbingers unilateral powers and allowed Arlecchino and Sandrone to eliminate him if needed. Columbina destroyed him. Afterwards the Tsaritsa revoked the Palestar Edict, the order to bring Columbina back.

108.comment: Eleven Fatui Harbingers: Capitano's letter and Councilor Tartaglia
108.content: Before leaving for Natlan, Capitano gave Pierro a detailed letter arranging the future of his subordinates. All his key people went to Tartaglia, along with his place in the Snezhnograd Veche as the voice of the Fatui soldiers. Sandrone explains that Capitano thought Tartaglia was immature but showed great potential and an unusual purity. He also wanted to keep Pulcinella and Pantalone from dividing his army and becoming unstoppable. By 7.0 Tartaglia, who had always assumed Capitano looked down on him, is buried in Veche paperwork.

109.content:
The Eremites (also: Eremites, Eremite, Eremite mercenaries, Eremite brigades): The Eremites are the desert mercenaries of Sumeru. They come from the Great Red Sand, whose ancient civilisations have collapsed, and they hire out their blades across Teyvat. Outsiders use "Eremites" as a blanket name for many separate brigades and tribes. Some are honourable, some are criminal, and some ignore the others entirely. They are the only authorised mercenary organisation in Sumeru, and many foreigners judge them as unscrupulous soldiers of fortune. The best-known members are Dehya of the Blazing Beasts and the Corps of Thirty who guard Sumeru City.

The Eremites hold a claim to part of the legacy of the desert's lost civilisations, which the official Sumeru teaser calls a "deterrent of last resort in a crisis". They have an open partnership with the Adventurers' Guild.

Structure: There is no overall chain of command. The Eremites are split into brigades and tribes, each with its own beliefs and code of conduct, and the groups overlap or conflict. Anyone can join the mercenary brigades. Traditionally only people from the desert may, but Rukh Shah is an exception. Some people simply borrow the name for their own benefit. Consultants and advisors help the groups talk to each other.

Members: Dehya is the best-known: a legend among Eremites, former Corps of Thirty and now Blazing Beasts. Rukh Shah, the Corps of Thirty's Parchamdar, is the youngest ever to hold the post. Aybak leads a group at Caravan Ribat that is under contract with the Akademiya to guard the town and maintain the Wall of Samiel. His group calls each other brother and sister. Rahman leads his own faction. Dehya's adoptive father Kusayla led Dakan Al-Ahmar. Mizri led Ayn Al-Ahmar in Port Ormos.

Abilities and limits: Eremite fighting is tied to their ancestry. The Sword-Dancers' skills are said to date from Deshret's civilisation and are now an art as well as a combat style. Eremite dance traditions descend from their ancestors' worship rituals. Elemental power among them is not innate but borrowed from Spirits of Omen, ancient desert spirits that dwell in their weapons and awaken in times of peril.

Goals: Most Eremites seek coin. They take commissions as guards, escorts, caravan protectors and fighters. Some groups follow causes: devout followers of King Deshret seek his resurrection or oppose the Akademiya's version of history, and some brigades act for their own survival. Dehya hopes to bring hope to the desert she considers home.

Methods: Contract work: guarding caravans and settlements, hunting monsters, escorting scholars and delivering goods. Many play the Genius Invokation TCG across Sumeru. Criminal factions blackmail, raid and extort. Deshret's Relics collected "records" of members' shameful deeds to bind them, the Tanit raised captured children as devoted "Falcons", and Dakan Al-Ahmar raided caravans for supplies during its revenge campaign.

Relations: **Akademiya.** The Corps of Thirty serves the Akademiya as hired peacekeepers, and the Akademiya's liaison officer is Effendi. The Akademiya's wider reputation among Eremites is poor, especially among devoted followers of Deshret. Aybak's group is also contracted to the Akademiya. After the reforms that followed the Archon Quest, Rahman's faction now works with Setaria to promote education among desert peoples. The Matra are the Akademiya's disciplinary officers, and their General Mahamatra Cyno hails from the desert.
**Adventurers' Guild.** An open partnership.
**Rival Eremites.** The Corps of Thirty has a tenuous relationship with other groups, and Rukh Shah warns visitors to be careful of Eremites outside the city.

Reputation: Outsiders see them as mercenaries who will do anything for coin. The scholar Nazafarin calls them true soldiers of fortune who will do anything for money. Impostors who use the name and do poor work for unwary foreign clients also drag down the reputation of the whole group. Dehya is considered a legend among them.

Status as of 7.1: Active in Sumeru as of 7.1, with the Corps of Thirty guarding the capital and brigades taking contracts across the desert.

Rahman's faction now supports the reformed Akademiya. Deshret's Relics and the Tanit are gone, and Dakan Al-Ahmar surrendered after avenging Kusayla. In 6.6, during the crisis that sealed Sumeru, Dehya was still working in the desert as an Eremite mercenary. No Eremite story in the Snezhnaya content (7.0-7.1) was found.

110.content: The Akademiya's permanently hired Eremite brigade in Sumeru City. It started as thirty founders hired by the sages and is said to be among the oldest Eremite groups. It now has more than thirty members, but keeps the name in memory of the founders. Its members wear teal-green scarves with a petal-like emblem like the Akademiya's, and its barracks are in the Citadel of Regzar. The Parchamdar, Rukh Shah, commands it, and Asfand serves as its Consultant. It keeps the peace in the capital and manages and coordinates the other mercenary brigades. Dehya is a notable former member.

111.content: The brigade of Dehya, who joined at a young age after her last argument with her adoptive father Kusayla. Kusayla had quietly arranged her place there to protect her from Deshret's Relics. During the Whirling Waltz event, the Traveler and Paimon became the Blazing Beasts' official partners.

112.comment: The Eremites: Deshret's Relics and Ayn Al-Ahmar
112.content: Deshret's Relics was a large Eremite faction that held its members by blackmail, having them leave behind "records" of their sins as proof of loyalty. Subgroups were **Ayn Al-Ahmar** and **Dakan Al-Ahmar**. The names refer to King Deshret's alleged true name, Al-Ahmar. Kusayla, leader of Dakan Al-Ahmar, died burning the records, and his followers took revenge on the Relics and on innocent travellers. The Relics' last leader Mishal was taken down by Dakan Al-Ahmar, Dehya and the Traveler. Ayn Al-Ahmar survived in Port Ormos under Mizri, devout in their worship of Deshret and disdainful of Greater Lord Rukkhadevata.

113.content: An Eremite faction near the Valley of Dahri led by Rahman, a longtime friend of Dehya. Maqrin and Tanina are other members. They believed the Akademiya's rumours that King Deshret would return, resented the forest and its Archon, and held the Village Keepers of Aaru Village as hostages. After learning the truth about Rukkhadevata, they helped the Traveler's party against the sages and, afterwards, work with Setaria to promote education among desert peoples.

114.comment: The Eremites: Tanit and the matriarchal tribes
114.content: The Tanit were a nomadic, matrilineal tribe in the Desert of Hadramaveth who venerated the Goddess of Flowers. They were led by a Matriarch and Nine Elders, traded in crocodile products, spices and essential oils, hunted wenut, and raised captured children as devoted "Falcons". They were eventually annihilated by the Traveler and Jeht after Matriarch Babel's schemes failed. The Shimti and Uzza were also matriarchal tribes. The Shimti, known for their beautiful women, were massacred by the Iab about 20 years ago after their chief Sinuhe took water from the Iab's well; only his adopted daughter Nefer survived. The Thamudian-descended Iab and Unut were later wiped out or scattered in the conflict set off by Nefer's revenge.

115.content: An Eremite clan likely descended from a man named Agha Farrokh, now led by his daughter Siman Farrokhzad, an Akademiya sage connected with Amurta and the Bimarstan. On her orders the clan dealt with the Fatui, completing a commission to kill a Fatui traitor for Dottore and then trying to capture Aranara for him. Lunja leads one of its groups.

116.content: Ancient desert spirits, or fragments of them, that can manipulate the elements and dwell in Eremite weapons. They awaken in times of peril and are summoned by high-ranking Eremites: Stone Drakes by Stone Enchanters, Wind Gledes by Galehunters, Dendro Spirit-Serpents by Floral Ring-Dancers and Pyro Scorpions by Scorching Loremasters. The lore suggests an awakened spirit is satisfied only once blood has been spilled.

117.content: The **Caracal Battalion** competes in Port Ormos for the Divine Knowledge Capsule; Ayn Al-Ahmar's Tariq and Tumart call them money-grubbing opportunists. **Thutmose** is a Deshret-devoted group seeking the secret of Al-Ahmar from researchers and the Fatui, from a base on Lamb-Devourer Rock. **Aybak's group** guards Caravan Ribat and the Wall of Samiel for the Akademiya.

118.content:
Fatui (also: Fatuus, the Fatui, Fatui of Snezhnaya): The Fatui (one member is a Fatuus; the name is Latin for "fools") are Snezhnaya's government, diplomatic corps and military in one body. They answer to the Tsaritsa, the Cryo Archon, who founded them 500 years ago with Pierro as their first member and Director. Under him the Eleven Fatui Harbingers each run a division. The Fatui are headquartered in Glupov, a fortress city inside Snezhnograd, and their emblem is the Palestar Banner. Abroad they present themselves as envoys of the Tsaritsa's goodwill, but most nations distrust them: in the Traveler's journey they took Gnoses from one Archon after another, using deceit, extortion, bribery and human experimentation along the way.

Structure: The Tsaritsa sits at the top. Below her, Director Pierro relays her appointments, assigns missions and convenes the Harbingers. Each Harbinger leads a division with personal subordinates, and below them are numbered companies and squads.

Known parts of the organisation include:
- **Debt Collection**: mostly Pyro Agents. It recovers debts owed to the Northland Bank, using as much force as it takes.
- **The House of the Hearth**: the intelligence arm, an orphanage that raises children as agents under Arlecchino, "Father".
- **The Northland Bank**: the state bank, presided over by Pantalone, which also funds and houses Fatui operations abroad.
- **The Armory Palace**: the royal weapons-development institution in Glupov, managed by Sandrone.
- **Fatui Internal Affairs**: also called the Okhranka. It investigates misconduct among the Fatui and reports to the Tsaritsa.

Leadership: **The Tsaritsa (Anastasya)** rules Snezhnaya directly, and the Fatui exist to carry out her will. **Pierro, "The Jester"**, is the Director of the Fatui, the first Harbinger and the Harbingers' leader. Each Harbinger takes a codename from Italian commedia dell'arte, a title and a rank number based on combat power.

Status of the seats as of 7.1:
- Director: Pierro, active.
- 1st: Capitano, incapacitated. His life force is merged with the Lord of the Night in Natlan, but the Tsaritsa kept his rank.
- 2nd: Dottore, dead.
- 3rd: Columbina, resigned.
- 4th: Arlecchino, active.
- 5th: Pulcinella, active.
- 6th: Scaramouche, resigned and erased from Irminsul. He now lives as the Wanderer.
- 7th: Sandrone, active.
- 8th: Signora, dead.
- 9th: Pantalone, active.
- 10th: never revealed.
- 11th: Tartaglia (Childe), active.

Goals: The Fatui serve the Tsaritsa's aim of a "perfect world", which means overthrowing the Heavenly Principles. In the Traveler's journey, that meant collecting the Gnoses: Harbingers were sent to each of the other six nations to obtain them, and by 7.1 the Tsaritsa held every Gnosis except the Pyro Gnosis, which was lost when Irminsul burned. They also develop Delusions and weapons, gain influence in other nations, and strengthen Snezhnaya against Celestia.

Methods: Abroad, the Fatui's usual pattern is to provoke or exploit a crisis and then offer "help" that leaves the local authorities in their debt. They bribe or collude with local elites, lend money through the Northland Bank and collect it ruthlessly, plant sleeper agents raised in the House of the Hearth, and use deniable operatives. Delusions (Vision-like devices that work for anyone and can be stronger than Visions, but drain or even kill their users) give their elite troops elemental power.

Relations: - **Other nations**: Snezhnaya keeps official relations with every nation, but its Fatui are distrusted nearly everywhere. Inazuma expelled them as a friendly party after Signora's plot, and the Liyue Qixing watch them closely.
- **The Traveler**: long a thorn in the Fatui's side, by 7.1 the Traveler is a trusted outsider. The Tsaritsa made them a "Consultant to the Tsaritsa".

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Fatui remain in power in Snezhnaya. Pierro mortally wounded Ronova with the new Eye of the Fatui but was left badly depleted. Ronova's curse is lifted, and Project Mistilteinn can resume.

Six Harbingers are active: Pierro, Arlecchino, Pulcinella, Sandrone, Pantalone and Tartaglia. Capitano's seat is kept, and the seats of Dottore, Columbina, Scaramouche and Signora are empty. Arlecchino's agreed price for helping build the new Delusion is that the House of the Hearth will become independent of Fatui affairs and that no more children will be trained as spies. This has been agreed but not yet shown in practice. Tartaglia commands most of Capitano's former troops, and corruption lists from Pulcinella and the House of the Hearth are being reviewed with the Druzhna's help.

119.content:
- **Skirmishers**: the common soldiers abroad, wearing mechanical suits that give their weapons and armour elemental power and shields. Variants include Cryogunner and Hydrogunner Legionnaires, Pyroslinger and Geochanter Bracers, and Electrohammer and Anemoboxer Vanguards. Their handbook entry says they advance into foreign lands to scout and lay groundwork without asking whether they will live, and that they rely on teamwork because each is weaker alone.
- **Cicin Mages**: Delusion-wielding mages (Cryo or Electro) who command swarms of small elemental Cicins and enjoy toying with their prey.
- **Agents**: elite Pyro or Electro operatives who blink in and out of sight and fight with blades. Pyro Agents staff Debt Collection.
- **Mirror Maidens**: elite Hydro users who fight through conjured mirrors.
- **Operatives**: covert Wind and Frost agents, seen in Fontaine.
- **Landcruisers**: war machines built by the Armory Palace with the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau.

120.content: Unlike Skirmishers, Oprichniki are formally recruited, rigorously trained volunteers, sent either to the Fatui's most important strongholds or to the deadliest front lines. They serve in Nod-Krai and Snezhnaya with kuuvahki-powered gear. Line Troopers, Vanguards, Grenadiers, Support Troopers, Medics and Bombardiers make up the ranks. Officers such as Fireblade Shock Troopers, Hailstorm Cannoneers and Thunderblitz Gvardiya fight with pure elemental power and mostly come from the Royal Military Academy. Oprichniki guard the Northland Bank's vaults in Snezhnograd with radios and access cards.

121.content: The Northland Bank lends generously and expects repayment in full and on time. When someone defaults, the Fatui's Debt Collection division, made up mostly of Pyro Agents, is usually sent and uses as much force as it takes. The bank sometimes chooses other options: in Nasha Town it turned the debtor Zhuoxin into an informant for ten years instead. Snezhnaya's deep cultural regard for loyalty and promises underlies the bank's claim to be "no ordinary bank".

122.content:
Fatui Internal Affairs (also: Okhranka, Fatui Internal Division, the Okhranka): Fatui Internal Affairs, also known as the Okhranka (Russian for "security"), is a special group within the Fatui that investigates misconduct among Fatui ranks. It answers to the Tsaritsa. Little else about it is known: canon names no members, leader or base.

It is not a combat division or a public face of the Fatui. It appears in canon only as the body that gets handed a case when the Tsaritsa wants a Fatui member's loyalty or conduct judged.

Structure: Canon gives no structure for the division: no ranks, no named staff, no headquarters. All that is established is that it is a special group of Fatui and that it reports to the Tsaritsa, not to a Harbinger. It should be treated as an unseen office. Scenes may refer to its existence, but should not show it with invented officers or an invented building.

Leadership: The only authority above the division that canon names is the Tsaritsa (Anastasya). The Harbinger Tartaglia, who describes the division to Arlecchino, is a messenger of the Tsaritsa's orders and is not shown to belong to it. No head of Internal Affairs is named through 7.1.

Goals: Its job, as canon states it, is to look into misconduct inside the Fatui and to deliver a formal verdict when the Tsaritsa asks, for example on whether a member has turned traitor and whether he is a threat to Snezhnaya.

History: Its earliest appearance in canon is in Version 6.3 (Song of the Welkin Moon, Act VII), during the crisis in Nod-Krai. Dottore, the Harbinger called the Doctor, was recalled to Snezhnaya on the grounds that he was redundant, but did not leave. He stayed to attack Columbina and seize the power of the Three Moons. When the Tsaritsa learned of this, she authorised Fatui Internal Affairs to review his case and reach a formal verdict on whether he had turned traitor and whether he threatened Snezhnaya. Tartaglia relayed this to Arlecchino while he was sent to receive the refugees from Nod-Krai.

Relations: Its relationship to the Fatui is that of an internal watchdog. It answers to the Tsaritsa, and its verdict on Dottore bound the Harbingers Arlecchino and Sandrone. Its dealings with Pantalone, the Northland Bank and the other Harbingers are not described.

Reputation: Canon gives no public reputation. It is spoken of matter-of-factly by senior Fatui, as a known part of the organisation.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is still the Tsaritsa's tool for judging Fatui misconduct. It has not appeared directly in any scene.

Its most recent mention is in Version 7.1, when the Tsaritsa said the suspect in the Seals of Life theft should be handed to it. Its future is not shown.

123.content: Fatui Internal Affairs, known as the Okhranka, investigates misconduct inside the Fatui and reports to the Tsaritsa. Little more is known. In 6.3 the Tsaritsa had it review Dottore's case after he ignored his recall in Nod-Krai; by the wiki's account it found he had acted against her will, which freed Arlecchino and Sandrone to eliminate him if he became a threat.
