In 7.1 she said a suspect in the Seals of Life theft should be sent to it.

124.content:
Feiyun Commerce Guild (also: Feiyun Guild, Fēiyún Shānghuì, Flying Cloud Commerce Guild): The Feiyun Commerce Guild is a powerful trading guild in Liyue, run as a family business. It deals in silk, tea and printed books. Its best-known member is Xingqiu, the second son of the Guild Manager, a studious young man with a mischievous streak.

The Guild apparently originated at Yilong Wharf in Chenyu Vale and still keeps the family's old home there. Merchants in Liyue Harbor know the family well, and its reputation depends on its children behaving as befits it.

Structure: The Guild's leadership is the family: a retired great-grandfather who founded it, a grandfather who is patriarch, a father who manages it, and an elder son who is heir. Xingqiu is the second son.

The family estate is a multigenerational household, with servants. The wiki lists Xu, Sheng and Hongxing as servants, Qiuwei as a retailer, Lixin as a messenger at Yilong Wharf, and An Su as a butler. The family members are not named in canon. Xingqiu's older brother is learning to run the business, and Xingqiu is expected to support him once he takes over, though Xingqiu is not required to shoulder the Guild's affairs.

Leadership: Xingqiu's father holds the post of Guild Manager. His grandfather is the patriarch, and a great-grandfather, styled "His Lordship", founded the Guild and is now retired. Xingqiu's brother handles business tasks such as arranging transport through the Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency. He and the father also host influential figures. Xingqiu once concluded from the way they treated Zhongli that Zhongli must be a high-profile person.

Goals: The Guild's goals are commercial: moving goods, selling them and keeping the family's reputation. It also wants its heirs to act the part. Xingqiu's brother tells him that if he cannot tidy a room he cannot tidy the world, because both brothers are responsible for the Guild's name.

Methods: The Guild trades silk, prints books and sells tea, and it has a warehouse in the Lisha region, left of Mt. Tianheng on the map. It hires the Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency to move and protect goods. A shop in Sumeru's Port Ormos sells jewellery and silk, and the materials used to make them.

Relations: - **Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency**: a guard company commissioned to move and protect the Guild's goods. It belongs to the Communications Office.
- **Guhua Clan**: Xingqiu studies its sword arts with his father's approval.
- **Ningguang, Yelan and Ganyu**: the family hosts or meets them. Yelan says she often has dealings with the family and expects Xingqiu will one day be "outsmarting everyone around him".

Reputation: Every merchant in Liyue Harbor knows of Xingqiu and the Guild. People see Xingqiu as kind, polite and promising, and parents hold him up as a model for their own children. Xingqiu says people see him only as the Guild's second son.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Guild is active, with Xingqiu still balancing its affairs against his wandering adventures. The wiki records no changes to it in 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

125.content: Xingqiu's family are unnamed in canon. His father is the Guild Manager, strict about behaviour befitting the Guild's name. His elder brother is the heir and lectures Xingqiu about messy rooms, bad calligraphy, skipped banquets and skipped meals, yet is gentler than the father. He once told the servants not to disturb Xingqiu's room, having mistaken the martial-arts novels under the bed for something more adult. Xingqiu in turn has developed an elaborate method for evading both, recounted in birthday mails.

126.content:
Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah (also: Five Sinners, the Five Sinners, Five Sinners of Khaenriah, Sinners of Khaenri'ah, Five Great Sinners): The Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah are five people who were once among Khaenri'ah's most admired, each the best in their field: "The Wise" Hroptatyr, "The Visionary" Vedrfolnir, "Gold" Rhinedottir, "The Foul" Surtalogi and the "Rächer of Solnari" Rerir. About 500 years ago, on the night they joined Dainsleif to storm the royal palace, they could not resist the call of the Abyss. They divided among themselves a world-shattering Abyssal power and became transcendent beings. When the cataclysm came, none of them defended their nation. Dainsleif, who fought beside them that night, has sworn he will never forgive them.

They were never a formal order. "Five Sinners" is what others call them, and the name stuck to all five. The power they took was the Abyssal power that King Irmin had the Traveler's sibling absorb. Dainsleif first named all five to the Traveler in Sumeru (4.7).

Members: - **Hroptatyr, "The Wise"**: President of the Universitas Magistrorum and Chief Royal Mage. He wanted limitless knowledge.
- **Vedrfolnir, "The Visionary"**: a prophet and Dainsleif's older brother. He wanted to see the future again.
- **Rhinedottir, "Gold"**: an alchemist of the Art of Khemia who wanted to create life. She later created Albedo.
- **Surtalogi, "The Foul"**: a knight who wanted supreme strength. He later became Skirk's master.
- **Rerir, "Rächer of Solnari"**: an ordinary intelligence officer. Dainsleif could not understand his fall until Nefer read his past in 6.1.

Dainsleif summed up their motives in 6.1: each was driven by a personal desire, and the Abyss tempted each of them through that desire. Rerir's was Tholindis: after watching his fiancée flee through a moon gate, he broke down and took the power hoping to follow her.

Structure: The five had no hierarchy, no leader and no shared goal. They came together only once, as allies Dainsleif called on for one night. Afterwards they scattered, and none of them has been shown acting with another since.

Goals: They shared no goal. What they had in common was that each wanted something beyond human limits: foresight (Vedrfolnir), infinite knowledge (Hroptatyr), the creation of life (Rhinedottir), supreme strength (Surtalogi) and Tholindis (Rerir). Afterwards each went after that desire alone:
- Hroptatyr resolved to leave Teyvat and merge with the Abyss to gain infinite knowledge.
- Surtalogi crossed the sea of stars looking for an opponent who could beat him.
- Rhinedottir went on making life through alchemy.
- Rerir tried to follow Tholindis into the moon gate.

History: Late in the Eclipse Dynasty, Vedrfolnir warned King Irmin at court that Khaenri'ah would fall if he kept to his path. Irmin had him blinded in both eyes and thrown into the dungeons. Furious, Dainsleif secretly called together Hroptatyr, Rhinedottir, Surtalogi and Rerir, and that same night they stormed the palace. Dainsleif and Surtalogi fought the guards, Hroptatyr and Rhinedottir disabled the palace's security measures, and Rerir went to free Vedrfolnir. The rescue succeeded. Then the Abyss tempted the five, and each betrayed Dainsleif by taking a share of the Abyssal power held by the Traveler's sibling. Even Vedrfolnir, the brother Dainsleif had come to save, took his share.

Relations: - **Dainsleif**: their former ally and the organiser of the raid. He calls them traitors to himself and to their nation and has vowed vengeance. He still remembers Rerir as a friend.
- **King Irmin**: their sovereign. Vedrfolnir and Hroptatyr were his most trusted servants until Vedrfolnir was blinded.
- **The Traveler's sibling**: the vessel of the Abyssal power the five divided.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 they act separately. Rhinedottir is the Ruler of Life, Surtalogi roams the stars, Rerir is trapped in the moon's reflection, and Hroptatyr and Vedrfolnir are unaccounted for.

- **Rhinedottir**: appeared in person in Snezhnograd in 7.1. She reclaimed the life authority stolen from Naberius and met the Tsaritsa.
- **Surtalogi**: last seen still seeking a worthy opponent, waiting for Skirk to surpass him.
- **Rerir**: sealed beyond the moon gate since 6.1. When Columbina met him there in 6.3 he was remorseful.
- **Hroptatyr**: in 7.1 only a memory of his younger self was met, preserved in his notebook's prism.
- **Vedrfolnir**: no confirmed whereabouts.

127.comment: Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah: The night of the palace raid
127.content: After King Irmin blinded and imprisoned Vedrfolnir for warning that Khaenri'ah would fall, Dainsleif gathered Hroptatyr, Rhinedottir, Surtalogi and Rerir and stormed the palace that same night. Each had a task. Dainsleif and Surtalogi fought the guards, Hroptatyr and Rhinedottir disabled the security measures, and Rerir freed Vedrfolnir. The rescue worked, but the five then gave in to the Abyss and divided among themselves the power Irmin had placed in the Traveler's sibling. Dainsleif was left alone and betrayed. The Wings of Fate's Course Intertwined glider lore calls the raid's "righteous deed" of saving the nation "but a deed done in passing".

128.comment: Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah: Dainsleif's vow against the Sinners
128.content: In Sumeru (4.7), Dainsleif told the Traveler that the Sinner who had empowered Chlothar was his older brother Vedrfolnir. He then named all five. They had been the hope of their nation, he said, and the six of them together should have stopped the Vinster King. Because none of them defended Khaenri'ah, they will never have his forgiveness, and he vowed vengeance. He contrasted them with the Traveler's sibling, saying the twins could still be reconciled. By 6.1 he was willing to go further: he hired Nefer to uncover Rerir's past and held open the gate that sealed his old friend away.

129.content:
Flower-Feather Clan (also: Tlalocan, the Flower-Feather tribe, Flower-Feather Clan settlement): The Flower-Feather Clan, whose older name is Tlalocan, is one of Natlan's six tribes. Its people live alongside the Qucusaurs, the proudest of the flying Saurians, and its elite flying squad patrols the skies on Qucusaur-back. The settlement sits among the cliffs of Quahuacan Cliff in northern Natlan, overlooking the ruins of Ochkanatlan. The current chief is Mutota. Its most famous member is Chasca, the Peacemaker who bears the Ancient Name Vuka.

Some clan members, like the Qucusaurs, have mastered riding Natlan's hot currents of gaseous Phlogiston without being burned. Joining the flying squad means passing a famously hard trial, and those who give up are called the "Wingless". The tribe was founded thousands of years ago by Lianca, a girl raised by dragons, as a refuge for people who had nowhere else to go.

Structure: A chief leads the tribe, advised by elders. Its pride and best-known institution is the Qucusaur Riders, the flying squad, which has both active and reserve members. Any applicant must be a capable warrior and must also win a Qucusaur's trust; the flying trials are held at a trial arena in the valley below the settlement. People who repeatedly fail, or who stop trying, are called the "Wingless". Many keep retaking the trials, some leave to work for other tribes, and some find other work in the clan. Clan members summon their Saurian companions by whistling or blowing a horn.

Leadership: Chief Mutota is a scarred, grey-haired veteran who values patience and caution above bravado. He likes to remind people that scars are a badge of honour but also a record of mistakes.

Mutota led the defence during the Abyss invasion and then the rebuilding. He accepted Iansan's help and asked the Traveler and Chasca to look into trouble inside the tribe. He gets on with ordinary members as well: Pixica calls him "Boss", and he coaches Wingless applicants himself. When the elder Allpa tried to depose him, he escaped capture only because he was out coaching, and he quickly rallied the tribe against her.

Members: - **Chasca**: Peacemaker and flying-squad warrior, bearer of the Ancient Name Vuka. She was raised by the Qucusaur Chimpu and adopted by Cusco's family.
- **Ifa**: a renowned Saurian veterinarian, known as the "Tlalocan Vet".
- **Mutota**: the chief.
- **Allpa**: a former elder and Flying Captain who found the infant Chasca. She is now imprisoned for her coup.
- **Cusco**: Chasca's adoptive father and Chuychu's father. He also checks injured Saurians.

Goals: The clan's ideals go back to Lianca: a place where the weak can live freely and without fear, where no one has to kneel to anyone. In practice its people guard their own territory from the air, keep watch over the ruins of Ochkanatlan, and protect the bond between riders and Qucusaurs that the clan is built on. Chasca says that clan pride, and especially the riders' pride, sometimes "borders on arrogance".

Methods: Riders fly Qucusaurs on patrol and in battle. Qucusaurs and some clan members can use the high-temperature currents of gaseous Phlogiston without being burned. Some members, such as the trainee Kallfu, ride the currents without any equipment. Riders are expected to train relentlessly: a Qucusaur that is not fully under control can kill both itself and its rider. To other tribes, a lone Flower-Feather member who starts whistling is a sign that something nearby is wrong.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the clan has recovered from the Abyss invasion under Chief Mutota, and its flying trials have resumed. Allpa and her accomplices are in custody.

Since 5.8 the clan has run a simple harbor at Quahuacan Cliff for people coming from Nod-Krai. No clan story developments were found in the 6.x Nod-Krai or 7.0-7.1 Snezhnaya Archon Quests. In a 6.7 limited-time event, Chasca agreed to plan a training exchange with Fontaine's Special Patrol, but whether it has started is not shown.

130.comment: Flower-Feather Clan: Qucusaur Riders and the flying trials
130.content: The Qucusaur Riders are the Flower-Feather Clan's elite flying squad. Applicants must prove themselves as warriors and then win a Qucusaur's approval in the flying trials, held at an arena in the valley below the settlement. Losing a Qucusaur's trust is the most common reason for failure, and the clan treats it seriously because an uncontrolled flight can kill both rider and Saurian. Chasca, who was raised by Qucusaurs, says even she had to earn their approval. Applicants call Qucusaurs by whistle or horn, and a weak, unsure whistle will not bring one. After the Abyss invasion the trials were held again. The arrival of Phlogiston Wings led Chasca to argue that wing users should be judged by different standards.

131.content: "Wingless" is the clan's name for people who fail the flying trials repeatedly or give up on them. They must give up their Saurian companion for their own safety, and life in the tribe can be hard for them. Some keep trying. Allpa eventually passed. Others, like Pixica, who runs the hot-air balloons, make peace with it and find other ways to reach the sky. Chasca says that only the best warriors attempt the trials at all, and that the clan quietly watches over the Wingless until their fighting spirit returns, as Qucusaurs watch their unfledged young. Allpa used the Wingless' longing to fly to win support for her Phlogiston Wings.

132.comment: Flower-Feather Clan: Peacemakers of the Tlalocan
132.content: The Peacemakers are the Flower-Feather Clan's mediators. As a child, Chasca was so prone to fighting that Allpa taught her from a woven scroll titled "Peacemaker - the Art of Communication", which taught that language is humanity's greatest weapon. Chasca later adopted the name for herself and her role. Peacemakers step into disputes between people, tribes, humans and Saurians, or Saurians among themselves, and settle them with words first and force only when words fail. In one story a pair of feuding chiefs signed a very formal joint statement thanking the Peacemaker for their "reconciliation".

key: Where Feathers Are Intertwined Like Flowers
133.content: The tribe's home sits on Quahuacan Cliff in northern Natlan, looking down on the ruins of Ochkanatlan. It is a settlement of floating platforms, hot-air balloons, Saurian stables and training grounds, with the flight-trial arena down in the valley. Residents include Chief Mutota, Saurian riders, guards, the trial-arena administrator Inkanak, the balloon operators Pixica and Zyanya, and the reputation advisor Abundi. A message board carries the vet Ifa's notes reminding people to bring their Saurians for regular check-ups. From 5.8 a simple harbor below the cliff receives people coming from Nod-Krai.

key: Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering
Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering
134.content:
Fontaine Research Institute (also: Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering, Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering): The Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering, usually just "the Institute", is Fontaine's centre for the study of machines and energy. It was founded by the genius inventor Alain Guillotin, whose clockwork mechanisms and kinetic cores are still built in Fontaine's factories. Unlike Sumeru's Akademiya, it has no governing or teaching role. Its central laboratory was wrecked by an explosion during Edwin Eastinghouse's Arkhium experiment, and the rebuilt Institute is better known for muddle and money trouble than for brilliance.

Many of Fontaine's mechanical inventions come from the Institute, though some projects have embarrassed it, such as the "Mekafish" water cleaners that began killing fish.

Structure: The Institute is a working organisation of researchers, engineers, technicians, assistants and clerks. Known departments include Advanced Artificed Technology Research and Development and the Department of Statistics and Mathematics; a Natural Ecological Environment Monitoring Department was dissolved after the accident. Notices mention executive, materials, logistics, finance investigation and disciplinary offices. Titles seen include Senior Technician, Senior Researcher, Researcher, Engineer, Research Assistant and Department Director.

Leadership: Raimondo is the Senior Technician appointed to lead the Institute, and Choiseul is its administrative officer. Both took over the rebuilding after the explosion. Founding Director Alain Guillotin is long dead.

Edwin Eastinghouse, the Senior Technician who led the Arkhium project, was first presumed dead, then dismissed for long unauthorised absence, and finally fired after being found alive. Choiseul says the Institute is better ordered without Edwin's influence. Augustus Lovelace claims that research spirit has been in freefall since Raimondo and Choiseul took over, and says the Institute used to be a paradise for researchers. Rogier Cotes is named as a deceased Third Director.

Members: Named staff include the engineer Anatole, who talks about the Institute to the Traveler in Liyue; Desnos, who handles recruitment at the temporary office; the researchers Xavier and Refait; and Maurice Juglar of Statistics and Mathematics. Delaroche, a former clerk now partly in charge of the Fishing Association, appears to remain formally a member. Former members include Edwin Eastinghouse and Nacker (both fired and sent to the Fortress of Meropide), Jurieu (a former assistant of Edwin who helped design the airship The Wingalet), and deceased members such as Bravais, Teilhard, Mosso Lombroso and Pierre Lefevere.

Goals: The Institute researches machines and energy for Fontaine's benefit. Its most ambitious project sought a way to survive the prophesied flood: researchers believed that harnessing Arkhium to defy gravity was the key, and planned to lift Fontaine into a "city in the sky". Since the disaster, leadership aims to stay solvent, restore order and keep the Arkhium ruins from exploding again.

Methods: Researchers prototype machines, kinetic cores and automatons and track hazards with Survey Anchors. The Arkhium project used an Experimental Field Generator, a huge device that creates a gravity-reduction field, powered by an Arkhium Kinetic Core with a suppression device. Edwin's Prototype Cal. Breguet clockwork meka belonged to this work. Unlike the Akademiya, the Institute does not administer or educate the people of Fontaine.

History: Alain Guillotin, who had been a member of the Narzissenkreuz Institute, a researcher at the Institute of Natural Philosophy and a Marechaussee Phantom hunter, founded the Institute. His inventions made it famous, and late in life he retired to his workshop, where he created Sandrone and Pulonia.

The Institute's crisis came when Edwin Eastinghouse's Arkhium experiment in the Central Laboratory overloaded. The explosion levelled most of the old Institute and sent blocks of anti-gravity water and remnants of the old ruins into the sky. The Callas Line aquabus route was shut down, and the Institute rebuilt at a new site near the ruins. Edwin was presumed dead.

Relations: Fontaine regards the Institute with mixed feelings: useful machines, poor accountability. Elphane finds its technicians' long-winded talk "ghastly", and Linorea holds a grudge over the Mekafish. It is separate from Sumeru's Akademiya. The Maison Gardiennage removed Edwin and Nacker to the Fortress of Meropide.

Reputation: Fontainians see the Institute as a source of both useful machines and disasters. Complaints include long-winded technicians, the Mekafish failure, the explosion and money worries. Engineer Anatole admits the incident "put the Institute on the map".

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Institute works from the New Fontaine Research Institute, still active but troubled. After Sandrone's death in Nod-Krai, her core was delivered to the Institute, and she has since reawakened in Fontaine.

The Institute is rebuilding under Raimondo and Choiseul, with financial problems, and Edwin and Nacker are in the Fortress of Meropide.

135.content: Alain Guillotin was the Institute's Founding Director, a prodigy raised at the Narzissenkreuz Institute who later researched at the Institute of Natural Philosophy and served in the Marechaussee Phantom with his sister Mary-Ann. He invented the Arkhe system and the Clockwork Meka. Legend says he retired to his workshop and published nothing. He created Sandrone and Pulonia before his death. His own entry holds the detail.

136.comment: Fontaine Research Institute: Edwin Eastinghouse and the Explosion
136.content: Edwin Eastinghouse was a Senior Technician and acknowledged genius who led the Arkhium project, building the Prototype Cal. Breguet meka and the Experimental Field Generator to lift Fontaine above the flood. He is dismissive of colleagues, treats lost researchers as replaceable and blames others for the explosion, saying he was inspecting other departments. After being found alive he was fired and sent to the Fortress of Meropide, where he still wants to research Arkhium.

137.content: Arkhium is a yellow, green and blue crystal and a potent energy source. Inert, it is stable; activated, it emits powerful pulses and can trigger chain-explosive resonance in nearby crystals. An inhibitor can make activated Arkhium inert. Exposure makes most people ill, but the Traveler and Paimon resist it. It occurs naturally in parts of Fontaine such as the Geode Mine Shaft beneath the Fortress of Meropide.

138.content:
Forest Rangers (also: the Forest Rangers, Forest Watchers, Vanara): The Forest Rangers are Sumeru's civil servants of the rainforest. They help travelers who are lost or in trouble, patrol the woods, watch the animals, and fight the spread of the Withering. Their main outpost is Gandharva Ville, "The City Above the Forest", in Avidya Forest. Higher-ranking members are called Forest Watchers and wear lighter green clothes. Tighnari is the Chief Officer, and Collei is an official ranger.

The Rangers are a public service, not a military unit. Shirin, their doctor, calls bows a common choice for hunting and for defence against monsters.

Structure: Two grades are seen: ordinary Forest Rangers and the higher-ranking Forest Watchers. Specialist roles include a doctor, a logistics chef and a search-and-rescue dog trainer.

The wiki lists Tighnari (Chief Officer), Amir, Ashpazi, Rana and Shirin as Forest Watchers, and Iraj, Izad, Kamran, Nasrin and Collei as ordinary rangers. Gandharva Ville's NPC list calls Shirin a ranger, so her rank is not fully consistent.

Leadership: Tighnari is the Chief Officer of the Forest Rangers. He is an Avidya Forest Watcher and a botanist who graduated from Amurta.

His character stories say that he first arrived at Gandharva Ville as an ordinary member, fresh from Amurta and parted from the Akademiya. After he arrived the Rangers began to rely on him as a knowledgeable and active researcher, and he eventually got everyone to go back to calling him "Forest Watcher", "Master" or "Mr. Tighnari". He is stern and often lectures travelers on survival and the forest, which is why his Wilderness Survival Skills Lecture is well known.

Members: **Tighnari**: Forest Watcher and Chief Officer; mentor of Collei. **Collei**: a trainee when first seen, an official ranger since 6.6. **Rana**: Forest Watcher from Vimara Village. **Amir**: trains the search and rescue dogs. **Ashpazi**: logistics supervisor and "Master Chef". **Shirin**: the Rangers' doctor. **Izad**: liaison to Pardis Dhyai. **Sag**: forest-patrol hound, captain of the dog team.

Goals: Protect the rainforest and the people who pass through it.

Concretely the Rangers help travelers in need, suppress Withering Zones, monitor beast populations and preserve the ecosystem of Sumeru's rainforests. They also send regular reports on the state of Avidya Forest to the researchers at Pardis Dhyai, who supply ecological help such as seeds and nutrients in return. Tighnari lists his troubles as pollution in the forest, adventurers who cause problems and rescue dogs that play with his tail, and says he has no larger worries.

Methods: Rangers patrol on foot, record anomalies in patrol logs, give travelers practical advice, and use trained dogs to search for missing people. Rana tells the Traveler during Into the Woods that when a missing person is found they should be given something easy to digest. They keep the outpost supplied: Ashpazi hunts and cooks as part of his logistics duties, and the Rangers' food at the outpost is a subject Tighnari takes an interest in (he asked for a recipe to put on the Rangers' menu).

Relations: The Rangers work with Pardis Dhyai's Amurta researchers on conservation. Tighnari's Amurta training links the Rangers to the Akademiya's scholars. They also treat the Aranara kindly: Rana befriended Arana as a child, and the quest series reveals their friendship. The Eremites around Gandharva Ville include a few mercenaries, and a group of Eremites under Tashfin attacked the Traveler there in 3.1, but they were mercenaries hired by an anonymous client, whom Paimon connects with the Doctor, and not part of the Rangers. Kamran says the Bimarstan advises Collei to rest despite her work.

Reputation: Travelers are told to flag down a Forest Ranger if anything happens. The Rangers are known for patient, practical help, and for Tighnari's lectures. Merchants bow to the diminutive Forest Watcher Tighnari, which amuses the rangers, according to his character stories.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Forest Rangers still patrol Avidya Forest from Gandharva Ville. Collei is an official ranger, and Tighnari remains their Chief Officer.

In the 6.6 Archon Quest Your Past Is Like a Garden, Naphis tells Collei she has finally become a full-fledged ranger, and Cyrus congratulates her on no longer being a trainee. Collei wrote to Sucrose that she is now an official Forest Ranger. Cyno introduced her to the party as the "official" ranger.

139.content: Tighnari is the Chief Officer of the Forest Rangers and a Forest Watcher at Gandharva Ville. His own entry carries his biography. In the context of the Rangers: he arrived as an Amurta graduate who had left the Akademiya, became the one the others looked to, runs training courses and raised funds through a dried-flower scheme with city flower sellers.

140.comment: Forest Rangers: Collei and the Rangers
140.content: Collei was a Trainee Forest Ranger when she first appeared, and said that her years in the wilderness made the work a natural fit for her. In the 6.6 Archon Quest Your Past Is Like a Garden she is promoted to an official ranger, with Naphis and Cyrus congratulating her. Kamran remarks that she was allowed to join only because the forest eased her Eleazar.

141.content: Gandharva Ville is the Rangers' main outpost in Avidya Forest, called "The City Above the Forest". Travelers, merchants and adventurers often stop there. Rangers, a few Vanara, researchers, Eremite mercenaries and traveling merchants share the village. Official map text says the remnants of the "kingdom of lost dreams" lie atop the tree. The location's own entry carries geography.

142.comment: Forest Rangers: Amir and the search dogs
142.content: Amir is the Forest Watcher who trains the Rangers' search and rescue dogs. Sag, a forest-patrol hound he considers his best student, is captain of the dog team. Travelers who cannot find a ranger can ask Sag for help.

143.content: Suppressing Withering Zones is one of the Rangers' core duties. They log pollution in the forest, and Rana mentions them in connection with monsters and unusually aggressive wildlife. Exposure to the Withering can make a person severely ill, as happened to Rana. Cure and cause belong to the lore of the Withering, not to this entry.

144.content: Pardis Dhyai is the Amurta research station near Avidya Forest. The Rangers send it regular reports on the forest, and its researchers send seeds, nutrients and other ecological help. Izad is the Ranger who handles this liaison, and he says the Rangers choose planting areas and distribute seeds to nearby villagers.

145.content:
Four Winds (also: the Four Winds, Four Wind Guardians, Wolf of the North, Lion of the South, Dragon of the East, Falcon of the West, Lionfang Knight, Dandelion Knight): The Four Winds are four guardians of Mondstadt: the Wolf of the North, the Lion of the South, the Dragon of the East and the Falcon of the West. The Anemo Archon Barbatos entrusted them with the city's safety before he vanished a thousand years ago. Mondstadt once worshipped them and built temples to them. Today the worship has faded, and the titles live on mainly through the Knights of Favonius, the wolf spirit Boreas and the dragon Dvalin.

They are a tradition rather than an organisation. There is no headquarters or roster, and who bears each title is a matter of old ballads, weapon lore and a few quest lines that do not always agree.

Structure: Each wind holds one compass direction and a symbol on a side of Mondstadt City. Per the wiki's trivia: the Lion above the main gate (south), the Wolf on the stairs up to the cathedral (north), the Dragon over the side entrance (east) and the Falcon on both sides of the Knights' headquarters entrance (west). The order's name, Favonius, is the Roman name for the west wind. Each wind had a temple, though only the Wolf, Lion and Falcon temples exist as ruins the Traveler can visit.

Members: - **Wolf of the North:** Boreas (Andrius), the great wolf king whose spirit dwells in Wolvendom, and the human Knight of Boreas he recognises. Known Knights of Boreas are a nameless wandering knight, Ravenwood, Rostam and now Varka, the Grand Master. Roland was named a candidate but never granted the title.
- **Lion of the South:** the Dandelion (Lionfang) Knight. Past holders include Vennessa, Arundolyn and Valentine; Jean holds it as of 7.1.
- **Dragon of the East:** Dvalin, the Wind Dragon, called Stormterror when Mondstadt feared him.
- **Falcon of the West:** most commonly Vennessa, said to have taken the title after her ascension, or symbolically the whole Knights of Favonius. This is disputed.

Goals: Barbatos charged the Winds with guarding Mondstadt and its people. In the ballads, the Wind Dragon is the one shown acting on that charge, fighting the corrupted dragon Durin at the height of the cataclysm as the city's last defender.

History: The wiki dates the formal establishment of the Four Winds to after Vennessa's rebellion against the aristocracy about 1,000 years ago, when Barbatos entrusted Mondstadt's safety to them before he disappeared. The Dragon Tome adds that Dvalin predated the others: the ballads say Barbatos befriended him and taught him to speak, so he is regarded as one of the oldest guardians and the longest worshipped. For roughly five hundred years people worshipped the Winds and built temples to them.

During the cataclysm five hundred years ago, Dvalin was badly wounded fighting Durin and slept for centuries. Afterward worship declined, the temples were abandoned and most people forgot the Winds. When Dvalin woke he believed Mondstadt had abandoned him, turned on the city and was called Stormterror, until the Traveler, Venti and their allies freed him from the Abyss Order's manipulation during the Prologue.

Relations: Barbatos is the one who set them in place, and Venti, who is Barbatos, still treats the Winds as his own. Dvalin is the Wind with the best-attested personal friendship with him. The Knights of Favonius inherited the Lion and Wolf titles through their Grand Master and the Knight of Boreas, so the order is the Winds' most active human heir. Dahlia, Barbatos' herald, serves the same god.

Reputation: Mondstadt remembers the Winds only dimly. Most people treat them as folklore. Dandelion seeds on the wind are said in the Temple of the Lion's text to be the Lion's blessing. After the Stormterror crisis the people of Mondstadt resumed their belief in Dvalin, and the Winds' symbols still mark the city. The ballad collections that tell their stories were compiled by scholars from bard songs, and the book itself warns that bards embellish history.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Four Winds are a fading tradition. Dvalin is again regarded as a guardian of Mondstadt; Boreas's spirit is in Wolvendom; Jean is Acting Grand Master and holds the Lion title; Varka is Grand Master and the Knight of Boreas. The Falcon is disputed.

No change to the Winds as a concept was found in the 6.x Nod-Krai or 7.0 to 7.1 Snezhnaya material checked. The wiki's holder list rests on a HoYoLAB anecdote about Varka.

146.comment: Four Winds: Wolf of the North
146.content: The Wolf of the North is both Boreas, the wolf king also called Andrius who now rests as a spirit in Wolvendom, and the Knight of Boreas, a human recognised by him. The Temple of the Wolf near the Thousand Winds Temple in Starfell Valley was originally a training ground and is now a monster-infested ruin. Known Knights of Boreas: the nameless wandering knight (original wielder of Wolf's Gravestone), Ravenwood, Rostam and Varka. Roland was a candidate who never received the title.

147.comment: Four Winds: Lion of the South
147.content: The Lion is handed down among the Grand Masters and Acting Grand Masters of the Knights of Favonius as the Dandelion or Lionfang Knight. The Temple of the Lion lies in Falcon Coast in Galesong Hill; dandelions riding the wind are said to be the Lion's blessing. Vennessa, Arundolyn, Valentine and now Jean are listed holders. The Lion symbol is above Mondstadt City's main gate.

key: East Temple of the Four Winds
148.comment: Four Winds: Dragon of the East
148.content: Dvalin is one of Barbatos' oldest friends among the Winds and has been worshipped the longest. Ballads say Barbatos won the people's trust for him and taught him human speech. Wounded by Durin in the cataclysm, he slept for centuries, woke to a city that feared him and was called Stormterror, and in A Long Shot said he was no longer part of the Four Winds. After the Prologue Mondstadt resumed believing in him. His temple does not exist as a visitable site.

149.comment: Four Winds: Falcon of the West
149.content: The most uncertain of the Winds. Common belief says Vennessa became the Falcon on ascending to Celestia, and the wiki reads Dainsleif's cryptic line the same way. Breeze Amidst the Forest suggests instead that the whole Knights of Favonius is the Falcon, which the book calls debatable. The Temple of the Falcon is at Windrise in Galesong Hill, between Mondstadt City and the oak where Vennessa is said to have ascended. The Falcon symbol flanks the entrance to the Knights' headquarters. The English name uses falcon, but the emblem looks like an eagle, which may be a translation quirk.

150.content:
Frostmoon Scions (also: Moonchildren, Frostmoon Scion, Scions of the Frost Moon): The Frostmoon Scions, also called the Moonchildren, are an indigenous people of Nod-Krai descended from the fallen golden realm of Hyperborea. Their home is the Frostmoon Enclave on Hiisi Island. For centuries they have worshipped the Goddess of the Frost Moon, and in particular the Moon Maiden Kuutar, who was later revealed to be the former Fatui Harbinger Columbina. They are led by the Moonchanter Lauma. They are known for antlered crowns, silver blood, a gift for speaking with animals, vegetarian food, charity and deep suspicion of outsiders who threaten them.

To most of modern Nod-Krai they seem ancient and set in their ways. They believe the wintry woods shelter them and that the full moon's light can cure every ill, and for generations they prayed to a goddess who never answered.

Leadership: Lauma, the Moonchanter, is the spiritual leader, healer and voice of the Scions. She was chosen for the role at birth because she was born with an antler crown, silver blood and an extraordinary sensitivity to moonlight. Her people bring her every question, and senior members salute her as she passes.

The title of Moonchanter dates from about 500 years ago, when Aila became the first to hold it. Before that the Scions were led by Archpriests or Archpriestesses who ran Hyperborea's ancient rites. Lovia was the last of them, and her name has been struck from the record.

Structure: The Moonchanter leads. Below her, in descending order, are:
- **Priestesses**, who carry more responsibilities.
- **Acolytes**, who must first pass an exam on hymns and blessings.
- **Adherents**, the ordinary followers.

Men of the tribe cannot become acolytes or priestesses. One Scion grumbled about this while hauling heavy festival decorations.

Goals: For generations the Scions' goal was faith itself: to honour the Moon Goddess, keep the old blessings alive and wait for a prophecy that the goddess would return. Under Lauma, especially since 6.0, the aim has shifted. In her words they are learning to thrive on their own, without relying on the Moon Goddess, and to make their home a better place to live. Lauma still defends their people: when the Fatui delivered their ultimatum she answered that the Scions would never hand anything over, and that with intruders' blood they would "draw an inviolable line in the snow".

Methods: Aila's reform turned the Scions toward benevolence and faith, and they avoid conflict with outsiders where they can. They hand out food in Nasha Town, even to Fatui soldiers who sneer at them. Lauma warned such soldiers that kindness is "the first lantern" left for those who stumble in ignorance, but those who still refuse the moonlit path will be shown its shadow by frosted blades. They eat no meat and live on spring water, fruit and vegetables.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Scions still live in the Frostmoon Enclave under Lauma. Columbina lives among them as herself, not as a goddess to be petitioned. Older Scions still bow and keep their distance from her, but the children are curious.

After the 6.0 revelation some members left. Those who stayed have joined the League and are trying to stand on their own. Lauma holds the Eternal Moon Marrow. In a 6.3 world quest the Scions refurbished a statue of Columbina, adding wings, and Lauma invited her to a feast. No new Frostmoon Scions story was found in the 7.0-7.1 Snezhnaya Archon Quests. In 7.0 Columbina appears only to see the Traveler off from Nod-Krai.

151.comment: Frostmoon Scions: Sacred bloodline and antler crowns
151.content: The Scions treat their Hyperborean bloodline as sacred. Its marks are silver blood, sensitivity to kuuvahki, antler crowns (said to be the Frost Moon's last gift to the Hyperboreans) and an ability to communicate with all living things. Antlers grow under moonlight. Lauma's sensitivity is said to occur only once a century, and her silver blood can be mixed into medicine. The Sacred Heir Project was an old plan to keep the bloodline pure so that a prophesied heir would revive Hyperborea. After the fall, the Hyperborean genetic methods were lost, so it relied on controlled family lines. It was meant to be wound down by the seventh generation to avoid inbreeding, but later priestesses only intensified it.

152.comment: Frostmoon Scions: Kuutar, the Moon Maiden
152.content: Kuutar is the Scions' name for the moon goddess born on Hiisi Island 400-500 years ago, whom they hailed as the successor of the Frost Moon. They carved Statues of the New Moon in her likeness across Nod-Krai. Their constant, demanding prayers drove her away. She joined the Fatui as Columbina, the Damselette, and centuries later returned to hide on Hiisi Island. She has said that while she lived among the Scions, people went solemn and stiff whenever she appeared. Since 6.3 she has lived among them by choice. On one visit to the Enclave with the Traveler, she noticed that the Scions' greeting had changed to "May the moonlight connect us" and was glad that they had changed.

153.content: Moonchanter is the title of the Frostmoon Scions' leader, created by Aila about 500 years ago to replace the Archpriest office. It is held now by Lauma, who was chosen at birth. The Moonchanter leads prayer and the community, heals, keeps the Moon Marrow and reads the true past with it. When the bloodline was stronger, one Moonchanter even sheltered the Moon Marrow inside her own body, though she could endure it for only two days. Lauma believed she could last five at most.

154.content:
Fruity Order (also: the Fruity Order, Order of the Fruit, Five Great Operatives): The Fruity Order is a Treasure Hoarder group that operates in Fontaine and Nod-Krai. It is run by an unnamed boss, with Five Great Operatives who carry fruit and plant codenames, and several dozen other members. Betrayal is punishable by death. Its members claim the order exists to keep order and balance in the world. They are more eccentric than most Treasure Hoarders.

Only three of the Five Great Operatives remain: "Guileless Wolfhook", "Ruthless Calla Lily" and "Trendy Zaytun Peach". "Tricky Bulle Fruit" and "Intrepid Valberry" have left.

Structure: At the top is the boss, unnamed. Beneath the boss are the Five Great Operatives: Zaytun Peach, Bulle Fruit, Wolfhook, Valberry and Calla Lily, each with a title (Trendy, Tricky, Guileless, Intrepid, Ruthless). Below them are several dozen ordinary members. The order belongs to the wider Treasure Hoarders.

Members: - **"Guileless Wolfhook"**, **"Ruthless Calla Lily"** and **"Trendy Zaytun Peach"**: the remaining operatives. Peach loves trendy slang, mocks outdated ideas ("Ley Lines are outdated") and hands out new names to people, such as calling Paimon the "Trendy Flyer". Wolfhook is polite and friendly while accepting majority votes against his own side, saying "This is how the world works". Calla Lily fights the Traveler in Villains and is the one who speaks for the order in the 6.5 event.
- **"Tricky Bulle Fruit"**: left the order after the Villains quest. He keeps a younger sister, Blanche, and is later found in the Fortress of Meropide.
- **"Intrepid Valberry"**: expelled or left earlier, then joined a different group.
- **Lakkaberry**: a fan who is not a member (see below).

Goals: The order says it exists to keep order and balance. In practice the quests show the members pursuing valuable potion formulas and pursuing those they see as traitors.

Methods: Theft, threats and intimidation. Members use slang and rank titles, settled one dispute in Villains by a vote, and treat betrayal as a capital offence. They hunted Bulle Fruit as a traitor over a potion formula, as seen in Villains. They have won the Treasure Hoarder booth at the Nod-Krai Trade Expo several years running, and in the latest expo they removed rival groups before they could cause trouble for a lookalike.

History: In Villains (4.1) the Traveler and Paimon meet Blanche, who is being threatened by Zaytun Peach and Wolfhook over her brother, Bulle Fruit, whom they call a traitor for keeping the "Pure Water" potion formula to himself. The Traveler helps Blanche and Bulle Fruit, and repels Calla Lily, who has come for him. By the end Bulle Fruit has left the order and later appears in the Fortress of Meropide. The Red and the Black (4.2) then shows Valberry's diary, which says he left the order and joined another group, the Elegant Tableware Confrerie, whose boss later fired him. In the follow-up Questions and Answers, Valberry is an NPC. In the Nod-Krai content, the Problem-Sorting Robot quest has the order steal "Curve"'s core from the Fatui and hide it in an Aino prospector robot, leading to Curve's rebuilding as Chard Lombro. The wiki infers that Wolfhook, Calla Lily and Zaytun Peach did this.

Relations: - **Treasure Hoarders**: it belongs to this wider group of thieves, but behaves as a distinct organisation with its own codenames and rules.
- **Fatui**: the order took Curve's core from them, according to the wiki's reading of the Problem-Sorting Robot quest.
- **Voynich Guild and the Nod-Krai Trade Expo**: the Guild's rules forbid trouble at the expo, and Calla Lily says so in her dealings with the organisers.
- **Traveler**: met Wolfhook, Zaytun Peach, Bulle Fruit and Calla Lily in Villains.

Reputation: Calla Lily says the order has proven untouchable so far, and a fan such as Lakkaberry wants to join it. The Curatorium of Secrets suspects the group may be outsiders to the area.

Secrets: The identity of the boss is not known. Calla Lily's pursuit of Bulle Fruit is explained by Valberry's diary as an order from "higher-ups".

Status as of 7.1: Active but diminished: three of five operatives remain, and the boss is unnamed.

As of the 6.5 event Calla Lily was still acting on the order's behalf in Nod-Krai. No Fruity Order content was found for 6.7 to 7.1.

155.content: The Five Great Operatives of the Fruity Order are known by a title and a fruit or plant name. Guileless Wolfhook is the soft-spoken one who supports majority votes. Ruthless Calla Lily fights in Villains and later speaks for the order at the expo. Trendy Zaytun Peach is the slang-loving one. Tricky Bulle Fruit held the "Pure Water" formula, left the order and is later found in Meropide. Intrepid Valberry was removed from the order and later worked for a different group.

156.content: Lakkaberry is an enthusiast in the 6.5 event Where Waves Meet the Reef who admires the Fruity Order and applied for an expo booth in its name. He is not a member. The order's real operative Calla Lily appears, tells him to meet her at the Nasha Town harbour after the expo. She says the order itself dealt with the rival Treasure Hoarders angered by his stunt.

157.content:
Garde (also: Gardes, Fontaine Gardes, Garde officers, Captain of the Gardes): The Gardes are the uniformed security officers of Fontaine's Maison Gardiennage, the nation's law enforcement service. They patrol the Court of Fontaine, handle everyday public order, and share the patrol work with Gardemek meka. Their captain is Grosrochard. They are the standard-issue face of the law, as opposed to the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol or the Marechaussee Phantom.

Gardes are ordinary civil servants. The open world shows them chatting in cafes, grumbling about assignments and retiring to a quiet life. In other Fontaine entries they are mostly background: someone who arrests, escorts or guards on behalf of the Maison Gardiennage.

Structure: The Gardes are one department of the Maison Gardiennage, listed with the Gardemeks, the Guard Poodle, the Marechaussee Phantom and the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol. A Captain heads them, currently Grosrochard. The Gardes and their Gardemeks make up the service's main force. The Special Patrol and the Marechaussee Phantom are its two special branches. The Special Patrol, led by Chevreuse, handles violent criminals whom ordinary Gardes would struggle with. The Phantom does investigation and answers directly to the Chief Justice.

Leadership: Grosrochard is the Captain of the Gardes. He is only ever mentioned: in Chevreuse's introduction he is the superior who wrote to her for the ninth time, asking her to be pickier about who joins the Special Patrol.

After the Traveler's part in the Roses and Muskets event, Grosrochard and Chevreuse both took to calling the Traveler "Proto-Boss". Turenna presents their joint assessment as the highest acknowledgment of both the Special Patrol and the Gardes. Garde Edler repeats the nickname and can quote his advice from memory.

Members: Named Gardes are few and come mostly from open-world conversations.
- Santallier: a patrolling Garde at the Quartier Lyonnais, who says he asked his superiors not to patrol that block, since the safest area in town sits across from the Champion Duelists' office, and was told that only he could take the task.
- Nolette: a retired Garde near the Vasari Passage, still proud of being a former officer of the Palais Mermonia, and regretful about failing to catch a pickpocket.
- Thurel: a retired Garde near the Fountain of Lucine, who later served in the Special Patrol and briefly at the Fortress of Meropide, and says their memory is fading.

Goals: Keep Fontaine's streets safe: patrol the Court of Fontaine, respond when citizens call for help, guard places and prisoners on behalf of the Maison Gardiennage, and hand serious investigation to the Phantom and violent cases to the Special Patrol. Gardemeks share this work, and Fontainians treat them as reliable helpers.

Methods: Gardes patrol on foot and with Gardemeks, which are pre-programmed to complete the tasks assigned to them. A Garde works with them rather than controlling them. Each Gardemek has a serial number for accountability, and a shout for help is said to bring a nearby Gardemek at once. The Maison keeps records of civil cases and transports and punishes hostages, and Gardes carry out such duties. For training it uses a standard-issue wargame.

Relations: The Gardes belong to the Maison Gardiennage. The Special Patrol and the Marechaussee Phantom sit alongside them in the same service. The Steambird newspaper uses the Maison's intelligence for its bounties.

Reputation: Fontaine's citizens regard the public security as "top-notch", as an Aquabus passenger puts it, and treat Gardemeks as dependable helpers. Individual Gardes are shown as dutiful but human: tired, nostalgic or complaining about assignments.

Secrets: Vaughn, a Garde, secretly served Marcel's organisation and planted Primordial Sea water as false evidence against Lyney. That is the only established case of infiltration of the Gardes.

Status as of 7.1: Active as of 7.1. The Gardes keep Fontaine's public order under Captain Grosrochard.

Nothing in the 6.x or 7.0-7.1 stories changes the Gardes' standing. Their latest appearances are limited-time events.

158.content: Edler is a Maison Gardiennage agent who appears only in limited-time events, among them Tracing Vanishing Trails (5.8) and the Moonlit Patrol Exercise (6.3), where she is in Nod-Krai with an improved version of the Maison's standard-issue wargame. She respects Captain Grosrochard, calls the Traveler "Proto-Boss", and once mistook Wislawa for a kidnapper in Fontaine, afterwards telling her she was a kind-hearted merchant.

159.content: Grosrochard is the Captain of the Gardes. Canon mentions him in Chevreuse's introduction, where he wrote to her for the ninth time to ask her to be more selective with Special Patrol recruits. He appears nowhere in person.

160.content: Vaughn was a Garde and secret accomplice of Marcel. During Lyney's trial he claimed the Gardes had found Primordial Sea water among Lyney's belongings, having planted it himself. After Neuvillette exposed him, he began to confess but was dissolved into water before naming his employer.

161.content:
Golden Troupe (also: Golden Troupe of Remuria, the Golden Troupe): The Golden Troupe was an order founded by Boethius, a Harmost of Remuria, from the survivors of the empire after its first fall. Its aim was to save Remuria and the Symphony (Phobos) so that music could unite the world in peace. It gathered in the Faded Castle, built music devices, studied spirit and fate, and used golems and sacrifice. It is long gone, but its remains lie under Petrichor in Fontaine.

Because its work is known only from ruins, items and later scholars' notes, the troupe is a historical faction: it is met through relics, not living members.

Leadership: Boethius, once one of Fontaine's greatest musicians and a Harmost of the God King Remus, gathered the remnants of Remuria into the troupe. The sources name no other officers.

Goals: The troupe wanted to save Phobos, the Symphony of Remuria, so that its power could unite the whole world and bring peace through music and the "Grand Symphony". Item text says Remuria's remnants never gave up their wish to rescue their waning civilisation and surpass fate.

Methods: Members met in the Faded Castle to study the spirit and fate, and built musical devices in imitation of Remuria's golden-age constructs, including autoharmonic music boxes that read scores. The troupe saw fate as a fixed script. By collecting and copying "cruel dramas" they produced what outsiders called magic. Its music was also used to record things, including magic, and conches carried information.

Status as of 7.1: The troupe no longer exists. Its remains are in Petrichor and the Faded Castle, and nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content was found that changes this.

Players meet it through the Faded Castle exploration in the Petrichor quests, the Ancient Autoharmonic Music Box, and the Golden Troupe artifact set.

162.content: A musician from a conquered island tribe, Boethius rose to be one of Remus's four Harmosts and a close friend of Cassiodor. He enforced Remus's orders against barbarians and Lochfolk, and when Remus relented he rallied Remuria's last armies, took the golden ichor and sealed the dragon Scylla. He was swept away with Remuria by the Symphony's tsunami, and the troupe was his attempt to continue Remuria's cause afterward. His full entry holds the details.

163.content:
Graffiti Alliance (also: the Alliance of graffiti artists, Natlan graffiti artists): The Graffiti Alliance is a group in Natlan that promotes the art and history of graffiti. Anyone can join, whatever their experience or style, and the Alliance gives new members free supplies and lessons. It is hundreds of years old and now has hundreds of members.

Members paint all over Natlan. The Alliance's headquarters is a plain-looking house at the Masters of the Night-Wind, but its members' works are not kept there. They are painted on cliffs, walls and houses across the region.

Structure: The Alliance is loose. There is no test or ceremony to join and no required meetings or duties. A new member is simply noted down by "Mural Maniac", the Guru-in-Chief, who manages the headquarters. Members are mostly out painting, and visit only to pay fees or ask for technical help. Dues are one thousand Mora per person each year, and members are expected to spread the word about the Alliance.

Leadership: "Mural Maniac" is the Guru-in-Chief and runs the headquarters. "Dopey Dazzler" is a mainstay who promotes a philosophy of avant-garde art. Neither has a stated real name; Dopey Dazzler says titles matter more than real names to graffiti artists.

Members: Known members are "Mural Maniac" (Guru-in-Chief), "Dopey Dazzler" and Yolo. Mural Maniac says anyone in Natlan holding a spray can and a paint bucket is probably a member. Yolo is also affiliated with the Collective of Plenty.

Goals: The Alliance teaches and spreads graffiti across Natlan. Some members, such as Dopey Dazzler, want to advance graffiti as a whole through "avant-garde" thinking, first in Natlan and then in the rest of the world.

Methods: The Alliance funds supplies and free lessons from yearly dues. Dopey Dazzler's advice is to study Natlan's landscape and customs to find the shape and colour of emotions, and her notebook says bold lines and vivid, bright colours are the key to eye-catching graffiti. Members mix pigments from local minerals, petals and saurian scales, according to Yolo.

History: The Alliance was established a few centuries ago, possibly by someone from the Masters of the Night-Wind. Outsiders told the Alliance that art elsewhere prized heritage, and a master then introduced the dues system. The fees have not changed for hundreds of years.

Relations: The Alliance's headquarters sits at the Masters of the Night-Wind. Its members admire the Scions of the Canopy's skill at heights. Dopey Dazzler treats the Adventurers' Guild as a model.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Alliance is active, with a headquarters and a couple of hundred members, and has money worries.

Following the end of the Natlan crisis, Mural Maniac says the Alliance has been expanding and recruiting artists from all over the world (limited-time event dialogue in 6.2). No later developments were found for 6.3-7.1; the 7.0-7.1 Archon Quests take place in Snezhnaya.

164.content: "Mural Maniac" is the Graffiti Alliance's Guru-in-Chief and an open-world NPC at the Masters of the Night-Wind. Mural Maniac welcomes visitors, admits anyone interested in graffiti on the spot, and worries about money because membership grew faster than the yearly dues can support. Mural Maniac considers taking portrait commissions to raise funds. In the limited-time event Soulblazers' Snowbound Journey, Mural Maniac appears in Mondstadt to scout locations for graffiti, and credits Mika with saving them on Dragonspine. Pronouns and age are not stated in the sources checked.

165.content: "Dopey Dazzler" is a graffiti artist and Graffiti Alliance mainstay who hosts the Traces of Artistry event in Natlan (5.0). She invites the Traveler and Paimon to travel to find inspiration, and preaches avant-garde art. She says the nickname came from a friend who praised her colour combinations while others laughed that she gets dopey blending paint, and that her real name is less important than her title.

166.content: Yolo is a member of the Graffiti Alliance and the Collective of Plenty who paints at the Alliance's gallery. Yolo says every piece of graffiti has a soul, and that long ago a group of mystics could infuse paint with the power of the Wayob to protect Natlan from calamities. Today the "soul" comes from pigments made of different minerals, petals and saurian scales.

167.content:
Grand Alliance (also: the Grand Alliance, seven-tribe alliance): The Grand Alliance was the coalition of Natlan's seven tribes, created to build the new nation of Ochkanatlan under Och-Kan, the Sacred Lord. It began as an agreement between autonomous groups, but Och-Kan, growing obsessive, gathered the tribes' authority into his own hands. The Alliance ended in a civil war: by the wiki's reading, six tribes rose with the Scarlet-Eyed Youth and the seventh stood with Och-Kan. It is a historical organisation, long gone by the present day.

It is known mostly through relics: Och-Kan's notes in the ruins of Ochkanatlan, and the texts on weapons belonging to its officers and rebels.

Structure: Seven tribes joined as autonomous groups. Their leaders handed over authority, and Och-Kan acted as the Alliance's single ruler. Known offices include the Ordnance Officer (held by Yupanqui) and the Recording Officer (Amoxcihuatl). The tribes also supplied labour: Och-Kan's notes describe requisitioning one laborer from every ten households for waterworks under his city.

Leadership: Och-Kan led the Alliance as the Sacred Lord, also called the Holy Sovereign. He took the reins after Xbalanque, the first Pyro Archon, entered the Sacred Flame. He held that Xbalanque alone deserved the title of god and that no other ruler should arise. Details of his rule and fall belong to his own entry.

Members: Known members and figures tied to the Alliance:
- Yupanqui: Ordnance Officer, who later joined the Scarlet-Eyed Youth against Och-Kan.
- Amoxcihuatl: Recording Officer.
- Ixquieh and Ahpub: twin chiefs of the Nanatzcayan and Teteocan.
- Lianca: First Speaker of the Flower-Feather Clan.
- Uenuku: left the Alliance with his Oceanid followers.

Goals: The Alliance was created to build Ochkanatlan, a new nation for the human tribes. Under Och-Kan the aim hardened into making humanity safe from "all that is beyond human comprehension", dragons and the Night Kingdom alike.

History: After Xbalanque entered the Sacred Flame, the seven tribes formed the Alliance and placed authority in Och-Kan's hands. The tribes' consent frayed as the Sacred Lord grew more suspicious. The Alliance ended in a civil war in which the Scarlet-Eyed Youth gathered heroes against Och-Kan and his city fell. (That the seventh tribe sided with Och-Kan is the wiki's reading, not a direct statement.)

Relations: - **Ochkanatlan**: the city the Alliance built, and its seat.
- **The Scarlet-Eyed Youth**: led the revolt of the six tribes.
- **Muratans**: by the wiki's account, the wandering branch of the seventh tribe, who later settled in Mondstadt; Vennessa is their representative in history.
- **Dragons and Saurians**: persecuted during Och-Kan's rule. The Youth was among those sympathetic to the Saurians.

Status as of 7.1: The Grand Alliance has been defunct since the civil war. As of 7.1 it appears only as ancient history.

168.content: The Holy Sovereign's Notes are Och-Kan's fragmentary writings in the Old Core of Chu'ulel and elsewhere in Ochkanatlan. They record his requisition of laborers from the tribes, the First Speaker's refusal, his fear that surviving dragons might regain their power, and his decision that there must be one ruler, one sovereign, one god. A later note shows that he saw himself as loyal to the Alliance to the end.

169.content:
Grand Narukami Shrine (also: Narukami Ooyashiro, the Grand Shrine): The Grand Narukami Shrine is Inazuma's chief religious organisation. It worships the Electro Archon and leads the faith of the Narukami people from the largest shrine in the nation, on the summit of Mt. Yougou on Narukami Island, beside the ever-blooming Sacred Sakura. Its head is the Guuji, Yae Miko, a kitsune who is also the Shogun's friend and the owner of Yae Publishing House. Its shrine maidens wear white and red.

The shrine's everyday work is receiving worshippers, handing out fortune slips and omamori, performing rituals and ceremonies, and protecting the Sacred Sakura and its offshoots, the Thunder Sakura. Use of military force is forbidden on its grounds, because it would dishonour the Shogun, so the shrine stands outside the Shogunate's armed jurisdiction while still serving the Electro Archon.

Leadership: Guuji Yae Miko leads the shrine. Worshippers and maidens call her "Lady Guuji" or "Lady Yae". She is solemn and mysterious in her ceremonial role and far more relaxed as head of her publishing house.

Miko says she never wanted to manage the shrine. The Kitsune Saiguu, her elder in the Hakushin line, persuaded her (partly by promising all the fried tofu she could eat) and then left on a "long trip" from which she never returned. The Guuji must attend every ceremony in full dress, which Miko finds the most tiresome part of the job.

Structure: Below the Guuji serve the shrine maidens. The Kuki Clan has supplied them for generations, and other old families such as the Inagi serve too. Newcomers start with simple tasks such as cleaning. Specific duties include greeting worshippers and handing out fortune slips, looking after particular people (Kano Nana is responsible for finding the Shuumatsuban ninja Sayu when she slips away), and being sent out on errands such as investigations. Toda acts as liaison between the shrine and the Yashiro Commission, handling fund-raising and manpower.

Members: - **Yae Miko**: Guuji and head of the shrine.
- **Miyuki**: a Kuki Clan shrine maiden, Kuki Shinobu's older sister. She is fiercely eager for Lady Yae's approval and a little jealous of Kano Nana.
- **Kano Nana**: shrine maiden, novel enthusiast and Miko's favourite at the shrine. She is Shikanoin Heizou's older distant cousin and is forever chasing Sayu.
- **Inagi Hotomi**: shrine maiden who greets worshippers coming for fortune slips. She descends from Inagi Misato, a shrine maiden who was the Kitsune Saiguu's friend 500 years ago.
- **Maki**: shrine maiden at the fortune-slip stall who explains the Sacred Sakura to visitors.
- **Enyashi Yukari**: a nervous newcomer who keeps the prayer-plaque area tidy.
- **Toda**: the Yashiro Commission liaison, usually found at the Kamisato Estate.
- **Gendou Ringo**: the curt maiden who hands out fortune slips. See the entry below for who she really is.

Goals: The shrine exists to serve and honour the Electro Archon, guide the people's worship, and keep the Sacred Sakura healthy, which in turn protects Inazuma from accumulated filth. Its maidens describe everything there as being done according to the Archon's will. Under Miko, the shrine also quietly works to protect Ei's path to Eternity and Inazuma's stability, sometimes in ways the Shogunate itself does not see.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the shrine is active and Yae Miko is still Guuji. With the Sakoku Decree gone, worshippers now come to give thanks and pray for business and safe journeys.

No new shrine storyline was found in the 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 (Snezhnaya) updates; Inazuma has no story content in those versions.

170.comment: Grand Narukami Shrine: Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual
170.content: The Sacred Sakura and its grafted offshoots, the Thunder Sakura, purify Inazuma by drawing filth into their roots. The roots are all connected, so filth flows toward the central roots beneath Mt. Yougou. It cannot dissipate on its own, so the Grand Narukami Shrine normally performs a Cleansing Ritual. Minor cleansings check the roots and set barriers that protect the roots from people and people from the filth. A major cleansing is due every 60 years. The barriers are broken with wards, the filth condenses into "defilement incarnate" (harmless in peaceful times, dangerous in troubled ones) and is destroyed, and finally the tumour at the central roots is purged. Records say that when the ritual once lapsed, centuries ago, monsters ran rampant and the seas turned black. The most recent major cleansing was done by the Traveler and Hanachirusato after Miko cancelled the shrine's own preparations.

171.content:
Guhua Clan (also: Guhua Brotherhood, Guhua Sect, Guhua School, Sect of Ancient Splendor): The Guhua Clan is a Liyue martial arts school that honours the wandering hero Guhua and teaches sword and spear. It was once famous across Liyue and beyond. Today only a few members remain, and its base, Wangshan Hall on Mt. Lingmeng, is falling apart. Xingqiu is its best-known member.

Its belief, as former member Chen the Sharp quotes it, is that the noblest martial virtue is to pursue what benefits other people. It was formerly called the Guhua Brotherhood and later the Guhua Sect.

Structure: There is no visible hierarchy beyond seniority and epithets. Members use titles such as Cloudpiercing Arrow (Huang the Third), Snowstriding Sword (Wen the Fourth) and Guhua Guru of Feiyun Fame (Xingqiu). Wangshan Hall is the headquarters and training ground. Visitors who ask for the master at the gate are told he is off in the mountains.

Leadership: No master is named in the present day. Guhua is honoured as founder and namesake but was never a master and never took a disciple. The actual founder was Boxuan, called Master Baixuan, a man Guhua had once favoured as a boy. After Guhua's death Baixuan founded the brotherhood in his name and called himself Guhua's disciple. Xingqiu is the clan's most celebrated talent: his profile says that when the clan's head read his verse on the Martial Principle, he wept and declared that it was the clan that needed Xingqiu, not the other way round.

Members: Members the Traveler can meet include Huang the Third and Wen the Fourth at Wangshan Hall, Sun Yu and Little Que'er at Huaguang Stone Forest (until Sun Yu leaves), and Xingqiu. Former members include Chen the Sharp, a grilled-fish vendor in Liyue Harbor, and Zhiruo, a waitress.

Huang the Third guards the gate and, hoping to raise Mora for repairs, lures visitors in Yilong Wharf into a paid tour of the hall with inflated claims. Wen the Fourth is a gloomy senior who worries about what happens to the clan's books when the last old members are gone. Wakamatsu is an Inazuman who slipped out during the Sakoku Decree, inspired by a martial tale, to seek training at the clan. The wiki lists him among current members, though his place is informal. After the Traveler opens Wangshan Hall's hidden chamber, he begs Wen the Fourth to take him as a disciple, and Wen tells him to start with the basics.

Goals: The stated aim of the remaining members is to restore the clan's former reputation, or at least to keep Wangshan Hall standing. Sun Yu had sought the adepti's advice on reviving the clan before concluding that this was going nowhere. Huang the Third and Wen the Fourth worry about leaving no successors.

Methods: The clan teaches the Three Guhua Greats: Light Piercer for polearms, Rain Cutter (Raincutter) for swords, and Life Ender for those who master both. Guhua is said to have worked them out at Lingmeng Chamber, now Wangshan Hall. New members start with the fundamentals, such as practising against wooden stakes. In its prime the clan travelled the world, doing justice with sword and spear.

History: Guhua was a peace-keeping martial nomad who trained at Lingmeng Chamber and never meant to start a school. After his death the boy he had once favoured, Boxuan or Master Baixuan, founded the Guhua Brotherhood. In its heyday it had a large following, and its members travelled Teyvat, known for sword and spear. Over the following centuries members deserted, and it went through several name changes, shrinking to the small Guhua Sect and then to today's Clan.

Relations: The clan has no formal alliances. Huang the Third drops his tour swindle when the Traveler threatens to report him to the Millelith. Xingqiu's family, the Feiyun Commerce Guild, is wealthy; his father let him learn martial arts from the clan to keep him out of the Wanwen Bookhouse for a day, knowing it was a declining art. The luxury dojo Xingqiu first trained in was not the clan's and had been rented to keep up appearances.

Reputation: In its heyday the clan's name rang like steel through Liyue Harbor. Now it is a faded name that many treat as a joke. Its members know it: Little Que'er calls it an archonforsaken martial arts club.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Guhua Clan is nearly extinct. A few members still keep Wangshan Hall, and no source shows a revival.

Sun Yu has left for Fontaine. Wen the Fourth and Huang the Third remain at the hall, the former with a possible new student in Wakamatsu. The clan's future is unknown.

172.comment: Guhua Clan: The Three Guhua Greats
172.content: The Three Guhua Greats are the clan's three secret arts: Light Piercer (spear), Rain Cutter (sword) and Life Ender (both together). Guhua is said to have worked them out at Lingmeng Chamber. Xingqiu's profile describes them as arts refined over the generations that waited for a worthy successor, and he was the one who grasped the Martial Principle.

173.comment: Guhua Clan: Wangshan Hall and Its Secret Chamber
173.content: Wangshan Hall on Mt. Lingmeng, in Chenyu Vale, is the clan's base. It is run down, and Huang the Third gives paid tours to raise money. Beneath the library the Traveler discovers a hidden chamber sealed by scrolls readable only with Elemental Sight, then trial areas and Guhua's inscriptions. Wen the Fourth says the hall was where Guhua was said to have reached enlightenment.

174.comment: Guhua Clan: Sun Yu and Little Que'er
174.content: Sun Yu and Little Que'er are two young Guhua disciples who grew up training together. Sun Yu wanted to revive the clan and sought the adepti's guidance near Huaguang Stone Forest. Que'er is hostile to strangers who approach him and has feelings for Sun Yu that he does not notice; he regards her as a sister. In the 3.3 commission series he gives up the search and decides to travel abroad. Que'er refuses to go and is left heartbroken, mistakenly believing he never cared for her.

175.comment: Guhua Clan: Huang the Third and Wen the Fourth
175.content: Huang the Third, the Cloudpiercing Arrow, is the cheerful swindler at Yilong Wharf who is fond of the hall and ashamed of what he must do to maintain it. Wen the Fourth, the Snowstriding Sword, is the gloomy senior who explains the clan's history. They talk like old comrades and tease each other about who was the better fighter a few years ago.

176.content:
Gunnhildr Clan (also: House Gunnhildr, Gunnhildr Family, the Gunnhildr Clan): The Gunnhildr Clan is Mondstadt's oldest family of knights. Its motto is "For Mondstadt, as always". Its roots go back to the priestess Gunnhildr, who stood with Barbatos against Decarabian, and the clan stayed loyal to the people through the age of the aristocracy. Many Knights of Favonius and Church clergy come from it. Jean is its best-known member today.

The clan was one of the founding houses of the aristocratic age, alongside the Lawrence and Imunlaukr clans, but unlike the Lawrences it never turned tyrant. When Vennessa rebelled, the Gunnhildrs sided with the people and were not exiled.

History: The clan traces itself to Gunnhildr, daughter of a nomadic clan leader who left Decarabian's city. She led her people alongside the wind spirit that became Barbatos and crowned him with laurels after Decarabian fell. In the aristocratic age the clan kept its oath to protect Mondstadt, and it sided with Vennessa's rebellion about 1,000 years ago.

**Decarabian's era.** The Biography of Gunnhildr says the clan's leader had served Decarabian and led his people out of the city rather than live under a despot. In the blizzards beyond the walls, his daughter Gunnhildr prayed, and a wind spirit heard her. The faith of her people let it build a small shelter and gave her the power to protect them. After her father died she became chief and the clan's first priestess. A shrine in the Thousand Winds Temple, where the clan prayed to Istaroth, is attested in weapon lore.

**After Decarabian.** When Barbatos won, the clan settled north in an old fortress. That land later became Dornman Port, and an NPC says the clan founded Mondstadt's first sanctuary of Barbatos there. Later, as the Church became a puppet of the nobility, the Gunnhildrs of the time threw the bishop sent from Mondstadt out of the sanctuary tower and tore it down, and the port has had no church since.

Structure: The clan is a family house of knights and clergy, not an organisation with ranks. Its identity is carried by its motto and its tradition of service. No head of the clan is named in canon. A cadet branch, the Dornmannshaven family, uses the motto "Sail Toward Freedom".

Members: Jean Gunnhildr, Master of the Knights of Favonius, is the clan's heir and public face. Her mother is Frederica Gunnhildr, the Alder Knight. Her younger sister Barbara Pegg was born into the clan but left with their father, Seamus Pegg.

Jean was raised by Frederica, with a strict regime, to succeed her as the clan's heir. Her profile says a Gunnhildr learns to say the motto before saying "Mommy". Frederica is a captain and long-serving front-line commander. Seamus Pegg, a former adventurer, is the Church's Cardinal of Daybreak and Seneschal. The parents' marriage ended; Barbara joined the Church and became a deaconess. Eckhard Gunnhildr is a modern historian of the clan and the author of the Biography of Gunnhildr. Historical bearers of the name are the priestess Gunnhildr and the Knight of the Golden Bough.

Goals: The clan's only stated purpose is its oath to the Anemo Archon: to protect Mondstadt, its land and all its people. The motto sums this up.

Relations: - **Knights of Favonius and Church of Favonius**: the clan supplies many knights and clergy, and its members hold senior posts in both. Frederica and Jean are knights; Seamus and Barbara serve the Church.
- **Barbatos**: Gunnhildr crowned the new Anemo Archon, and the clan has served him since.
- **Lawrence Clan**: the Biography contrasts the Gunnhildrs with the scheming Lawrences. Eula, of the disgraced Lawrence line, serves under Jean's command today.
- **Ragnvindr Clan**: the other house known to have escaped exile.
- **Imunlaukr Clan**: the third founding house of the aristocracy, not mentioned in the present day.

Reputation: Gunnhildrs are seen as reliable and old-fashioned in the best sense. Jean is trusted across Mondstadt, and the Alder Knight is a heroine to the young. The weight of the name is also a burden: Jean's profile says the lineage can feel heavy.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the clan remains in service. Jean is Acting Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius.

Frederica went north with Varka's expedition as second-in-command, was later sent back to defend Dornman Port, and is now said to be on a secret mission known in detail only to Jean. No clan developments from 6.7 to 7.1 were found.

177.content: The Biography of Gunnhildr is a history of the clan's apical ancestor, compiled by Eckhard Gunnhildr, a modern Mondstadt historian, from fragments of aristocratic-age legend. A copy can be found in Dawn Winery. It tells the priestess Gunnhildr's story and ends by predicting that the clan will keep its duty to the Anemo Archon.

178.content: "For Mondstadt, as always" is the clan's motto. Jean links it to the sense of duty that made her give up childhood play, and her Vision story says she heard it in her mind when she received her Vision. The cadet Dornmannshaven branch has its own motto, "Sail Toward Freedom".

key: School of the Theory of Knowledge
179.content:
Haravatat (also: Haravatat Darshan, School of Semiotics, School of the Theory of Knowledge, Darshan of Semiotics): Haravatat is the Sumeru Akademiya's school of semiotics, the study of signs, meaning and language. It covers linguistics, ancient runes and the translation of old texts. Its colour is black, its crest shows a bull, and it is led by Sage Rushd. It is the smallest Darshan by enrolment, but it has produced Alhaitham, the Akademiya's Scribe, and the veteran scholar Faruzan.

Haravatat sees language and writing as the core of the world. The Akademiya receptionist Sitt sums it up as deciphering ancient texts or creating new words. Because its focus includes ancient languages, the Darshan's work overlaps with Vahumana's study of history.

Structure: Haravatat is one of the Six Darshans, with one Great Sage at its head. Its disciplines include linguistics, ancient runes and syntax, as in Gregor's remark that his Haravatat classes spend their time on syntax and structure rather than literature. Members range from students and Driyosh to researchers and mentors.
