Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Hiiragi Chisato acts as head of the Hiiragi Clan and the Commission. Her father remains imprisoned.

The Commission's rules for foreigners are looser than during the Sakoku Decree, which Ei abolished after her duel against the Shogun in Transient Dreams. The wiki does not record a new commissioner. No Inazuman story was released in 5.8 to 7.1, so nothing found changes this picture.

235.comment: Kanjou Commission: Hiiragi Shinsuke and the Fatui plot
235.content: Hiiragi Shinsuke was head of the Hiiragi Clan and Kanjou Commissioner when the Traveler reached Ritou in 2.0. He seems friendly: he receives the Traveler as an honoured guest and invites them in. In truth the Fatui had enlisted him with promises of power and wealth, and he stockpiled Crystal Marrow for them. He met Signora and planned to keep the Traveler indefinitely stuck in Ritou so they would not interfere. His daughter Chisato overheard and helped the Traveler escape. After the plot was unravelled he was imprisoned and awaits the Shogun's punishment.

236.content: Chisato is Shinsuke's daughter and the acting head of the Hiiragi Clan. She lives at the Hiiragi Estate in Ritou. In 2.0 she asked the Traveler to deliver a private letter to Kujou Kamaji in exchange for helping them out of Ritou; the delivery earned the Traveler a Travel Permit from Kamaji. After her father's arrest she became a figurehead and, after the forged marriage plot in 2.6, took a firmer hand. She says that despite her worry, anyone who commits a wrong must answer for it.

237.content: The Outlander Affairs Agency in Ritou is the Kanjou Commission's office for documents and requests from non-Inazumans. During the Sakoku Decree it charged vast and arbitrary fees to stranded visitors. Yurika, the inspector, asked two million Mora from the Traveler before Thoma negotiated six hundred, and Thoma says this was normal. After the Commission was purged of corruption, the Agency became more lenient and charged only 500 Mora. Without a Travel Permit, outsiders could not leave Ritou, and Kanjou ashigaru would turn the Traveler back at the town's edge until Kamaji granted a permit.

238.content:
Khaenri'ahn Dynasties (also: Dark Sun Dynasty, Black Sun Dynasty, Blacksun Dynasty, Khaenriahn Dynasties): Khaenri'ah, the subterranean kingdom that fell in the cataclysm 500 years ago, had two known ruling dynasties. The older Crimson Moon Dynasty is known almost only through a legend. The later Eclipse Dynasty was the last, and its final king, the Vinster King Irmin, pursued Abyssal power until the kingdom collapsed. The later house's Chinese name means "Black Sun Dynasty", and the legend that describes the change speaks of a "dark sun" replacing the crimson moon.

The two are linked by blood and by grudge. Descendants of the Crimson Moon line still exist; Arlecchino of the Fatui is one. In the Eclipse era the crown hunted such descendants as potential rivals.

Structure: Canon gives no organisational chart for either house. The Eclipse Dynasty ruled through a king, a council of the kingdom's most respected figures and a royal court, with royal guards (the Black Serpent Knights) and a Universitas Magistrorum for research. Vedrfolnir and Hroptatyr were the most trusted members of Irmin's council. A Knight Marshal named Anfortas served under Irmin and took the regency afterwards. The Perinheri legend describes the Crimson Moon era as a realm under a "great ruler" (addressed as "high lord of the nobles"), with sages as advisers and an orphanage whose graduates later became knights; the book's footnotes call alchemy and the Beastmaster Knights the era's mainstays.

Leadership: No Crimson Moon ruler has a name in canon. The Eclipse Dynasty's last ruler was Irmin, the one-eyed Vinster King, who became the kingdom's undoing. See Irmin's own entry for his character; this entry covers the dynasty as an institution. After his fall, Knight Marshal Anfortas declared himself Regent while "unknown threats" faced the kingdom.

Members: Legend: the orphanage founded in the Crimson Moon era produced the knight Perinheri, and the foreign "princess" Angelica later joined it; Perinheri's rival Hleobrant came from the descendants of those who forsook their god. The legend's main events take place after the change of dynasty. Tholindis, a Universitas researcher in the Eclipse era, came from a minor branch distantly related to the main Crimson Moon line. Arlecchino carries the blood too, though she learned of it only after Pierro told her.

Goals: The Eclipse Dynasty's stated aim in All Is Foretold, through Rerir's work, was to protect itself by removing any possible rival. Irmin's own aims turned toward Abyssal power and the machinery of "secrets from beyond the skies". The Crimson Moon remnants in the same quest, such as Tholindis' ally Orlog, wanted the old dynasty restored. The Perinheri legend adds that a sage of the Crimson Moon era hoped for children from beyond the world, among them beings who could "transcend the gods", and the ruler told him to do as he pleased.

History: **Crimson Moon era.** Only the legend remains. In it a crimson moon shone over the underground realm, outside things leaked in from beyond the world, and a sage advised the ruler to prepare for a child who could surpass the gods. Later the crimson moon set and a dark sun took its place. That dark sun was the Eclipse Dynasty, and the book's notes place the change of rule probably around the Archon War.

**Eclipse era.** The Eclipse Dynasty ended with the cataclysm 500 years ago. Under Irmin the kingdom pursued Abyssal power. The Traveler's Sibling arrived and was named heir, Vedrfolnir was blinded for warning against Irmin's path, and Dainsleif's raid on the palace on his brother's behalf let the Five Sinners take the Abyssal power Irmin had drawn into the Sibling. The kingdom then fell, and the Heavenly Principles' response left the survivors cursed.

Relations: - **Court of Khaenri'ah**: the Eclipse Dynasty's royal court under Irmin, covered in its own entry.
- **Arlecchino**: a Crimson Moon descendant whose Balemoon Bloodfire draws on Abyssal energy and slowly corrupts her, so she uses it with great caution.
- **House of the Hearth**: Pierro hints that it began as the old orphanage of the legend, and that its later link to the Fatui could be his doing.

Status as of 7.1: Both dynasties are gone. Their legacy survives in the curse of the Khaenri'ahns, the Abyss Order and in Crimson Moon descendants such as Arlecchino.

As of 7.1 canon has not shown a revival of either house. Khaenri'ah itself is a ruin beneath Teyvat. The 6.x Nod-Krai Archon Quests revisit the Eclipse era through the memories of Five Sinners such as Rerir and Vedrfolnir, but show no restored dynasty.

239.content: The Crimson Moon Dynasty is Khaenri'ah's older ruling house, known chiefly through the legend Perinheri (also titled Hleobranto Innamorato). Under it, alchemy and Beastmaster Knights had their peak, and its sages founded an orphanage for children from other worlds, from which came many of the kingdom's best knights. The dynasty ended when a dark sun replaced the crimson moon. Its descendants carry the Balemoon Bloodfire, as Arlecchino does, a power that draws on Abyssal energy and corrupts its user. She was warned that if the corruption reached her heart she would become a different person.

240.content: The Eclipse Dynasty was Khaenri'ah's last ruling house, ending with King Irmin in the cataclysm 500 years ago. It favoured mechanical engineering and knowledge from beyond the sky over alchemy and the beast-masters, and later Abyssal power. Its royal guards, the Black Serpent Knights, included Dainsleif the Twilight Sword and Halfdan, and its research body was the Universitas Magistrorum. The Traveler's Sibling was adopted into the royal house as the heir. The dynasty's end brought the cataclysm and left the Khaenri'ahns cursed.

241.content:
King Deshret's Priests (also: Desert Priests, Hermanubis Priest, priests of King Deshret, Heirs of the Burning Sun): King Deshret's Priests, also called the Desert Priests, were the priesthood who served the god-king of Sumeru's desert in his ancient kingdom. They wore the same style of head ornament as their head, Hermanubis, the Greatest of Sages and one of the king's Seven Pillars. They guarded the king's knowledge, and when forbidden knowledge ravaged the land they built the temples that held it back. Canon says little about them directly. No priest is shown alive in the present, and most of what is known comes from ruins, relics and one dying priest's recorded memory.

Three threads survive: the priest Kasala's recording (Archon Quest, 3.1), Hermanubis' followers who founded the Temple of Silence, and flavour text about descendants who keep the old ceremonies. The wiki page for the group is a stub, so treat anything beyond these as unknown.

Structure: Canon gives no ranks or headcount. Hermanubis stood over all the other priests, and the priests wore a head ornament like his. The Gilded Dreams circlet, Shadow of the Sand King, is a gold-inlaid headband once used by desert priests in imitation of a legendary ruler's.

Leadership: Hermanubis was the guide of all the priests. Chosen from among the Tighnarians by King Deshret, he was a renowned sage and warrior known for being sincere, steady and kind.

Even his fellow Pillars respected him. After Deshret's death he led his followers to Tulaytullah. Kasala is the only other named priest; canon does not say he answered to Hermanubis directly. His own biography belongs in his separate entry.

Members: Only two members are named: Hermanubis as head, and Kasala as one of the last priests to serve under the king.

Kasala presided over a temple that later lay buried under the sands, and was entombed there. Other priests appear only anonymously in murals and slab records.

Goals: The priests served the god-king and his ideals of justice and abundance. When forbidden knowledge spread, their task became containment. Kasala's last words ask the children of the desert to drop old grievances and remember the kindness that saved them.

Methods: In the disaster the priests built temples at Greater Lord Rukkhadevata's summons, and she infused them with the divine power of life (Dendro). That tempered the damage. The wiki links these to the structures called the Towers of Betrayal. Kasala spent his life guarding one.

History: **The disaster.** In his grief over the Goddess of Flowers, Deshret exposed the land to knowledge that, in Kasala's words, did not belong to this world. It spread like a plague: crazed whispers, dark grey scales, a drained land. Rukkhadevata came from the forests and had the priests build her life-infused temples. The embers of the civilization survived in Aaru Village. Kasala says Deshret finally sacrificed himself, because the knowledge would blight the world as long as it existed, and that Rukkhadevata exhausted her strength and took the form of a small child.

**Kasala's end.** Kasala guarded a temple for the rest of his life and left a recorded memory there, found in "Secret of the Scorching Desert" (3.1) by Alhaitham, Cyno, Dehya, Candace, Rahman and the Traveler.

Relations: - **King Deshret**: the priests' lord. Kasala calls him "my eternal lord" and "the proud king of the desert".
- **Hermanubis**: their head, and the founder of the group's lasting successor, the Temple of Silence.
- **Greater Lord Rukkhadevata**: the Dendro Archon who directed the priests' temple-building. In Kasala's account she and Deshret were allies, not enemies.
- **Eremites**: a number of them believed Rukkhadevata had betrayed the king. Kasala's testimony contradicts that, which shook Rahman.
- **Akademiya**: scholars of the Akademiya hold a hollow body named the Temple of Silence. The real Temple, descended from Hermanubis' followers, works separately but has been rebuilding ties since the Oathkeeper quest.

Status as of 7.1: The priesthood no longer exists as such. Its heritage continues through the Temple of Silence, now led by Sethos, and through descendants who claim it.

No new material on the priests was found for 6.x or 7.0-7.1, which are set in Nod-Krai and Snezhnaya. The most recent mention is the limited-time Ruins Exploration event in 6.1.

242.content: Kasala was one of the last priests to serve King Deshret. After the king's sacrifice he continued to serve by guarding one of the temples built at Rukkhadevata's direction, in what is now called the Mysterious Ruins beneath the Mausoleum of King Deshret. He was entombed there. The party found his inscription and heard his last message in "Secret of the Scorching Desert". In it he warns that knowledge can destroy a civilization, describes the disaster, honours Rukkhadevata and Deshret, and urges the children of the desert to drop old grievances and hold on to the memory of her kindness. His voice narrates the cutscene known as Lost Legacies in the Sand.

243.content:
Knights of Favonius (also: Ordo Favonius, Favonius Knights, the Knights of Favonius): The Knights of Favonius are Mondstadt's order of knights, founded about 1,000 years ago by Vennessa, with Barbatos' help, so that aristocrats could never rule again. They guard the city and its roads, keep order, make and enforce the law, and help manage the Church of Favonius. In practice they are Mondstadt's government. Their headquarters is in Mondstadt City.

Nobody in the order was knighted by royalty. In Mondstadt, "knight" is a title earned through the duties a person takes on.

Leadership: Grand Master Varka, the Knight of Boreas, is a huge, cheerful, famously strong man who hates paperwork. Jean Gunnhildr, the Master and Dandelion Knight, has governed as Acting Grand Master since Varka left on a long expedition half a year before the Traveler arrived.

Boreas (Andrius) recognised Varka as the north wind's human champion, and Jean calls him "the legend of his generation". Jean was made Dandelion (Lionfang) Knight at fifteen and was promoted from captain to Master during the Eroch affair. Varka has told her that if he does not return, she is to succeed him and train the next Knight of Boreas. Officers the Traveler meets most often:
- Kaeya: Cavalry Captain and Quartermaster
- Albedo: Chief Alchemist and Investigation Captain
- Eula: Reconnaissance Captain
- Hertha: Logistics Captain and Coordinator
- Note and Skeiron: captains of the 2nd and 3rd Companies
- Lohen: Vice Captain of the Ranged Company
- Lisa: Librarian
- Amber: the last Outrider

Structure: A single Grand Master leads the order. The Master is the reserve and becomes Acting Grand Master whenever the Grand Master is away. Below them are ten Captains, each heading a numbered company; the companies can be disbanded and re-formed as needs change. Their specialties include general affairs, reconnaissance, ranged fire, logistics, technical support, cavalry and alchemical investigation. There are also special units such as the Outriders. Becoming a knight takes written and practical exams. Not every member is a knight: Sucrose is an Assistant Alchemist, and Noelle serves as the Knights' maid while she keeps trying to pass.

Goals: The Knights exist to protect Mondstadt and the freedom Vennessa won. That means keeping monsters, bandits and foreign schemes away from the people, upholding order fairly, and making sure no tyrant ever rules again. Under Varka they also strike at distant dangers, such as the Abyss in the north, before those dangers reach home.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the expedition has come home and Varka is back. He divides his time with the Favonius Keep in Nod-Krai, so Jean still runs daily affairs as Acting Grand Master.

A small garrison under Anselm holds the Keep, which also serves Nefer's Northern Intelligence Network as a post for watching Abyssal attacks. Seamus Pegg is back as Seneschal of the Church. The 5th Company's captaincy has been vacant since Adorno's death in 6.6, and Lohen remains Vice Captain. No new Knights of Favonius story developments were found for 6.7-7.1; the 7.0-7.1 Archon Quests take place in Snezhnaya.

key: Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius
244.comment: Knights of Favonius: Grand Master, Master and the knightly titles
244.content: The Knights have one Grand Master. The Master is the reserve who becomes Acting Grand Master when needed, which is why people call Jean both "Master Jean" and "Acting Grand Master". The Dandelion Knight, also called the Lionfang Knight, carries Vennessa's title. Jean has held it since she was fifteen, and it is linked to the "Lion of the South" among the Four Winds. Earlier holders were Vennessa, Arundolyn (the "Lion of Light") and Valentine. The Knight of Boreas is a human knight recognised by the wolf god Boreas, who acts as intermediary between the god and the people. Known holders are the Wandering Knight, Ravenwood, Rostam and now Varka, whom Boreas judged the rightful bearer of the title in this age. As Varka put it in a letter Mika read aloud, "There are ten captains in the Knights of Favonius but only one Grand Master."

245.comment: Knights of Favonius: Companies of the Knights of Favonius
245.content:
- **1st, General Affairs**: plans the economy, regulations and city management, and prefers to recruit knights injured in front-line service. Its captain is unnamed.
- **2nd**: captained by Note. It is apparently the Garrison, with Wernher as Disciplinary Officer.
- **3rd**: captained by Skeiron. It is apparently the Vanguard, the largest company, responsible for the front lines, discipline and coordination between arms.
- **4th, Reconnaissance**: led by Captain Eula. It patrols the wilds, Dornman Port and its trade route. Mika is its surveyor.
- **5th, Ranged**: once archers, now also musketeers, providing fire support in small squads. Adorno was its captain until he died. Lohen is Vice Captain and the captaincy is vacant.
- **6th, Logistics**: led by Hertha. It runs the baggage train, resources and records, and posts bounties and requests. Its previous captain, Anselm, joined the expedition.
- **7th, Combined Arms**: a re-formed company with both ranged and melee fighters. During a limited-time event Phonia predicted that Frederica Gunnhildr would lead it, and knights now call her "Captain Frederica".
- **8th, Support**: inventions, explosives and the new muskets. It works with the 10th. Nymph is its Field Officer.
- **9th, Cavalry**: led by Kaeya; earlier captains were Diluc and Feroux. Every rider except Kaeya went on the expedition.
- **10th, Investigation**: led by Albedo. It provides alchemical inventions, investigates strange phenomena and runs remote reconnaissance. Sucrose is its assistant alchemist.

246.content: The Outriders are a special scout-archer unit of the Knights. They were founded by Amber's grandfather, a former Liyue mercenary leader who joined the Knights after a Favonius doctor saved his life. He trained every member in his archery and gliding. When he suddenly resigned and vanished four years ago, rumours spread that he had defected, and the Outriders fell apart. Amber, who joined just before he left, is now the only Outrider. She works around Mondstadt City and assists other companies. More recently she has asked Jean for unofficial helpers on patrol, but they are not Outriders.

247.content: Half a year before the Traveler arrived, Grand Master Varka led about eighty percent of the Knights' manpower north, including the elite knights and the cavalry. Seamus Pegg (who handled its paperwork), Frederica Gunnhildr (second-in-command, as stated during a limited-time event) and Mika (front-line surveyor) went with him. Varka had glimpsed a calamity in the north, and he did not know at first that it would lead to Nod-Krai. The expedition also quietly gathered wolf spirits split off from Andrius. Along the way it met Capitano, missed two Weinlesefests, and sent Mika home with a letter. For most of the Mondstadt story, the people at home know only that the Grand Master is far away. As Kaeya put it, if Varka has time to write letters, "it's probably nothing serious".

248.content: The Favonius Keep is the expeditionary force's camp in Nod-Krai's Wavechaser Plain, and its large tent smells of dandelion wine. Anselm, formerly captain of the 6th Company, supervises it and handles the administration Seamus used to do. Knights stationed there include Ekbert, Erminie, Laurent, Leifhelm, Nannina and Winfried. After Dottore's defeat, Varka kept a small garrison there by agreement with Nefer, so the outpost could also serve the Northern Intelligence Network in watching for Abyssal attacks. Varka still returns there periodically.

249.content: Eroch was a knight of Varka's generation who often criticised Varka for falling short of the chivalric code. He rose to Inspector, and Varka trusted him with Mondstadt's affairs, including the seal on Ursa the Drake, whenever the Grand Master went abroad. Envious of Varka's fame, Eroch let Dottore's Segments draw him into treason. Four years ago he woke Ursa. Crepus Ragnvindr died stopping the drake with a Delusion, and Eroch ordered Diluc to keep the truth quiet for the Knights' reputation, so Diluc resigned. Jean reported it. Varka had his inner circle investigate and gave Jean authority to act. Jean fought him in two formal duels, losing the first and winning the second decisively (as a knight recalled during a limited-time event), and Eroch was expelled. When Varka finally cornered him, Eroch killed himself, laughing. Varka's character story calls this his most devastating defeat, and in 6.4 he wrote to Diluc to apologise.

250.content: "Honorary Knight" is the title the Knights of Favonius gave the Traveler for helping resolve the Stormterror crisis. The Traveler is not formally a member. Knights across Teyvat, including the expedition's men in Nod-Krai, greet them by this title, and Varka had heard of the Honorary Knight before inviting them to Nod-Krai.

251.content:
Komaniya Express (also: Komaniya, Komaniya Delivery): Komaniya Express is a well-known delivery company based in Inazuma. It is widely praised for punctual and safe delivery, and it has recently begun expanding its service overseas. Its best-known employee is Kirara, a nekomata and the company's Gold Level Courier.

Business has been good enough that the company has hired more staff. Its couriers carry a logo at the waist, which Kaedehara Kazuha recognised when he met Kirara abroad.

Structure: Canon shows a simple structure: an owner or boss, couriers, a warehouse with an "Undelivered Packages" section, and a customer feedback board where clients can leave star ratings. There is a Gold Level Courier title, created for Kirara. The company has an office in Inazuma City, where customers can bring packages.

Leadership: The owner is not named. They are shown as supportive. Kirara's profile says they never considered letting her go, and they designed the Gold Level Courier title overnight when they heard she had delivered every parcel in the Undelivered Packages section.

Members: Kirara is the one employee canon names: a youkai (a nekomata) who loves her job and human society, and whose reputation has done much for the company.

Kirara is the sole courier handling international deliveries, because she is the quickest of the staff. She sometimes changes back into her original cat form and climbs over walls to keep to a schedule. Her profile says she takes a polite, friendly attitude with clients; customers describe her as safe, punctual and vivacious.

Goals: The company's evident aims are fast, careful delivery, customer satisfaction and growth into other nations. Kirara's own motive, which the company benefits from, is that she treats every delivery as an outing and wants to keep her job.

Methods: Couriers deliver parcels on foot and across rooftops, and ask recipients for a signature. Kirara tracks down the right recipient for stranded packages in her spare time, so the "Undelivered Packages" section of the warehouse ends up empty. Customers can rate service on a feedback board.

History: **Before Kirara.** The company had a long reputation in Inazuma as the most reliable delivery service; asked which firm is most dependable, people there mention Komaniya Express first.

**Kirara joins.** After Yae Miko, the Lady Kitsune of the Grand Narukami Shrine, saw how much Kirara enjoyed the streets of Inazuma City, she recommended that she seek work at Komaniya Express. Miko's reasoning was that to blend into human society one must work like an ordinary human.

**Overseas expansion (3.7).** The company recently began delivering to other nations. Kirara's first appearances abroad are in Mondstadt, where she spoke with Diona at the Cat's Tail, and in Liyue Harbor, where she delivered to Hu Tao.

Relations: **Yae Miko.** Kirara's mentor in human society. Miko says packages addressed to Guuji Yae at the Grand Narukami Shrine must be treated as top priority.

**Tenryou Commission.** One of the addresses Kirara knows best, since she climbed the Tenshukaku roof in her first days in Inazuma City, and it receives the bandits she delivers.

**Chiori.** An old customer in Fontaine, an Inazuman designer who dressed Kirara in her current outfit. Kirara's deliveries to Fontaine are in part deliveries to her.

**Hu Tao.** A customer in Liyue who asked whether the company could deliver living people or those in between. Kirara's tails stood on end.

Reputation: Komaniya Express is the best-regarded courier firm in Inazuma. Typical customer feedback is "safe and punctual", "service assured" and "vivacious and adorable". Kirara's tireless record has raised the firm's renown, and no package is undeliverable.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Komaniya Express remains in business, now offering overseas delivery. Kirara handles all international orders.

No 6.x or 7.x story content found in this research changes the company's status.

252.comment: Komaniya Express: Kirara and the Gold Level Courier title
252.content: When Kirara first arrived she noticed that some packages could not be delivered because of wrong addresses, moved recipients or wrong names. She quietly recorded the details and used her routes and spare time to find each recipient. The warehouse's Undelivered Packages section became empty, the owner at first thought they had been robbed, and the owner created the title Gold Level Courier for her.

253.comment: Komaniya Express: Kirara in Liyue Harbor (Summoners' Summit)
253.content: During the limited-time event Duel! The Summoners' Summit!, in Roll! A Sea of New Acquaintances, the Traveler, Paimon and Kazuha met Kirara in Liyue Harbor. She was lost on her first delivery there. She explained that Komaniya Express had just begun overseas service and that she now effectively travels the world as part of her job. She was looking for the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, where she asked Hu Tao for a signature and a five-star review.

254.content:
Korolevskiy Troupe (also: Korolevskiy Theater Troupe, Royal Troupe): The Korolevskiy Troupe is a performance company in Snezhnaya that specialises in opera, theatre, ballet and musical performance. It performs at the Korolevskiy Theater in Snezhnograd and is very popular, especially among the Fatui Harbingers and Mitya. Its two star performers are Odette, Prima Ballerina, and Vodyanitsa, Prima Donna. Both also have a hidden life beyond the stage.

The name is Russian for "royal". The troupe's reputation rests on its leading women, whose work critics compare with the older, more classical Snezhnayan stage tradition. A critic in the theater says their performances drop the excess of traditional grand-tragedy opera in favour of restraint and elegance. The official map description of the theatre is about the work behind the illusion: success is measured by whether the audience can be given a moment's escape into something beautiful.

Structure: Canon names no director or manager. The two top roles are Prima Ballerina (Odette) and Prima Donna (Vodyanitsa). Odette's character story shows the two principals also coordinating the programme, preparing costumes and calming nervous newcomers before their first performance. Below them are the chorus and ballet performers, who appear mostly unnamed. The wider theatre has its own stage and front-of-house staff, such as the ticket-seekers' queue, critics and local fans, but individual staff are minor.

Members: Odette, the Prima Ballerina, is calm, exacting and nearly expressionless on and off stage. Vodyanitsa, the Prima Donna, is a Water Imp (a Snowland fae) whose singing is said to carry an otherworldly allure; she is lively and outspoken.

Odette Spessiva comes from an old ballet family and was taught by her mother Violetta. Her admirers call her dancing precise and austere, and the press describes it as "perfection, polished to an icy sheen". Vodyanitsa is the last of her kind on the stage: the Water Imps once filled Snezhnaya's streets and stages with song, but by the time of her story most had left, and she stayed on at the Korolevskiy Theater. The two are friends and the troupe's senior figures, and few colleagues can talk freely with Odette outside a performance.

Goals: The troupe's stated purpose is performance: giving audiences a beautiful illusion, with the labour kept behind the curtain. No political aim is attributed to the troupe as an organisation. Its two leading performers have additional commitments outside the theatre (see secrets).

History: Nothing is recorded about the troupe's founding. The only dated material comes from the Chapter VII period. Before the Traveler's visit, Odette and Vodyanitsa had already built their reputations: critics use their names as shorthand for the theater, and the old-style gloom of grand tragedies has given way to their sharper, cleaner shows. Violetta's earlier career is part of the troupe's past, and her injury left Odette to carry the Spessiva name forward.

Relations: - **Fatui and Harbingers**: the wiki says the troupe is especially popular among Fatui Harbingers. After the Traveler's visit, Tartaglia, Arlecchino and Sandrone can be seen as audience members at the theater. Odette works for the Fatui and, per the wiki, is the favoured candidate to inherit her mentor Signora's Harbinger seat.
- **Mitya**: a notable fan of the troupe.
- **Rokot**: Odette (as Lelek) and Vodyanitsa belong to this anti-Project-Stuzha group, though neither knew the other was a member at first.

Reputation: Highly regarded, with devoted fans and a queue that never shortens. The audience praises Odette's austerity and Vodyanitsa's voice. Gossip about Odette's coldness is a running joke: one tale has a nobleman reserving a whole row and waiting two hours with a bouquet only to be told she had left by the side door. Others, including Zamorov and Taisiya, fight over which of the two stars represents the theater best.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the troupe is active at the Korolevskiy Theater in Snezhnograd. Odette and Vodyanitsa are both playable characters.

The Korolevskiy Theater is an open area in Everfrozen Earth with its own Meeting Point (unlocked via the world quest One Yet to Take a Bow) and a set of NPCs. Odette and Vodyanitsa appear in the theater after the Chapter VII events. Nothing further about the troupe is canon beyond 7.1.

255.content: The Korolevskiy Theater is a subarea of Everfrozen Earth in Snezhnograd where the troupe performs. Its named staff and visitors include Balkonov, Osipova, Pisemsky, Polovikova, Roshchina, Shuvalov, Taisiya, Vzdykhalov, Yadova and Zamorov. The wiki notes that the theater and the troupe may take their name from Nepla Korolevitsna, wife of the fae Filipov, though this is not confirmed.

256.comment: Korolevskiy Troupe: Odette and Vodyanitsa as a pair
256.content: The Prima Ballerina and Prima Donna contrast in manner and stand close in friendship. Odette is quiet and dry. Vodyanitsa teases and drags her to meals. A backstage scene shows Odette giving Vodyanitsa honey candy "for your throat" and Vodyanitsa insisting that she saw Odette smile, which Odette explains away as the expression the role required. Post-quest dialogue also has Odette complain that Vodyanitsa would ambush her backstage if she skipped one of her performances.

key: School of the Theory of Curiosities
257.content:
Kshahrewar (also: Kshahrewar Darshan, School of Technology, School of the Theory of Curiosities, Darshan of Technology): Kshahrewar is the Sumeru Akademiya's Darshan of technology. It covers mechanisms, architecture and puzzle-solving, and its colour is white with a lion on its crest. Its sage is Firnas. It built much of Sumeru City, but it has been underfunded since the loss of its greatest scholar, Pir Kavikavus. Its best-known graduate is the architect Kaveh, the Light of Kshahrewar.

Kshahrewar's designs shape ordinary life: a cheap single-storey house plan that serves as a template across the city, and loom designs behind Sumeru's textile industry. Most people never notice the theory behind these. The Darshan also studies King Deshret's ancient technology, which it has not yet explained.

Structure: Kshahrewar is one of the Six Darshans, with one Great Sage. According to the receptionist Sitt, it began as a school for studying and building propulsion mechanisms, and its scope grew because making machines draws on many kinds of knowledge. Its disciplines now include architecture, mechanical skills and puzzle-solving. Members are students, researchers and teachers. Many scholars are serious about sculpting as a hobby, Firnas says.

Leadership: Firnas is the current Kshahrewar Sage. He reasons like an engineer, comparing crises to faulty machines. His predecessor was removed after the Akademiya-Fatui plot.

Hosseini, in the 2.7 event A Muddy Bizarre Adventure, mentions "our great tutor Firnas". In 6.6 Firnas is one of the six sages gathered at Caravan Ribat. He judged that the Irminsul anomaly resembled a malfunctioning machine and spoke of stress fractures. At Aaru Village he reported on the Jinn breaching the defences and helped move the villagers north. He later judged the Temple of Silence plan sound with manageable risk.

Members: Kaveh is the Darshan's most celebrated alumnus: a Kshahrewar graduate with honours, the architect of the Palace of Alcazarzaray, and known as the Light of Kshahrewar. His mother Faranak graduated from Kshahrewar and was a famous architect too. Faruzan is a Haravatat professor, but her theories underpin the Darshan's mechanics. She also studied there for a time. Alhaitham's grandmother was a Kshahrewar scholar who raised him. Jazari is a researcher who wants to follow Kavikavus and win the Pir Kavikavus Prize.

Goals: Kshahrewar wants to design and improve working things: buildings, looms, machinery and ancient mechanisms. Its scholars also want to revive their school's standing. Jazari hopes the rediscovery of Kavikavus' work will do that. The wiki says that, likely because of the accident, the Darshan came to advocate strict control over machines and technology, and a forum poster says those above wanted a stable, peaceful society.

History: **Pir Kavikavus.** A prodigy who joined some time after the cataclysm 500 years ago, Kavikavus became a Herbad before thirty. He was friends with the Aranara Aralohita. He was the last person recorded to enter the Ruin Golem on Devantaka Mountain for systematic research. In an accident his research was lost and he likely died. Since then Kshahrewar has been regarded as in decline, with no raise in funding and no major breakthroughs. The Akademiya's prize for outstanding young scholars bears his name.

Relations: - **Haravatat**: Kshahrewar built its mechanics on Haravatat's old work, notably Faruzan's. Faruzan says Kshahrewar tried to recruit her, with more students and a bigger budget.
- **Dori**: the merchant lends Mora to Kshahrewar and to Kaveh. Dori says they signed a private contract: she has the Mora, they have the technology.
- **Tighnari's view**: he called Kshahrewar and Spantamad researchers quite prejudiced, so he would not trust them with a delicate matter.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, Firnas is the Sage. The Darshan remains underfunded, and no Kshahrewar-specific story was found for 6.7 to 7.1.

Its scholars were involved in the 6.6 Irminsul and Akasha work. The 7.0 and 7.1 Archon Quests take place in Snezhnaya and do not involve the Darshans.

258.content: Firnas is the Kshahrewar Sage, appointed after the previous sage fell with Azar. Earlier, Hosseini called him a "great tutor" in an event. In 6.6, at Caravan Ribat and the Temple of Silence, he approached the crisis like an engineer: the anomaly looked like a malfunctioning machine, not an outside attack, and he warned of supply problems on a move to the desert. He also remarked on sculpting among Kshahrewar scholars and asked Faruzan whether she had once studied in his Darshan.

259.content: Pir Kavikavus was a Kshahrewar prodigy who joined some time after the cataclysm, reached the rank of Herbad before thirty, and was friends with the Aranara Aralohita. While investigating the Ruin Golem on Devantaka Mountain, an accident destroyed his research and he likely died. Aralohita saved some of his work behind puzzles. In 3.0, Jazari used a recovered paper to seal the Golem's Chaos Core. The prize that honours him goes to a scholar under forty with groundbreaking research.

260.content: Jazari is a Kshahrewar researcher who worries about money and hopes to follow Kavikavus in studying the Ruin Golem. In Vimana Agama he tells the Traveler about Kavikavus and says Kshahrewar is concerned only with genuine techniques. In Until Vana is Healed he uses Kavikavus' rediscovered paper to seal the Chaos Core and hopes this revives Kshahrewar.

key: the Kujou Clan of the Tenryou Commission
261.content:
Kujou Clan (also: Kujou family, House Kujou, the Kujou Clan of the Tenryou Commission, Kujou-ke): The Kujou Clan is one of Inazuma's three great families and the head of the Tenryou Commission, the Raiden Shogun's executive arm for security and the army. It is regarded as the most loyal and powerful of the families supporting the Shogun's rule. During the Vision Hunt Decree the Kujou enforced the Shogun's order to seize Visions, through the general Kujou Sara. Its head, Kujou Takayuki, was then exposed as having worked with the Fatui for his own gain. His younger son Kujou Kamaji now leads the clan as acting head. Its estate stands next to Tenshukaku.

The clan counts three generations of difficulty in this period: Takayuki's disgrace, the Shogun's postponement of its punishment, and the rival Takatsukasa waiting to replace it. Its members are not of one mind. Several of them doubted the decree while carrying it out.

Structure: The clan head is also the Tenryou Commissioner. Under him the family splits duties: Kujou Masahito commands the Shogun's Army at the Kujou Encampment on the Kannazuka front, Kamaji handles the Commission's civil business in Inazuma City, and Kujou Sara leads the Commission's forces as a general. Shogunate samurai, yoriki and doushin serve beneath them, and the Takatsukasa Clan supports the Kujou in running the Commission. Kujou retainers and security staff are called the clan's own guard.

Leadership: Kujou Takayuki, the former head, is under house arrest. Kujou Kamaji is acting head and Tenryou Commissioner in his place. Masahito and Sara serve as generals.

Takayuki was proud and rigid, loyal to the family's influence above all else. Kamaji is an earnest, self-doubting official who has questioned the Shogun's policies privately but never found anyone to tell. Masahito is a soldier who thinks the war can no longer be won cleanly. Sara is the Shogun's most devoted general.

Members: Kujou Takayuki (former head), Kujou Masahito (general), Kujou Kamaji (acting head), and Kujou Sara (adopted daughter, general). Kujou Shigeyori is the clan's founding-era ancestor.

Goals: Protect the Shogun's rule and keep Inazuma secure. Under Takayuki this meant enforcing the Sakoku and Vision Hunt Decrees and protecting the clan's influence. After his fall the surviving Kujou have a narrower goal: to keep the Tenryou Commission from passing to the Takatsukasa and to earn back the Shogun's trust. Kamaji said in the duel that he accepted the clan's decline as punishment for doubting without acting.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Kujou Clan still heads the Tenryou Commission under acting head Kamaji. Takayuki remains under house arrest awaiting punishment, and the Shogun has postponed any ruling on the clan. Masahito and Sara continue to lead the Shogun's forces.

262.content: The Tenryou Commission ("Bugyou of the Shogun's Domain") is the Tri-Commission's executive arm, responsible for public security and military affairs. It enforced the Vision Hunt Decree and, with the Kanjou Commission, the Sakoku Decree, and posts notices on Inazuma's bulletin boards. It is led by the Kujou Clan and uses Shogunate samurai, yoriki and doushin. Sara, Masahito and Kamaji serve as its leaders. Its rank structure includes police and detectives such as Heizou, and its headquarters stands in Inazuma City beside Tenshukaku. The Commission has a high desertion rate and was in disarray after Takayuki's removal.

263.content: The Takatsukasa have served the Kujou for generations and support them in heading the Tenryou Commission, but the two clans have long been at odds over its leadership. The head is Takatsukasa Susumu. His younger brother Isamu was the police station head and was murdered; Isamu's daughter is Takatsukasa Chika. After Takayuki's fall, Takatsukasa members tried to oust the Kujou by coercing Kamaji into signing a confession that painted themselves favourably, using a hidden mountain base on Mt. Yougou. Ei ended the matter in To Hear Mortal Hearts, and the clan abandoned the base. In the name, takatsukasa means "master of falconry".

264.content: The Kujou Encampment is a fortress at the front line in Kannazuka, said to have been built by Kujou Shigeyori in a single night in the age of the cataclysm. During the civil war Kujou Masahito commanded the Shogun's troops there. He thought the war was a stalemate that either side could win if it dragged on. After the ceasefire he predicted that any peace would be short-lived.

265.comment: Kujou Clan: Takayuki's collusion with the Fatui
265.content: Takayuki agreed to advance the Vision Hunt Decree so that the Fatui could sell Delusions, in return for power, wanting to keep his clan's influence and believing the Fatui would be no match for the Shogun. He sent the Shogun optimistic, false reports of the war. Yae Miko planned to turn Sara against the Tenryou Commission by proving this. With help from Ayaka, Thoma, Yoimiya and the ninja Sayu, the Traveler obtained his falsified report and the Fatui letters. Sara read them and confronted him; he confirmed it and gave selfish reasons. After this, the Shogun was displeased; he aged overnight and lost his post. He is now under house arrest.

266.comment: Kujou Clan: Kujou Kamaji and Hiiragi Chisato
266.content: Kamaji is Takayuki's younger son and runs the Commission's civil business in Inazuma City. In Chapter II, Chisato asks the Traveler to take a letter to him; she calls him her love and the two begin writing. In the Cypressus Custos Chapter (2.6), a marriage between them is announced. Kamaji says Chisato proposed first, but she tells the Traveler she never sent a letter. Ayato suspects a plot by the Kanjou Commission's plotters to use the match, and resolves it with the Traveler's help. Chisato asserts her own authority at the end.

267.comment: Kujou Clan: Kujou Sara and the Kujou family
267.content: Sara is a tengu who was found unconscious by the roadside, a Vision in her hand, after being thrown from a cliff while fighting monsters near her mountain home. Takayuki saw her as a child sent by heaven, named her Sara and raised her as a soldier. She is grateful to him but knows he does not look at her as he does Kamaji; Kamaji is the one who treats her as family. She believes the Shogun saved her life by granting the Vision. Soldiers first thought she was a boy when she began to train young, and one punishment from Takayuki taught her to keep a distance from others.

268.content:
Lawrence Clan (also: House Lawrence, the Lawrence family, Lawrence noble family, Glacial Seal): The Lawrence Clan was the foremost noble house of Mondstadt's aristocracy. It began as hardy frontier survivors, grew into arrogant rulers and, about a thousand years ago, was deposed by Vennessa's rebellion and driven out of the city. Its descendants still live in Mondstadt, where the name draws hostility. The best-known member today is Eula, who left the clan's ways behind and serves in the Knights of Favonius.

The clan's emblem is the Glacial Seal, which stands for a cold, composed, unshaken character. Eula now carries it. The Lawrences are counted among Mondstadt's historic great clans with the Gunnhildrs, Imunlaukrs and, later, the Ragnvindrs, but only the Lawrences are remembered as tyrants.

History: **Before Mondstadt.** The clan lived outside Decarabian's city and survived the frozen wilderness as pioneers, which led them to think of themselves as conquerors. **Early aristocracy.** When Barbatos refounded Mondstadt, the clan's leader Venerare had a statue of him raised in the plaza, inscribed with an oath from the leaders of all the clans. In this period the clan's nobles hunted to show their strength and shared the spoils with the people, and royal mages kept the history and taught virtue. **Late aristocracy.** The Lawrences' view of themselves slid from conquerors to overlords to kings. They tore down the statue, the mages abandoned their duties, and the gladiatorial games became bloodsport. A thousand years ago they were effectively rulers of Mondstadt City. Vennessa, an enslaved gladiator, rose against them with Barbatos' help, and the clan was overthrown and forced to leave the city for good.

Members: Known members: Venerare (early leader), Lord Lawrence and his son Barca (a thousand years ago, manga), Kreuzlied (disowned), and in the present Eula, her uncle Schubert and her cousin Lessig. Eula is the only playable one.

Goals: The clan's later generations cling to the dream of recovering Mondstadt and its former glory, and they raise children to fit the rule they feel entitled to. Individuals who give up that dream, as Eula has, are rare.

Methods: Historically the clan ruled by force of arms and by the arena. Today it has no power, so it relies on pride, etiquette and discipline and, in one case, secret alliance with outsiders. Schubert plotted with the Fatui to take Mondstadt back, regardless of the harm to ordinary people.

Culture: The clan puts great stress on looking noble in the eyes of commoners. Children are taught by the best tutors available in combat, dance, cooking and etiquette, under a regimen most would call abusive. Art is called the clan's "second soul". In battle a Lawrence must appear refined and unshaken, and being knocked down or frozen is thought shameful.

Reputation: Ordinary Mondstadters hold the clan in poor regard and some become aggressive at the mere mention of the name. Descendants are treated as a social threat. Before joining the Knights, Eula said, almost every shop refused her money, so she hunted and cooked for herself. When clan members clashed with locals, the Knights arrived to mediate, with little effect.

Relations: - **Mondstadt Aristocracy**: the Lawrences were its foremost clan.
- **Gunnhildr, Imunlaukr and Ragnvindr Clans**: other great clans. Uncorrupted houses such as the Gunnhildrs stayed after the rebellion, while the Lawrences were driven out.
- **Wanderer's Troupe**: Kreuzlied, a disowned Lawrence, was its last known member. The troupe's attack on the city failed.
- **Knights of Favonius**: the order replaced noble rule. Varka and Jean allowed Eula to join despite the uproar, since her combat skill was too valuable to waste.
- **Fatui**: Schubert called them ruffians but treated them as useful business partners.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the clan has no power and no known home. Eula serves as a Knights of Favonius captain, and many of her family regard her as a traitor.

Schubert was taken into custody after the plot with the Fatui failed. Lessig gave up his wild plans and decided to return to Mondstadt, wanting a city where people do not fear his family. No new Lawrence Clan story was found for 6.0 to 7.1.

269.content: The Glacial Seal is the symbol of the Lawrence Clan. It represents the clan's temper since the early days of Mondstadt: cold and unsullied, undaunted by flame, composed in every circumstance. Its mark appears on weapons and artifacts of the Royal Series and Noblesse Oblige and on Eula's namecard. Eula currently carries it.

270.content: Schubert Lawrence, Eula's uncle, believed present-day Mondstadt had fallen into ruin for lack of noble oversight. In The Spindrift Shall Never Return to the Sea he secretly worked with the Fatui to restore proper rule, indifferent to civilian risk. He is easily flattered, and being praised lowers his guard. The Traveler and Eula foiled the plan, and he was taken into custody. Eula found it disgusting, but also surprising, since she had known the other nobles as people who complained and did nothing.

271.content: Lessig, Eula's cousin, appeared in the limited-time event Secret Summer Paradise. Having heard of a way to restore the clan's honour, he went to Sumeru through Liyue and found that nobody knew or cared about his name. He lost his wallet, lived rough and ended up at the Veluriyam Mirage, where he tried to fix things and made them worse. When the Traveler, Collei and Eula found him he thought Eula had come to drag him home. Instead he said he wanted a Mondstadt where people did not fear him and decided to return, realising Eula had seen the truth before the rest of the clan. Eula offered to help him tell his parents.

272.content: Venerare led the Lawrence Clan when new Mondstadt was founded. She guided the people to build the first statue of Barbatos in the plaza, with an oath inscribed by the leaders of all the clans. Her descendants in the late aristocracy tore the statue down, so the oath was lost and does not appear on the rebuilt statue. A book says she helped Leonard reach Pilos Peak, though how the two were related is unclear.

273.content: Kreuzlied was born a Lawrence and turned against the clan; he was disowned. He joined the Wanderer's Troupe as its last known member, wielding the greatsword The Bell, and after the troupe's failed uprising was spared severe punishment because of his privileged birth. He then founded an underground society against the aristocracy, which later aided Vennessa. His real name and fate are unknown. Weapon lore calls him a traitor and outcast from the ruling Lawrences.

274.content:
Legion of Soulblazers (also: Soulblazers, the Legion of Soulblazers, the Legion): The Legion of Soulblazers is a loose group of friends and pen pals led by Varesa of Natlan. Members come from several nations and began as a comic-book fan club. They are devoted to The Soulblazer Saga, a comic series about Natlan's fight against the Abyss, and treat its hero Fietena as a role model. Varesa says the group's real aim is to share life's joys and get rid of life's woes. It appears only in the limited-time event Soulblazers' Snowbound Journey (6.2).

Before that event the members had never met in person. They kept in touch by writing letters and trading illustrations. The Traveler and Paimon join the Legion during the event and take the group's oath. The Legion has no known base, charter or official standing in any nation; it is a club of friends.

Structure: There is no formal hierarchy beyond a captain. Varesa is the captain. Xilonen is called vice captain during the event, a title she says she ended up with without quite agreeing to it. She is standing in for her pen-pal-turned-student Nepecha and says she is not a member of the fan club herself. Alrani calls Varesa "Captain" and often speaks for the group, and Tang Yigang jokes that her camp duty, logistics, is the easiest job. New members are sworn in with a short ceremony that uses a mask of Fietena as the relic and a shouted oath.

Leadership: Varesa is the captain: a cheerful, huge-appetited competitor from the Collective of Plenty who trains with her coach Iansan. She leads by enthusiasm, sets the training plans for the race, and takes personal responsibility for her teammates, saying she feels powerless as their captain when Minnie's parents press her to quit. Xilonen, the vice captain, is the practical one. She keeps the group's training sensible, notices when a teammate is hiding something, and steps in when words are needed.

Members: - **Varesa**: captain; from Natlan's Collective of Plenty.
- **Alrani**: a student at the Sumeru Akademiya who is still writing her thesis. She is the group's most formal speaker and runs the oath.
- **Tang Yigang**: from Liyue. Dramatic, easily excited about the Saga, and prone to catching colds on the cold mountain.
- **Minnie**: from Mondstadt. A young artist and prop maker who suggested the Dragonspine meetup. Her parents worry about her health and her plans.
- **Nepecha**: a girl in Natlan's Children of Echoes tribe, not present at the event because she is unfit for extreme sports. Xilonen represents her.
- **Traveler and Paimon**: inducted during the event.

Goals: The Legion exists to share life's joys and get rid of life's woes, in Varesa's words. The members read and discuss comics together, eat together and support one another.

The comic fandom was the original bond. The tenets they recite come straight from the Saga: peace is not won by tears and strong words alone, and fighters should be ready to give everything even when the cause may fail. Their motto asks them to meet pain and defeat without fear and to keep championing love and imagination. In practice the Legion's goals are mostly personal. It backs Minnie's wish to work in comics and gets her to the finish line of the race.

Methods: Members write letters, trade illustrations and share copies of the comics, handing spare volumes to newcomers. In person they discuss the series, eat large meals, rest and train together. They recruit by lending out comics and inviting people in, and they swear in members in a ceremony that uses a Fietena mask as a relic and a shouted oath.

Status as of 7.1: The Legion is last seen at the end of the 6.2 event, with Minnie free to travel and the group still in touch. It has not been mentioned again in anything checked through 7.1.

Nothing suggests the Legion has been dissolved. Varesa remains its captain and still appears as a playable character, but no later quest or event features the group.

275.comment: Legion of Soulblazers: The Soulblazer Saga
275.content: The Soulblazer Saga is a long-running comic series, published by Yae Publishing House, that dramatises Natlan's struggle against the Abyss during the Cataclysm. Varesa says it runs to 12 volumes, with other comic series focused on the Pyro Archon, and that its characters are based on real people although it is mostly meant as entertainment, not history. The hero is Fietena, a rookie warrior who grows into a commander and survives a period of disillusionment, with friends such as Wanjiru and Mavuika at her side. In volume 2, as shown in the event, Fietena goes into her first battle with Mavuika and the others, with the Pyro Archon confronting the monsters' leader while the rest deal with the minions. Fietena wears five different masks in the story. Varesa's own combat mask is modelled on one of them, and a different one serves as the oath relic. The wider franchise has merchandise such as badges, notepaper and figures.

276.comment: Legion of Soulblazers: Legion oath and tenets
276.content: Members swear a short oath by shouting it aloud, which Varesa says is about believing in something enough to shout it for the world to hear. The wording used in the event vows never to fear pain and defeat and to always champion love and imagination. The two founding tenets are taken from the Saga: that tears and strong words alone will not broker peace, and that the Soulblazer will give their life fighting darkness even if the fight is in vain. The oath is taken while holding a mask of Fietena as a relic. Varesa picks the mask Fietena wore when she returned to the fight after her darkest period.

277.content: Minnie is the Mondstadt member of the Legion. She is an artist and prop maker, Nepecha's long-time pen pal, and the one who proposed the Dragonspine meeting. She is a young member of the group and a local of Mondstadt, where her older brother Patton works at the tavern and her parents want her to choose a safer career. She hopes to work in the comic industry, and she made a deal with her parents that a ranked result in the race would make them take her seriously. She is thoughtful, anxious about letting teammates down, and keen to rest properly when Xilonen insists. During the race she stops to help an injured rival, which costs her team a medal. Her parents allow her to travel afterwards, subject to caution.

278.comment: Legion of Soulblazers: Nepecha and the Legion
278.content: Nepecha is a member of the Legion who stays in Natlan. She is a girl from the Children of Echoes, and Xilonen is her teacher and something like family. She and Minnie are pen pals, and Xilonen says Nepecha praises Minnie as an artist and as a source of life advice. Nepecha wanted to join the Dragonspine event but is not fit for extreme sports, so she asked Xilonen to attend in her place. She had friends from the tribe contribute to a group painting for Minnie, which Xilonen delivers early to help persuade Minnie's parents.

279.content:
Lightkeepers (also: the Lightkeepers, Lightkeeper, Ratniki, Warriors of the Nightingale): The Lightkeepers are Nod-Krai's militia against the Wild Hunt, the Abyssal host that has haunted the borderland since the Cataclysm. Solovei the Torchforger founded them about 500 years ago, and a royal edict from Snezhnaya made Nod-Krai an autonomous region under their protection. They are led by a Starshyna, currently Nikita, from the fortress-city of Piramida. Their fighters are called Ratniki, and every one of them carries an Oath Lantern. Their emblem is a nightingale holding a burning wick in its beak.

They are volunteers, chronically short of people, and proud of it. In their own words they "shine the eternal light of hope into the endless snow-swept plains". Playable members are Flins and Illuga.

Structure: - **Starshyna**: the single leader, based in Piramida.
- **Sergeant Majors** (sometimes addressed as Captains): each is responsible for an area of Nod-Krai and coordinates its squad leaders.
- **Squad Leaders**: command a squad, marked by a special brooch on the left lapel of the uniform.
- **Ratniki** (singular Ratnik): the ordinary fighting members.
Every Ratnik carries an Oath Lantern, which lets other Lightkeepers and the Starshyna detect where they are. Members disabled by injury may be moved to other posts if they want to keep serving. Disobeying direct orders brings real trouble. There are also non-combat staff such as doctors and a blacksmith.

Leadership: Nikita, a middle-aged veteran the Ratniki fondly call "old man", is the current Starshyna. He took over about a decade ago when his predecessor Sigurd fell fighting the Wild Hunt.

Goals: Their stated purpose, in Nikita's words, is to safeguard the freedom and peace of Nod-Krai. In practice this means holding back the Wild Hunt, protecting the merchants and travellers who cross their lands, and keeping alive the "paradise" (Elysium) that Solovei defended before the Tsaritsa's court. Illuga describes Nod-Krai as an Elysium built by human hands and kept alive by generations of Lightkeeper sacrifice. He prefers self-reliance to waiting for any god, even the new Moon Goddess.

Methods: Lightkeepers patrol the land, answer Wild Hunt incursions wherever they appear, and keep watch from lighthouses and camps. They have planted Tideseal Stones across Nod-Krai to stop the Wild Hunt from seeping in. Their oath, sworn by every new member, ends: "We are the Lightkeepers, who shine the eternal light of hope into the endless snow-swept plains." Flins names prudence, modesty and loyalty as their three cardinal virtues.

History: When the Cataclysm struck about 500 years ago, Abyssal beasts overran Nod-Krai and the northern court could no longer protect its borderlands. Solovei, a Snezhnayan noble, came south, and with power lent by Aila, priestess of the Frostmoon Scions, drove the darkness back. The survivors raised a lighthouse in the mountains, and Solovei won a royal edict for Nod-Krai's autonomy in return for an oath of vigilance and sacrifice.

Since then the Lightkeepers have been nearly wiped out several times and rebuilt each time. About a decade ago, a great battle against the Wild Hunt killed Starshyna Sigurd and most of the order, and destroyed Illuga's village. Nikita had to rebuild almost from scratch. The disaster convinced many young people of the Lempo Isles that the old tales were true, and they volunteered. Three years before the Traveler came, a Wild Hunt surge at Kipumaki Cliff overwhelmed the Nightmare Orioles. Captain Olsson died covering the retreat of Illuga and the badly wounded Ivar.

Relations: - **Frostmoon Scions**: allies since Aila aided Solovei. Flins mentions that some former Scions recently joined the Lightkeepers, apparently after Lauma revealed the truth about the false sky.
- **Knights of Favonius**: allies. Varka's expedition fought the Wild Hunt alongside them, and Illuga has fought beside Varka.
- **Fatui and the Tsaritsa**: Nod-Krai is formally Snezhnayan, but its autonomy rests on the old edict. Flins notes that Lightkeepers do not habitually say "Her Majesty the Tsaritsa".
- **The Wild Hunt**: their enemy since the Cataclysm.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Lightkeepers are active under Starshyna Nikita, still understrength but recruiting again, and part of Nod-Krai's new League.

Illuga is their League representative, and his squad is rebuilding a Lightkeeper outpost at Cliffwatch Camp. The Wild Hunt has been leaderless since Rerir was cast out and the Abyss's imitation of Roland expired in 6.4, but its incursions continue. No new Lightkeepers story was found for 7.0-7.1, whose Archon Quests take place in Snezhnaya.

280.content: Every new Lightkeeper swears an oath in seven lines, which is also carved on Oath Lanterns and on a monument at the Final Night Cemetery. It moves from a vision of the sky swallowed by silence, through a promise that whoever keeps the flame burning need not descend into darkness, to a vow to burn "bones and blood" as fuel and "make life greater than death". It ends: "We are the Lightkeepers, who shine the eternal light of hope into the endless snow-swept plains." Oath Lanterns are standard equipment. Through them other Lightkeepers and the Starshyna can find a Ratnik, and lanterns of the fallen are still found across the southern isles.

281.content: Starshyna is the title of the Lightkeepers' leader. Solovei the Torchforger was the first. Later holders include Sergei Semyonovich Mayakov and Sigurd, a famously brave longsword fighter whose warning bell was said to make beasts flinch. Sigurd vanished in the great battle about a decade ago. The present Starshyna is Nikita, who fought beside him and rebuilt the order afterward.

282.content: Piramida is the Lightkeepers' headquarters, a city on top of an ancient castle that was once the palace of Nod-Krai's fae governor, built around a giant golden-age lighthouse. A statue of Solovei the Torchforger watches over it, and the great mead hall at its summit hosts victory banquets where the first pour goes to the dead. The Arrow of Terpikeraunas is housed there.

283.content: A Ratnik (plural Ratniki) is an ordinary fighting member of the Lightkeepers. The word comes from an old Slavic term for a warrior of a militia or host. Flins calls himself "a humble Ratnik" and says the role, keeping humanity's light burning on nights when monsters roam, suits a nocturnal creature like him perfectly.

284.content:
Liyue Qixing (also: Qixing, Seven Stars of Liyue, the Liyue Qixing): The Liyue Qixing ("Seven Stars of Liyue") are a committee of seven business leaders who govern Liyue. Each is a magnate in their own field, and each holds a title named after a star of the Big Dipper. They meet at Yuehai Pavilion on Yujing Terrace in Liyue Harbor. For millennia they carried out the policies of Rex Lapis, the Geo Archon, and handled day-to-day government. Since his apparent death, which he staged, they have ruled Liyue without divine guidance. The best-known members are Ningguang, the Tianquan, and Keqing, the Yuheng.

Liyue's people call them "the hands and feet of Rex Lapis". They oversee all of Liyue's major trades, and very little business, inside or outside the nation, escapes their notice.

Structure: The seven members are equal in rank, but they divide the work clearly. Known seats:
- **Tianquan** (Ningguang): keeps Morax's book of ancient laws and its amendments, and handles foreign relations.
- **Yuheng** (Keqing): land, livelihood, construction works and real estate.
- **Tianshu** (Uncle Tian): plans policy and advises from behind the scenes, and traditionally rarely appears in public.
- **Kaiyang**: an unnamed current member.
- **Tianxuan**: mentioned in Ganyu's stories, but the current holder is unnamed.

The remaining seats have never been named in canon. Responsibilities overlap: water quality falls under the Yuheng, yet a Tianquan amended the sanitation act on sabotaging water sources, and every member helps make law. The Millelith (Liyue's security force), the Ministry of Civil Affairs and the Eight Trades (the offices running Liyue's major industries) all answer to the Qixing.

Leadership: Ningguang, the Tianquan, is the Qixing's most public face. Keqing, the Yuheng, is known for hard work and for doubting reliance on the gods.

Most members keep a low profile and play it safe. Ningguang is the exception: she lives in the floating Jade Chamber, appears all over Liyue Harbor and is the subject of endless gossip. Keqing works in the field, from the south wharf to the Chasm, and once made a famous speech at the Rite of Descension asking how long Liyue could depend on Rex Lapis. Uncle Tian, the Tianshu, passes as an old, forgetful fisherman at the docks, and only a handful of people outside key posts know who he is. The Kaiyang has not been shown on screen. The Kaiyang proposed a multinational wargame to the Tianquan and, together with her, approved a long-term partnership with the Traveler.

Methods: The Qixing govern through law, money and information. Morax's ancient laws, with each Tianquan's amendments, are published with a 279-page commentary, and every citizen gets a copy. Merchants treat any loophole as fair game until the Qixing patch it, which is why Ningguang is privately called the "Tailor of Liyue".

History: **Founding.** When the Archon War ended, Liyue turned to commerce and craft, and those who prospered most formed the Qixing. Ganyu, who had fought for Morax, stayed on as their first secretary.

**End of divine rule (1.0).** Rex Lapis was apparently killed during the Rite of Descension, and the Qixing sent the Millelith after the culprit. Childe remarked that the Qixing had always been suspicious of the Fatui. The Qixing then received word in secret that the god was not really dead. They declared that he had died failing a divine trial, dropped the hunt for the killer and moved to fill the power vacuum, which brought them into open confrontation with the adepti. When the Fatui released the ancient god Osial, the Qixing, the adepti, the Millelith and the Traveler fought him together, and Ningguang dropped her Jade Chamber on him. The Qixing then held the Rite of Parting and took over all of Rex Lapis' duties together with the Eight Trades.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Qixing still govern Liyue. Ningguang and Keqing remain in office, and the rebuilt Jade Chamber floats above Liyue Harbor again.

During the 6.3 Lantern Rite, Ningguang and Keqing looked into a strange moon phenomenon and artifacts excavated near the Chasm, while Ganyu consulted the adepti. No further Qixing story developments were found for 6.4-7.1. The 7.0-7.1 Archon Quests take place in Snezhnaya.

285.comment: Liyue Qixing: Qixing titles and seats
285.content: Each seat of the Qixing is named after a star of the Big Dipper, in Chinese reading. Five titles appear in official material. The Tianshu (Dubhe) is Uncle Tian, who plans policy behind the scenes. The Tianxuan (Merak) is mentioned in Ganyu's stories but no current holder is named. The Tianquan (Megrez) is Ningguang, who keeps the laws and runs foreign relations. The Yuheng (Alioth) is Keqing, who oversees land, livelihood and construction. The Kaiyang (Mizar) is an unnamed current member who is addressed as "Lord Kaiyang". The two remaining stars' names are fan extrapolations that have never appeared in canon. Members are addressed as "Lady Tianquan", "Lady Yuheng" and so on, and are of equal rank.

286.content: Yuehai Pavilion on Yujing Terrace is where the Qixing meet, discuss official business and rule on matters affecting all of Liyue. Their day-to-day operations and staff are based there, though some days all seven members are away on private business. Ganyu works there as General Secretary, alongside junior secretaries such as Huixin. Those with civil matters are sent on to the Ministry of Civil Affairs. Bu'yun at the pavilion controls access to the Jade Chamber. In the Liyue Archon Quest the password to go up was "Excuse me, do you sell the moon here?"

287.comment: Liyue Qixing: The Qixing and Wangshu Inn
287.content: Wangshu Inn in Dihua Marsh was built by the Qixing and is secretly run by them; it already stood about 500 years ago, when Yelan's ancestor Rongzhao passed by it. It gives the yaksha Xiao a place to rest and covert support in his fight against evil spirits. It also collects intelligence on notable people entering Liyue. All its staff are Qixing agents, including the boss Verr Goldet and the innkeeper Huai'an.

288.comment: Liyue Qixing: The Qixing take power
288.content: After Rex Lapis was apparently killed at the Rite of Descension, the Qixing at first hunted the culprit. Then a secret message told them the god was not dead, and they abruptly ended the investigation. They announced that he had died failing a divine trial and moved to take sole control of Liyue. This set them against the adepti until the Fatui unleashed Osial, when Qixing, adepti, Millelith and the Traveler joined forces. Ningguang sacrificed the Jade Chamber to defeat him. At the Rite of Parting she told the people that the contract with Rex Lapis had ended and that Liyue must build a new age of prosperity. Keqing told the Traveler that the Qixing always repay their debts. Zhongli, watching in mortal guise, called their seizure of power the best parting gift he could have wished for.

289.content:
Lochknight (also: Lochknights, Lochknight order, Knights of the Lakelight): The Lochknights were the knights of Fontaine's legends: sworn, in silver armour, to protect the Oceanids (spirits born of pure water), the unpolluted springs and one another, and to resist the golden empire of Remuria. Their leader was Erinnyes. They are remembered less as a documented order than as a tale retold in plays, poems and films, and the Fontinalia Festival commemorates them.

Canon itself says their history is "heavily shrouded in legend". Remurians dismissed them as barbarians who worshipped a false god, so most of what survives comes from later romance.

Structure: The Lochknights were a band of sworn knights around a leader, not a state office. The books name a court of followers: Agricane, Blancandrin, Drest, Guillaume of Gellone (whose sword is Narbonnais), Marsile, Naimes, Otkerus of Rhenanie and Tulpin, with Kudenin of Dunnaer named in NPC dialogue. In the Chanson the knights come from many regions and unite behind Erinnyes. There is no recorded rank system, headquarters or founder.

Members: Erinnyes is the one figure tied firmly to the order: High King of Aremorica, a singer who claimed to hear the voice of Egeria, and the unifier of Fontaine's tribes against Remuria. She has her own entry. The other named knights appear only in legend-style sources.

Goals: By the oath, Lochknights protect the Oceanids and the pure springs until "the pure spring flows as before", protect their fellow believers in Egeria, and drive the Remurian "golden usurper" out of Fontaine. Two vows run through every version of the pledge: never draw a sword against those who pledge faith in Egeria, and never compromise in the face of evil. The legends also give the knights a quest for the Pure Grail, a vessel said to grant any wish and wash away sin, and to welcome Egeria back.

Methods: War and oath. Erinnyes united warring tribes by force of arms, then required them to pledge themselves to Egeria, and her army struck at Remurian holdings. Remurian sources call these acts atrocities and call her mad. The legend's version is gentler: courtly councils, tournaments and a quest.

History: The Lochknights are placed in the last years of the Remurian Empire, when Remus' rule over Fontaine was being resisted from the northern border, Aremorica. Erinnyes united the tribes and made her stand. When Remuria sank, Egeria was freed and became the new Hydro Archon, and the knights laid down their armour not long afterwards. A few decades after the fall, the idea of the Lochknight died out. An old legend says Egeria gave a Lakelight Lily to the last Lochknight as a farewell present.

Relations: - **Oceanids and Egeria**: the order's reason for being. The knights serve the "Mistress of Many Waters", and the Oceanids are the spirits born of pure water.
- **Remuria**: the enemy. Remurians, such as the musician Goldoni speaking for Boethius' regime, called Lochknight tales ridiculous ravings.
- **Marechaussee Hunters**: later monster-hunters; some of their members descend from Lochknights.

Reputation: In modern Fontaine the Lochknights are beloved literary heroes. Their adventures are told in plays, poetry and films, such as the historical film "Lochknight of the Lance" (seen in a limited-time event) and a play about a mounted python and the Pure Grail. Remurian-era views were hostile: the Empire called them barbarians, and their tales fictions told by slaves.

Status as of 7.1: Defunct for centuries, existing now only as legend and festival.

No Lochknight story development was found for 6.x or 7.0-7.1. The name still appears in item text, the Fontinalia Festival and Remuria-related lore.

290.content: The Fontinalia Festival commemorates the Lochknights' search for the Oceanids and the return of Egeria. Traditionally, people dress as the knights, raise golden cups and go from door to door asking for pure water. In recent years Furina turned it into something closer to a carnival, trading the pure-water custom for candy, and children now call "Trial or treat!" at each house. A Fontinalia Film Festival, part of the limited-time event Roses and Muskets, was added by the Fontaine Film Association.

291.content: The Lakelight Lily is a pale-blue flower that grows where Water Veins meet, notably in Erinnyes Forest. Its meaning in the language of flowers is "waiting" and "everlasting promise". The legend that Egeria gave a lily of this kind to the last Lochknight as a farewell is the origin of a living custom: Fontainians pick a lily for those starting a long journey, wishing them a road as calm as pure water and a safe return.

292.content:
Maison Cardinalice (also: Cardinal House): The Maison Cardinalice is one of the government offices of Fontaine, based in the Palais Mermonia in the Court of Fontaine. It oversees financial approvals and related administration, which in practice means reviewing and signing off on expense reports and salary payments from other offices.

It is a separate body from the Maison Gestion, which handles documents and general administration, and from the Maison Ordalie, which runs the courts under Chief Justice Neuvillette. Ordinary Fontainians rarely deal with it directly. Most of what is known comes from office workers who must submit paperwork to it.

Structure: No internal ranks, departments or staff names are given in canon. The Maison Cardinalice is one of the offices that share the Palais Mermonia with the Maison Gestion, the Maison Ordalie, the Maison Gardiennage and the Marechaussee Phantom. It receives batched summaries from other offices rather than individual claims.

Leadership: No head of the Maison Cardinalice is named in game text. The wiki infobox lists Chief Justice Neuvillette as leader, but the quests show something narrower: when a sum is large enough, the Maison Cardinalice sends the matter up to Neuvillette for approval, and its requests for written explanations are said to come from him. Treat his leadership as unconfirmed.

Goals: Its role is to control spending and to make sure that salaries and expense payments are reviewed and signed before money leaves the public purse. Workers who deal with it describe a system built around audit trails, including end-of-year checks on where funds came from.

Methods: Approval is slow, written and cumulative. Claims are batched monthly, reviewed, signed and only then paid. If an expense raises questions, the person who made it must submit a written report. For large totals, the Maison Cardinalice submits the matter to Neuvillette himself.

Relations: Its closest working partner in the quests is the Maison Gestion, whose staff depend on it for payment approval. Because Neuvillette signs off on large sums, the Chief Justice sits at the top of its approval chain in practice. It shares the Palais Mermonia with the other Fontainian governing offices.

Reputation: Among those who deal with it, the Maison Cardinalice is seen as slow and exacting. Palais Mermonia bureaucracy is a running joke, and this office is the last obstacle in the payment chain. The Strict Adherence to Office Codes furnishing set, which includes items named after the Maison Cardinalice, recreates the regimented, always-busy look of the Palais.

Status as of 7.1: As of Version 7.1 it is still an active office in Fontaine. Nothing about it was found in Nod-Krai or Snezhnaya content, and no scandal, reform or change of leadership has been shown.

293.content: In A Certain Trifle, Cornelia of the Maison Gestion explains how an office expense is paid. The claimant signs a request; receipts are compiled into monthly reports; everything goes to the Maison Cardinalice at month's end; payment follows once the review and signatures are done. The same approval covers salaries across the Maison Gestion, and the Maison Cardinalice may pass a large sum to Neuvillette. A queried expense needs a written report. Iaune, the Gestionnaire in the quest, decides to buy a keycap himself rather than risk needing the Chief Justice's signature.

294.content:
Maison Gardiennage (also: Maison Gardiennage of Fontaine, Fontaine law enforcement service, Fontainian law enforcement): The Maison Gardiennage is Fontaine's law enforcement service. Its main force is the Gardes, the uniformed officers, together with the Gardemeks, the clockwork meka that patrol with them.
