The Bank's purpose is to channel the flow of Mora and wealth, and Pantalone aims to take the continent's economy out of the gods' hands. According to Vesna, he once told the Tsaritsa that the Bank would become the beating heart of finance for the whole world.

Methods: The Bank lends generously. If a borrower defaults, an agent from the Fatui's debt-collection division is usually sent, using as much force as needed, though other options are tried too. In Nod-Krai the branch gave a loan to Zhuoxin; instead of collecting, it made him a spy for ten years, which he accepted to protect his family. Branches also exchange funds for the Fatui. In Liyue the Bank marks its bags with elemental energy, to identify what belongs to it.

History: **Origins.** Pantalone founded the Bank soon after he became a Harbinger.

**Liyue.** The Liyue branch was set up before the Traveler arrived. In the first Archon Quest chapter it served as a rendezvous for the Traveler and Tartaglia. After Tartaglia's attack on the authorities during the Osial incident, Ningguang made the Bank pay a large sum in reparations, which left its staff resentful. In Endless Smoke she confronted them over spying on her.

Relations: The Bank is tied to the Fatui but is not identical to them, and the exact tie differs by account. Harbingers use its funds, and Liyue's Qixing are wary of it. Tartaglia helps in Liyue. Pulcinella oversees some branch openings. Dottore's research was funded by Pantalone, who in turn received an immortality elixir.

Reputation: Liyue customers know the Bank for generous loans but also for hard methods; rivals such as Gentry De'an claim it used underhanded means to establish itself. Staff stress client service and security. In Snezhnaya it is spoken of as extremely secure.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Bank operates normally with Pantalone as president. The Seals of Life it stored in Snezhnograd were returned to their donors at the end of the 7.1 Archon Quest, and the Bank is negotiating compensation for damaged or missing seals.

Branches continue in Liyue, Sumeru City, Fontaine and Nod-Krai; nothing in 7.1 shows any branch closing.

355.content: The main branch in Snezhnograd has a huge underground complex reached by a short train ride. The most valuable items are stored there. Oprichniki guard it with radios and access cards, monitoring devices and lasers cover it, and the deepest vault is protected by four turrets that Pantalone can control.

356.content: The only non-local bank in Liyue, in Feiyun Slope. It exchanges leftover funds from Tartaglia into Mora. Manager Andrei, receptionist Ekaterina and guards Vlad and Nadia work there; Ekaterina refuses to confirm direct Fatui ties.

357.content: A regional branch in Nasha Town run by Jarosznski. It looks unremarkable outside but is a fortress of defences and alarms inside. It made Zhuoxin into a spy in exchange for his debt.

358.content:
Order of Skeptics (also: Shamaniyya, Nagarjunites, the Skeptics, Vijnanapati, Nasuraia): The Order of Skeptics, which the Akademiya calls the Nagarjunites, is a small group of scholars living in the Girdle of the Sands in southern Sumeru. They descend from an Akademiya Darshan that came to the desert 500 years ago, during the cataclysm, and helped the Pari purify the Harvisptokhm. They have long since cut ties with the Akademiya and are rarely acknowledged. Their creed is the "transmission of knowledge at all costs" and that "conflict is the natural order of Teyvat". In 3.6 their leader Nasejuna turned on the Pari and tried to take the Great Songs of Khvarena for the Abyss Order.

Outsiders also know them by the name Shamaniyya. Their leaders hold the title Nasuraia, also read as Vijnanapati, which the game glosses as "one who has epiphanies". Many people in the rainforest treat them as a myth.

Structure: The order is led by a single Vijnanapati, the equivalent of a sage. Ranks below that are not described, and canon names only a handful of members. The order keeps a camp near the Temir Mountains in the desert. Its old archives burned, so much of its structure and ritual knowledge has been lost.

Leadership: Leaders are called Nasuraia or Vijnanapati. Nagarjuna, a one-armed sage, is counted as the first. The last, Nasejuna, fled in 3.6, and the order is currently leaderless.

Before his betrayal Nasejuna was stationed in the Girdle of the Sands to study the Abyssal phenomenon there. Pyrrho, who calls himself one of the order's oldest qualified members and a desert native, praised him as more knowledgeable than anyone he had met and said he was helping the order recover its traditions.

Members: - **Nagarjuna**: the first Nasuraia, a one-armed sage who led the founding scholars.
- **Nasejuna**: the last known Vijnanapati, now a defector.
- **Pyrrho**: a desert-born member who is suspicious of outsiders.
- **Sosi**: a member who studies the order's documents and keeps looking for the truth despite finding discrepancies between records and reality.
- **Aryadeva**: a former elder who left to write light novels in Sumeru City but is still best versed in the order's traditions.
- **Nagahvaya**: a Herbad who calls himself a Skeptic and a follower of Nagarjuna; he is in the Desert Pavilion.
- **Klingsor**: a former ranger who became an Abyss Herald.

Goals: Under its founders the order's duty was to keep the Harvisptokhm purified and remember the heroes who fought the Abyss. Its stated ideals are the transmission of knowledge at all costs and the belief that conflict is the natural order of Teyvat. Pyrrho says the surviving members want to recover the order's lost traditions and glory. Nasejuna's real aim was different: to use the Great Songs of Khvarena to destroy the Harvisptokhm so that the Abyss would flood Teyvat, which he called bringing truth without mercy to an unjust world.

Relations: - **Pari**: the order's oldest bond, symbolised by the Kory Drums. Zurvan sealed the Oasis after Klingsor's attack, and the Pari still guard the Harvisptokhm.
- **Sumeru Akademiya**: the order was once one of its Darshans, but the Akademiya calls it the Nagarjunites and the two have long been separate. The Akademiya's investigation team led to Klingsor's fall.
- **Abyss Order**: Klingsor, a former member, is now one of its Heralds, and he and Nasejuna worked together.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the order has no leader, and its few members remain in the Girdle of the Sands. No newer Skeptics content was found after the 3.6 Khvarena of Good and Evil chapter.

The Harvisptokhm has been purified and the Sign of Apaosha is gone. Nasejuna and Klingsor are at large, and Pyrrho and Sosi remain in the desert.

359.content: Nasejuna was the last Vijnanapati of the Order of Skeptics, stationed in the Girdle of the Sands to study the Abyssal phenomenon there. He learned that his ancestors, who resisted the land's impurities, were heroes in Khaenri'ah's eyes but were smeared and forgotten by the Akademiya, and he plotted with the Abyss Order. In Khvarena of Good and Evil he guided Sorush and the Traveler to the Great Songs of Khvarena while secretly planning to use them to destroy the Harvisptokhm. When the plot was revealed he showed contempt for the Pari, attacked and fled. He is currently at large.

360.content: Klingsor was once a ranger of the Order of Skeptics and a descendant of Hadura of the Schwanenritter. Resentful of how Khaenri'ahns were remembered, he doubted the order's origin story. Hundreds of years ago he was sent to accompany an Akademiya investigation team into Khaenri'ahn ruins. He found material that confirmed his doubts, heard a "gospel" and became an Abyss Herald, and later led an attack on the Vourukasha Oasis. In 3.6 he gave Nasejuna the documents that won him over and fought beside him. His fate after that battle is unknown.

361.content: Aryadeva is a former elder of the Order of Skeptics living in Sumeru City near the Kalimi Exchange. He left the desert to write light novels and is planning a Light Novel Society, though Yae Publishing House keeps rejecting his manuscripts. Nasejuna calls him a ridiculous old geezer but relies on him, since Aryadeva is the best versed in the order's traditions. After the plot failed, Aryadeva said he had kept one Kory Drum away from Nasejuna on purpose.

362.content:
Pale Star Court (also: Pale Star's royal court, Pale Star Royal Court): The Pale Star Court was the empire and royal court of the Belyi Tsar (White Tsar), whose personal name was Monomakh Snezhnyi. He united the rival Snowland Fae kingdoms of the far north under one crown, and his realm is the direct ancestor of the nation of Snezhnaya. Later texts also use the name for his regime as the first Cryo Archon. It ended when he fell in the Cataclysm about 500 years ago, and Anastasya, the Tsaritsa, took his place.

Fae chroniclers call the Tsar "Emperor" and "lord of all fae". The court's memory survives in Nod-Krai and Snezhnaya through books, a palace-tomb, and fae nobles who remember it. It is history rather than a living institution.

Structure: The court was a fae empire built on clan loyalty. The Tsar sat at the top, with fae Grand Dukes ruling territories under him. The Grand Dukes were clan rulers of peoples such as the Domovoy, and the court had ministers who handled matters like finance. A personal guard, the Druzhna, answered to the Tsar and was mustered in wartime; the Tsaritsa later kept it as her own guard.

Leadership: The Belyi Tsar, Monomakh Snezhnyi, founded and ruled the court. He claimed a "sacred bloodline" that set him above other fae, though the fae chronicle suggests the claim was a way to appear legitimate. He later became the first Cryo Archon and God of Love.

As a youth he was taken into the House of Hesperides by Yalyane Morevna, who taught him the spear, and he fought with a polearm named Frostbreath during his campaign. In the book's account, the Emperor's reasoning was practical: giving in to Miscislav would only invite worse wars for the next generation. He is shown as merciful too, returning the bodies of fallen enemy dukes to their clans.

Members: The court's people were the Snowland Fae: Domovoy, Snegovik and Snegurochka, Vila, Jack Frost and others, plus beings such as Volkodlak and water imps (the Dalegrad clan) who were once rivals. Humans were later admitted by the Tsar. His closest figures include Aksinya (his foster daughter), Zver (a Chimeric Winged Lion he named), Koshchei, Pavlina and Alvis. The Lantern Fae Flins, who claims to be six or seven hundred years old, is listed as formerly of the Pale Star Court.

Goals: At first the court's aim was to unite all fae under one banner and secure the frozen north. After the Tsar learned the truth about Hyperborea and his own nature, his private aim became to complete his ascension as a Primordial Human. He established the Hvergelmir institute to build a "Proto Man" and seek the vacant seat in the court of the stars. This purpose was the Tsar's own, not the court's public programme.

History: **Unification.** The Tsar raised Kitezh, the first city of Snezhnaya, on frozen ground and made it the imperial capital. Seventy-six years later (in the fae calendar), he told the Vila to stop paying tribute to King Miscislav of the Volkodlak. Miscislav accused the court of breaking a standing peace, demanded thirty times the tribute the Vila had paid, and the Emperor refused. Miscislav then attacked Kitezh. In three battles (at Kitezh, in the foothills, at the frozen lake and on the plains) the Tsar killed Miscislav and Grand Dukes Skoldyryt and Vodyanoy with his thrown spear. All remaining fae clans then swore loyalty to him and he took the title Belyi Tsar.

Status as of 7.1: The court no longer exists as a state. It ended with the Belyi Tsar's death roughly 500 years ago.

As of 7.1 its ruins and relics remain: the Pale Crown Palace (the Tsar's mausoleum in the White Birch Snowgrave), the House of Hesperides, and the Tsaritsa's Snezhnaya built on its foundations. Long-lived fae such as Flins, listed as formerly of the court, still carry its memory. No further story about the court itself was found for 7.1.

363.comment: Pale Star Court: Battle of Kitezh and King Miscislav
363.content: King Miscislav, the Blood-Devourer, ruled the Volkodlak and led the Miscislavli alliance. The Vila paid tribute to him until the Tsar's envoys told them to stop. Miscislav then demanded a huge tribute from the Pale Star Court, and the Emperor refused. His host included the Nyholmgarthir (bovine Volkodlak), the Dalegrad (water imps) and the wolf-like Cirnareka. The Tsar threw his spear like an arrow and killed Miscislav, Grand Duke Skoldyryt of the Nyholmgarthir and Grand Duke Vodyanoy of the Dalegrad. Seriviiki of the Cirnareka escaped. Miscislav's skull is said to be kept in the Zapolyarny Palace treasury. A sudden icy fog that misled the Schpekin Legion is recorded by historians, but its cause is unknown.

364.content: Kitezh was the first city of Snezhnaya and the Pale Star Court's imperial capital, built in the fae style on frozen ground. It remained the seat of power until the Tsar moved to Snezhnograd. The Abyss later destroyed Kitezhgrad, and Novokitezhgrad was built to replace it under the supervision of Alvis.

365.comment: Pale Star Court: House of Hesperides
365.content: A mountain manor in Fellfrost Peak and home of the Snegovik and their Grand Duchess. The receptionist Raduzhnaya says it was built by the first Snegovik Grand Duchess after the Belyi Tsar unified the north and founded the Pale Star Court. It has changed leaders but still looks as it did originally. According to a book on Snezhnayan history, the young Monomakh was taken in here by Yalyane Morevna.

366.content: Hvergelmir was a research institute for bio-alchemy and Shadow Realm study, founded by the Belyi Tsar and entrusted to Aksinya. Its goal was to find the stairway to the vacant seat in the court of the stars, using a "Proto Man" as the key to let the Tsar become the Primordial Human. It modified Hyperborean devices into firearms, and Koshchei's work there led to the Aberrant Chimeric Monsters.

367.content: The Druzhna were the personal guard that the Tsar mustered in wartime. They are mostly Vila. Filipov, a fae spy and infiltrator who foiled Skoldyryt's plan in the second battle, later commanded them. After her coronation the Tsaritsa chose not to call the Druzhna against rebels and founded the Fatui instead. Today they answer only to her and are also responsible for containing Shadow Realm breaches, under Vesna.

368.content:
People of the Springs (also: Meztli, Meztli tribe, the People of the Springs): The People of the Springs (Meztli) are one of Natlan's six tribes. They live by the hot springs and coast of Toyac Springs, in a settlement also called "People of the Springs". Their Saurian partners are the swimming Koholasaurs. They are famous as guides, mapmakers, surfers and hosts, and their land is the tribe most popular with visitors. Their current chief is Amina. Mualani, a guide and surf-shop owner, bears the tribe's hero Ancient Name, Umoja ("unity").

The tribe is easygoing and fond of music, fishing, watersports and long soaks. Its chief jokes that seriousness is a rare virtue among her people. It has still produced some of Natlan's most respected warriors, and it suffered heavily in the Abyss's attacks on Natlan.

Structure: Like the other tribes, the Meztli are led by a chief, with the tribe's elders behind them. When Amina's grandfather died, the elders voted her in because of her many new ideas. The tribe shares in Natlan's tribal institutions: its members take part in the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame, and its Wayob, the ancestral spirit in the Night Kingdom, grants Ancient Names to worthy members. Hero names are tied to their tribe, and the Meztli's is Umoja. In the wiki's comparison of the tribes, they are paired with the Hydro element and the Flow-Inverted Wayob Manifestation.

Leadership: Chief Amina leads the tribe. She is young, full of ideas and determined to take her job seriously. She took over after her grandfather died, and the late warrior Atea was her mentor.

Amina's grandfather taught her that "positivity should be our guiding star", and she quotes him. As chief she has designed a new stage, strengthened patrols, run the defence of the tribe during the Abyss invasion and dealt with scammers who used the tribe's legends. She believes the Natlanese dead are reunited in the Night Kingdom. She says that idea is also how Ancient Names carry heroes' memories forward.

Members: - **Mualani**: playable Hydro guide who runs the Leisurely Puffer watersports shop. She bears Umoja and fought in three Night Warden Wars without ever needing resurrection.
- **Amina**: chief.
- **Atea**: an elder warrior with a Pyro Vision, titled Candlekeeper. She died of long-term Abyssal corrosion during the Chapter V story.
- **Kaiulani**: an Ancient Name bearer and veteran warrior.
- **Nuu**: a famous guide who taught Mualani.

Goals: The tribe wants to live well and share that with others. It keeps its springs clean and welcoming, guides travellers safely through Natlan, defends its home against the Abyss, and keeps its heroes' memories alive through Ancient Names. Its founding legend sets its central value: companions matter more than the prize.

Methods: **Guiding.** The Meztli have a long tradition as guides and cartographers. Their ancestors "measured the world with their feet" and turned dangerous paths into maps. Guides are expected to bring clients to their destination safely. As Nuu put it, guides are not treasure hunters.

**Hot springs.** The tribe has both natural and artificial springs. The natural springs are hotter and are for locals and vetted visitors. After some travellers were scalded, an unwritten rule now says outlanders must first acclimatise in the cooler artificial springs. Atea spent years digging new artificial springs so that more visitors could enjoy them.

**Livelihood.** Tourism is the tribe's main income, and its hot springs are famous across Teyvat. The tribe's leisure is fishing, music, surfing and relaxing alongside the Koholasaurs.

Reputation: Across Natlan the tribe is known as the place to relax. An official description calls it the tribe most popular with visitors from afar. Its guides are said to know Natlan better than the birds do.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tribe is at peace and rebuilding after the Abyss war, with Amina as chief.

Mualani is active and travels. In 6.0 she helped throw the Traveler's farewell party before the trip to Nod-Krai. In Linnea's story quest (6.5) she entered the Spirit Envoy Championship in Nod-Krai with her Koholasaur partner Mamala. Meztli traders such as Hinaeia Nui sell the tribe's goods in Nod-Krai. No tribe-specific story developments were found for 7.0-7.1.

key: first chief of the People of the Springs
369.comment: People of the Springs: The first chief and the mysterious island
369.content: For as long as the Meztli have existed, they have told of a mysterious island in a rarely visited Domain that promises wealth and glory. Few have ever reached it, and even top guides cannot guarantee passage. In Mualani's Tribal Chronicle (5.0), she guided the Traveler and two Sumeru scholars there. Statue text left by the first chief tells his story: a restless treasure hunter whose companions trusted him to the end. He gave up the glowing prize, which was also the warning sign of an eruption, to bring everyone home alive. Then he founded the tribe. Nuu explained that the chief left the legend and map on purpose, to lure young guides into the challenge and teach them what he had learned.

370.comment: People of the Springs: Umoja and the heroes of the Springs
370.content: Umoja ("unity") is the Ancient Name of the People of the Springs' hero line. Its known bearers are Uenuku, Tupac and Mualani. Uenuku, the Treader of the Rainbow, travelled with Xbalanque, served in the Grand Alliance and later left. Tupac, Uenuku's descendant, was a giant of a man whom no Saurian could carry. In songs he breaks mountains, makes hot springs, fights a two-tailed whale, and spars with the young Tenoch over a drinking horn. Five hundred years ago he was one of the six warriors who joined Tenoch against the Abyss. Gravely wounded, he lived long enough to carry Mavuika to the Sacred Flame. In Into Eternal Night (5.0), Tupac's projection appeared to Mualani in the Night Kingdom. He passed his memories to her and told her she would unite the tribes.

371.comment: People of the Springs: Atea, the Candlekeeper
371.content: Atea was an Ancient Name bearer with a Pyro Vision, a famous Night Warden Wars veteran, and a neighbour and friend of Mualani. She loved the hot springs and threw parties for her "hot spring buddies", including Kaiulani, Liliuo, Vichama and Mavuika. Years earlier an Abyssal monster had impaled her. She survived, but the corruption stayed in her organs, so she could no longer fight on the front line or bathe in hot water. She turned instead to digging cooler artificial springs for visitors. In Home of the Hot Springs (5.0), she destroyed an Abyssal pylon at an abandoned spring, and the Traveler purified the fresh contamination. She told Mualani she had only days left, gave the Traveler her talisman to deliver to Mavuika, and died soon afterwards with Mavuika at her side. Amina, whom she had mentored, called her an elder she deeply respected. Her spirit later helped the Traveler in the Night Kingdom (5.3).

372.comment: People of the Springs: Hot-spring etiquette of the Meztli
372.content: The People of the Springs keep two kinds of springs. The natural springs are hotter, and locals and vetted visitors use them. The artificial springs are deliberately cooler. After some travellers were scalded, an unwritten rule took hold that outlanders must first get used to the artificial springs, a "trial" in Atea's words, before using the natural ones. In scenes, locals greet guests by asking whether they have had a bath today, and an ailing person may be forbidden hot water altogether.

373.content:
Ragnvindr Clan (also: Ragnvindr Family, House Ragnvindr, the Ragnvindr Clan): The Ragnvindr Clan is a rich and respected Mondstadt family who own the Dawn Winery, the city's premier winery. It takes its name from Ragnvindr, the Dawn Knight, who sided with Vennessa against the aristocracy about 1,000 years ago. It is one of the two known noble houses that were not exiled when the aristocracy fell. Its present head is Diluc.

The winery dominates Mondstadt's drinks trade, and Diluc's profile calls him in effect the uncrowned king of the city because of the money and gossip network that comes with it. The family's recent history is shaped by the death of Crepus Ragnvindr and the break between the family and the Knights of Favonius that followed.

Structure: Diluc is head of the family and owner of the winery. His adopted brother Kaeya belongs to it by adoption.

The household is small. Crepus, the previous head, is dead. Staff are close to the family: Adelinde is head housemaid and ran the winery for a time when Diluc left, and Elzer is a long-serving employee who also minds the winery when Diluc is away. Other named winery staff include the winemaker Connor and warehouse manager Ernest. The staff mourned Crepus and treat Kaeya as part of the household.

History: The family's namesake Ragnvindr was a young nobleman and knight's squire in the aristocratic age who joined Vennessa's rebellion. Later generations ran the winery. Four years before the main story Crepus died, Diluc left the Knights of Favonius, and he returned to take over the winery.

**Ragnvindr.** Ragnvindr was moved by the enslaved Dawnlight Swordswoman of the Wanderer's Troupe, who kept singing of freedom as a gladiator. After she died in the arena he buried her with her sword and took the title Dawn Knight in her honour. He sided with Vennessa. Afterwards, he turned the aristocrats' public baths into the Mondstadt Library. The Ballads of the Squire are said to be his songs.

**Crepus.** Crepus dreamed of becoming a knight when he was young, but he was not accepted. He became a talented winemaker and wished his son to become the most esteemed knight. He took in Kaeya, a boy who was found at the winery about ten years before the main story, and raised him as a son.

Members: Diluc Ragnvindr is the head. Kaeya, adopted by Crepus, is Diluc's estranged brother and is Cavalry Captain of the Knights. Crepus is dead. The founder-figure is Ragnvindr, the Dawn Knight.

Diluc and Kaeya were once close and now keep their distance. Staff in Taste of Home (3.8) say Kaeya is always welcome at the winery, and Adelinde says she has never considered him an outsider. Kaeya's profile calls him an adopted son of the Ragnvindr family and says he has not called Diluc "brother" for a long time.

Goals: Diluc's profile gives him a simple creed behind the winery's motto "Shine True": evil must not go unpunished, he must never settle for mediocrity, and the dawn will one day come. The family's wider role is to supply Mondstadt with wine and cider, and to support the city, as the old mutual support between winery and Knights recalls.

Methods: Business is run from the manor, with Diluc as owner. At his request the winery has developed alcohol-free drinks, including apple cider, which sells as well as dandelion wine. Diluc himself does not drink alcohol, and gives work as the reason. By night he hunts monsters and criminals alone.

Relations: - **Knights of Favonius**: a long history of mutual support; Crepus and Diluc both served the city this way. Since Crepus's death Diluc has distrusted the order, though he still cooperates with it in a crisis.
- **Gunnhildr Clan**: the other house known to have escaped exile.
- **Lawrence Clan**: the former rulers, exiled after the rebellion.
- **Fatui**: Diluc tracked them as the source of the Delusion that killed his father.
- **Dawn Winery**: the family's seat and business; see the Dawn Winery location entry.

Reputation: The Ragnvindrs are among Mondstadt's best-known and most affluent houses. At winery festivities, fathers present their daughters to the unmarried winery master, and onlookers joke that Diluc should stay married to the winery. Diluc is known as the Dawn Winery's owner; few link him to the Darknight Hero.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Diluc runs the winery, remains outside the Knights and keeps up his night patrols. Kaeya remains a Knights captain. No new family developments were found for 6.7 to 7.1.

374.comment: Ragnvindr Clan: Ragnvindr, the Dawn Knight
374.content: Ragnvindr was born into Mondstadt's upper class during the aristocratic age, became a knight's squire and grew sick of the nobles' indifference to the common people. He befriended the enslaved Dawnlight Swordswoman and, after she died fighting in the arena, buried her together with her sword, The Flute. He chose "Dawn Knight" as his title in her memory and took Vennessa's side. After the rebellion he converted the aristocracy's baths into a library. The Ballads of the Squire are said to be his own songs. It is unknown whether he joined the Knights of Favonius or whether the winery began with him.

375.content: Crepus was the head of the family and of the Dawn Winery until his death. He wished for his son Diluc to become the most esteemed knight, and he told him, "Sometimes, life can change in an instant." He raised Kaeya as a second son. When Ursa the Drake attacked the winery's convoy, he used a Delusion, and the power that defeated the drake also mortally wounded him. Winery staff such as Elzer and Connor remember him as a talented winemaker and a father figure. In Taste of Home (3.8), Adelinde says Crepus mixed and named a nearly alcohol-free drink to comfort the young Kaeya after a punishment.

376.comment: Ragnvindr Clan: Dawn Winery household staff
376.content: Adelinde is the head housemaid who kept the winery running while Diluc was away and still says Kaeya is part of the winery family. Elzer is a long-time employee who regarded Crepus as a father figure and manages the winery whenever Diluc is absent. Connor is the winemaker and Ernest the warehouse manager. All are devoted to the family.

377.content:
Rokot (also: the Rokot, Рокот): The Rokot is a covert popular movement in Snezhnaya that serves "the common people" and works against Project Stuzha, the Tsaritsa's grand scheme that has strained the country's supply of Kresnik Kristall. Members use codenames and mostly do not know who one another are. The movement avoids violence and tries to help the public by quieter means. The Fatui keep watch on it and count it as an opponent. Alyosha, Vodyanitsa and Odette are members, and the Traveler joins in the Archon Quest.

The name is the Russian word for a rumble. The Traveler and Paimon joke about whether it means a howl or a gust of wind. The movement acts as an outlet for people who disagree with how the country is run but have no easy way to be heard. Alyosha describes it as giving the disaffected false identities and an outlet for their frustrations.

Structure: The Rokot is deliberately loose. Members get a codename on joining, usually do not meet in person and often do not know each other's real identities, which keeps each one independent and means nobody else is exposed if something goes wrong. Members choose their own methods, so long as the result does not break the group's principles, and they may also choose not to act at all, since many members have never done anything. A president approves new recruits by letter and sends notices to all members.

Leadership: No leader is named. The only authority shown is a "president" who answers recruitment requests, and the leadership's notice to members ends with a motto: "We act only for the greater glory and solidarity of our nation. May the aurora shine ever on and the tundra always stand firm." Nothing identifies the president or where he works.

Members: Alyosha (a hunter from Sretomorozsk), Vodyanitsa (Prima Donna of the Korolevskiy Troupe) and Odette (Prima Ballerina of the troupe and a Fatuus), plus the Traveler. Trapeznikov, a research-minded NPC, also belongs.

Goals: The Rokot wants to improve ordinary people's lives and to see Project Stuzha ended, which is why it opposes the plan's backers and, on occasion, the Tsaritsa herself.

Methods: The Rokot works by gathering information, steering evidence toward people with authority and doing small acts of service, such as recon, repairs and distributing Kristall.

History: Nothing in the sources checked says how the Rokot began. It first appears in the 7.0 Archon Quest after the Traveler reaches Snezhnaya. In Gunfire in the Silent Lands the Fatui officer Polonsky mentions the group to Alyosha, who then explains it to the Traveler. In Silence Alone is Disfavored the Traveler joins. The Chapter VII story then turns on the exposure of Lelek.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Rokot is active. Its president remains unnamed, the codename Lelek is retired, and its members continue everyday good works in Snezhnaya.

Odette is suspended and may rejoin later under a new codename. The Traveler remains a member with a codename of their own choosing. Nothing in 7.0 or 7.1 resolves the long-term fate of the movement.

378.content: Lelek was the Rokot's most famous and most infamous member, an anonymous figure who made ending Project Stuzha an obsession. Vodyanitsa says Lelek used threats, coercion or bribery to change votes in the Veche, unlike the more decent members. Valeriy knows the codename from Armory Palace files as a lone operator. In Lelek's Confession Chugunov blames Lelek for the deaths of two merchants, but Vodyanitsa objects that such a roundabout method is not Lelek's style; the killer was in fact Ronova, disguised as Alyosha. The holder is Odette, who joined while serving the Fatui. Citing the effect of Lelek's radical actions on its reputation and on social stability, the Rokot withdrew the codename for good and suspended her.

379.content:
Royal Energy Commission of Snezhnaya (also: Energy Commission, Snezhnaya Energy Commission, Royal Energy Commission): The Royal Energy Commission of Snezhnaya, often just the Energy Commission, is the state organisation responsible for Snezhnaya's energy upkeep. It maintains the Kresnik's Torches, the furnaces that make Snezhnayan cities habitable, and manages the transport and use of Kresnik Kristall, the ore the torches burn. It answers to Zapolyarny Palace.

Its staff are mostly administrators, inspectors and technicians who travel between torches. A few are scientists: Mitya, an expert in energy technology, also works on Pierro's Project Mistilteinn at the Armory Palace.

Structure: The Commission has a President, a Vice President and rank-and-file administrators, technicians and prospectors who work in the field. The post of President fell vacant on Izmaylov's death and has been covered by an Acting Chair assigned from Zapolyarny Palace, with Zaretsky as Vice President. Its people are constantly on the move, because the torches they tend are spread across the whole nation. Staff such as Rakitina inspect local torches, while others, such as Yelagina and Zaretsky, work in the central Kresnik's Burning Heart beneath Snezhnograd. Zavyalov and others report that outdoor teams sometimes cross paths with Shadow Realms.

Leadership: The Commission has been led by an Acting Chair, Zarechnaya, since its long-time President Izmaylov, an old Domovoy, died. She was sent from Zapolyarny Palace to keep the Commission running until a permanent chair is found.

Zarechnaya says the post could not be left empty, since the Commission is vital to people's livelihoods across Snezhnaya, and hopes to return to the Palace soon. She finds the handover paperwork in perfect order yet suspects things have been carefully hidden, and then shrugs it off as long as the Commission keeps functioning. Zaretsky, the Vice President, grumbles about the High Table and the gangs and says some matters left by the former Chairperson now fall to people lower down. Staff such as Zybina still call Izmaylov "the President" out of habit.

Members: Named staff, all met as NPCs in 7.0, include Zarechnaya (Acting Chair), Zaretsky (Vice President), Yelagina (keeps the central torch's log), Rakitina (inspects a local torch), Zavyalov, Zybina (who has to handle technical problems alone), and Mitya. Izmaylov is the deceased President. Manez is a former member who left for family reasons.

Goals: The Commission exists to keep Snezhnayans warm and alive. Its work is to keep the Kresnik's Torches running, supply them with Kresnik Kristall, and ensure that ore and heat reach every settlement. Rakitina describes the network design: instead of one mega-torch for the entire permafrost, which proved a pipe dream, Snezhnaya maps habitable zones with torches as local nodes joined by railways, cutting the heat lost in long-distance transport. The Eye of Graeae says that before the torches existed the land consisted only of Frigid and Subzero zones, utterly unsuited to human habitation.

Methods: Routine work is inspection and logging: staff listen to a torch, check its exhaust pipes and record its state, then clear faults. Ore is mined mainly in Novokitezhgrad and shipped by rail to every torch. A village such as Alatyr, which has no train station, can lose its deliveries and risk freezing, as a Druzhna soldier fears in the quest Gunfire in the Silent Lands. When teams find a Shadow Realm while travelling, protocol is to leave safely and report it to the Druzhna.

Relations: - **Zapolyarny Palace and the Tsaritsa**: the Commission is affiliated with the Palace, which sent its Acting Chair.
- **Druzhna**: they take over Shadow Realm reports that Commission teams pass on.
- **High Table and the Izmaylov gangs**: Izmaylov led both the Commission and the High Table, so their histories are linked. Gang members say the Commission and Druzhna leave them the thankless jobs.
- **Snezhnaya Royal Railway Transport Bureau**: carries the ore the Commission oversees.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Commission still operates under an Acting Chair, Zarechnaya. Its president Izmaylov is dead.

Content checked for 7.1 gives no Commission-specific story; Mitya's fix note in the 7.1 patch notes only concerns an Elemental Type icon.

380.comment: Royal Energy Commission of Snezhnaya: Kresnik's Torch
380.content: A Kresnik's Torch is a furnace that burns Kresnik Kristall and keeps a temperature-controlled zone alive around a city or settlement. Every Snezhnayan city is built around one, the loading-screen text credits the Belyi Tsar with creating it, and smaller civilian models stand across the land. The most important one is the central torch in Kresnik's Burning Heart beneath Snezhnograd, built soon after the Belyi Tsar's work at the Pale Crown Palace ended, where prototype torches still stand. The Commission is the organisation responsible for overseeing and maintaining them. In gameplay, small torches dispense Kresnik Energy for the Eye of Graeae.

381.comment: Royal Energy Commission of Snezhnaya: Kresnik Kristall
381.content: Kresnik Kristall is the crystalline ore that Snezhnaya burns for warmth. Quest text describes it as power refined from the authority released when the Cryo Dragon lost control in Snezhnaya about 6,000 years ago, and Aksinya says the outpouring turned ley lines into veins of pure crystal. Early settlers are said to have found the veins by following Kristall Bugs. It burns very efficiently, and it is mined mostly in Novokitezhgrad and sent out by rail, with the Commission overseeing transport and use.

382.content:
Rtawahist (also: Rtawahist Darshan, School of Illuminationism, the Rtawahist school): Rtawahist is one of the six Darshans, the great schools of the Sumeru Akademiya. Its field is illuminationism, the study of the stars, including astronomy and astrology. Its members believe the sky reflects truth and that the stars write people's destinies. Its school colour is blue, and its crest shows an elephant-like mascot.

The Darshan's name comes from the Zoroastrian concept of Asha Vahista, "best truth". In Sumeru only academics may study astrology, although other forms of fortune-telling are allowed. Shakir is the current sage. Azar was its sage until Chapter III, when he fell as Grand Sage of the Akademiya.

Structure: Rtawahist is led by a sage, one of the Six Great Sages who sit on the Akademiya's advisory councils. Below the sage come professors, researchers and students. Students may take elective courses in Darshans other than their own, although how often that happens is not stated. Its disciplines include astronomy and astrology. Students work on star charts, dissertations and papers, and scholars keep regular long hours.

Leadership: Shakir is the current Rtawahist sage. Azar was the Darshan's sage and the Akademiya's Grand Sage before he was removed.

Shakir looks stern but is soft-spoken. He is devoted to his work and tracks his tasks on a whiteboard. He once taught Layla and, in the Chapter III quest As All Falls to Emptiness, helped the Traveler with his expertise on dreams and foresight.

Members: - **Shakir**: sage and the Akademiya's expert on dreams and foresight.
- **Layla**: a student of Theoretical Astrology, chronically sleep-deprived, who sleepwalks and finds her work finished in the morning.
- **Azar**: former sage and Grand Sage, now exiled.
- **Haypasia**: a researcher the Akademiya considers a genius for linking to the Irminsul with Spirit Borneol after three years of training.
- **Ashk, Qushji and Farghani**: scholars met in the open world, who watch the sky or calculate star courses.
- **Kaveh's father**: a Rtawahist scholar who entered the Interdarshan Championship 20 years ago and later died helping a caravan stuck in quicksand.

Goals: Rtawahist holds that the stars show the truth about the world and that studying them will lead to it. Ashk says the untouchable sky conceals the truth, and that the stars "show" a destiny rather than decide it, because a decided destiny could be changed. Ashk adds that mortal sight is limited and asks who can guarantee they see all the celestial signs clearly.

Relations: - **Other Darshans**: Rtawahist is one of six schools and the others (Amurta, Spantamad, Haravatat, Vahumana and Kshahrewar) each have a different specialty and colour. Sitt's service-desk line sums up Rtawahist as watching the sky or calculating.
- **The Steambird**: a magazine whose astrology column by Mona is popular among Rtawahist scholars.
- **Cyno**: he is a former General Mahamatra rather than a member, but he arrested Azar in Chapter III.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Rtawahist is led by Shakir. Azar remains in exile in the Avidya Forest, and no new Rtawahist story was found after Chapter III.

Layla, Shakir and other scholars appear in the open world and in events. The Darshan continues its research on the sky.

383.content: Azar was the Rtawahist sage and the Grand Sage of the Sumeru Akademiya. After Greater Lord Rukkhadevata died, he and other sages wanted a new god, and he accepted Dottore's offer to build one. He locked up Naphis and Baladhuri for opposing it, harvested the city's energy through a dream samsara, and threatened Nilou to shut down her performance. In Chapter III Cyno arrested him; after the Irminsul was restored he and his accomplices supposedly repented and were exiled to the Avidya Forest.

384.content: Shakir is the current sage of Rtawahist. He is tall, with long brown hair, a full beard and round golden glasses, and wears a deep blue sherwani. He is stern in manner and soft-spoken in practice. He was once Layla's master and helped the Traveler during As All Falls to Emptiness by contributing his expertise on dreams and foresight.

385.content: Layla is a Cryo character and a student of Theoretical Astrology in the Rtawahist Darshan. She is prone to sleepwalking and loses sleep over academic stress, and believes "the Stars' Blessing" is why she wakes to find her papers completed. Her own character story says she is slower to finish papers than her peers, but has good observation and estimation skills. Her full entry is a separate character entry.

386.content:
Saurian Relics Association (also: Saurian Relics Association (Faction), the Saurian Relics Association): The Saurian Relics Association is a Natlan organisation that gathers, appraises and studies relics left by the ancient saurians. It was founded by Copan, a scholar of the Collective of Plenty. It is poorly funded and of uneven reputation. Its branch at the Chuwen Fair in the Stadium of the Sacred Flame has become a souvenir counter, a notice board and, in the manager's words, a giant flea market.

Its name promises dragon scholarship, but the Chuwen Fair counter's own map description notes that its interests also include many topics unrelated to saurians.

Structure: The Association employs researchers and excavators, accepts donations from the public, and manages excavation sites across Natlan that visitors enter for a fee. At one long-running site, the guard Quipia charges 300 Mora to dig. The Chuwen Fair branch is managed by Siyah, a Child of Echoes. Relics are appraised at an unnamed "headquarters". No present leader is named.

Goals: The Association's stated aim is to study the treasures of the age of the ancient dragons and keep them in Natlan. Its notices say relics must not be sold to foreign merchants or research institutions. Surveying and analysis inside Natlan are allowed once the relevant access fees are paid.

Methods: It appraises and exhibits finds, charges entry fees at dig sites and access fees to foreigners who wish to study relics, and posts "research bounties" with money rewards. Chuno, for example, took a bounty to decipher Iridescent Inscriptions to make up an overspent monthly budget. Its announcements give each find a use, such as a mount saddle or a back-muscle trainer, dated with instruments.

Reputation: Mixed. Siyah admits the collection has "essentially turned into a giant flea market". Researcher Hoa has doubted one of its conclusions. On the other hand, the Speaker's Chamber has publicly thanked the Association for its excavations and said an object related to early Phlogiston Engraving will be used for research at the Temple of Pax.

History: Copan is the earliest known figure. Artifact text describes a scholar of the Collective of Plenty who called himself President of the Association, carried woven scrolls and tinkered with mysterious mechanisms. When the Cataclysm destroyed his scrolls, he put his research aside and helped adapt machines of the secret source from ancient ruins to aid warriors. He later joined the Ochkanatlan Adventure Team and died on the way to the Tonatiuh. At some later point a group of Association members was commissioned to investigate Ochkanatlan and disappeared, so the Association has avoided anything to do with the place.

Relations: It has close ties to the Collective of Plenty (its founder and an investigator) and the Children of Echoes (its shopkeeper and several researchers). The Speaker's Chamber has expressed appreciation for its work. It serves Natlan's public and visitors but refuses relic exports. During Nefer's Research Spillover quest, her private thought is a guess that Zompaynco's arrival might worry the Guild about rivals.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Association is an ordinary part of Natlan life. Its Chuwen Fair counter becomes available to the Traveler once Tona's Flame's Restitution reaches level 50, and it sells goods for Pyro Sigils. Before then Siyah explains that stock has arrived in a random state and is not yet sorted.

387.comment: Saurian Relics Association: Siyah and the Chuwen Fair counter
387.content: Siyah manages the Association's branch at the Chuwen Fair. He is a Child of Echoes, who he says are reputed to have a knack for business, which is why he was made shopkeeper, though he says the shop really needs a storage specialist. He says the Association's official purpose is to collect and sort relics, but in truth it has become a giant flea market. For Pyro Sigils the counter sells weapon ascension materials, Mora and furnishing blueprints. It sits beside the Association's message board.

388.comment: Saurian Relics Association: Association message board
388.content: The Chuwen Fair board posts commissions, hiring notices and announcements, cycling through different messages. Posts include a recruitment drive for analysts, provenance experts and excavators, and finds credited to Hoa, to Akeor with the traveling scholar Tahmures, and to Tizoc of the Collective of Plenty. The Speaker's Chamber answers one post, and a joking thread about Citlali's supposed divination tools also appears.

389.content: Copan was the Association's founder and self-styled president, a scholar of the Collective of Plenty. He died in the Cataclysm era as a member of the Ochkanatlan Adventure Team. Liriwu refers to him as "Uncle Copan" in a note. Little more is stated.

390.content: Members of the Association once took a commission to investigate Ochkanatlan, the ruined city north of the Flower-Feather Clan's territory, and vanished. Manqu, a Child of Echoes who also works with the Association, tells the Traveler that both his tribe and the Association forbid him from going there.

391.comment: Saurian Relics Association: Research bounties and Chuno
391.content: Chuno, a researcher, takes Association research bounties to cover his bills. His current project is deciphering Iridescent Inscriptions, a task he says has never been completed. He is angry at a seller who once sold him fake "Remnants of the Secret Source" and wants only genuine fragments.

392.comment: Saurian Relics Association: Zompaynco in Nod-Krai
392.content: Zompaynco, an investigator from the Collective of Plenty, came to Nasha Town because he heard Nod-Krai had ruins related to saurian relics. He hates the cold, warms himself by a furnace and is more taken with Nod-Krai's machines than with his research. He wants to meet the Frostmoon Scions, and Nefer's quest has him asking for an introduction through Lyylikki. He says the funds he requested are for research, and admits he cannot keep buying "funny little machines".

393.content:
Schwanenritter (also: Schwanenritters, Swan Knights, heroes of Dahri): The Schwanenritter ("Swan Knights" in German) were an order of Khaenri'ahn knights who fought the Abyssal monsters when the cataclysm struck Khaenri'ah about 500 years ago. Led by Knight Marshal Anfortas, they escorted able-bodied survivors up into Sumeru and held the line with machines called Ruin Golems. Their known members all fell, one by one, in a foreign land. Nagarjuna's scholars, the future Order of Skeptics, honoured them as the "heroes of Dahri".

Almost everything known about them comes from texts left in Sumeru's ruins, not from living witnesses. Their story is told through logs, letters and epitaphs.

Structure: Canon gives only fragments of the order's organisation. Its head was the Knight Marshal, and below him were ranks such as Knight Commander and Garrison Commander, whose relative order is unknown. Members carried epithets, such as "Sentinel of the Golden Hall", "Beard-Father" and "Damsel of the Dale". The order's machines were called Mechanical Wardens. Its size, founding and place in the Khaenri'ahn state are not stated.

Leadership: Knight Marshal Anfortas led the order and, when King Irmin was left "indisposed" by the crisis, proclaimed himself Marshal Regent and led the Regnum Concilium Ultimum, the Final Kingdom Council.

Under Anfortas, Hadura served as a Garrison Commander and later as a Knight Commander, and received the epithet "Sentinel of the Golden Hall" for a successful operation that stalled the beasts. Anfortas lost his left eye in the fight that ended with Hadura's execution. A coded message left on Ruin Guards in Dharma Forest, attributed to him, says the Schwanenritters "fought to the last one".

Members: Four named members are known:
- **Anfortas**: Knight Marshal and Marshal Regent, the last of them standing.
- **Hadura**: "Sentinel of the Golden Hall", a Knight Commander. Later called a traitor, executed and given a knight's funeral anyway. Klingsor of the Order of Skeptics later called Hadura his ancestor.
- **Hildric**: "Beard-Father". Died of multiple-organ failure in a foreign land.
- **Ynghildr**: "Damsel of the Dale". Went missing in battle against the dark beasts, leaving only her signet ring and a second personal item.

Goals: First, to hold back the dark beasts that overran Khaenri'ah, and second, to get the survivors who could still fight or work out of the dying kingdom and onto the surface. In Sumeru the aim narrowed to fighting the cataclysm to the end. The Order of Skeptics later took up that purpose.

Methods: The knights fought with Mechanical Wardens, huge Ruin Golems of an earlier design than the common Ruin Guards. Hadura also ordered a proving-ground workshop to activate all its self-defence systems before the evacuation went on, because the workshop was unsuitable for the Wardens' large-scale attacks. In Sumeru the order salvaged parts from broken golems to keep weapons working, for want of spares.

History: **Cataclysm.** Khaenri'ah's use of knowledge from beyond the skies, understood to be forbidden knowledge, ended in an onslaught of dark beasts. While Irmin was unfit to rule, Anfortas took the regency, and the order chose to leave the kingdom.

**Evacuation.** The knights led able-bodied survivors through the Girdle of the Sands and east to the Dharma Forest, using the Ruin Golems against the monsters. Once on the surface, some refugees were afflicted by a strange disease that turned them into monsters, and some of those not yet affected chose to go back underground.

**Last stand.** In Dharma Forest the knights fought beside Nagarjuna's Akademiya darshan, who acknowledged them as the "heroes of Dahri" despite the bad name Khaenri'ahns had earned for the cataclysm.

Relations: - **Khaenri'ah's crown**: the order served a kingdom whose king, Irmin, was incapacitated at the crisis. Anfortas replaced him at the council.
- **Order of Skeptics**: Nagarjuna's darshan fought beside the knights and later continued their cause. Hadura's relatives presumably followed Nagarjuna and joined them.
- **Abyss**: the enemy throughout. The later Abyss Order is a separate story.

Status as of 7.1: The order no longer exists. Its last known member, Anfortas, is presumed dead.

Nothing about the Schwanenritter was found in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content. Their ruins and logs in Sumeru remain the only places their story is told.

394.content: Anfortas was the Knight Marshal of the Schwanenritter. When King Irmin became "indisposed" in the cataclysm, he declared himself Marshal Regent and led the Final Kingdom Council. He led the survivors into Sumeru and fought to the end, losing his left eye to Hadura. Like Irmin, he is one-eyed. See his own entry for his biography.

395.comment: Schwanenritter: Hadura, Sentinel of the Golden Hall
395.content: Hadura began as a Garrison Commander who ordered defensive systems armed so the evacuation could go on. As a Knight Commander they were given the epithet "Sentinel of the Golden Hall" after leading a successful operation against the beasts. Later they betrayed the order and destroyed a machine, and Anfortas executed them, losing an eye. Hadura was the last of Anfortas' comrades, so a proper knight's funeral was granted. Klingsor, much later, called Hadura his ancestor. Canon does not say why they betrayed the order. Their gender is not stated here; the wiki uses "they".

396.content: Hildric, "Beard-Father", died of multiple-organ failure in a foreign land, and the Schwanenritter chronicle asks that he rest in peace there. Ynghildr, "Damsel of the Dale", went missing in a battle with the dark beasts. Only her signet ring and one other item were recovered, and a knight's funeral was arranged. Later quest text reveals she was not simply lost: she became a Shadowy Husk and kept guard over the control module of the Valley of Dahri golem until the Traveler defeated her in Vimana Agama: Jazari's Chapter.

397.comment: Schwanenritter: Ruin Golems and Mechanical Wardens
397.content: Three huge Ruin Golems stand in Sumeru: in the Desert of Hadramaveth, the Valley of Dahri and on Devantaka Mountain. The wiki identifies them as the Schwanenritter's Mechanical Wardens. In Vimana Agama, Jazari notes that the golem's Amiti device carries Khaenri'ahn patterns of an earlier type than those on common Ruin Guards. The golems' work logs are the main source for the order's last days.

398.content:
Scions of the Canopy (also: Huitztlan, Huitztlan tribe, the Scions of the Canopy, Scion of the Canopy): The Scions of the Canopy, also called the Huitztlan, are one of the six tribes of Natlan. They live in a village of huge trees and platforms hung by ropes off the cliffs of Coatepec Mountain, alongside their saurian partners, the Dendro Yumkasaurs. They are known as couriers, hunters and explorers, and they love extreme sports. Their chief is Wayna. The tribe's best-known member today is the Saurian Hunter Kinich, and the Pyro Archon Mavuika was born among them about 500 years ago.

The tribe's hero lineage is the Ancient Name "Malipo", tied to the legendary Turnfire: the ancestor Yupanqui, the cataclysm hero Burkina, and now Kinich have carried it.

Structure: The tribe is led by a chief, currently Wayna, together with a council of elders. Its village, also named "Scions of the Canopy", is a sub-area of Coatepec Mountain. According to the official site, the ancestors hung giant trees on the cliff with ropes and grappling hooks, which gave the tribe its name. Within the tribe operates the Courier's Longhouse, a courier agency led by Michica, which delivers goods that are not too valuable, fragile or dangerous. The tribe also runs a Learning Lodge where elders teach the children for free.

Leadership: Wayna is the chief. He insists he is not as old as the nickname "Uncle Wayna" suggests: in his view, leading the tribe simply means he has the most adventuring experience of anyone in it. He is easygoing and fond of risk, but he still warns people not to be reckless. He borrowed a Spiritspeaker Stone from Citlali of the Masters of the Night-Wind, and he gave it to the Traveler's group when they set out to rescue Kachina.

Members: - **Kinich**: Saurian Hunter, former courier, current bearer of "Malipo" and one of Natlan's six modern heroes. He is bound by contract to the self-proclaimed dragonlord Ajaw.
- **Mavuika**: the Pyro Archon, born to an ordinary Scions of the Canopy family before the cataclysm.
- **Wayna**: the chief.
- **Michica**: manager of the Courier's Longhouse.
- **Vichama**: a famed scout and Ancient Name bearer who helped the Traveler's group find Kachina's Ancient Name. He died defending the village in the Abyss invasion.

Goals: The Scions want to honour their ancestors, keep their bonds with the Yumkasaurs, and serve Natlan as its messengers and pathfinders. For generations they have also cared for Kongamato, the ancient Yumkasaur called the Mountain King, and kept his Abyssal corruption in check.

Methods: The tribe earns its living from delivery and hunting commissions. Its people climb, rappel and grapple across terrain other Natlanese avoid, and they track and hunt dangerous saurians. Visitors come for extreme sports: rock climbing, rappelling, bungee jumping and "volcano parkour". Natlan's local Adventurers' Guild is said to be made up mostly of Huitztlan.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tribe is back in its cliff village under Chief Wayna, rebuilding after the 5.1 Abyss invasion killed many of its people.

Kongamato's corruption is now sealed by a protective shell, so the yearly Turnfire Night is no longer needed, and the Mountain King has offered to train future heroes. No new tribe story developments were found for 6.0-7.1; the 6.x Archon Quests take place in Nod-Krai and 7.0-7.1 in Snezhnaya.

399.comment: Scions of the Canopy: Turnfire and the Malipo name
399.content: The Turnfire was Och-Kan's weapon of oppression. It burned anyone who looked back at it. Yupanqui stole it, used it on the tyrant's army, then looked back and burned for a hundred days before falling into the Night Kingdom. The Ancient Name "Malipo" comes from it. Its bearers are Yupanqui, Burkina and, today, Kinich, whose profile title is "Turnfire Hunt". Malipo is one of the six heroic Ancient Names, and a bearer who truly connects with it can receive memories of earlier holders. Mavuika notes that Malipo also means "cost" or "price".

400.comment: Scions of the Canopy: Kongamato, the Mountain King
400.content: Kongamato is a gigantic Yumkasaurus, Burkina's partner from the cataclysm, who joined the great heroes against the Abyss. Abyssal corruption both stretched his lifespan and threatened his sanity. The tribe kept him asleep in a cave and fed him Mountain King Flamegranates grown from the Mother Flamegranate Tree. Some tribesfolk think he is huge because of a special build, but the Archive says he has just lived a long time and eaten far too much. After the last Turnfire Night a shell formed around him that stops him from absorbing or leaking Abyssal energy. He now trains the tribe's warriors.

401.comment: Scions of the Canopy: Turnfire Night
401.content: Turnfire Night was the tribe's ceremony, usually held every year, to commemorate their ancestors and drain the Mountain King's Abyssal corruption. A flame bearer, traditionally the current Malipo, led a delegation that lit braziers with kindling from the Sacred Flame and carried the fire into Kongamato's cave. In Kinich's story quest the corruption was building up faster than usual. Kinich planned to put Kongamato into a Beastly Rift provided by Enjou, and Wayna reluctantly agreed. Elder Trinidad, believing they meant to kill the Mountain King, smashed the device. Kongamato woke and badly burned him. Kinich and the Traveler subdued the saurian, and Kinich refused his plea to die, telling him to live with his shame. The shell that formed afterwards made this the last Turnfire Night.

402.comment: Scions of the Canopy: Courier's Longhouse
402.content: The Courier's Longhouse is the courier agency based in the Scions' village and managed by Michica. It handles ordinary deliveries, not extremely valuable, fragile or dangerous goods. Michica regularly loses patience with couriers who lose packages. Kinich and his late father once worked for it.

403.content:
Seahook Gang (also: the Seahooks, the original Seahook crew): The Seahook Gang was a gang of thieves and bandits that once held real sway in Nod-Krai, centred on Nasha Town. It no longer exists in its original form: its boss was killed by his own men and the rest scattered. Today the name is used by impostors who want its intimidating reputation. The best-known former member is Jahoda, now an employee of Nefer's Curatorium of Secrets.

Almost everything the world knows of the gang comes from Jahoda's memories, since she joined when it was already established. She describes it as a hard place where making friends was foolish, though some members looked after one another in their own way.

Structure: The gang had a boss, an unnamed man spoken of with a mixture of respect and exasperation, and mid-level leaders such as Zinaida, who brought Jahoda in. Members included skilled earners like Ihanti, who relied on persuasion rather than brute force. Most of the rank and file were thieves who drank, feasted and fought together. The base was a house in Nasha Town where Jahoda had her own room as a child.

Leadership: The original boss is never named. He is shown as shrewd but fond of his youngest member: he coached Jahoda on how to quiet a rowdy crowd, took her stray apple in the middle of a negotiation, and docked her share when she secretly returned a necklace. One of his sayings was "Grant rest to those who seek it", a code Jahoda and Ihanti both remember. Zinaida, who once protected him, later calls him a blood-soaked bandit chief.

Members: - **Jahoda**: recruited as a child by Zinaida; now an employee of Nefer's Curatorium of Secrets and a playable character. Her own entry carries her story.
- **Zinaida**: a former mid-level leader who brought Jahoda into the gang. According to the intel Nefer holds, she now works for the Voynich Guild as a treasure hunter and covert bodyguard of the port supervisor Manez.
- **Ihanti**: a skilled earner and smooth talker who treated Jahoda as a sidekick. In the Intel Quest "They Who Abandoned the Past" (6.2) he is dying, and he is dead by the end of it.
- **Ratfan**: the wiki lists him as formerly of the gang, but canon presents him as a rich merchant who bribed members to kill their boss. Jahoda killed him.

Goals: The gang lived by theft and banditry, according to Jahoda. Ihanti stood out from "dumb scams and petty robberies" by getting victims to hand money over willingly. Beyond profit, no ideology is stated.

Methods: Theft, robbery and swindling, plus rough "business deals" with rich targets. In the one job shown in detail (Jahoda's Character Story 2), the gang captured a merchant known as a black-hearted swindler, made him repay his victims and then split the rest among themselves at an all-night feast.

History: **Rise.** Nothing is known of the founding. By the time Jahoda arrived the gang was powerful enough to be called a hidden force that once controlled Nasha Town.

**Fall.** Jahoda's Character Story 3 says the rich merchant Ratfan bribed members to assassinate their boss, then burned the evidence with oil. The gang fell into chaos and scattered. In a looser account in the Heizou anecdote, Jahoda says the old leader ended up thrown overboard while underlings fought over the scraps.

**Aftermath.** Jahoda stalked Ratfan over many nights, was badly wounded, and eventually killed him. Nefer then took her on as an employee. By Jahoda's story, Nefer had told her where to find Ratfan and saw her as a pawn who might remove a troublesome man.

Relations: - **Nefer and the Curatorium of Secrets**: Nefer employs Jahoda and, in Jahoda's story, pointed her at Ratfan. Nefer keeps watch on what remains of the gang.
- **Voynich Guild**: employs Zinaida as a treasure hunter and bodyguard.
- **Treasure Hoarders**: Nefer once offered Jahoda introductions to more reliable Treasure Hoarders as a career option, and Jahoda refused.

Reputation: The name once carried weight and still frightens people, which is why impostors borrow it. Heizou was relieved to learn his targets were only impostors, since he did not fancy facing the real gang and its international cohort. Jahoda treats the gang as a past to leave behind and says Ihanti was no friend.

Status as of 7.1: The original gang is gone. Impostors still use the name in Nod-Krai, and a few ex-members are said to have crossed to Fontaine.

Zinaida works for the Voynich Guild, while Ihanti and Ratfan are dead. Jahoda works for Nefer. No new Seahook Gang story was found for 6.3-7.1.

404.content: Zinaida is an open-world NPC in Nasha Town, titled Treasure Hunter. She was a mid-level leader in the Seahook Gang and recruited Jahoda. As a child Jahoda would slip out to wake her in the night to talk through bad days, and Zinaida would carry her back to bed. She now guards Manez, the port supervisor, for the Voynich Guild, and says that beats protecting a blood-soaked bandit chief. Nefer invites her to visit Jahoda at the Curatorium; Zinaida says it is best left as it is.

405.content: Ihanti was a Seahook Gang member skilled at persuading people to hand over money, and he took Jahoda along as a sidekick. In 6.2 he posts a bounty at the Adventurers' Guild with a stolen pendant as collateral. When Jahoda finds him he is terminally ill, nearly blind and has been robbed. He says his wife and daughter are gone. He asks to be left to die in peace, reminds Jahoda of the boss's code, and gives her a doll he made himself. He is dead the next day and leaves a short letter.

406.content: Ratfan was a wealthy Nod-Krai merchant. According to Jahoda's Character Story 3, he used money to have gang members kill their boss, burned the evidence, and bought intelligence from a mysterious businesswoman. Jahoda hunted him over many nights, then killed him in revenge. He is dead before the Traveler reaches Nod-Krai.

407.content:
Seven Pillars (also: Seven Sages, seven monk-kings, King Deshret's Seven Pillars, Seven Pillars of King Deshret, Seven Pillars of Al-Ahmar): The Seven Pillars, also called the Seven Sages or seven monk-kings, were the chief retainers of King Deshret (Al-Ahmar), the desert god-king of ancient Sumeru. He gave them his power, and they served as his "pyramid of authority". Three were gods he had defeated: Heryshaf the Goat King, Sobek the Crocodile King and Thoth the Ibis King. Bennu and Shesepankh were intelligent constructs he built, and Hermanubis was a human sage raised to be his familiar. The seventh, the Dendro Dragon Apep, was named a Pillar by Deshret but never accepted it.

Almost all of them are gone. Hermanubis died long ago. In 6.6 the three Kings, who had been shut in Aaru for thousands of years, were freed, and Bennu and Shesepankh were woken. Together they voted to open Aaru to the people of Sumeru.

Structure: Heryshaf stood at the head, as deputy-king and Minister of Ministers. Heryshaf, Sobek and Thoth were the highest-ranking and are called the Three Retainers. Each Pillar had a style of office. Heryshaf was Minister of Ministers, Sobek Captain of Captains, Thoth Scribe of Scribes, Hermanubis the Greatest of Sages, Bennu the Most-Radiant and Shesepankh the Most-Holy. Apep carried the title Dragon King, the Supreme Spirit, which Deshret and the other six devised and which Apep herself dismissed.

Leadership: Heryshaf was chief of the Pillars and the "right hand" of King Deshret. Above him stood only the king, who raised the Pillars to run his realm. Hermanubis led the priestly class. A Pillar's rank came from the king, and as Thoth puts it, a retainer's fate, including any chance to walk away, was the king's to decide.

Goals: The Pillars existed to serve Deshret's rule and his dream of protecting his people. In the Lay of Al-Ahmar, the three Kings urged him to seek a way past the Heavenly Principles by taking control of the past and defeating death. In 6.6 Heryshaf says Deshret's greatest wish was to protect his people, which is the standard he asks the Pillars to apply when deciding what to do with Aaru.

History: **Origin.** Several thousand years ago Deshret split his power among sages across the desert. Among the Pillars, Sobek, Thoth and Heryshaf had been gods defeated in the Archon War. The Lay of Al-Ahmar says the three urged Deshret to defy the Heavenly Principles after he mourned his losses. Heryshaf and then Thoth were rebuked, but Sobek talked Deshret round to seeking forbidden knowledge and immortality. In that legend Deshret then built a huge labyrinth and shut himself inside, and his kingdom was buried by the sand in a single night.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Pillars no longer act as an order. Heryshaf, Sobek and Thoth are free, and Bennu and Shesepankh are awake. Hermanubis is gone, and Apep keeps her distance.

Heryshaf and Thoth have settled, for the time being, in the Temple of Silence, subject to Sethos's agreement. They declined to move their statues there, as Thoth refuses to leave his statue in Hermanubis's home. Aaru is open and the people of Sumeru may modify it. No new content about the Pillars was found for 6.7 to 7.1.

408.content: Heryshaf, Sobek and Thoth were the highest-ranking Pillars. The Lay of Al-Ahmar curses them as the three retainers who flattered Deshret into seeking forbidden knowledge. Heryshaf is enigmatic and neutral and gives few opinions, but he is dry and sharp in 6.6. Sobek was once hot-tempered and competitive but has grown easygoing after thousands of years of tabletop games. Thoth is clever, quick-witted and fond of chess. His nickname for the others, "Goatie" and "Croco", appears in 6.6. Their long confinement softened them, and Thoth says prison can teach a person to cherish what they have.

409.content: Bennu and Shesepankh were intelligent constructs made by Deshret, not gods. Bennu guarded the gates of Aaru and the Golden Slumber within, and is serious, earnest and stern with careless colleagues. Shesepankh oversaw all the Jinn, whose mother was Nabu Malikata, and is leisurely, curious and fond of questions. They stood still after Deshret's death. In 6.6, Heryshaf woke them by invoking the right of the Three Kings, and they responded "Saint Bennu" and "Saint Shesepankh" with their will awakening. Bennu has said he admires Hermanubis most among the Pillars, while Shesepankh misses Hermanubis's willingness to take responsibility.

410.comment: Seven Pillars: Hermanubis and the Temple of Silence
410.content: Hermanubis was a Tighnar sage and warrior picked by Deshret to be his familiar, the only Pillar to rise from humanity. He was sincere, steadfast and kind, and he guided the priests. After Deshret's fall he took his followers to Tulaytullah and founded the Temple of Silence to guard Deshret's knowledge and technology. When the king of Gurabad attacked, he shattered himself and left his power to his followers. The wiki says two Ba fragments of his power were later held by the Temple, and that they were fused within Cyno. Heryshaf called Cyno "Hermanubis's representative" in 6.6.

411.comment: Seven Pillars: Apep and the seventh seat
411.content: Deshret named the Dendro Dragon Apep a Pillar in his pact with her, but she never accepted it, and the other six never met her in council. Thoth jokes that she is like a card one never draws. Her relations with Deshret were a bargain for forbidden knowledge. In 6.6 Heryshaf says Apep and Hermanubis's representative had both voted ahead of time to open Aaru.

412.content:
Shenglu Hall (also: Shenglu Chamber): Shenglu Hall governs Liyue's glazed ceramics industry. It is one of the Eight Trades, the commerce sectors that answer to the Liyue Qixing. Its members are said to descend from tribes that lived near the Chasm long before Rex Lapis arrived, and the trade depends on materials from the Chasm.

The Hall is one of only four of the Eight Trades named in canon. In English its name is a "Hall", which follows the Chinese word for a government office.

Structure: Shenglu Hall is a trade body, not a military or religious order. Canon names an industry representative, Miss Ruoyu, who speaks for the glazed ceramics trade, and a research department, Human Culture and Civilization Research, headed by Wanyu. Ordinary members are ceramics merchants and craftspeople, who are told to follow the Qixing's guidance.

Leadership: Miss Ruoyu is the Hall's industry representative.

She has been discussing the reopening of the Chasm mine with the Tianquan, Ningguang. The notice says she may go to inspect the situation herself because of the continued incidents there. Nothing more is known about her.

Members: - Miss Ruoyu: industry representative.
- Wanyu: Head of Human Culture and Civilization Research. A scholar who was on her way to a conference when two Geovishap Hatchlings and three Pyro Slimes attacked her near Lingju Pass. Zhongli and the Traveler saved her. She had seen four miners and a child heading toward Nantianmen and said so.
- Muning: not an official of the Hall but a specialist of the Ministry of Civil Affairs posted at the Chasm. Canon says his family plays a significant role in the Hall and the porcelain trade.

Goals: Keep the glazed ceramics trade supplied and calm. The Hall's main concern in canon is getting the Chasm mine open again, because its ceramics rely on resources from that area.

History: According to the Chasm safety technician Jinwu, tribes already lived near the Chasm before Rex Lapis arrived. They gathered Glazed Sand Crystal and traded finished porcelain. After he came they made blood pacts with his yaksha and became his allies, fighting Azhdaha and the monsters of the cataclysm. Most later moved to Liyue Harbor and formed Shenglu Hall, whose glazed ceramics were an art handed down through the generations.

Relations: Under the Liyue Qixing, with Ningguang as the Tianquan dealing with its representative. A sister Hall in the Eight Trades. The Ministry of Civil Affairs runs the Chasm and posted Muning there. Its trade need links it to the Chasm Exploration Team's work.

Reputation: Jinwu calls its members nitpickers. Beyond that, canon does not describe how the Hall is regarded.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Hall remains an active part of the Eight Trades. Nothing about it was found in 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 (Snezhnaya) content. Its most recent canon appearance is its notice about the Chasm mine.

413.content: The Feiyun Slope bulletin board carries a Shenglu Hall announcement. Industry representative Miss Ruoyu and the Tianquan have discussed restarting the Chasm mine and made progress. Ningguang, speaking for the Qixing, expressed deep concern about the closure's effect on the glazed ceramics trade and promised to organise the reopening quickly. Because of continuing incidents, Miss Ruoyu says she may investigate personally. Ceramics merchants are told not to panic and to follow the Qixing's guidance.

414.content: Wanyu is a scholar of Shenglu Hall and head of its Human Culture and Civilization Research. In the Historia Antiqua story quest she appears in the third part of No Mere Stone, attacked by monsters near Lingju Pass on her way to a conference. She is rescued, tells Zhongli and the Traveler that she saw four miners with a child, and leaves for her conference.

415.content:
Shogun's Army (also: Shogunate Army, Bakufu Army, Shogunate forces, Inazuma Shogunate army, Army of the Shogun): The Shogun's Army is the military of the Raiden Shogun, Ei, and of the Inazuma Shogunate. It keeps peace and order across Inazuma and is divided among the three bodies of the Tri-Commission. The Tenryou Commission, led by the Kujou Clan, provides the main fighting force. The Kanjou Commission handles border security, and the Yashiro Commission handles protection of shrines, festivals and public events. Some members serve the Shogun directly. Its soldiers are also called Shogunate Samurai, and their ranks are modelled on those of the historical Tokugawa shogunate.

Players first meet the army enforcing the Vision Hunt Decree and the Sakoku Decree in Chapter II, and fighting the Watatsumi Army around the Kujou Encampment in Kannazuka. After the Traveler and their allies brought the Vision Hunt Decree to an end, the army stopped seizing Visions, and a ceasefire now stands between it and the Watatsumi Army.

Structure: Soldiers are assigned to a commission, and each commission gives them a different job.
- **Tenryou Commission**: the executive arm of the Shogun and the army's main fighting force. It handles security and military matters and is led by the Kujou Clan.
- **Kanjou Commission**: guards Inazuma's borders, finances and customs. Its soldiers, under the Hiiragi Clan based in Ritou, are the ones who stop travellers at the port.
- **Yashiro Commission**: protects shrines, festivals and public events. It is led by the Kamisato Clan.

A few serve the Shogun directly, outside any commission: Hatamoto and the Okuzumeshuu.

Leadership: The Raiden Shogun, Ei, is the army's head, and the Kujou Clan commands it in her name through the Tenryou Commission. Kujou Sara, an adopted tengu, and Kujou Masahito are its two Generals.

Sara is described as the pride of the army. She is the Vision Hunt Decree's main enforcer, she surveys battle lines and plans training herself rather than commanding from the rear, and she is said to hold herself to a regimen over ten times as tough as ordinary troops. Her profile says she gave clear orders forbidding harm or exploitation of civilians while carrying out the decree. Masahito, the eldest son of Kujou Takayuki, commands at the Kujou Encampment.

Goals: The army exists to keep order and defend the Shogun's realm. Under the Vision Hunt Decree, the Tenryou Commission's job was to seize Visions across Inazuma, which were to be set into the Statue of the Omnipresent God in service of Ei's pursuit of Eternity. The Tenryou Commission also had the stated aim of putting down the Sangonomiya rebellion, and the Kujou Encampment was set up to guard against revolt from Watatsumi Island. Sara in particular believed that Visions in the hands of people with "incorrectly aligned" minds would unsettle the foundations of Inazuma.

History: Most of the army's visible history is recent. About a year before the Traveler's arrival, the Shogun instituted the Sakoku Decree and the Vision Hunt Decree, with the Fatui manipulating the Tenryou and Kanjou commissions behind the scenes. The Tenryou Commission carried out the Vision Hunt. In response the Sangonomiya Resistance (the Watatsumi Army) formed, and the two armies fought a war that had stalled by the time the Traveler arrived. The Traveler and their allies helped end the Vision Hunt Decree, and the Shogun's Army agreed a ceasefire with the Watatsumi Army, signed by Kujou Sara and Sangonomiya Kokomi with the Traveler as witness.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the army remains Inazuma's military, but under a more open, post-decree Shogunate. The Vision Hunt and Sakoku decrees are gone and the ceasefire with the Watatsumi Army holds.
