The Tenryou Commission has no confirmed new commissioner: Kamaji is acting clan head, Sara and Masahito remain Generals, and Takayuki is under house arrest. No Shogun's Army events were found in the 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 (Snezhnaya) content.

416.content: The Tenryou Commission is the Shogun's executive arm and the part of the Tri-Commission responsible for security and military matters. The Kujou Clan leads it, and its troops are the army's main fighting force. It enforced both the Vision Hunt Decree and the Sakoku Decree, which gave it the worst desertion problems of the three commissions. Its leadership is unsettled after Takayuki's collusion with the Fatui was revealed.

417.content: The Kujou Encampment in Kannazuka is the headquarters of the Shogun's Army under the Tenryou Commission and was built to guard against rebellion from Watatsumi Island. Its fortress is attributed to Kujou Shigeyori. Kujou Masahito, the Shogunate Officer Toranosuke and the yoriki Iwakura Mitsunari are among the NPCs there.

418.content:
Shuumatsuban (also: Shiyuumatsu-Ban, Shuumatsu-ban, the Shuumatsuban): The Shuumatsuban is a secret unit of ninja in Inazuma, part of the Yashiro Commission's hidden side and answerable to the head of the Kamisato Clan, currently Kamisato Ayato. Most Inazumans do not know it exists. It takes on matters that are awkward for the higher-ups to handle openly. Its best-known member is Sayu, a sleepy young ninja who is far better at hiding from work than doing it.

The name is written 終末番 and glossed by the wiki as "End Squad". The wiki reports its informal slogan, taken from a fortune-slip series, as a promise to send in the Shuumatsu against traitors and criminals alike. Inazuma's safety is its stated concern, but it is neither public nor peaceful.

Structure: There is no public structure. The unit reports to the Kamisato Clan head, who is also the Yashiro Commissioner. Beneath him are ninja and support staff, with most identities classified.

Ayato says the unit reports directly to the head of the Kamisato Clan, and it passed to him when his father died. Orders are carried by staff such as Ogawa, who delivers orders and receives reports on ambush missions. Kazuaki appears in Thoma's hangout looking after the unit's stored belongings, and Kano Nana is assigned to keep an eye on Sayu. Koharu, a Kamisato household servant, is a ninja in training. Members receive a monthly salary; Sayu's is 200,000 Mora.

Members: Sayu is the best-known ninja. Other named ninja include Hisashi, Gaumaru and the ninken Inu Shoushou. Most members are orphans raised from a young age by the unit.

Ayato says the unit takes in orphans and raises them, which he considers the surest way of securing loyalty. Sayu was raised there since childhood and is very loyal despite her laziness. Dogs also serve: Inu Shoushou is a ninken in ninja attire, paired with a human partner. Identities are classified so thoroughly that members who die on top-secret missions are not publicly commemorated.

Methods: Ninjutsu and stealth, escape and concealment, and combat when needed. Sayu explains in her hangout that the unit deals with matters that are "inconvenient" to the higher-ups, and that this sometimes includes ambushing people. Ayato describes the unit as his means of resolving situations he cannot involve himself in directly. Ninken serve as partners.

Goals: Keep Inazuma safe and deal with threats, traitors and criminals without publicity, in service of the Kamisato Clan and the Yashiro Commission. Ayato describes his own work as being for all of Inazuma.

Relations: Its closest tie is to the Kamisato Clan and Ayato, who commands it. Ayaka cares about Sayu's wellbeing and has arranged for Kano Nana to watch over her. Thoma deals with the unit with Ayato's consent. In Sayu's hangout, Ogawa is aghast when a client asks the unit to move against the Tenryou Commission.

Reputation: Almost no one in Inazuma knows it exists, and fewer know that Sayu belongs to it. Those who do, mostly Kamisato Clan insiders and the Traveler, see it as loyal and efficient, if grim.

History: Before Ayato, his father led the unit. Players first met it in Version 2.0 with Sayu's release, and its inner workings were shown in Sayu's and Thoma's hangout events (both tagged 2.2 on the wiki).

Status as of 7.1: Active and still secret as of 7.1. No later story has changed its status in the sources checked.

419.content: Sayu is the unit's "resident ninja" and is famous for avoiding work. She sleeps and hides to grow taller and has mastered escape and concealment techniques accordingly. When missions appear, she vanishes, and by the time she is found a more suitable ninja has been assigned. Her colleagues know that she will not betray the unit's principles or shirk truly important jobs. Ayaka has arranged for Kano Nana to keep an eye on her. Her own entry carries her full details.

420.content: A red Shiba ninken in ninja attire, with scarring near the left eye. He and his owner went on missions together until the owner left on a top-secret mission and never returned. Shoushou waited by the shore near Konda Village. Thoma and the Traveler eventually calmed him with the owner's old training kunai, which Kazuaki found in the warehouse. The unit agreed to cover his expenses.

421.content: In his voice-overs Ayato says it is a secret unit reporting directly to the Kamisato Clan head, and it came to him after his father passed. It lets him act where he cannot appear himself. He adds that most members are orphans raised in the unit from childhood, which makes their loyalty close to guaranteed. In another line he hints that the unit is not his only resource.

422.content:
Snezhnaya Royal Railway Transport Bureau (also: Transport Bureau, Railway Transport Bureau, Chicota, Snezhnaya Imperial Railway Transport Bureau, Transportation Bureau): The Snezhnaya Royal Railway Transport Bureau, usually called the Transport Bureau and sometimes Chicota, is the organisation in charge of Snezhnaya's railway system. Its staff run Central Station in Snezhnograd and the trains that cross the snowfields. The wiki also notes an uncommon translation as the Snezhnaya Imperial Railway Transport Bureau.

Canon treats it as both a transport service and a guardian of order. Weapon lore makes the head of the Chicota the "guardian of law and order" and gives each head an oath. The wiki page on the organisation is only a stub, so most of what is known comes from NPC dialogue and item text.

Structure: Named job titles in the Bureau are Conductor, Safety Officer and Ticket Agent. Conductors work on the platforms and aboard trains, safety officers stand watch at the station concourse and platforms, and ticket agents sell passage. Staff listed at Central Station include the conductors Aryna, Bazhenov, Kholodnaya, Kira and Rudov, the safety officers Gurevikov, Iliana and Sochikov, and the ticket agent Voskresensky. Other conductors such as Lukova and Baryatinsky are found aboard trains that can be summoned at several stations.

Leadership: No present-day head is named. Weapon lore describes the leader of the Chicota as the keeper of law and order within Snezhnaya, who must judge by the law that binds all living beings even when he feels sorrow and compassion as a person.

Goals: The Bureau's duties, as seen in its staff, are safe and orderly travel and the security of the stations. Bazhenov describes Snezhnograd Central Station as the lifeline of the city and the city as the heart of Snezhnaya, so even a tiny error is unacceptable. The oath adds a larger aim of sanctioning acts of terror and preserving peace along the long borders.

Methods: Staff manage crowds, ask passengers to board and leave in an orderly way, and guard the exit gates. Kira says that, under new regulations, staff are authorised to carry out random checks on anyone seen as a potential risk, including luggage inspection and questions about the traveller. The official map text for Central Station confirms that visitors pass inspections by Bureau staff before taking the elevator up to the centre of Snezhnograd.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Bureau remains active, with staff at Central Station and on trains. No Bureau-centred story was found in the sources checked for 7.0 and 7.1.

The Bureau is mainly a world-building organisation with ambient NPCs and the Covenant of Frost and Snow weapon lore. This file is intentionally short because canon about it is thin.

423.comment: Snezhnaya Royal Railway Transport Bureau: Chicota
423.content: Chicota is the alternate name of the Bureau used in the Covenant of Frost and Snow text. Its head is the guardian of law and order in Snezhnaya, and each head swears the oath that descends from the legend. The weapon was said to be given to such a guardian, not to Eprokin, an unexplained name.

424.comment: Snezhnaya Royal Railway Transport Bureau: Central Station staff
424.content: Central Station is the largest station in Snezhnaya and the entry to Snezhnograd. Visitors who leave the platforms pass inspection by Bureau staff before riding the elevator into the city. Bazhenov watches the exit gates, Gurevikov and Iliana keep platforms orderly as safety officers, Kira greets arriving passengers, and Voskresensky acts as a ticket agent.

425.comment: Snezhnaya Royal Railway Transport Bureau: Train conductors
425.content: Lukova can be met aboard a summonable train at Central Station, Svetloledovka, Sretomorozsk and Rankova Zorya. Baryatinsky serves on a train reachable from Central Station, Morepesok and Rankova Zorya. He emphasises passenger safety and quick corrective action if the train is threatened.

426.content:
Snezhnograd Veche (also: the Veche, Veche, Snezhnogradskoye Veche): The Snezhnograd Veche (Snezhnogradskoye Veche, "the Veche") is Snezhnaya's legislative assembly. It sits in the Veche State Hall in Snezhnograd and decides matters by majority vote in sessions chaired by a Speaker. The Tsaritsa founded it to take over the administration once the fae princes' rule ended. The Speaker is the Fatui Harbinger Pulcinella, and the Fatui steer most of its decisions.

The word "veche" belongs to medieval Russian tradition, where it names a public assembly that debated and decided key matters. In Snezhnaya the body has kept the name and the procedure, but its members are mostly the powerful: Harbingers, nobles, merchants and officials, each speaking for an interest group.

Structure: Sessions are chaired by a Speaker, who opens the floor, manages motions and calls the final vote. Business follows a pattern: officials present reports, representatives speak in turn, a proposal is drafted or amended, then the members vote and the Speaker announces the result by percentage. Policies are set for a Veche "period" and stay in force until the next one. A new proposal follows "the usual procedure" and is raised as a motion at a later session. Visitors may attend from the audience seats if arranged in advance, but they cannot speak.

Leadership: The Speaker is Pulcinella, the Fifth Fatui Harbinger, "the Rooster", who is also Mayor of Snezhnograd and of Glupov. Members call him "Lord Rooster" at sessions.

The first Speaker, also the first Mayor of Snezhnograd, was the human Ioanna Ivanovna N., a former Hexenzirkel witch who was appointed by the Tsaritsa and later became Pulcinella's teacher. Sandrone calls Pulcinella the linchpin of the Veche, because everything involves him and he knows how to mediate any issue, which she says is what the Tsaritsa values most in him. Councillor Euphrosiniya complains that he finds excuses to dismiss her heating proposals, while Councillor Golitsyn says his house stands with the Rooster.

Members: Known members and speakers in the 7.0 and 7.1 story:
- **Pulcinella**: Speaker.
- **Pantalone** ("the Regrator"): finance and the Northland Bank.
- **Tartaglia**: speaks for the Fatui soldiers. He privately sympathises with Stuzha's critics and keeps raising concerns, but says he has held back from casting a dissenting vote because the Tsaritsa would never let him get away with it.
- **Sandrone** ("the Marionette"): speaks for engineers and researchers.
- **Euphrosiniya Ignatyevna Trubetskaya** ("Euphie"): Privy Councillor and head of House Trubetskoy. She has put forward at least five proposals for heating in the town of Zolnyy.
- **Eteri Vsevolodovna Strivozha**: Vila councillor, descendant of Saint Strivozha, and nostalgic for the Belyi Tsar's age.
- **Andrei Dmitrievich Golitsyn**: second-rank noble, Active Privy Councillor.

Goals: Officially the Veche exists to handle the administrative issues that arose when the fae princes lost their power. In practice its work under Pulcinella is steering national policy, above all the long Project Stuzha energy-rationing program. In the story, members argue over the fairness of distribution, the interests of factories and soldiers' families, and whether the Fatui's central planning is sustainable.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Veche continues to meet under Speaker Pulcinella. Project Stuzha was kept going in 7.0, then paused.

After Ronova lost her Authority in 7.1 the wiki says Project Stuzha resumes, though no vote has been shown. No new Veche story was found in the 6.x Nod-Krai content or in 7.1 beyond this context, and no change of Speaker is known.

427.comment: Snezhnograd Veche: The Speaker and the Rooster
427.content: At Veche sessions the Fatui Harbinger Pulcinella is addressed as "The Rooster" or "Lord Rooster". As Speaker he reports statistics, calls "Order", opens and closes the floor, supports the drafting of proposals, and announces votes. He ends sessions with a standard line about debating "only for the greater glory and solidarity of our nation".

428.content: The Veche's first chairperson was a human named Ioanna Ivanovna N., codename "J". She was a member of the Hexenzirkel with no magic or combat training, left the witches after marrying, and was appointed by the Tsaritsa as the first Mayor of Snezhnograd and Speaker. She mentored Pulcinella, and Golitsyn credits her grace for his house's standing. She died centuries ago, and in the Hexenzirkel story her line of followers continues.

429.comment: Snezhnograd Veche: Project Stuzha and the Veche vote
429.content: Project Stuzha is a set of energy reforms passed by the Veche that cut household and factory use of Kresnik Kristall so that energy can be sent to the Armory Palace. It was intended to last about six months but was extended repeatedly by majority vote, and the 7.0 vote kept it with 61%. Pierro later reveals it served Project Mistilteinn, the Tsaritsa's weapon against the Heavenly Principles using Stellar Linchpins.

430.comment: Snezhnograd Veche: Snezhnograd Veche State Hall
430.content: The Snezhnograd Veche State Hall is where the Veche holds its regular meetings. Its map description says citizen representatives from various groups deliberate on newly issued laws, in a tradition kept from Snezhnaya's early days, and that it is presided over by "The Rooster". In the hall are the councillors Eteri and Euphrosiniya and the Privy Advisor Golitsyn.

431.content:
Spantamad (also: Spantamad Darshan, School of Elementalism, the Spantamad school): Spantamad is one of the six Darshans of the Sumeru Akademiya. Its field is elementalism, the study of the elements and the elemental reactions and changes that follow from them, with related work in Ley Line studies and alchemy. Its school colour is red. Because Ley Line research needs fieldwork, it has the most Driyosh, the Akademiya's traveling scholars. Lisa of the Knights of Favonius and Cyno both studied here.

Its crest shows a peacock with seven feathers above a tree, which the wiki reads as the seven elements and the Ley Lines of the Irminsul. The Darshan's name comes from the Zoroastrian goddess Spenta Armaiti, who is associated with the earth. Spantamad has also had the highest percentage of Interdarshan Championship winners.

Structure: Spantamad is led by a sage, one of the Six Great Sages, and staffed by professors, researchers and students. A large share of its scholars are Driyosh: they travel in the field to study Ley Lines. Its disciplines include alchemy, elemental science and Ley Line studies.

Leadership: Alkindi is the current Spantamad sage. Cyrus, a retired professor, is a former sage.

Alkindi was once Cyrus's classmate and rival. He threw himself into many research fields for years before becoming sage, and his receding hairline is blamed on academic stress. He is tall, with grey hair and round blue goggles, and wears a crimson sherwani. In As All Falls to Emptiness (Chapter III) he helped the Traveler by investigating Ley Line anomalies.

Members: - **Alkindi**: the current sage.
- **Cyrus**: a retired professor and former sage who raised Cyno as a foster son.
- **Lisa**: a former student who graduated in two years, got disillusioned with the Akademiya and joined the Knights of Favonius.
- **Cyno**: a former student of Cyrus who became General Mahamatra.
- **Hosseini**: a Driyosh from Vimara Village, a Spantamad researcher on Ley Lines who is under 30 but looks middle-aged from thesis stress. He appears in Version 2.2's event quests.
- **Abattouy**: a researcher who studied mechanical lifeforms and was expelled for continuing; he later built Karkata.

Goals: Spantamad researchers treat the Seven Great Elements as the essence of all matter and life. They aim to understand elemental reactions, how Ley Lines behave and what alchemy can produce, and to apply that knowledge. Hosseini's own goals show the school's practical side: he wants to use ancient devices such as the Energy Amplifier and Pursina's Spikes, and regrets that the Spikes lie unused in the Akademiya's warehouses.

Relations: - **Other Darshans**: Spantamad is one of six, alongside Amurta, Rtawahist, Haravatat, Vahumana and Kshahrewar. Rtawahist, its sibling in astronomy, also had its sage replaced after Azar's fall.
- **The Knights of Favonius**: Lisa carries her Spantamad training to Mondstadt and works as the order's librarian.
- **The Fatui and Sumeru politics**: nothing in the sources read ties the Darshan as a whole to the Fatui plot, though Cyno, once its student, played a key role in Chapter III.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Spantamad is led by Alkindi. No new Spantamad story was found for 6.x-7.1.

Ley Line studies and alchemy continue in the Akademiya. Scholars such as Hosseini and Gafoor remain minor figures in events.

432.content: Alkindi is the current sage of Spantamad and a former classmate and rival of Cyrus. He is tall, with medium-length grey hair that flares at the sides, round blue goggles and a crimson sherwani. His receding hairline is blamed on academic stress. In Chapter III's As All Falls to Emptiness he helped the Traveler by studying Ley Line anomalies.

433.content: Cyrus is a retired Akademiya professor and former Spantamad sage. Lisa and Cyno were his students, and he raised Cyno as his foster son. His line "Change is the only constant" is on Bimarstan's Proverb Column. He once nearly died exploring the Great Red Sand and was saved by the Temple of Silence. He also protested the rule that kept desert-born students out of the entrance exam, and his formal protest letter ended up unclaimed in the House of Daena.

434.content: Hosseini is a Driyosh in Spantamad from Vimara Village who appears in event quests such as Energy Amplifier. His hair has greyed from the stress of getting papers approved. For his thesis he went to collect a preserved Irminsul Fruit found by Liyue's Adventurers' Guild. Treasure Hoarders ambushed him and the fruit burst into fragments, so the Traveler helped recover them. He admires inventor-researchers such as Pursina, who made Pursina's Spikes, and Ayesha, who made a Chaos Prospector.

435.content: Driyosh are the Akademiya's traveling scholars. Spantamad has the most of them because Ley Line research needs fieldwork. Their commissions often reach the Adventurers' Guild, which is how the Traveler meets scholars such as Hosseini.

436.content:
Spina di Rosula (also: Spina, the Spina, Thorny Rose Association): The Spina di Rosula is a Fontainian organisation that helps ordinary people and takes on the problems the Gardes cannot or will not handle. Callas founded it, and his daughter Navia is now its President and "Boss". Its members work from Fleuve Cendre, the undercity beneath the Court of Fontaine, and from Poisson. Officially it describes itself as law-abiding and citizen-focused, and it cooperates with the authorities where needed. Navia's own description is "a business partner" that helps with any problem, using the velvet glove or the iron fist as the case demands.

The Spina also runs a quieter, harder side. It has enforcers for the dirty work, and it keeps order in Fleuve Cendre better than the Court of Fontaine ever tried to. Core businesses sustain the Spina, while much of Navia's problem-solving brings little profit, and its help can come with conditions. Navia's profile notes that people who adopt her own description of the Spina will find it easier to make friends with her.

Structure: The Spina has a single President. Navia lists her titles as president, leader, commander-in-chief, executive director and Boss, and members simply say "Boss". Below her are advisors and specialists rather than a rigid rank ladder. Florent is Senior Advisor and Yvette is Technical Advisor. Areta is the organisation's physician, Archenoul a diver on its payroll, and Tetreaux a bartender in Fleuve Cendre. Faustier, Rege and others do manual and construction labour, Hinterman is a fisherman, and Sonny and Luca are the enforcers.

Leadership: Navia is the second President. She took the post from her father Callas, who founded the Spina, after his death. She is cheerful, tireless and theatrical, and her own people treat her as the one to bring problems to.

Navia says plainly that she will not become the same sort of person as her father, though some veterans think she is becoming more like him. She says the Spina has changed a lot since Callas's day and she intends to be "the president for the Spina of today". Unlike Callas, she says she is willing to hear opinions. In the Romeuf case she handed her former members over to the law instead of settling it privately.

Members: Current members named in canon include Florent (Senior Advisor), Yvette (Technical Advisor), Areta (physician), Archenoul (diver), Tetreaux (bartender), Faustier and Rege (manual and construction labour), Hinterman (fisherman) and Sonny and Luca (enforcers). Consigliere is the organisation's tortoise confidant, and Bizerte leads its Simulanka branch. Former members include the founder Callas and his wife Clementine, who are dead; Melus and Silver, who were dissolved in the flood; Colter, who was dismissed and detained; Romeuf, who left and is imprisoned; and Virgil, who was killed.

Goals: The Spina exists to help the people of Fontaine, above all the poor and the forgotten, and to investigate matters that the Gardes would not or cannot. Its public statement is that it is a citizen-oriented society involving many walks of life, focused on hard problems among the common folk, and cooperative with the Fontainian authorities. Navia puts it more briefly: the work is "a little bit of everything", but the focus is always on solving other people's problems. Under Navia, the Spina also aims to rebuild Poisson, keep Fleuve Cendre safe and keep faith with the people who died for it.

Methods: The Spina prefers to settle matters peacefully, through mediation, negotiation and favours, but it does not rule out force. In Fleuve Cendre it mediates conflicts, manages relations with the Court of Fontaine and keeps the peace. Residents say that under the Spina it is much harder to find illegal funding and that anyone who starts an armed fight may be "sent away to start a new life in the ocean". It also supports its people with supplies, household help, jobs and sponsored study. Tetreaux says that, in theory, nothing exists that can only be solved by force, and that the Spina will resolve a problem with minimal harm.

History: Callas founded the Spina and led it as first President. A dispute over funding the aquabus split the organisation, and after Callas died in a duel three years before the Fontaine Archon Quest, his daughter Navia took over.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Spina di Rosula is active under President Navia, with Florent as Senior Advisor and Poisson's reconstruction under way.

Navia remains President and has represented the Spina outside Fontaine, as at the Nasha Town trade expo. Colter has been dismissed, awaiting the end of his sentence and a welcome back. Romeuf and his followers are in prison. The Simulanka branch exists only in an event story. No Spina-specific story developments were found for 7.0-7.1.

437.comment: Spina di Rosula: Fleuve Cendre base
437.content: The Spina's seat is in Fleuve Cendre, the settlement in the sewers beneath the Court of Fontaine. For centuries it was a gray legal area where the Court had no jurisdiction, once ruled by gangs and then by a protection racket under the outlaw Eduardo Baker. Today the Spina is its de facto governing body, and many members also live there. Residents include ex-convicts, people who have served time in the Fortress of Meropide, the poor and orphans. The air is damp, there is little sunlight and children are often left to themselves, but the Spina supplies food, medicine and help with household affairs. Tetreaux tends the bar. During the Fontaine Archon Quests the Traveler stays at the base between cases.

438.comment: Spina di Rosula: Sonny and Luca
438.content: Sonny, called "White Glove", and Luca, called "The Fisherman", are the Spina's enforcers. Sonny does the talking in a courtly, theatrical manner and Luca speaks very little. Navia says anyone who is not in the mood to talk will be dealt with by White Glove. They help the Traveler during the Aqueous Tidemarks and A Fontainian Message quests, and they hunt down Virgil, a rogue member who dealt in Sinthe. They are later found beside Consigliere in Fleuve Cendre.

439.comment: Spina di Rosula: Melus and Silver
439.content: Melus, the elder, and Silver, the younger, were Navia's two attendants and bodyguards after Callas's death. Melus managed her supplies, memos and daily logistics. When Primordial Seawater flooded Poisson they were dissolved while trying to save others. Their consciousnesses were forged into Oceanids, which helped shield Navia from the other victims who wanted to absorb her, long enough for Neuvillette to rescue her. They are the reason Colter blamed Navia.

440.content:
Sumeru Akademiya (also: Akademiya of Sumeru, Six Darshans): The Sumeru Akademiya is both Sumeru's government and the most prestigious academy in Teyvat. Greater Lord Rukkhadevata founded it, and its main building, the Akademiya, sits on the Divine Tree above Sumeru City. Its scholars are divided into six Darshans (schools), each led by a Sage, and one Sage serves as Grand Sage. It runs Sumeru's day-to-day affairs, from trade and ports to hospitals and law. The old sages under Grand Sage Azar confined the Dendro Archon and plotted with the Fatui to make a new god. Since their fall, the Akademiya has served Lesser Lord Kusanali (Nahida), and its current Grand Sage is Naphis.

It accepts students of any age and from any nation, provided they pass its hard entrance exams. Its scholars travel all over Teyvat to research, and in Mondstadt, Liyue or Inazuma a travelling Sumeru scholar fretting over a thesis is a familiar sight.

Structure: The six Darshans began as the Six Great Schools that Rukkhadevata founded with the Akademiya, and today the two names mean almost the same thing. Each has a specialty and a uniform colour:
- **Amurta**: biology, ecology and medicine (green). The oldest and largest Darshan.
- **Rtawahist**: illuminationism, meaning the stars, astronomy and astrology (blue).
- **Spantamad**: elementalism, ley lines and alchemy (red).
- **Haravatat**: semiotics, languages and ancient scripts (black).
- **Vahumana**: aetiology, history and the social sciences (yellow).
- **Kshahrewar**: technology and architecture (white).

Each Darshan is led by one of the Six Great Sages, and the central leader among them is the Grand Sage. The Grand Sage's office is above the House of Daena. Alongside the schools are administrative bodies: the **Mahamata** (civil officials, including the Scribe), the **Matra** (disciplinary officers under the General Mahamatra), the **Navbed** (trade and taxes), the **Vizier** (the Grand Bazaar and Treasures Street) and an office called the **Temple of Silence**, which handles information unfit for the public.

Leadership: Grand Sage Naphis, the Amurta Sage, is a man of integrity with a legendary temper. He was Tighnari's teacher. Lesser Lord Kusanali now guides the Akademiya directly.

The current sages were introduced together in 6.6: Naphis (Amurta, Grand Sage), Baladhuri (Vahumana), Shakir (Rtawahist), Alkindi (Spantamad), Rushd (Haravatat) and Firnas (Kshahrewar). Naphis and Baladhuri kept their seats because they had opposed Azar's conspiracy, and the other four replaced sages who were removed.

Goals: In principle the Akademiya exists to pursue and spread wisdom and to help the God of Wisdom govern Sumeru. Its three virtues, Admonition, Ingenuity and Praxis, are the "branches", "leaf-veins" and "roots" of the nation of wisdom. Its six cardinal sins mark the knowledge it considers too dangerous to pursue. Under Azar, these ideals hardened into control: the sages wanted to monopolise knowledge, restore Irminsul and replace a god they found disappointing.

Methods: The Akademiya governs mainly through the **Akasha System**. Rukkhadevata created it and the Akademiya expanded it after her death. It delivered knowledge to anyone wearing an Akasha Terminal, filtered by clearance, and it carried decrees and announcements. New material entered it on Jnagarbha Day through the Grand Sage's console. Unknown to most people, it drew its computing power from users' dreams. After the cataclysm the sages slowly stigmatised dreaming so that no one would notice. Leaked Knowledge Capsules ("Canned Knowledge") are banned, and the Matra pursue smugglers. The Akasha was shut down after Chapter III.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Akademiya is led by Grand Sage Naphis and five other sages, under Nahida's guidance. After the 6.6 Irminsul crisis, people have returned to Sumeru City and are rebuilding.

Irminsul has burned and Aaru now stores the world's information. Cyno remains General Mahamatra and Alhaitham remains Scribe. No new Akademiya story developments were found for 6.7-7.1.

441.comment: Sumeru Akademiya: Six cardinal sins and three virtues
441.content: In the Akademiya's early days, researchers reshaped terrain, controlled the weather and reached for the stars and for life and death. To protect them from their own knowledge, six sins were declared to be the root of all crimes: interfering with human evolution; tampering with life and death; delving beyond the universe; investigating the origin of words; revering gods without acts of devotion; and attempting the forbidden and fearing none. Every later rule builds on them, and Cyno judges by them, "even sages". Over time most people forgot them. In 3.4, Alhaitham noted that Siraj's Hive project counted as research on human evolution. The three virtues, Admonition, Ingenuity and Praxis, are the qualities the Akademiya praises, and the Sumeru talent books are named after them.

442.content: Driyosh are students on leave to gather research material; they apply through an eligibility review with interviews. Passing one thesis graduates a student. A Dastur has passed two and may research at the Akademiya instead of travelling. A Herbad is a senior researcher in a leadership role. Above them are the Six Great Sages and the Grand Sage. Seniority depends on progress, not age. Thesis review panels are feared, and some students pile up rejected manuscripts.

443.comment: Sumeru Akademiya: Mahamata, Matra and the Scribe
443.content: The Mahamata are Akademiya alumni sent across Sumeru to oversee information, enforce decrees and run public services such as trade and the Bimarstan hospital. The Scribe, Alhaitham's post, belongs to the Mahamata. The Matra are disciplinary officers who punish serious academic offences such as plagiarism and misused funds, and who inspect for Canned Knowledge and smuggled books. They are led by General Mahamatra Cyno, whom some scholars snipe at for not being a renowned researcher. The Navbed manages trade, ports and taxes, and the Vizier oversees the Grand Bazaar and Treasures Street.

444.content: Grand Sage Azar and three other sages accepted Dottore's offer to build a new God of Wisdom from Scaramouche. They locked up Naphis and Baladhuri, who objected, and forged letters in Naphis' name to recruit Tighnari. Khajeh, the Haravatat Sage, went to Gandharva Ville to press Tighnari in person. The sages harvested energy through an Akasha dream samsara, opened Akasha Terminals to visitors, threatened Nilou and banned public performances. They also refused Cyno's investigation, and he resigned. After Kusanali was freed, Cyno arrested Azar and made him repent before her. Azar and his accomplices were removed and sent to the Avidya Forest. Cyno thought the punishment too light, but he respected his god's decision.

445.comment: Sumeru Akademiya: Acting Grand Sage Alhaitham
445.content: After Azar's fall, the officials choosing his replacement nominated Alhaitham to be Grand Sage and help Kusanali run the Akademiya. He refused, saying he did not want to lead or even be a sage, but he agreed to act as Grand Sage in the meantime. During that time he dealt with Siraj's collective-consciousness "Hive" (Pride and Prejudice, 3.4). He then resigned so the temporary post would not become permanent, and went back to being Scribe, reportedly on the same salary.

446.comment: Sumeru Akademiya: Corps of Thirty and the Akademiya
446.content: The Corps of Thirty is the oldest Eremite brigade and is named after the thirty mercenaries the sages first hired. It keeps the peace in Sumeru City under a permanent contract and coordinates the other mercenary brigades. Its Parchamdar is Rukh Shah, and Effendi is the Akademiya's liaison. In 6.6 a member, Qanafiya, was exposed as a Fatui mole paid in ancient gold coins and was caught by Cyno.

key: Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency
447.comment: Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency
447.content:
Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency (also: Secure Transport Agency, Sword and Strongbox Agency): The Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency is a guild of guards for hire based at Yilong Wharf in Liyue. Its guards escort valuable cargo and lone travellers so that bandits and wild beasts cannot rob them. It is a sub-organization of the Communications Office, which handles shipments and transport across Liyue. Its best-known guard is Gaming.

The agency advertises delivering goods safe and sound and giving clients peace of mind, and warns that customers bear every consequence of not honestly disclosing what is in the cargo.

Structure: The agency is a sub-organization of the Communications Office. Hanqian, a guard who calls himself one of the leaders and "half an owner", is a senior figure; an owner has stepped back after the leadership group thinned out. Staff are called guards for hire. The recruitment notice offers food and lodging and excellent pay, and asks for physically fit applicants who can endure hardship and heavy labour.

Members: Gaming is the agency's gold-standard guard, a young man praised for pleasing clients while beating off bandits, and who also leads the Mighty Mythical Beasts troupe. Dip Yeuk is a newer guard and drums for that troupe. Hanqian, an open-world NPC at Yilong Wharf, is a leading guard. Huang the Third is another guard Hanqian worries about.

Goals: The agency's business is delivering goods and clients intact. Its guards also protect customers who are travelling alone through mountains and forests.

Methods: Guards focus on stamina, endurance and weight training rather than adventurers' skills. They train in horse stance, and Gaming has asked for plum blossom poles in the yard to firm up their fundamentals. Gaming's character story shows guards lifting cargo by hand to build strength.

History: Gaming joined as a temporary hand during a Lantern Rite when he led a Fontainian merchant there while a lead guard was short of staff, and was kept on as an official guard after that run. The agency is first documented in version 4.4.

Relations: - **Communications Office**: parent organization; per Hanqian the partnership changed the agency's rhythm.
- **Mighty Mythical Beasts**: Gaming's Wushou troupe, whose members are the agency's guards.
- **Millelith**: guards hand over criminals to them.

Reputation: Merchants favour its guards, and a thanks plaque to Gaming praises his hawk-like sight. Public notices show a mix of admiration, jokes and complaints.

Status as of 7.1: The agency is open at Yilong Wharf and recruiting. No later developments were found for 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

448.comment: Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency: Hanqian
448.content: Hanqian is an open-world NPC at Yilong Wharf, a guard and one of the agency's leaders. He trains hard, worries about his colleagues and says punches only get strength through real practice. He is blunt about hiring: chivalry matters more than anything.

449.comment: Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency: Yilong Wharf agency bulletin board
449.content: A bulletin board beside Hanqian displays the agency's advert and notices from passers-by, including recruitment, sparring requests, complaints and invitations. The messages cycle at random when read.

450.content:
Tanit (also: Tanit tribe, Tanit Tribe, the Tanit, Tanit Eremites): The Tanit were a nomadic Eremite tribe of Sumeru's Desert of Hadramaveth, matrilineal and led by a Matriarch and Nine Elders. They worshipped the Goddess of Flowers, traded in crocodile goods, spices and oils, and raised stolen or lost children as Falcons. Their last camp, the Tanit Camps, lay on the desert's southern edge. The tribe was destroyed in the events of Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters...

The Tanit were the oldest of the wandering desert tribes and had many branches. They valued words and knowledge but distrusted the Akasha. They had no unified law and no written rules, only what was "written in their blood and habits", and they hated traitors from within more than any outsider. The Traveler meets them through Jeht, who joined the tribe after her father Jebrael's death.

Structure: The tribe was matrilineal. A Matriarch led it, and Nine Elders held authority beside her. Babel had most of the other elders removed before the Traveler arrived, so by then power sat with her and her chosen lieutenants, notably Azariq, her "Left Hand". Warriors, guards and Falcons served under them. Jeht joined as a "half-outsider", since her father Jebrael had been born to the tribe and left it.

Leadership: Babel Tanit was the Matriarch. She presented the tribe as a family and used that word to justify punishing anyone she called a traitor. She tasked Jeht with removing the remaining elders by accusing them of betrayal. In truth she was consolidating power for herself, with Azariq's help and with Snezhnayan supplies and technology obtained from the Fatui. Once she had what she wanted she turned on the Fatui, claiming she had never meant to share the Eternal Oasis with them.

Members: Named members at the time of the Traveler's visit include Babel; Azariq, her trusted "son" and Left Hand; Aderfi, who fled after trying to have the Traveler removed; the guards Hugeweh and Mendas; the farmer Yuften; and the Falcons Nayram and Rezki, two of Babel's best. Jeht was a member until the tribe fell. Her father Jebrael and his companion Samail had belonged to the tribe earlier and left it.

Goals: Publicly, the Tanit sought to prosper as a tribe and to find the Eternal Oasis, a legendary place in the desert. Babel's own goal was larger. She wanted the Eternal Oasis, and after the Traveler became the master of the Jinni Liloupar, she wanted the Orchard of Pairidaeza too, so she could be the sole prophetess of Nabu Malikata and rebuild the glory of the desert empire that existed before its destruction, overthrowing the Sumeru Akademiya.

Methods: The tribe fought with ordinary warriors and with Falcons, and it hired mercenaries when needed. Babel ruled by suspicion: accusations of treachery, assassination of rivals and elders, and sending groups of followers into dangerous places. The groups she sent to the Eternal Oasis died, and she made it taboo to follow them. She also sent scouts to other tribes to warn them of Jeht's "treachery" in advance, so the Eremites would see her as dangerous.

Relations: - **Eremites**: the Tanit are one of several desert tribes. Babel deliberately cast Jeht as a traitor to them, so the other tribes would turn on her.
- **Fatui**: Babel traded with them for supplies and technology, then double-crossed them. Azariq was secretly allied with them, and she later sold Jeht to their scientist Froderock Fronkonsteen.
- **Sumeru Akademiya**: ties of convenience. The Tanit hire out as guides and escorts and read Akademiya books, but distrust the Akasha.

Status as of 7.1: The Tanit are gone. Babel is dead and the tribe was destroyed by Jeht and the Traveler, leaving only a few survivors. The Tanit Camps are now empty.

Jeht left the tribe's ruin to travel on her own and later led a mercenary group, and nothing in canon through 7.1 shows the tribe returning.

451.content: Babel Tanit was the Matriarch of the Tanit tribe, who raised herself to power by having elders removed and cheating the Fatui. She spoke warmly of the tribe as a family, and showed particular favour to Jeht, while planning to use or kill her. She died at Jeht's hand in Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters... Her own character is described in her NPC entry.

452.content: Falcons were children taken in or plundered by some desert tribes and raised devoted to the elders. In the Tanit, only a few became favoured. Babel, Tadhla (the Bent-Winged Falcon), Nayram and Rezki were Falcons. A weapon's text suggests the custom grew from the training of King Deshret's priests, in a distorted form.

453.content:
Tenryou Commission (also: Tenryou Commissioner, Tenryou-bugyou, Tenryou Bugyou): The Tenryou Commission is the Raiden Shogun's executive arm in Inazuma: it keeps public order, commands the military and police, and enforced the Vision Hunt Decree and the Sakoku Decree. It is one of the three bodies of the Tri-Commission and is led by the Kujou Clan. After the Fatui plot in Inazuma was exposed, its Commissioner Kujou Takayuki was removed, and his son Kujou Kamaji now leads it as acting head.

Its name refers to Tenryou, the part of Inazuma City directly governed by the Shogun, below Tenshukaku. Its headquarters stand in the Tenshukaku area above Inazuma City, and the Kujou estate is directly adjacent to Tenshukaku.

Structure: The Commission is led by the head of the Kujou Clan. Its military side is the Shogun's Army, whose generals include Kujou Sara and Kujou Masahito; Masahito commands from the Kujou Encampment on Kannazuka. The wiki lists a chief samurai and security head (Okawara Goemon), a quartermaster (Yasutake) and a Shogunate officer (Toranosuke). Below these are Shogunate samurai (such as Inaba Kyuuzou and Ogura Yuu), yoriki (such as Takasaka Izumi and Iwakura Mitsunari), and doushin, the foot officers who patrol the city. Shikanoin Heizou is listed as a Tenryou "Detective" among the doushin.

Leadership: The Commission is led by Kujou Kamaji, an official who fills in as Proxy Clan Head. Generals Kujou Sara and Kujou Masahito command its forces. Sara is a tengu adopted into the Kujou Clan.

Kamaji is the younger son of Takayuki and handles the Commission's government business in Inazuma City. Before the Fatui plot came out he was doubtful about the Vision Hunt and Sakoku Decrees but kept his doubts private. He took over after his father's fall, and Masahito, who as the elder son had the right to the headship, passed it to him because he judged Kamaji the better fit. Kamaji's sweetheart is Hiiragi Chisato, who was left as figurehead of the rival Kanjou Commission after her father's fall.

Goals: Officially the Commission preserves order and carries out the Shogun's will. Under Takayuki this meant keeping the Shogun's decrees running at any cost to preserve the Kujou Clan's influence. Under Kamaji it is trying to preserve the clan's honour and adjust to a country that no longer follows the decrees.

Methods: The Commission runs patrols and police, mans checkpoints, keeps wanted lists and posts notices on Inazuma's bulletin boards. During the Vision Hunt Decree it carried out the confiscation of Visions from ordinary people, setting up the Vision Hunt Ceremony at the Statue of the Omnipresent God. It enforced the Sakoku Decree against illegal entry and exit, while the Kanjou Commission handled legal travel. It was also the Shogun's field force against the Watatsumi Army in the civil war.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Kamaji acts as head of the Kujou Clan and the Commission. Takayuki remains under house arrest.

The Sakoku and Vision Hunt Decrees are no longer in force. The Commission's forces are led by generals Sara and Masahito. No Inazuman story was released in 5.8 to 7.1, so nothing found changes this.

454.comment: Tenryou Commission: Kujou Takayuki and the Fatui plot
454.content: Kujou Takayuki was head of the Kujou Clan and Tenryou Commissioner until the end of Chapter II. A year before the Traveler arrived the Fatui promised him support and generous rewards if he pushed the Vision Hunt Decree, and he accepted, thinking the Fatui no real threat. He lied to the Shogun in letters. He also adopted Kujou Sara. After the Traveler exposed him in Omnipresence Over Mortals, the Shogun stripped him of his post and he was placed under house arrest, denied bail and awaiting punishment. His son Kamaji replaced him as acting head.

455.comment: Tenryou Commission: Kujou Kamaji and the Tenryou duel
455.content: Kamaji is the younger son of Takayuki and acts as clan head. Before the scandal he was an official handling the Commission's government business in Inazuma City and privately questioned whether the decrees were really good for people. After the scandal he says he is trying to stem the chaos and trusts that the next generation can mend its forebears' mistakes. He loves Hiiragi Chisato, the daughter of the Kanjou Commissioner, and they exchange letters. In Reflections of Mortality he challenges the Raiden Shogun to a duel for the Commission, knowing he will lose, and impresses her with his honour.

456.comment: Tenryou Commission: Kujou Sara and Kujou Masahito
456.content: Both are generals of the Shogun's Army who serve the Kujou Clan. Masahito, the clan's eldest son, commands from the Kujou Encampment on Kannazuka. He disliked the Vision Hunt Decree and believed it harmed the people, but kept fighting the Watatsumi Army and warned his father about the Tatarigami on Yashiori Island. Sara is the Shogun's aide, an adopted tengu who keeps her Vision as an exception. In 2.1 she works with the Traveler to expose Takayuki. See their own entries for fuller detail.

457.content: The Commission's headquarters stand in the Tenshukaku area above Inazuma City (the wiki lists it as a point of interest of Tenshukaku). Yoriki Okawara Goemon, Mikoshi Genjirou and Yata Kouki and the doushin Watanabe work there, and the Kujou retainer Ikeda Soushirou appears there as well. The police station and day-to-day patrol offices are in Tenryou, the commercial street below the castle.

458.content:
The Black Serpents (also: Black Serpents, Shadowy Husks, Shadowy Husk, Royal Guard of Khaenri'ah, Khaenri'ahn Royal Guard): The Black Serpents are what is left of Khaenri'ah's Royal Guard, the knights who served under Captain Dainsleif before the nation fell. The curse on Khaenri'ah wore away their minds and memories. The Adventurer Handbook says only a will to "fight for something, someone, and some matter" remains. Depending on how worn they are, they are called Shadowy Husks or Black Serpent Knights. Outside quests they appear as elite enemies in the Chasm's underground mines and in the Spiral Abyss.

Canon files them under the Abyss, but they are not the Abyss Order, and the two meet in the Chasm. Many of them still guard what they once swore to protect.

Structure: No ranks or chain of command survive among the cursed. In life they were the Royal Guard under the Eclipse Dynasty, with Dainsleif as captain and bearer of the title "Twilight Sword". The wiki dates his promotion to about the time Irmin made the Traveler's sibling a vessel for Abyssal power. Today the Handbook groups them into two kinds. Shadowy Husks come as archers (Defender), lancers (Line Breaker) and banner bearers (Standard Bearer). Black Serpent Knights come as dual-axe fighters (Rockbreaker Ax) and greatsword fighters (Windcutter). Individual enemies in the Chasm carry names and epithets, such as Skeld, Augur of the Mirrors, and Serkir, Scribe of Swords.

Members: Few members have histories. Halfdan, an elite Royal Guard, led the Chasm band. Irizar and Zephaniah fought beside the Children of Echoes in Natlan. Ynghildr was a Schwanenritter lost in Sumeru, not a Royal Guard, and Irizar and Zephaniah are called only Khaenri'ahn soldiers. Their sub-entries carry the detail.

Goals: Their purpose survives only as fragments. Dainsleif's order to protect the people of Khaenri'ah at all costs still guides Halfdan's band, and those people are now hilichurls, whom the knights shelter. Elsewhere the cursed seem to defend a place or duty, such as the control module of the Ruin Golem in Devantaka Mountain.

Methods: In battle they are durable and use slow elemental attacks. When a player's shield fully absorbs one of their hits, they buff themselves or nearby allies at the cost of some of their own health. This is a gameplay note, not lore.

History: **Before the fall.** The Royal Guard served the Eclipse Dynasty. Dainsleif led them as the Abyssal power that destroyed Khaenri'ah rose.

**The cataclysm.** When Khaenri'ah fell about 500 years ago, its people were cursed, and the Guard's members faded into armoured shades that outlived their memories.

Relations: Dainsleif is their former captain and the one person who can still reach them. The Abyss Order's amplification device, meant to lift the curse, only caused them agony. Hilichurls, former Khaenri'ahn civilians, are the people they protect. The Children of Echoes remember Irizar and Zephaniah first as villains and then as heroes.

Reputation: Most of Teyvat knows them only as monstrous armoured enemies. The Children of Echoes first told a tale of two evil Khaenri'ahn soldiers, which Irizar and Zephaniah had themselves requested so the tribe would stay wary of the Abyss. Titu reversed that after learning the truth.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Black Serpents survive only as cursed enemies. The one organised band seen, in the Chasm, lost its leader Halfdan in the Archon Quest. Nothing new was found for 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

459.comment: The Black Serpents: Halfdan and the Chasm Knights
459.content: Halfdan was an elite of the Royal Guard who kept Dainsleif's final order to protect Khaenri'ah's people. Cursed and eroded, he still guarded dying hilichurls entering the Chasm, recognised Dainsleif and shielded others from the Abyss Order's device at the cost of his life. His spirit passed on after Dainsleif told him Khaenri'ah still stood.

460.comment: The Black Serpents: Irizar and Zephaniah
460.content: Two Khaenri'ahn soldiers who held the line for the Children of Echoes in the Sulfurous Veins during the cataclysm. Their souls were bound to an endless fight against the Abyss when the Shadow Pins sealed the cavern. They asked the tribe to remember them as villains, and the Traveler later set them free.

461.content: A Schwanenritter who went missing fighting the "Onslaught of Dark Beasts" in Sumeru. Only her signet ring and one other item were recovered, and Anfortas believed the order had fought to the last. In truth she became a cursed knight and guarded the Ruin Golem's control module until the Traveler defeated her.

462.content:
The Crux (also: Crux Fleet, the Crux Fleet, Crux): The Crux is an armed fleet based in Liyue Harbor and led by Captain Beidou. Its sailors carry cargo across seas no ordinary merchant would risk, fight sea monsters and pirates, and are famous throughout Liyue for daring voyages and rich bounties. Its flagship is the Alcor. Everything it does is approved by the Qixing, in the words of Beidou's profile, "more or less".

Its crew is fiercely loyal to Beidou, and she in turn risks her ship for strangers. The fleet is also known for its feasts, its hired chefs and its guests, which have included Xiangling and the Inazuman wanderer Kaedehara Kazuha.

Structure: The crew is split into two arms. The Spear of the Crux is trained for naval warfare and handling cargo deals. The Shield of the Crux is trained in survival and safe navigation: maritime rescue, cartography, weather reading and even counselling, and it also plans the crew's recreation. Beidou's hangout quests show both arms training an outsider, one with a boat-handling drill and one with seamanship lessons from the ship's surgeon, navigator and a sailor.

Leadership: Captain Beidou, the Uncrowned Lord of the Ocean, established and leads the Crux. When she goes ashore for business, Chief Mate Juza minds the Alcor and the crew, as he tells visitors himself.

Beidou treats her crew with respect and in return they trust her to tame storms. Juza says he was a dockworker with no direction until she invited him aboard. His version of the legend is that Beidou stood at the wheel in a terrible storm and sang a fishermen's song until the waves died and dawn broke. He tells new sailors that story over drinks after their first safe return.

Members: Beidou is the only playable member. Kaedehara Kazuha is a temporary crew member, taken aboard at Ritou while wanted in Inazuma, and he stayed even after the Vision Hunt Decree ended. Xiangling is a regular guest rather than crew, sailing with them in search of new seafood ingredients.

Goals: Profit and freedom, in that order, with a strong streak of justice. Beidou tells the Traveler that almost every confrontation the Crux faces is settled by negotiation, that weapons come out only when talks fail, and that the Alcor opens fire only in a fight to the death. In her words the ship is there to deter or to destroy, and the fleet is an armed crew with a sense of justice rather than war-hungry lunatics.

Relations: Beidou and Ningguang, the Tianquan of the Liyue Qixing, are an odd pair. Beidou does not fear her as most of Liyue does and insists nobody is her boss. Ningguang says she hires Beidou, never the Crux. Ningguang's advisers call Beidou unpredictable, but Ningguang calls her the most reliable person in Liyue. Ningguang also lays hefty fines on the fleet's shipments, which Beidou simply pays, and the two play chess and bet against each other.

Reputation: Every merchant in Liyue Harbor knows Beidou and her crew. The harbour tells exaggerated tales of her feats, from cutting a sea monster in two to winning money from Ningguang at chess, and merchants gossip about the fines she pays on shipments. Children look up to her. Criminals such as Treasure Hoarders fear and avoid her. Her crew consider her capable of anything and the stories grow with every telling.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Crux is active and still led by Beidou. Juza keeps the Alcor, which is anchored off Guyun Stone Forest while Beidou is in the city.

It last featured prominently in the 6.5 expo event. No 6.x Nod-Krai Archon Quest or 7.0 and 7.1 Snezhnaya content was found that changes the fleet's status.

463.content: The Alcor is the Crux's flagship, anchored off Guyun Stone Forest when at rest. The map text says it crosses oceans and can penetrate tempestuous storms. Juza calls it the fastest ship on Liyue's seas, armed to the teeth, and says pirates flee at the sight of it. A world quest, A Lone Ship in Guyun, has the Traveler help the crew with small chores after Juza first mistakes them for an intruder. The name comes from a star. Beidou says in a hangout quest that the Alcor is thought an omen of death.

464.comment: The Crux: Shield and Spear of the Crux
464.content: The Shield of the Crux covers survival: rescue at sea, charts, weather, counselling and crew recreation. The Spear covers naval warfare and cargo deals. In Life on the High Seas, Yinxing teaches the Traveler about health risks (underestimating danger is the answer to the greatest danger for new sailors), Huixing about navigation and Xu Liushi about reading storms, with Beidou setting a test afterward. In Beneath the Surface, the Spear's training uses older Skirmish Boats kept as backups on the Alcor.

465.content: Juza is the Chief Mate of the Alcor. He is loud, proud of the ship and devoted to Beidou, a former dockworker she invited aboard. When Beidou is ashore he treats unknown visitors suspiciously and threatens to have them fed to the fishes, until Yinxing steps in. His name is Inazuman in style, which fits the fleet's links to Inazuma.

466.comment: The Crux: Kazuha aboard the Alcor
466.content: Kazuha joined the Alcor at Ritou as a temporary sailor, hiding from those hunting him after the Vision Hunt Decree. Beidou did not realise at first that he was a trained swordsman and told her crew to take care of him. They welcomed him for his skill and for predicting weather, and overlooked his reticence about his past. After the Decree ended he stayed, and Kazuha's profile calls the Crux his new home. The crow's nest gives him space to think.

467.comment: The Crux: The Beidou and Ningguang arrangement
467.content: Ningguang is said to be the Crux's hidden owner. Neither woman accepts that. Ningguang hires Beidou, not the Crux; Beidou says they are equals. The Qixing's administrators see her as a lawbreaker who pays hefty fines without complaint, while the two women still keep each other company over chess and cooperate when Liyue's greater good is at stake.

468.content: Haishan was a leviathan-like sea monster that merchants were bound to meet sooner or later. Beidou had challenged it many times with the Crux. She struck it down after a four-day fight in which the fleet pinned it with ropes and harpoons. Her Electro Vision appeared afterwards. The crew sang a sea shanty during the battle, per her profile. Zhang Shun, a sailor injured then, retired and became a peddler.

469.comment: The Crux: Xiangling's feasts aboard the Crux
469.content: After a long voyage, the Crux held its customary three-day banquet and hired the then little-known Xiangling to save money. She objected to being asked for Yue-style seafood, but Beidou's offer of a fifty thousand Mora retainer won her over. Beidou told the crew to call her "Madam Xiangling" and predicted she would be famous. Xiangling has since joined voyages to find new ingredients, though she does not always heed Beidou's advice on what is edible.

470.comment: The Crux: Nod-Krai Trade Expo booth
470.content: During the limited-time event Where Waves Meet the Reef (6.5), the Crux took part in the expo in Nod-Krai with a new Alcor-class warship. The vessel was built for a special purpose, was launched quietly alongside a supply ship and had no naming ceremony, so she was just called No. 2. Beidou hoped to name her at the expo debut, and afterwards lets the Traveler choose between "Alkaid" and "Alioth" (the choice is the player's). Beidou met Navia and Clorinde there.

471.content:
The Steambird (also: Steambird, The Steambird newspaper, Steambird Newspaper): The Steambird is the main newspaper of the Court of Fontaine, read across Teyvat. Its office stands in Quartier Narbonnais, and its Chief Editor is Euphrasie. Its best-known reporter is Charlotte. Besides news it runs a reader-submission column, and it organises the La Verite Prize for journalism.

The paper covers everything from celebrity gossip and opera to politics, crime and science. Its pitch on the Newsstand Board is "your credible source of the unbelievable truth". Euphrasie says a good newspaper should be a lighthouse of truth. The paper also works as a community notice board through its "Tales of Humanity" column, which is the in-game explanation for Fontaine's Reputation system.

Structure: The paper is led by Chief Editor Euphrasie. Beneath her is a staff of reporters who each cover an area, plus a photographer, a reviewer, a columnist and a trainee. Sir Arthur, apparently a mechanical newscaller, stands in Quartier Narbonnais shouting headlines and special issues. The office, called the main office in an item description, is in Quartier Narbonnais of the Court of Fontaine.

Leadership: Euphrasie is the Chief Editor. She runs the paper, assigns and recalls reporters such as Charlotte, and deals with the complaints and threats that follow. She speaks formally and with dry humour.

Euphrasie also posts the paper's commissions for locals' everyday troubles, helps the Palais Mermonia put up wanted posters for criminals and dangerous monsters issued by the Maison Gardiennage, and uses the paper's sources to find the right people for jobs. An earlier Chief Editor, Nellie Cochran, interviewed Alain Guillotin. In Charlotte's recruitment story, Euphrasie personally approached Charlotte to ask her to become a special correspondent.

Members: Key people: Euphrasie (Chief Editor), Charlotte (reporter and special correspondent), Sir Arthur (newscaller), and columnists such as Mona. Nellie Cochran is a historical Chief Editor. Charlotte's father Galanopoulo, a veteran reporter and nature photographer, is listed among the staff, and the paper first published the photos he and Charlotte took.

Goals: The paper's stated purpose is to keep information flowing so that everyone can understand what is happening around them, and then to let readers express themselves through "Tales of Humanity". Euphrasie calls it a lighthouse illuminating humanity. Practically, it also needs to be read: its pages mix serious reports with gossip because, as the Traveler puts it, trivial stories grab attention and sell copies.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 The Steambird is active in the Court of Fontaine with Euphrasie as Chief Editor. Sir Arthur, Charlotte and the columns continue as before.

Euphrasie's Reputation menu and the "Tales of Humanity" commissions remain available, and the La Verite Prize is still described in the Opera Epiclese bulletin. Nothing checked indicates that The Steambird changed in 6.x or in 7.0-7.1, and it plays no part in Snezhnaya content.

472.content: Euphrasie is the Chief Editor of The Steambird and can be found in Quartier Narbonnais. Her map description says she posts commissions for local residents' troubles, helps the Palais Mermonia put up wanted posters for criminals and monsters the Maison Gardiennage wants, and uses the paper's sources to find the best-suited people. In the Steambird Interview quest (after Chapter IV Act II) she recruits the Traveler as a "troubleshooter" for Tales of Humanity, which unlocks Fontaine's Reputation menu. She is formal and wry and given to sighing, and she claims to have settled the Traveler's suitability before the interview began. Her idle line says a good newspaper should be a lighthouse of truth.

473.content: Sir Arthur is the Steambird's herald in Quartier Narbonnais. He cries "Extra, extra!" followed by headlines, and says "beep-boop". His content changes with story progress and ranges from opera and exhibition notices to crime news, rumours and special issues. He once announced that his regular maintenance had been completed and asked the public not to believe rumours that he had been stolen and split into three. The wiki lists his title as "The Steambird". He appears to be a machine, but canon does not say so outright.

474.content: Tales of Humanity is the Steambird's reader-submission column, begun so that people could express themselves and not only read. Euphrasie says it is "drowning in all manner of content" and that this is acceptable, because readers also want light reading and helping them is good for the paper's reputation. Many locals use it to post commissions, which Euphrasie coordinates; small jobs feel like splinters to those who write in. It is the in-game basis for Fontaine's Reputation system: finishing commissions raises the Traveler's standing, and Euphrasie later offers harder jobs.

475.content: The La Verite Prize is organised by The Steambird and, per Charlotte's profile, funded by it. The Opera Epiclese bulletin calls it the most prestigious media award in all of Teyvat. It honours the best individual and collective achievements in newspapers, magazines, journals and other media, with a ceremony held at the Opera Epiclese.

476.content: The Newsstand Board is a news board in Quartier Narbonnais, beside Angelique near Hubel's shop. It pitches the Steambird as "your credible source of the unbelievable truth" and notes that the stand also sells La Gouttiere and other magazines. Its messages rotate. Samples include the crowbar-wielding honored citizen detective, a reopened drowning case, the rising-water panic, and a verdict report by Charlotte on the trial after the serial disappearances case. La Gouttiere's pieces are gossip in tone, for example on Clorinde and on the Fontaine Research Institute explosion investigation.

477.content:
Treasure Hoarders (also: Treasure Hoarder, the Treasure Hoarders): The Treasure Hoarders are a gang of bandits who hunt treasure in ruins and domains all over Teyvat and get rough with bystanders who happen to be nearby. They are poorly organised because the groups are so far apart. The gang's official description credits a founder called Reed Miller, who called it "an organization of mutual cooperation." The group is said to have originated in Nod-Krai. Members join over crime or lack of steady income, and they tend to burn through loot fast and stay poor.

Members use a raven (Ravenwing) motif, and most wear a mask to hide their faces from the law. The few unmasked ones are either important or bait to draw victims into traps. Not all members get along, and some are looked down on more than others. The Nod-Krai content shows that the gang's roots were more idealistic than its present: a thief who wanted a world without borders.

Structure: There is no known central command or fixed headquarters. Each region has its own groups, some led by a named boss such as Freckle Huang in Liyue. The wiki describes them as disorganised, mainly because of the distances between groups. Some members belong to sub-groups of the wider organisation, such as the Fruity Order in Fontaine. In Nod-Krai several groups follow in the footsteps of their founder.

Leadership: Today no overall leader is named. Regional bosses include Freckle Huang (Liyue, defeated in a Guizhong quest) and "Boss" or "Big Sis" in Liyue, who turns out to be Yan'er. The legendary leaders are the three holders of the Reed Miller name: Avrelian, Alia and Brahe, all long dead. See the entries on each. Hiljetta, the "Black-Barreled Hag," is a retired but renowned Hoarder in Nod-Krai who wants to restore the gang's old glory.

Members: The wiki lists many members by region. A few are worth knowing.
- **Mondstadt**: small-time thieves such as Tyler and Nimrod (an informant to Kaeya), plus the elite Raptor.
- **Liyue**: Freckle Huang (leader), Yan'er ("Boss"), Carmen, Liuliu and Wallenstein. Liyue is the gang's main haunt, including beneath the Chasm.
- **Inazuma**: Shun, Kojirou, Koichirou and others.
- **Sumeru**: Narzam, Pabag and others.
- **Fontaine**: the Grand Thief and several nicknamed members.
- **Natlan**: Coztic and Matthias.
- **Nod-Krai**: Hiljetta, Kaleva, Basu and Hoyka.

Goals: Most members want treasure and a living. Their reasons for joining vary, but the wiki says they are usually crime or a lack of stable income. The idealistic founders had a bigger aim, an "Elysium" for the poor and hungry built on the wealth of the powerful. Hiljetta and others in Nod-Krai want to claim Reed Miller's hidden treasure and restore the gang's reputation.

Methods: Treasure Hoarders sack ruins, domains and chests, ambush travelers, and get rough with anyone who stumbles on them. In Liyue the leader called "Boss" leaves false trails and notes so that curious adventurers walk into ambushes. When beaten, they throw smoke bombs and vanish. Masks hide identity. Some groups in Fontaine use rogue or stolen Clockwork Meka, and some groups travel with a Sumpter Beast.

History: **Origin legend.** Nod-Krai folklore says the gang was founded by Reed Miller, an infamous master thief who buried a "great treasure" in the land that became Nod-Krai. The real story is told in quests of 6.3 and is covered in the entries below.

**Founding.** About 500 years ago, Avrelian, the son of a Snezhnayan officer and a Frostmoon Scion mother, graduated from the Snezhnayan military academy, "died in the line of duty" on paper shortly after becoming a non-commissioned officer, and turned to banditry. He raised the black raven emblem, gathered the forsaken and despised, and preached a world without borders. He was manipulated by Rotwang into stealing the Sampo Mill, then gave himself up in Snezhnograd hoping to speak to the Tsar. He was executed without ever meeting the Tsar.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Treasure Hoarders remain active, scattered local gangs across every nation. No 7.0-7.1 story content about them was found. Their last major appearance is in the Nod-Krai content: the Reed Miller legend, Hiljetta and the Proofs of the Cognoscenti (6.3).

The 6.3 quest series revealed the truth about Reed Miller. Tolfin gave the Traveler a raven insignia (which he believes Avrelian left behind) as a keepsake, and Hiljetta wants the Traveler to visit for further sparring matches.

478.content: In Nod-Krai folklore, Reed Miller is the Treasure Hoarders' founder and an infamous master thief who buried a great treasure. In truth the name was worn by at least three people: Avrelian (first), Alia (second) and Brahe (third). Brahe wrote many conflicting legends under other names, such as "Brahe the Bard" and "Grand Duke Trubetskoy," so that nobody could use the name seriously. Popular tellings are collected in the book The Legends of Reed Miller, Thief Extraordinaire. Others have adopted the name since; Jahoda named her chic badger partner Reed Miller XIII, and Netochka dreams of being the next Reed Miller.

479.content: Avrelian, nicknamed Relya, was the first Reed Miller and the Treasure Hoarders' founder. He was the son of a Frostmoon Scion Maiden and a Snezhnayan officer, and after his parents died he was adopted by an officer named Mikhnenko. He attended the Snezhnayan military academy and befriended Solovei, with whom he went treasure hunting; on one such hunt a young Brahe, the governor's adopted son, told them where the treasure was. Shortly after becoming a non-commissioned officer he faked his death. Avrelian dreamed of an Elysium for the poor and founded the gang under a raven emblem. Rotwang told him of his Frostmoon blood and a destiny as ruler of Elysium and got him to steal the Sampo Mill. Persuaded by Solovei to explain himself to the Belyi Tsar, he was arrested without meeting the Tsar and executed in public, in view of Solovei and Alia.

480.content: Alia was the second Reed Miller and Aila's older twin sister. Their adoptive grandmother Lovia, the Frostmoon Scions' Archpriestess, raised them in seclusion on Hiisi Island and had them kill other Scions and drink their blood. Alia escaped, apparently after Avrelian stole the Sampo Mill, and joined the Treasure Hoarders. After Avrelian's execution she took his mask and reorganised the gang, raiding the governor's palace for Nasha Town's poor. She and Solovei worked to stop Rauthvangi's plan to use the Pillar of Embla to pierce the false sky, and she gave her life by casting herself into the Sampo Mill and igniting it. Her last wish was that her sister live a life of happiness and freedom. Local legend made her a fae.

481.content: Brahe was the adoptive son of Prokhor Trubetskoy, governor of Nod-Krai, and later the last governor himself, and the third Reed Miller. He regarded Avrelian and Alia as true idealists and himself as a realist who understood human malice. After the Cataclysm he faked his death in the records and, over years, seeded contradictory legends about Reed Miller, including an invented companion named "Wagtail." He built the Great Treasure and later turned it into the Proof of the Cognoscenti trial, a test of wit rather than greed. A former academy instructor, Sukhotin, once found the vault, mistook him for a thief and stood down on recognising Avrelian's gauntlet.

482.content: Hiljetta is a very old woman living in an alcove in Wavechaser Plain and a retired Treasure Hoarder known as the Black-Barreled Hag for her fighting skill. She wants to bring back the gang's glory days under Reed Miller. She holds the last Proof of the Cognoscenti and gives it only to someone who will restore the legacy. She resents Brahe, her ancestor, for cheapening Reed Miller's legacy. After the Traveler beats her in a spar she hands it over. Her grandson Tolfin is a wandering storyteller and merchant who steered the Traveler to her, has a special bond with Weasel Thieves and travels with a weasel named Huginn. Hiljetta scolded him for not telling the Traveler that they were all linked to the gang.

483.content: Liyue is where the Treasure Hoarders are most visible. Freckle Huang leads the group in a Guizhong quest and is defeated there. Notes in several world quests refer to a female "Boss" who lays false treasure trails to lure adventurers into ambushes; she is later revealed to be Yan'er, also called "Big Sis." Yan'er is a childhood friend of Hiromi and Shun; after the Sakoku Decree she and Shun went treasure hunting in Liyue. She tried to plunder ruins south of Wuwang Hill during The Chi of Yore, and later teamed with Raptor on a raid on the Abyss Order. They hired the Grand Thief, who died. Beidou of the Crux frightens Liyue's Hoarders.

484.content: The Grand Thief is a popular Hoarder, said to come from Fontaine. After Osial was defeated, a group of Hoarders banded together to distract the Abyss Order while the Grand Thief slipped in to steal valuables. The Traveler and Paimon find the defiled statue and his kneeling corpse in Involuntary Sacrifice (Archon Quest Chapter I, Act IV, We Will Be Reunited). The cause of his death is unknown.

485.content: Fontaine's Hoarders roam the countryside in groups. Some use rogue or stolen Clockwork Meka for mining or guarding. Others belong to sub-groups such as the Fruity Order. Some members have crossed the sea to Chenyu Vale. According to the wiki their standing seems fairly high.

486.content:
Tri-Commission (also: Sanbugyou, San-bugyou, Three Commissions, Three Commissioners): The Tri-Commission (Sanbugyou, "Three Commissioners") is the collective name for the three organisations that run Inazuma's government under the Raiden Shogun. The Tenryou Commission, led by the Kujou Clan, handles security and the military. The Kanjou Commission, led by the Hiiragi Clan, handles finance, customs and the borders. The Yashiro Commission, led by the Kamisato Clan, handles shrines, festivals and ceremonies. An Inazuman in Liyue compares them to Liyue's Qixing and Eight Trades and to the Knights of Favonius.

The three commissions can check one another. The Hiiragi and Kujou are described as political rivals who keep each other in balance. The Yashiro is the only one of the three that stayed out of the Fatui's scheme.

Structure: Each commission has its own clan, its own commissioner and its own staff. The wiki lists them like this:
- **Tenryou Commission**: Kujou Clan; head of public security, military and police affairs, enforcer of the Vision Hunt Decree and of the Sakoku Decree against illegal entry or exit.
- **Kanjou Commission**: Hiiragi Clan; the financial arm, supervising the borders, trade and bureaucracy, and enforcing the Sakoku Decree for legal entry and exit.
- **Yashiro Commission**: Kamisato Clan; the cultural arm, handling ceremonies, celebratory events and public festivals, and managing shrines and temples. It is considered the commission closest to the Raiden Shogun.

Soldiers of the Shogun's Army are assigned to each commission.

Leadership: The Raiden Shogun rules over the three. The Kujou, Hiiragi and Kamisato clans lead the Tenryou, Kanjou and Yashiro Commissions. Kamisato Ayato leads the Yashiro Commission, which was untouched by the Fatui scandal.

Kujou Kamaji (Tenryou) and Hiiragi Chisato (Kanjou) are acting heads of their clans, as their fathers Kujou Takayuki and Hiiragi Shinsuke fell after the Fatui plot came out. In the Cypressus Custos Chapter a wedding announcement refers to both as Proxy Clan Heads. Kamisato Ayato leads the Yashiro Commission as clan head, and the wiki lists his sister Kamisato Ayaka among its leaders and Thoma among its staff.

Goals: The Tri-Commission carries out the Shogun's decrees and handles ordinary government. During the Vision Hunt and Sakoku Decrees this meant seizing Visions and sealing the borders in the name of the Shogun's eternity. Since those decrees ended, its work is again security, trade, ceremony and the relations among the clans.

Methods: Each commission governs through its specialty. The Tenryou Commission uses soldiers, patrols and wanted lists. The Kanjou Commission uses financial control, permits and border assessments at Ritou. The Yashiro Commission works through festivals, shrines and the Kamisato Estate's retainers, and controls the Shuumatsuban, a clandestine ninja organisation used for gathering information.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Tri-Commission stands, with Ayato leading the Yashiro Commission and acting heads Kamaji and Chisato leading the Tenryou and Kanjou.

The Vision Hunt and Sakoku Decrees are gone. Former commissioners Takayuki (under house arrest) and Shinsuke (imprisoned) are still awaiting the Shogun's punishment. The sources checked show no later story, up to 7.1, that changes this.

487.content: The Yashiro Commission manages shrines, festivals and cultural events and is led by the Kamisato Clan; its headquarters are at the Kamisato Estate. Kamisato Ayato is its Commissioner and clan head. Because its work is mostly civilian it has less influence than the Kanjou and Tenryou. The soldiers assigned to it are relaxed and caring toward the people. It runs the Shuumatsuban. It was untouched by the Fatui because Ayato declined their offer, and it gained some sympathy after Chapter II. Its members include Ayato, Ayaka and Thoma, and the Komore Teahouse, a Kamisato-linked business, is run by Taroumaru.

488.content:
Universitas Magistrorum (also: the Universitas, University of the Magisters): The Universitas Magistrorum was a Khaenri'ahn institute of learning whose members worked in astrology, alchemy and other arts. It was directly subordinate to the Vinster King Irmin and held real influence in the kingdom.
