Before the cataclysm it was led by President Hroptatyr, "The Wise", with Eftirvit, later called Pierro, as Vice-President. After Irmin became obsessed with the Abyss, it turned into a major centre of Abyssal research. What became of it after the kingdom fell 500 years ago is not stated.

The name is Latin, roughly "University of the Magisters". The institute is known only through memories, book text and story quests set in the last years of Khaenri'ah, never as a place the Traveler visits in the present day.

Structure: At the top were a President, who was also the Chief Royal Mage with the royal title "The Wise", and a Vice-President. Beneath them worked professors and researchers, among them Professor Mimameith (the teacher of both leaders) and the Moon Marrow researcher Tholindis. The Universitas also held a collection of literary works, and in at least one legend it had a champion fighter. It answered to the king directly and had no other known superior.

Leadership: Hroptatyr was the President, a rising prodigy who had studied under Mimameith and was favoured by the king. Eftirvit, his friend and rival, was passed over for the presidency and served as Vice-President. Both were counted among the most promising scholars of their generation. Rhinedottir remarked to Hroptatyr that the Vice-President did not hide his envy, and Hroptatyr answered that missing the presidency spared Eftirvit a great deal of stress.

Members: Named members are Hroptatyr, Eftirvit (Pierro), their teacher Professor Mimameith, and Tholindis, a young Moon Marrow researcher. Alf is described in the legend Perinheri as the greatest warrior in the Universitas Magistrorum.

Goals: The Universitas served the crown by forecasting from the stars, working with alchemy and seeking sources of power for the kingdom. Under Irmin's growing fixation, its purpose narrowed to understanding and using the Abyss. Individual researchers had their own aims, such as a cure for Mimameith or an alternative energy source to the Abyss.

History: **Before the cataclysm.** The institute was an established, esteemed body. In their youth Hroptatyr and Eftirvit studied under Professor Mimameith there and became its leading minds. Hroptatyr rose to the presidency.

Relations: - **King Irmin**: the direct master of the institute, whose Abyss obsession redirected its work.
- **Eclipse Dynasty**: the royal house it served. Pierro is described as having served it as a royal mage.
- **Crimson Moon Dynasty**: the Universitas studied the Crimson Moon's remains, and Tholindis was a hidden descendant of the dynasty.
- **Fatui**: Pierro, its former Vice-President, later headed the Fatui. In 7.1 Arlecchino said that whatever methods the Universitas used on the Crimson Moon were centuries old and "history", and that she cared more about the future.

Status as of 7.1: The Universitas Magistrorum no longer exists as a known body. Its two leaders live on as the Fatui Director Pierro and as Hroptatyr, a Sinner of Khaenri'ah whose memory was glimpsed in 7.1. Canon does not say whether the institute itself survived the cataclysm.

489.content: Hroptatyr and Eftirvit studied side by side under Professor Mimameith at the Universitas and were its brightest scholars. Hroptatyr became President and the royal mage titled "The Wise"; Eftirvit became Vice-President. When Mimameith fell ill from her work on the Abyss, Hroptatyr found a way to extract the Authority of Death from the Crimson Moon, but realised it would curse her to endless suffering and refused to use it, without telling Eftirvit why. She died, and Eftirvit grew bitter. Around the time Eftirvit brought Paimon down from Celestia, Hroptatyr summoned the Traveler's sibling. Hroptatyr later took a share of the sibling's power, became a Sinner, and gave Eftirvit a notebook of his research and a prism holding his memories before leaving. Pierro told Paimon in 7.1 that, five hundred years on, he still felt unable to step out of Hroptatyr's shadow.

490.comment: Universitas Magistrorum: Moon Marrow lab and Tholindis
490.content: The Moon Marrow lab at the Universitas studied the remains of the Crimson Moon as a possible new power source for Khaenri'ah. After Irmin shifted resources to the Abyss, Tholindis, a young researcher from a hidden branch of the Crimson Moon Dynasty, was its only remaining staff member. She found that the Moon Marrow could open a spatial gateway to a place where time runs backwards, the "moon's reflection", but could not explore it for lack of funding and technology to keep the gate open. She was engaged to Rerir. On the night of the raid, trapped by monsters, she jumped through a Moon Gate into the reflection, and her loss pushed Rerir toward joining the Five Sinners. Her fiancé's earlier role as an executioner of the Crimson Moon's descendants is told in the quest A Nation That Doesn't Exist.

491.content: Chaos Permeation was a minor spell developed by the Universitas to mock Vision wielders. A user drew on Abyssal energy to create negative pressure in reality that called up the flow of an element, producing effects like an elemental power. In Khaenri'ah it was a party trick for performances and parades, and ordinary street performers needed months of practice to shift just one element. Surtalogi, who understood Abyssal power, mastered it almost at once, cycling through all seven elements on his first attempt. He renamed it the Seven-Shifting Serpent and taught it to his disciple Skirk, who uses it to hide her Abyssal powers on Teyvat.

492.content:
Vahumana (also: Vahumana Darshan, School of Aetiology, Darshan of Aetiology, Vahumana scholars): Vahumana is one of the six Darshans (schools) of the Sumeru Akademiya. Its field is aetiology, the study of the causes and origins of things, and it covers history, sociology and other social sciences. Its colour is yellow. It is led by Sage Baladhuri.

The name comes from the Avestan Vohu Manah, "Good Mind", as the other Darshan names are drawn from the Amesha Spenta. Its emblem's mascot resembles a horse.

Structure: Vahumana is one of six Darshans, alongside Amurta, Haravatat, Kshahrewar, Rtawahist and Spantamad. Each has a Sage at its head, and the six Sages sit together in the Akademiya's leadership. Scholars carry ranks such as Herbad (Yarshater is a Vahumana Herbad) and Professor (Manetho is a Vahumana professor in the quest Dance of Death: Serpent and Scorpion). Students normally take an entrance exam that decides which Darshans they are eligible for.

Leadership: Baladhuri is the current Vahumana Sage.

He is a kind, gentle scholar, tall, with an elaborate stone-grey beard he is proud of. He took office before Azar fell from power. He and Naphis of Amurta opposed the Akademiya's secret collaboration with the Fatui and were locked up by the other four Sages until the conspiracy collapsed. Tighnari calls him "Uncle Baladhuri", which shows a personal bond. Baladhuri has a wife and a young daughter and is devoted to them. He teaches students such as Khaldun and, in Where Flowers Awaken (6.6), stays with them through the city's crisis.

Members: Known Vahumana scholars include the following.
- Baladhuri: the Sage.
- Khaldun: a researcher and Baladhuri's student.
- Yarshater: a Herbad who helped translate the Scroll of Streaming Song.
- Manetho: a professor named in a Sumeru quest.
- Nefer: assigned here as a student (see history), now listed as a former member.
- Vikram: mentioned by NPCs as one of the candidates for Grand Conservator.

Methods: Vahumana scholars study history and society. They mount expeditions to ruins and bring artefacts back for study. They also translate old documents, often with the Haravatat, who handle language and runes. Cooperation has its edges: in the Scroll of Streaming Song, a Haravatat Herbad (Tafazzoli) added footnotes correcting the Vahumana translators, and the Vahumana Herbad Yarshater replied in the margin that he had never been told. The wiki infers these remarks are annotations, since the House of Daena lets borrowers annotate books.

History: Sitt places the roots of Vahumana in the reaction to King Deshret's remaining theories, and it later grew into the basis for the social sciences. Nothing more precise about its founding is stated.

Relations: - **Haravatat**: the nearest neighbour in translation work. They collaborate and also criticise each other's methods.
- **Amurta**: Naphis and Baladhuri were allies against the Akademiya's secret plans, and the two Darshans co-design food-preservation products.
- **Sumeru Akademiya**: Vahumana is one of its six schools, and its Sage sits among the Sages.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Vahumana is active under Baladhuri.

No Vahumana-specific story developments were found in the 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content checked, apart from Baladhuri's appearances in the Sumeru section of the 6.6 Archon Quest (Where Flowers Awaken, A Divergence Leading to Oneself). The 7.0-7.1 Archon Quests take place in Snezhnaya.

493.content: Baladhuri is the Sage of Vahumana, a kind man who opposed the Akademiya's deal with the Fatui and was imprisoned for it. He is a devoted husband and father with a prized beard, and Tighnari calls him Uncle. He is a teacher first, and stays with his students through the 6.6 crisis.

494.content: A three-volume book collection in the House of Daena. Vahumana researchers recovered torn pages from desert ruins and translated them. The Haravatat Herbad Tafazzoli and the Vahumana Herbad Yarshater trade footnotes about mistranslations and about what each knew while they worked together. It is a small example of scholarly rivalry between the two Darshans.

495.content: As a student from the desert, Nefer was assigned to Vahumana without sitting the entrance exam, a rule that held during Azar's time. Cyrus objected on principle that anyone admitted had a right to take the test. She says in a voice-over that Vahumana grew popular again after Azar's exile. Nefer is listed as a former member.

496.content:
Voynich Guild (also: the Voynich Guild, Voynich): The Voynich Guild is a commerce guild of local merchants based in Nasha Town, Nod-Krai, and one of the most powerful forces in the region. With no government in Nasha Town, it is the nearest thing to a regulator. It manages trade deals, imports and exports, business certificates and many disputes.

Nefer, owner of the Curatorium of Secrets, is a member, and the Curatorium's headquarters stands directly behind the Guild's. Its representative in the Nod-Krai League is Tarno.

Structure: No guildmaster, charter or rank structure is given in canon. Tarno is the manager of its Nasha Town souvenir outlet. According to Zinaida's intel text, the Guild also hired Zinaida, a former Seahook Gang member, as a covert bodyguard for Manez, the port supervisor. The Guild keeps a bulletin board in Nasha Town for business notices.

Leadership: Leadership is unnamed. After the crisis in Nod-Krai, Tarno, the outlet manager, became the Guild's representative in the League. He hosted the League's opening ceremony and gave its welcome address in that role.

Members: Known members and staff are Nefer, who is also the owner of the Curatorium of Secrets, and Tarno, listed as a "Voynich Guild" employee. The Guild issues certifications: Sarin says a bounty hunter lost his Guild certification over his old habits (limited-time event, Clink Clank Clash).

Goals: The Guild's stated aim, in its bulletin-board announcement, is to promote economic activity in Nasha Town. It hopes people will find endless business opportunities there.

Methods: The Guild issues business certificates, manages trade deals, handles imports and exports, and investigates and resolves disputes when its name is called in. A merchant who was robbed just before reaching the city was told to go to the Guild. They brought back his stolen goods and bought them all, in a story the merchant told as an example of the Guild's reach (limited web event, 2024).

History: Canon gives no founding history. The Guild first appears in the Marvelous Merchandise web event (2024), where a traveling seller describes Nod-Krai as a wild place that plays by its own rules and the Guild as the strongest force in the area. Its own members first appear in 6.0 (Luna I).

Relations: **Curatorium of Secrets:** closely linked, since Nefer is a member and the two headquarters are back to back. **Frostmoon Scions:** Lauma approached the Guild for a joint investigation of the stolen Moon Marrow. **League:** Tarno represents the Guild. **Others:** the Guild is one of several factions in Nasha Town's power balance, alongside the Curatorium, Speranza and the Fatui.

Reputation: Liben was told it is the strongest force in the area, and his experience bore that out. Ningguang considers it a significant player worth cultivating.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, the Voynich Guild remains Nasha Town's leading merchant body, with Tarno speaking for it in the League.

The sources checked show no Voynich Guild story content in 7.0 or 7.1.

497.content: Tarno is a manager at the Voynich Guild's Nasha Town outlet, which runs the souvenir shop. After the crisis in Nod-Krai he became the Guild's representative in the League and hosted its opening ceremony. He greets visitors in a friendly, helpful way and offers whatever help he can. His wiki profile has no further background.

498.content: The Nod-Krai Trade Expo is an annual event hosted by the Voynich Guild in Nasha Town. In the Where Waves Meet the Reef event (6.5, April to May 2026), Nefer asks the Traveler to help Jahoda handle VIP guests. Guests include Beidou, captain of the Crux fleet, and Navia, who leads an underworld organisation. The Guild forbids violence at the venue, so officials from Liyue and Fontaine had to wait before arresting an arms syndicate that had taken an interest in the expo. Nefer refuses to let customers be seized at the expo, so Chevreuse notes that only deals made through the expo are protected; Nefer agrees she cannot interfere outside it, on condition that the Traveler takes part in the operation.

499.content: During the Marvelous Merchandise web event (November 2024), a seller named Liben describes his trip to Nod-Krai. He was robbed by vagrants before even entering Nasha Town, where he found no courts of law or Knights of Favonius. Someone told him to visit the Voynich Guild, the strongest force in the area. The Guild recovered his goods and then bought everything from him. He was robbed again on the way out.

500.content:
Wanderer's Troupe (also: Swordsman's Troupe, the Wanderer's Troupe, Wanderers' Troupe): The Wanderer's Troupe, also called the Swordsman's Troupe, was a group of travelling musicians who were also skilled fighters. A thousand years ago they wandered across Teyvat, then ended their journey in Mondstadt, where they stormed the city to overthrow its tyrannical aristocracy. They failed, and the troupe broke up, but its memory lives on in artifact and weapon lore and in the people it inspired.

Its four known members were the Conductor, the Sojourner (a harpist), the Dawnlight Swordswoman and Kreuzlied. They owned no sheet music, played swords for flutes and bows for harps, and performed for friends and for foes alike. The troupe's story is told only through item text and a few related books, so details are sparse and its members are known by titles rather than names.

Members: - **The Conductor**: the leader. He kept a book of the troupe's journeys called The Widsith and died holding it.
- **The Sojourner (the harpist)**: a privileged man from Fontaine who left home to wander. A skilled archer, he wielded The Stringless, a harp that was also a bow.
- **The Dawnlight Swordswoman (the Sword Dancer)**: wielder of The Flute, a sword that sang as she swung it. Her origin is unknown.
- **Kreuzlied**: a disowned member of the Lawrence Clan and the last to join. He carried The Bell, a greatsword with a clock in it.

Goals: The troupe set out to perform and to see the world, and its members decided there was so much to sing about that they wrote their journey down in The Widsith. Once in Mondstadt, they learned how the aristocracy treated the people and decided to end its rule by force.

Methods: Music and combat were one skill. The Flute made a flute-like sound depending on its swing angle, The Stringless fired arrows that followed its tune, and The Bell's clockwork gave the troupe a combat rhythm. The harpist reportedly lured birds with his harp and shot them down, and never looked at the sky while playing, which one companion read as the hunter's mercy and others read as arrogance. Artifact lore says the troupe's performances had two audiences, friends and foes, and that they once entered Mare Jivari to perform for their enemies.

History: **Wandering.** The troupe travelled all over Teyvat and through harsh lands such as the desert and the burning Mare Jivari. Members came from many places. **Arrival in Mondstadt.** Their journey ended in Mondstadt around the time of Ludi Harpastum. The harpist fell in love with a woman who had been chosen as the Harpastum maiden, the one who would be claimed by a member of the tyrannical Lawrence Clan. **The uprising.** The troupe stormed Mondstadt's city to overthrow the aristocracy. It failed: the Conductor and the Sojourner died in the fighting, the Sojourner covering his friends' retreat and playing until he ran out of songs and arrows. The Dawnlight Swordswoman was enslaved as a gladiator. Kreuzlied was left alive because of his privileged birth, and what punishment he received was never made public.

Relations: - **Mondstadt Aristocracy and Lawrence Clan**: the troupe's enemies. Kreuzlied was himself born a Lawrence.
- **Ragnvindr**: inspired by the Dawnlight Swordswoman, he became the Dawn Knight and turned against the corrupt nobles.
- **Vennessa**: aided by Kreuzlied's society when she rebelled.

Reputation: The troupe is largely forgotten. The Widsith's lore says the memory of the rebellion faded, yet the spirit of resistance remains. Item lore treats it with fondness: the troupe's end is mourned, and the dying notes of its instruments are described as the last sound it made.

Status as of 7.1: The troupe is long gone. Nothing in canon through 7.1 shows its members returning, though the Wanderer's Troupe weapons and artifacts survive in the world.

No story content about the troupe was found for 6.0 to 7.1.

501.comment: Wanderer's Troupe: The Sojourner's love story
501.content: The harpist, who came from Fontaine and was well loved by the ladies of its Court, left home to follow a wandering life and seek his destiny. In Mondstadt, by a lake, he met a stern, unsmiling maiden who was to be offered up as the Ludi Harpastum maiden of the Lawrence nobles. Item lore records his promise to break her chains and see her smile once. When the uprising came, he fired his last arrow for his comrades, for freedom and against the nobles who had taken her joy. He died unnamed in a foreign land, regretting only that he never sang another love song. Artifact lore (Feather of Homecoming) notes that the Mondstadt sky reminded him of his homeland. The wiki notes that "Sojourner" is an unofficial name.

502.content: She wielded the sword The Flute and moved to music, "beautiful as the light on water, elegant as the chirping lark". After the failed uprising she was made a gladiator but still sang of freedom. Ballads of the Squire quotes her challenging a young Ragnvindr about the lives he placed on a pedestal, asking whether he had not once known freedom. Ragnvindr watched her last fight, buried her with her sword and named himself the Dawn Knight after her title.

503.content: The Widsith is the troupe's travel journal. The members had no sheet music and turned the notes they played into words. The Conductor held it tightly even in death. The weapon of the same name is a catalyst. Its text says the troupe's song was an anthem of rebellion and that their last act was an attempt to storm the city and sentence its rulers.

504.comment: Wanderer's Troupe: The Bell and Kreuzlied
504.content: Kreuzlied, a Lawrence who became the troupe's outcast member, wielded a greatsword with a clock in it. Its ticking gave the troupe a combat rhythm, and its text calls its strike the toll of the bell of judgment. After the troupe's defeat the weapon was soaked in acid and rusted. Kreuzlied avoided harsh punishment because of his birth, and later founded a secret society to carry on his companions' work.

505.content:
Wangsheng Funeral Parlor (also: Wangsheng, Wangsheng Parlor, Hall of Rebirth, Wangsheng-tang): The Wangsheng Funeral Parlor is the funeral house of Liyue Harbor, on Feiyun Slope. It arranges burials, cremations and memorial rites for the dead of every rank, and it also performs the rites that send off adepti. It is run by the Hu family, which has held the Directorship for 77 generations. The current Director is Hu Tao, and Zhongli works there as consultant. The parlour also keeps a duty most people never see: watching the border between life and death, and burning away the fetor that leaks across it.

In Liyue, people tend not to talk to Wangsheng staff or to dwell on what they do. The parlour treats that as part of the job, and its stated client philosophy is that everyone who departs, whatever their wealth or standing, deserves a ceremony that honours them.

Structure: The head is the Director, a title passed down the Hu family; Hu Tao is the 77th. Under her are undertakers who carry out ceremonies and prepare burials and cremations. The wiki lists the Ferrylady and Meng among them. Hu Tao also invites consultants from different trades to lecture the undertakers once the parlour closes each day, so that funeral practice is taught as a body of knowledge, not as habit. Zhongli is the most revered of these lecturers. Commissions are taken at a board outside the door, where clients write requests on blank wooden tiles and slide them under the door.

Leadership: Hu Tao is the 77th Director. She is a cheerful, eccentric young woman who treats the work seriously beneath the jokes. Zhongli is the parlour's consultant; Hu Tao teases him for being old-fashioned while trusting him more than anyone else.

Before her came Old Hu, the 75th Director and her grandfather, and Hu Tao's father, the 76th. Her great-uncle, Baizhu's master, was Old Hu's younger brother, according to the wiki. Zhongli handles ceremonies that rely on exact tradition. His profile says Hu Tao asks him to help with the rites for sending adepti away, because the tradition now exists only in texts and almost nobody alive has seen it performed.

Members: - **Hu Tao**: 77th Director.
- **Zhongli**: consultant who lectures the undertakers on rites and etiquette. In the Archon Quest Tartaglia introduces him to the Traveler as consultant to "an organization known as Wangsheng" and a trusted associate of the Fatui.
- **The Ferrylady**: an undertaker who stands outside the parlour at night. She prepares ashes silently while families stay shut in their rooms, and she does not speak to the bereaved, following old custom.
- **Meng**: a newer undertaker who joined, according to the story quest, so he could ask the Director to search for his dead childhood friend Big G.
- **Past Directors**: Old Hu (75th) and Hu Tao's father (76th), both dead.

Methods: Funerals follow traditional steps: a wake, burial, a memorial plaque, cremation where requested. Hu Tao's own approach is flexible about style but strict about respect. The parlour's secret technique is the Art of Homa, which purifies the border between life and death and burns away fetor. Practitioners use Homa altars and the Staff of Homa. Hu Tao says doing it right takes great focus and no hesitation in the face of death; a faulty performance can shorten the caster's life or even kill them at once, depending on how much fetor they take in.

History: **Origin.** By the parlour's own account, after the Archon War the Yaksha accumulated karma while fighting vengeful gods, and part of it became a plague that swept Liyue. Frightened people took it for a divine curse. A few realised the plague could be stopped by purifying the air and burning the infected dead; they became the parlour's founders, and after many years the plague ended. Since then their successors have preserved the balance between life and death.

**Recent generations.** Old Hu and Hu Tao's father were the 75th and 76th Directors. Ten years before the Traveler arrived, the two went to Wuwang Hill to burn away a runaway growth of fetor. Her father, unable to let go of his regrets, faltered at the last moment and died on the spot. Old Hu contained the damage, but the fetor he absorbed killed him soon afterwards, before he was sixty. The nearby village was abandoned and the hill changed permanently. Hu Tao succeeded them.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the parlour is active. Hu Tao is Director and Zhongli remains consultant. Hu Tao appears in the 6.3 (Luna IV) Lantern Rite story with her friends, but no story about the parlour itself was found for 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 (Snezhnaya).

The most recent major Wangsheng story is the 5.3 Springtime Charms event, a limited-time event whose ritual Hu Tao survived. The Ferrylady, Meng and the other undertakers continue to serve.

506.comment: Wangsheng Funeral Parlor: Hu Tao as Director
506.content: Hu Tao is the parlour's 77th Director. See her own entry for biography and personality. In the parlour she leads the undertakers through funeral processions and decides how each ceremony will go, and she is the one who takes parties into the border to speak with the dead. Her unusual approach, equal parts showmanship and solemnity, is described in the parlour's methods.

507.comment: Wangsheng Funeral Parlor: Zhongli, Wangsheng consultant
507.content: Zhongli is the parlour's consultant. He teaches the undertakers and supplies the exact customs of rites, especially ceremonies for sending adepti off. Hu Tao teases him for being old-fashioned, yet trusts him most. He joined after staging his death as Rex Lapis. His own entry carries the full story.

508.content: The Ferrylady is an undertaker, found outside the parlour at night. She prepares burials and cremations and, by old custom, does not speak to the families of the dead. Strangers who speak to her surprise her, and she may take them for lost souls. During Springtime Charms she is the person people ask about Hu Tao's whereabouts. The wiki notes her name may refer to Charon.

509.comment: Wangsheng Funeral Parlor: Meng and Big G
509.content: Meng is a newer undertaker who joined the parlour to ask Hu Tao to find his childhood friend Big G, who died in an accident. With the Traveler's help, Hu Tao takes Meng and Big G into the border, where Big G says goodbye and moves on. Meng takes unpaid leave afterwards. The story is part of Hu Tao's story quest.

510.comment: Wangsheng Funeral Parlor: Art of Homa and fetor
510.content: Fetor is the energy that leaks out when the border between life and death is disturbed. It ages the living, causes weakness and coma, and can kill; adepti can see it and humans generally cannot. The parlour's secret Art of Homa burns it away with altars and the Staff of Homa, and demands total focus. Minor leaks are routine for the parlour. A major leak may require purifying the whole border, which is what happened in Springtime Charms.

511.comment: Wangsheng Funeral Parlor: Border between life and death
511.content: The "border" is a place most people never know exists, reached from Wuwang Hill. Ley Lines run wild there, and the dead who are unwilling or unable to leave linger. Hu Tao holds farewell ceremonies there and asks the dead questions. The parlour monitors it so that death does not spill out. Visitors must keep calm and follow Hu Tao's lead.

512.comment: Wangsheng Funeral Parlor: Wuwang Hill disaster
512.content: According to Springtime Charms, a limited-time event, ten years before the Traveler's arrival Old Hu and his son went to Wuwang Hill to burn away a runaway fetor growth. Hu Tao's father, unable to let go of his regrets, faltered and was killed instantly. Old Hu contained the damage but died soon afterwards. A nearby village was abandoned and the hill changed permanently. Hu Tao took over as Director.

513.comment: Wangsheng Funeral Parlor: Commission board and special offers
513.content: Outside the parlour hangs a board of wooden tiles. Clients write their commission on a tile and slide it under the door. During Hu Tao's story quest, her advertising scheme appears on the back of each tile as a "buy one get one free" offer for whoever holds it.

514.content:
Watatsumi Army (also: Watatsumi Troops, the Resistance, Sangonomiya Rebels, Sangonomiya troops, Sangonomiya Samurai, Watatsumi forces): The Watatsumi Army, also called the Resistance, is the armed force of Watatsumi Island in Inazuma. It was raised against the Vision Hunt Decree and the Shogunate's Sakoku order and is led by Sangonomiya Kokomi, the island's Divine Priestess, with General Gorou commanding in the field. Its soldiers are called Sangonomiya samurai or troops, and the Shogunate calls them rebels. The decree is now abolished, so the army works as peacekeepers and rebuilders.

Its ranks include people who had lost their Visions, people who feared losing them, and people who simply opposed the decree, Visions or not. The Resistance also hid those unwilling to fight the Shogun's forces. Its bases are Watatsumi Island, where the Sangonomiya Shrine stands, and Fort Fujitou on Yashiori Island.

Structure: The army is organised into small numbered units named after fish: Herring, Stingray, Swordfish and Gorgasia. Each is divided into numbered squads (Herring I, Swordfish II, Gorgasia II and so on). Kokomi sits at the top, Gorou is general, and officers such as Kaida Ryouma hold camps like Fort Fujitou. Rank-and-file soldiers are Sangonomiya samurai in a standard uniform based on the ashigaru foot-soldier. It is red and white, with the Sangonomiya crest on the back and on the right shoulder guard, and soldiers such as Nathan carry a cross-bladed spear (juumonji yari). The Traveler was made captain of Swordfish II.

Leadership: Sangonomiya Kokomi, the Divine Priestess, is the supreme leader. She is a brilliant strategist who plans for every scenario in advance. General Gorou, who is open-hearted and trusted by his troops, leads the soldiers on the battlefield.

Kokomi inherited the Priestess role through the Sangonomiya bloodline. It passes on the will of the dead god Orobashi in a mortal body, to defend Watatsumi Island. She has read military treatises since childhood, favours winning wars at the lowest cost by shaping the larger strategic situation, and in her story quest admits privately that she never wanted to be a leader, though her bloodline made it inevitable. The islanders say "Things will be alright as long as Her Excellency is here." Gorou came up through the ranks. In one crisis his unit's captain fell, and he led a feint that held the line for days until Kokomi's own relief force arrived. That earned him command of Gorgasia II and later the generalship. He is humble and straightforward. His troops call him the "ever-victorious pointy-eared general," and he has a short temper in the heat of battle.

Members: Notable members: Kaida Ryouma, an officer at Fort Fujitou who once worked for the Kujou Clan on Narukami Island and who remembers the Kujou brothers as sympathetic to commoners; Teppei, a logistician turned front-line captain; and many named samurai, including Moriguchi, Takahashi, Denjirou, Arisawa and Koutoku. Kaedehara Kazuha was sheltered by the Resistance before leaving Inazuma to join the Crux. Beidou and Kazuha appeared at the battle of Nazuchi Beach as mercenary reinforcements that Kokomi brought.

Goals: During the war the army's aim was to resist the Vision Hunt Decree and to protect Watatsumi Island and its people. It also opposed the Sakoku Decree, which was imposed at the same time. Kokomi had her own aim as well, which was to win in a way that kept costs low. After the war the army's aims are to keep the peace, rebuild the island's economy, and root out Fatui remnants.

Reputation: Among the islanders the army is deeply trusted, and Kokomi's name is a byword for reassurance. Gorou is beloved by his men, and even Shogunate warriors repeat his "ever-victorious" nickname. The Shogunate treated it as a rebel force during the war.

Status as of 7.1: The Vision Hunt Decree has been repealed and the Watatsumi Army no longer fights the Shogunate. It serves as peacekeepers and helps the island recover, while still clearing out Fatui remnants.

Peace talks with the Tenryou Commission followed, and Kokomi created a new corps for island defence. No new Watatsumi Army story was found in 6.0 to 7.1.

515.content: Swordfish II is a special operations unit that Kokomi gives the Traveler to captain in Sword, Fish, Resistance. Members named in canon are Koutoku (a former provisional squad leader), Kaneda, Shikishima and Yoshihisa. The unit investigates the disappearance of supplies near Fort Mumei while staying at Bourou Village. In the Reunion anecdote, the members still call the Traveler their captain and invite them to a bonfire party.

516.content: Fort Fujitou is the Resistance camp on Yashiori Island. Kaida Ryouma is its officer, and workers and a blacksmith live there. Teppei brings the Traveler there to meet Gorou, and the camp is the base from which the fight against Sara's troops is organised. After Kokomi's story quest the camp's background soldiers withdraw.

517.content: Teppei was a logistics officer who wanted to make a name for himself. He guides the Traveler to the Resistance and becomes captain of Herring I. Fatui supporters gave him a "secret weapon" that was really a Delusion. It drained his life, and he died rapidly aged. Kokomi ordered all use stopped afterwards.

518.content:
Yae Publishing House (also: Yae-dou): Yae Publishing House is a light-novel publisher and bookshop in Inazuma City. Yae Miko, the Guuji of the Grand Narukami Shrine, founded it and is its editor-in-chief. She started it, by her own account, because she wanted more entertaining light novels to read. Its flagship event is the periodic "This Novel Is Amazing!" writing contest, and its books are read well beyond Inazuma.

The ground floor is a shop where the house sells its own titles. Editors, authors and illustrators work under Miko, who is feared and relied on in equal measure.

Structure: Miko is boss, founder and editor-in-chief. Under her are editors who each manage particular authors, such as Kuroda (executive editor and shopkeeper, who handles Chang the Ninth), Shigeru (Junkichi's editor), Aratani (organises the writing contest and runs author correspondence) and Onodera (organises release events). Authors write under pen names more often than not. The shop on the ground floor sells the house's books directly, including serialised volumes and early printings.

Leadership: Yae Miko decides what gets published. She is known to be warm and bookish in the house and openly mercenary about profit, and she teases her authors about their deadline excuses.

Miko says she has never written a novel herself and that being an editor is its own entertainment. She told the Traveler that if they ever finish their journey and want it recorded, she might write it, if she has time. She is said to review the house's novels personally. She has also sent manuscripts back for being "not free enough", telling the author to ignore genre fashions and write the story well. In one character story, the author's very next manuscript worried her only because the pen name seemed too ordinary for its content.

Goals: The house exists to publish and sell light novels. Miko's own motives are entertainment and a taste for watching writers struggle with deadlines. Commercial success also matters: she is described as having an obsessive side about profit. The house wants to attract new talent, and the writing contest is its way of finding it.

Methods: The house runs the "This Novel Is Amazing!" contest, invites past winners to judge it, and holds writers' submission events. It publishes light novels in serial form, then collects them into volumes. Citlali notes that a serial takes about two weeks to reach Natlan and about a year before it is collected as a single volume. It also prints comics, guidebooks and military-strategy works such as the Teyvat Art of War, which Kokomi loves. It sells collectable first and deluxe editions and gives away early prints as gifts, as Miko did for the Legion of Soulblazers. It keeps in touch with authors by mail, even for those who never show up in person.

History: The house is no more than 500 years old. Ei, who withdrew into the Plane of Euthymia about that long ago, says there was no Yae Publishing House at the time. By the time of the Traveler's first visit to Inazuma the house was a giant of the industry and a lively bookshop. During the Sakoku Decree (before Transient Dreams) it could not invite outlander authors or send them royalties. Afterwards its editors eagerly planned visits.

Reputation: Inazuma's publishing giant: famed for light novels, bestsellers and the "This Novel Is Amazing!" contest. Fans make pilgrimages to buy its books.

Kuroda says many light-novel readers from other islands travel to the shop, and calls it a "pilgrimage". Kokomi names the house's military-strategy publications as her favourites, and Citlali says she has read almost every novel it has published. Not every reader is impressed: Chang the Ninth's editor Aratani calls his themes slightly dated, though his book sells steadily.

Status as of 7.1: Active and thriving as of Version 7.1. Miko still runs it, the bookshop in Inazuma City still sells its books, and the contest is still held.

No canon shows any change in the house's standing in the 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content checked. Its latest appearances in canon are the 6.2 Witch's Homework quest with Onodera and the Soulblazers event gift.

519.content: Kuroda is the executive editor of Yae Publishing House and runs its bookshop in his spare time. He edits Chang the Ninth, wishes he had gone to Liyue to chase him for manuscripts during the Sakoku Decree, and wanted the author to use a flashier pen name. He knows the collection value of the house's books. For the Traveler's friend Citlali he handed over a first edition of "Shogun Almighty: Reborn as Raiden With Unlimited Power" and the limited deluxe edition of "Pretty Please, Kitsune Guuji?", which are no longer sold. He is nervous around Miko and, when Ei visited, worried she was there to inspect regulations or fire safety.

520.comment: Yae Publishing House: This Novel Is Amazing contest
520.content: The house's recurring writing contest is famous across Teyvat. Past winners are invited to serve as judges. Chang the Ninth entered and won with his martial-arts novel, "First Apprentice of Guhua". The title is a nod to a real-world light-novel guidebook. In Yae Publishing House's Invitation (2.0), Aratani sends gifts and letters to Chang the Ninth and Zhenyu to ask them to judge.

521.comment: Yae Publishing House: A Legend of Sword
521.content: "A Legend of Sword" is a six-volume space-opera adventure by Zhenyu, illustrated by Calx. Zhenyu is Xingqiu's pen name. Liyue publishers had rejected it, so Xingqiu printed a few copies privately and left them at Wanwen Bookhouse. A merchant carried one to Inazuma, where it was a smash hit and later reached Fontaine. It sits at the top of the bestseller list. Xingqiu is surprised to learn this. Kokomi is an enthusiastic reader.

522.comment: Yae Publishing House: Ms. Hina and That's Life
522.content: "That's Life" is a magazine whose advice column is answered by "Ms. Hina". Readers love her, and a fan club of three has formed in Inazuma City. Its club rules are not to pry into her identity, not to say controversial things and not to push the column on the uninterested. Gorou secretly writes the replies. He enjoys it, he says, because letters let readers treat him as a friend, unlike soldiers who are reserved around a general.

523.comment: Yae Publishing House: Mr. Nine and Nod-Krai
523.content: In the Witch's Homework quest "Alan Smithee, Author of Fischl", Mr. Nine, in danger in Nod-Krai, writes to the house. Onodera travels to Mondstadt to commission the Traveler and Fischl, who adopted a persona from Mr. Nine's "Flowers for Princess Fischl". They first suspect Chang the Ninth, who is not Mr. Nine, and then use Oz to track her to Nod-Krai, where Nicole is revealed. Mr. Nine tells them she buried Chang's royalties in his yard.

524.comment: Yae Publishing House: Irodori Festival stall
524.content: During the limited-time event Hues of the Violet Garden, the house co-hosted Ritou's Irodori Festival with the Yashiro Commission. Murata ran its official stall, Fukumoto a children's book booth, and Onodera planned the release party of A Legend of Sword. Kuroda regretted that Chang the Ninth could not deliver a manuscript in time. Kokomi's pen-pal visit and Gorou's lucky draw appear in the same event.

525.content:
Yaksha (also: Yakshas, the Yakshas, Five Yakshas, Five Mighty Yakshas, Guardian Yakshas, Vigilant Yaksha, yaksha adepti): The yakshas were a fierce kind of illuminated beast-adepti. After the Archon War, Morax summoned them to wage an unending war on the monsters, plagues and curses born from the hatred of defeated gods. Five were the strongest and became known as the Five Yakshas. The work burdened them with karmic debt, and nearly all died, went mad or vanished. Only Alatus, now called Xiao, remains.

In Liyue the yakshas are now mostly forgotten, though statues and a few old books still keep their memory. The wiki spells "Yaksha" with a capital only for the five foremost, but the word is also used for the whole kind.

Structure: The yakshas were adepti, not a mortal organisation. Many served, but five stood above the rest: Bosacius, Indarias, Bonanus, Menogias and Alatus. Bosacius, the eldest, led them. The wiki lists Pervases as a lesser yaksha who was slain in the Archon War, and the book notes many other yakshas of unknown name who also died or fled.

Leadership: The yakshas answered to Morax, the Geo Archon, who summoned them. The book says they followed him wherever battle took him. Bosacius, the eldest, was their leader.

Members: - **Alatus (Xiao)**: the last yaksha. Morax freed him from a cruel god who had enslaved him and gave him the name Xiao for his protection.
- **Bosacius**: leader of the Five, an Electro yaksha with four arms. He left his treasures at Minlin, later went mad and forgot his own name, and died in the Chasm as the "Nameless Yaksha".
- **Indarias, Bonanus, Menogias**: the other three of the Five, all dead.
- **Pervases**: a junior yaksha who died in the Archon War and whose spirit lingers in a crane statue at his run-down temple near Mt. Tianheng.

Goals: Their duty was to defend Morax's rule and Liyue by purging the monsters and miasmas that grew from defeated gods' lingering hatred. The cinematic gives their oath as restoring order through slaughter and purging evil through battle, to which they gave their lives.

Methods: They fought without mercy, as the book puts it. They are adeptal arts users: Xiao performs Dream Trawler to cultivate himself and Mortal Lingering was used by Pervases. Xiao's Nuo Dance of Evil Conquering, a rite for purging demons and divine karma, is thought to have been practised by several yakshas, each in their own version.

History: Morax summoned the yakshas to purge the demons born from the bodies and hatred of the gods he had defeated. For about a thousand years they fought. The accumulating karmic debt wore at their souls: some raged, some went mad with fear, some turned on their own, and some were lost to illusion. Three of the five died, a fourth vanished and the rest of the many yakshas died or fled. Alatus alone survived.

Relations: - **Morax and Zhongli**: the yakshas shared a special bond with Morax, who named Xiao and Pervases himself. As Zhongli he prepares medicine for Xiao to ease his karmic pain.
- **Other adepti**: respect the yakshas' strength. Xiao holds high seniority and is called Conqueror of Demons; Ganyu has asked him for training, though Xiao thinks himself unfit to teach her.
- **Liyue Qixing**: its secret agents built Wangshu Inn at Dihua Marsh to support Xiao's duty.

Reputation: Long ago mortals revered the yakshas as Liyue's protectors, raising large statues (for example at Luhua Pool) and offering chants and food to ease their pain. Today the statues are battered and the features worn away. The surviving books, such as Yakshas: The Guardian Adepti and the "Ode to Windborne Wraith" chapter of a travel guide to Liyue, are dull and little read, and the Liyue edition omitted the latter. Hu Tao notes that talk of curses and miasmas would cause panic if people knew they were real, so the yakshas remain legend.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Xiao is the only living yaksha. The 5.x to 7.1 material checked adds nothing new about the yakshas.

Xiao still keeps watch over Liyue, living at Wangshu Inn. Version 7.0 added only a cosmetic Echo for him, and the Nod-Krai and Snezhnaya story content did not revisit the yakshas.

526.content: Bosacius (Electro, Marshal Vritras, eldest and leader), Indarias (Pyro, General Musatas), Bonanus (Hydro, General Chizapus), Menogias (Geo, General Kapisas) and Alatus (Anemo, the Golden-Winged King and Conqueror of Demons) were the strongest yakshas. Only Alatus, now Xiao, lives. The wiki gives the element for Indarias and Menogias from their Japanese voice actors; Bonanus is Hydro by elimination.

527.content: A volume from the "Hidden Wonders and Folklore of Liyue" series, written in archaic, wordy prose by a Sumeru scholar. It says Rex Lapis summoned the yakshas to purge demons, that the five strongest were Bosacius, Indarias, Bonanus, Menogias and Alatus, and that after a thousand years only Alatus survived. It adds that at the Lantern Rite people see a glow at Guyun Stone Forest and hear a flute among the marsh reeds of Dihua Marsh, which they take as the Vigilant Yaksha at work. Starsnatcher buys it during the Alatus Chapter and Paimon and the Traveler read it.

528.content: In this setting karma builds up in those who slay the lingering remnants of fallen gods. It wears away at the soul, causing rage, madness and pain, and it taints the surroundings: Xiao's karma can strengthen nearby monsters and stain mortals who stay near him. Xiao and Yelan attribute the madness of Rongzhao, who fought beside Bosacius without a Vision, to that karma, reasoning that without a Vision he could not resist it for long. Hu Tao says part of the yakshas' karma once became a plague in Liyue, which the founders of Wangsheng Funeral Parlor stopped by purifying the air and burning the dead.

529.comment: Yaksha: Nuo Dance of Evil Conquering
529.content: A rite for purging demons and divine karma. The wiki notes the English name was rewritten to match its use as a title. Liyue's rulers, who know Xiao's truth, call his millennia of work the "Bane of All Evil". It is not known how many other yakshas used the same technique.

530.comment: Yaksha: Wangshu Inn and the yakshas
530.content: The Liyue Qixing's secret agents built Wangshu Inn at Dihua Marsh to give Xiao a place to rest and to help him purge plagues. Verr Goldet and Huai'an run it and cover for the damage his night work can cause. The wiki says it has stood at least since the years after the cataclysm, about 500 years ago.

531.comment: Yaksha: Xiao and the other yakshas
531.content: Xiao's character story and voice-overs describe a reserved warrior who avoids mortals for their sake and does not want sympathy, believing his fallen comrades would find tears a stain on their memory. He is fond of his fellow yakshas. When the Traveler met Pervases, he quickly grew nostalgic. Xiao's own entry carries his full history.

532.content:
Yashiro Commission (also: Yashiro Bugyo, Yashiro Bugyou, Sha-bugyou, Yashiro Commissioner): The Yashiro Commission (Sha-bugyou, "Commission of Shrines") is one of the three bodies of Inazuma's Tri-Commission, alongside the Tenryou and Kanjou Commissions. It handles shrines, festivals, ceremonies and the cultural life of the people, and is run by the Kamisato Clan from the Kamisato Estate on Narukami Island. The Commissioner is Kamisato Ayato. His sister Ayaka is its warm public face. Behind the festivals it also commands the secret Shuumatsuban ninja.

It has less raw influence than the Tenryou and Kanjou Commissions but is the best liked. Its soldiers are relaxed and care about ordinary people, and in the Inazuma Archon Quests it stayed clear of the Fatui's schemes. All three commissions hold the same authority and can keep one another in check.

Structure: Authority sits with the Kamisato Clan. Ayato, as Clan Head, is the Commissioner and handles governance, while Ayaka handles the clan's public image and dealings with ordinary people. The Commission is headquartered inside the main building of the Kamisato Estate. Representatives such as Hirano, Hirotatsu and Madarame Hyakubei work at the estate, and other listed staff include Furusawa, Kazumasa, Ogawa and Takami. Shogun's Army soldiers assigned to it are described as more relaxed than those under the other commissions. The clan also owns the members-only Komore Teahouse in Inazuma City and controls the Shuumatsuban.

Leadership: Kamisato Ayato is the Yashiro Commissioner and head of the Kamisato Clan. He keeps a low public profile, works on government affairs and is known as clever, polite and hard to read. His sister Kamisato Ayaka, the Shirasagi Himegimi ("White Heron Princess"), is the clan's popular public face.

Ayaka says that after their parents died she and Ayato took responsibility for clan matters together, though she still relies on Ayato for every important decision. Ayato took the post young, after his father's early death, following his parents' wishes and to protect Ayaka. A character story says that at first nobody was impressed by the inexperienced young head, and that he stabilised the clan's position. Thoma, who came to Inazuma from Mondstadt, serves as housekeeper and is a trusted fixer.

Goals: Officially the Commission arranges ritual matters, shrines and public festivals, so that both the gods and the people are pleased. Its quieter aim, shown through Ayato, is to protect Inazuma and the Kamisato Clan, deal with corrupt officials, and use the Shuumatsuban where the Commissioner cannot act openly. The Commission also proposed repealing the Vision Hunt Decree, according to Ayaka.

Methods: Public work includes festival planning, ceremonies and community outreach. Ayaka says the Commission and shrine maidens share festival affairs, and that safety concerns such as fire prevention are planned in advance rather than cancelling events like fireworks. Ayato prefers to deal with corrupt officials within legal bounds, though he uses a wide range of methods.

Relations: Within the Tri-Commission, which divides the executive powers of what Ayaka's profile calls the Triarchal Council, the Yashiro are equal to the Kujou-led Tenryou Commission (security and military) and the Hiiragi-led Kanjou Commission (finance and borders). Ayaka says Yashiro proposals to repeal the Vision Hunt Decree were vetoed by both. Naoe Hisamasa calls the Yashiro the commission closest to the Raiden Shogun. The Grand Narukami Shrine's Guuji Yae Miko and Ayato work together because their duties overlap, though she dislikes his ways and calls him the "Yashiro rascal".

Reputation: Many Inazumans see it as the least controversial of the commissions, and as caring. After the Archon Quests, which left it mostly unaffected, it gained slightly more influence and goodwill. The public admires Ayaka warmly. Ayato is far less known, and rumours about him run from meticulous festivals to political tricks.

Secrets: The Shuumatsuban is a secret unit that reports directly to the head of the Kamisato Clan. Ayato inherited command from his father. Most members are orphans taken in young, which Ayato says guarantees loyalty. Members' identities are highly classified, and members who die on secret missions are not publicly honoured.

History: The Commission's early history is not described. Its recent past is tied to the Kamisato Clan's decline: Ayaka says the clan once failed to protect a swordsmith of national significance. The Fatui harassed it, many clan people were lost, and the Shogunate's trust fell. This aged their father and badly damaged the clan's standing. Ayato rebuilt it, and Ayaka says the Commission is now unified again.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Yashiro Commission is active under Ayato and remains based at the Kamisato Estate.

The wiki shows no major role for it in the Nod-Krai or Snezhnaya storylines of 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

533.content: The Shuumatsuban is a secret organisation of ninja under the Yashiro Commission. It is led by the head of the Kamisato Clan, currently Ayato, and its members report to him. Its work is espionage, intelligence gathering and covert action, and its slogan appears to be about sending the Shuumatsu to end traitors and criminals alike. Sayu is described as its resident ninja, and its headquarters is a ninja village. Members are paid monthly: Sayu's salary is 200,000 Mora. Most members are orphans raised from a young age, so loyalty runs deep. Known members include Inu Shoushou and Momoyo, plus staff such as Ogawa and Kano Nana. The retired Nakanishi and Taroumaru are former members.

534.content: The Komore Teahouse in Inazuma City is owned by the Yashiro Commission. Entry is members-only, limited to people the Kamisato Clan approves, and the clan often uses it as a local base and private meeting place. Its boss is Taroumaru, a Shiba Inu and a former Shuumatsuban ninja dog, who was famous with dog lovers, even overseas, before the Sakoku Decree. Other staff include Kozue, Nobumori and the retired Nakanishi. Customers leave payment in a box after drinking tea.

535.content: The Kamisato Estate is the clan's residence. The Yashiro Commission Headquarters is inside its main building, and staff such as Furuta, Koharu, Hirano, Hirotatsu and Madarame Hyakubei work there. Its map text says the Commission's duties are so pervasive that even Shogunate officials cannot follow them, and that the Shirasagi Himegimi is more popular than the head of the household.

536.content:
Yinyuan Hall (also: Yinyuan Chamber): Yinyuan Hall governs Liyue's salt industry and is one of the Eight Trades under the Liyue Qixing. Its members descend from people who survived the fall of Sal Terrae, the last haven of the God of Salt, Havria. The Hall tells a story of her death that the truth contradicts.

The Hall's version blames the Geo Archon Morax, who they say killed Havria out of envy. Zhongli, Morax's current vessel, corrects this in the Sal Flore story quest.

Structure: Yinyuan Hall is a trade body for salt merchants and producers. The only named member is Wanyan. The Hall passes down its history among its own people by word of mouth.

Members: Wanyan is the only member named. In Sal Flore she first said she was an archaeologist but lacked even basic archaeological knowledge. She is in truth a devotee of Havria from the Hall, and she wanted proof that Morax was guilty. She joined Zhongli, the Fatui researcher Kliment and the Traveler in the sealed ruins of Sal Terrae.

Goals: Its trade is salt. Beyond that, the story shown in canon is Wanyan's personal aim to prove her god's death was Morax's crime.

History: The Hall's origins lie in the Archon War. Havria refused to fight, gave way to other gods and finally held a small plot at Sal Terrae. According to Zhongli, her people's king killed her with a sword as a mercy, because her kindness could not protect them. Her power spread out and turned most of her followers into salt. The survivors scattered across Liyue, and some reached Liyue Harbor, which Morax protected, and eventually formed Yinyuan Hall.

Relations: Under the Liyue Qixing, in the same Eight Trades as Shenglu Hall. Its tradition is hostile to Morax, Liyue's old archon, though the Hall sits in his harbour city.

Secrets: The Hall holds a mistaken belief rather than a secret. The truth was told only to Wanyan, within a sealed ruin, so other members should not be assumed to know it.

Status as of 7.1: Active as of 7.1. The last event concerning the Hall in canon is the Sal Flore story quest from Version 1.1. No appearances were found in 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 (Snezhnaya) content.

537.comment: Yinyuan Hall: Havria and the Hall
537.content: Havria was a gentle, weak god of salt who fled the Archon War and was killed by her own king. The Hall's descendants believe Morax assassinated her. Zhongli says the sword found in Sal Terrae was the murder weapon, not her relic, and that her people acted from mercy. She left two relics: a chalice that refills itself with salt and a ruler that covers ground in salt.

538.content: Wanyan is a follower of Havria and a member of Yinyuan Hall. She posed as an archaeologist to seek proof against Morax, and she heard the truth from Zhongli in the ruins of Sal Terrae. She refused to believe it at first.

539.content:
Yun-Han Opera Troupe (also: Yun-Han Troupe, Yunhan Opera Troupe, Yun-Han Opera Company): The Yun-Han Opera Troupe is the best-known Liyue Opera company in Liyue Harbor. The house of Yun has run it for generations, and its current director is the opera singer and playwright Yun Jin. It performs regularly at Heyu Tea House.

Liyue Opera is a traditional art handed down over generations, and its performers usually work in troupes; canon calls this the most acclaimed of them. Beyond its star, it is a working organisation of veteran performers, a manager and backstage staff.

Structure: A director sits at the top and makes the big decisions. Managers handle daily work. Yunning is the manager seen in canon, and Yinggong looks after wardrobe and props. Many veteran performers belong to the troupe, and some joined under Yun Jin's grandfather. No other ranks or headcount are given.

Leadership: Yun Jin is the director, the troupe's lead performer and the author of its new plays. Her manager Yunning handles bookings and press.

Yun Jin's grandfather directed the troupe before her, and long-time fans called him "Sir Yun". After she took over, those fans came to her shows too and began to use the same title for her. Business circles call her "Director Yun" because she makes the big decisions. Veterans follow her lead in rehearsal, but offstage they treat her like a granddaughter and nag her about diet and tastes. Yunning is protective and anxious about Yun Jin's safety and public image.

Members: - **Yun Jin**: director, singer, playwright and star. See her own entry.
- **Yunning**: manager. Panics when Yun Jin disappears to seek inspiration, screens interviews and had the Millelith pursue tabloid impersonators.
- **Yinggong**: wardrobe and props manager and stagehand. He also makes paper theatre plays for children as a hobby and appeared in the 3.4 Lantern Rite event.
- **Veteran elders**: unnamed senior performers, some from her grandfather's time, who stay devoted to traditional Liyue Opera.
- **Yun Jin's grandfather**: former director, unnamed.

Goals: The troupe's work is to perform Liyue Opera well and keep the art alive. Under Yun Jin it also stages new plays beyond the classic repertoire. Yun Jin has privately wished to sing the stories of ordinary people's joys and sorrows rather than the adepti legends that dominate the genre. That is her own wish, and canon does not call it troupe policy.

Methods: The troupe performs for paying audiences at Heyu Tea House, where Yun Jin appears from time to time. Fans gather there hoping to catch her and ask about her schedule, which keeps the tea house busy. According to Yun Jin, troupe rules forbid accepting private gifts from patrons. Interview requests go through the manager and not directly to the star.

History: The Yun family were famous weaponsmiths about 500 years ago, and over time the family took up Liyue Opera. By the time of Yun Jin's grandfather the Yun-Han Opera Troupe existed.

Yun Jin's mother took up the mantle from her grandfather and was a famous opera singer in Liyue Harbor, and her father is a playwright. Yun Jin grew up around the troupe, and its veterans watched her grow into a rising star. She debuted young and later became director.

Relations: - **Heyu Tea House**: the troupe's regular venue. Its owner, Fan Er'ye, earns a great deal from Yun Jin's shows.
- **Xinyan**: a close friend of Yun Jin. The elders look down on rock 'n' roll, so Yun Jin keeps her visits secret from them.
- **Adventurers' Guild**: Yunning commissioned it in 2.4 to find Yun Jin.
- **The Millelith**: Yunning had them pursue tabloid impersonators.

Reputation: The troupe is regarded as the most famous opera company in Liyue Harbor. Yun Jin's character story says nine out of ten Heyu Tea House patrons are her fans. The elders are known for being devoted to traditional Liyue Opera and rather rigid about other kinds of music.

Status as of 7.1: Active as of 7.1. Yun Jin still directs the troupe and performs in Liyue Harbor.

No news of the troupe was found in 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 (Snezhnaya) content.

540.content: Yunning is the manager of the Yun-Han Opera Troupe and appears in Yun Jin's Hangout Event. When Yun Jin vanished days before a big show, she commissioned the Adventurers' Guild and begged the Traveler to find her, afraid the audience would tear the place down and that Yun Jin might get hurt. She insists on handling interviews herself and had the Millelith pursue the fake Steambird reporters. In canon she is excitable, dramatic and fiercely protective of her star. Her full name, age and background are not given.

541.content: During the 3.4 Lantern Rite event "The Exquisite Night Chimes", Yinggong ran a paper theatre for children in Liyue Harbor, and the Traveler helped perform "Homeward, Bravebeard". He explained that he works for the Yun-Han Opera Troupe on wardrobe and props, that he can carry a tune after years with the troupe, and that backstage helpers had the festival off. He stayed in the city himself because his parents had died two years earlier. He says paper plays are simpler than Liyue Opera because one person can do everything.
